articleTitle: Performance Comparison of FOC and DTC Techniques for SynRM in EV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Synchronous Reluctance Motors (SynRM) are becoming popular in electric vehicles, renewable energy, and domestic applications over PMSM and Induction machines due to their advantages, such as the absence of rare earth materials, less copper losses, robust construction, and high efficiency. The performance of a SynRM is enhanced by its rotor geometry through improving the saliency ratio, along with its control strategies. This work focuses on the performance evaluation of control strategies, comparing two distinct methods applied to Synchronous Reluctance motors: Field oriented control (FOC) and Direct torque control (DTC), targeting EV applications. These control techniques are prominent strategies for SynRM, offering precise control over speed and torque. The features of both methods are illustrated and simulated for various EV torque and speed testing profiles using MATLAB/Simulink software.

articleTitle: A High-Gain Non-Isolated Boost-SEPIC DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Renewable energy sources have become one of the most effective approaches to mitigate environmental problems, especially in the face of the significant increase in greenhouse gas emissions in recent years. In this context, it is evident that the use of sustainable energy sources positively contributes to the planet. To optimize the use of these sources, voltage boost converters are crucial as they allow for energy processing and the interconnection of sources and loads with different voltage levels. However, despite traditional converters like the Boost converter being theoretically capable of achieving high voltage gain with high duty cycles, the stress on components and the associated losses are also high, making their use less efficient. This article proposes a new non-isolated high voltage gain DC-DC converter, the Boost-SEPIC, inspired by conventional Boost and SEPIC converters.

articleTitle: Improved Active Frequency Drift Islanding Detection Method for Grid-Tied Distributed Energy Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Anti-islanding protection/detection (AIP) is required for the grid connected distributed energy resources (DERs) due to the concern of personnel and equipment safety. Passive AIP and communication-based AIP methods are not desirable in DERs because of larger Non-Detective Zone (NDZ) for the former and expensive communication infrastructure for the later, respectively. Active AIP method, such as active frequency drift (AFD) was reported for DERs owing to its simple design and smaller NDZ. However, AFD method affects quality of the DER output current due to the AFD current injection. The performance of the AFD injection is determined by NDZ and total harmonic distortion (THD) of the output current. This paper proposes two AFD current injections, (i) combined sine and rectangular injection, and (ii) combined sine and trapezoidal injection. The former proposed AFD current injection generates 25% less THD compared to the conventional AFD injection, and the latter one generates 39% less THD. The reduction in THD at the proposed current injections can increase reactive power injection and result in less NDZ and quicker island detection. The effectiveness of the proposed AFD current injection waveforms is theoretically analyzed and verified through time domain simulation results.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis of SEIG-ELC System Using Markov Modelling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: One of the main power producing devices in the nation's remote locations is the self-excited induction generator. An electronic load controller (ELC) is used to regulate voltage and frequency when the load is perturbed while operating in an isolated mode. Changing environmental conditions have an impact on the SEIG-ELC system's ability to store extra generated power in a dump load during a power outage. To analyze reliability of the isolated system, this work presents three-component Markov modelling, which consists of an induction generator, a voltage sensor, and IGBT switches under both normal and adverse weather conditions.

articleTitle: Novel Converter Topology for Bipolar DC Programmable Power Supply Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Bipolar programmable DC-DC converters are capable of generating a user-defined voltage waveform of either polarity across the output terminals. These versatile power supplies are used in power electronics testing, and industrial processes requiring a precise and variable bipolar voltage. This paper presents a novel isolated DC-DC converter developed based on the full-bridge topology for bipolar programmable power supply application. The proposed converter is designed for a rated power of 625 W and can provide a variable output voltage ranging from + 100V to -100V, allowing precise control within a 1 kHz frequency range. The isolation feature is implemented to ensure safety and reliability, which is critical for applications involving the testing of sensitive electronic equipment. The performance of the proposed converter is validated for bipolar as well as unipolar modes through simulation studies using MATLAB software. The simulation results confirm the proposed converter's capability to deliver stable and precise bipolar as well as unipolar power, indicating its suitability for use in advanced programmable power supply systems.

articleTitle: Quality Factor Optimization of Single-Layer Air Core Toroidal Inductors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The paper proposes a design methodology aimed at maximizing the quality factor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(Q_{L})$</tex> of single-layer foil-wire based air-core toroidal inductors having a specified outer radius and a target inductance value at a given operating frequency. The optimal ratio between the inner and outer radius of the toroid is analytically obtained, following which the optimal value of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(Q_{L})$</tex> is shown to be proportional to the outer radius of the toroid. A comprehensive design methodology is then proposed for the optimized toroidal inductor. The proposed optimization is experimentally validated using three toroidal inductors, all having the same outer radius but different inner radii. It is demonstrated that the inductor with the optimal design exhibits the highest quality factor.

articleTitle: A Novel Six-Switch Two-Output Port Isolated DC-DC Converter Acting as a DC Transformer for Battery Voltage Step-Up and Battery-to-PV Changeover Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel isolated six-switch DC-DC converter, consisting of two output ports - one isolated and one non-isolated, at different voltage levels catering to diverse voltage applications. The non-isolated port allows for an inverted buck-boost operation, whilst the isolated port with a secondary-to-primary High-Frequency Transformer (HFT) turns ratio <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> exhibits a pure DC transformer operation with a non-inverted polarity, i.e. its output voltage scales the input battery voltage by a factor of N. Continuous Conduction Mode (CCM) steady-state analysis of the converter is detailed and MATLAB® SIMULINK simulation waveforms for the converter operation under various modes are outlined. The closed-loop current controller is designed and tested with step load changes and the switchover from the battery-fed system to a Photovoltaic (PV) array is displayed to ensure its efficacy.

articleTitle: Advanced Sample-Based ANN MPPT for TCT Solar Panels in Partial Shading Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Due to their inherent potential and environmental benefits, renewable energy sources represent the most effective and sustainable alternatives for generating pollution-free energy in the contemporary era. Among these, solar energy stands out as a particularly promising option for supplying the essential power and energy needed to advance civilization. When the PV panel is shaded the output power will reduced. To overcome this issue MPPT is required. There are soft computing-based MPPT techniques available, but these are iterative-based. These are time-consuming but the ANN-based MPPT is fast to predict the global peak. In this paper a novel sample-based Artificial Neural Network (ANN) based MPPT method to optimize power extraction from Total Cross-Tied (TCT) configured photovoltaic panels under partial shading conditions. The proposed method along with TCT with different PSC. The proposed MPPT is compared with the Perturb & Observe (P&O), Incremental conductance (INC), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Cuckoo Search (CS). The proposed method is simulated with Matlab/Simulink software to examine the tracking time and efficiency. The proposed method is implemented using the DSP F28379D Launchpad micro controller (32-bit) and Chroma PV simulator. The result reveal that ANN MPPT is fast and better performance compare to other conventional methods.

articleTitle: Dual Switch Switched Inductor-Capacitor Network-Based High Gain DC-DC Converter with Reduced Switch Current Stress and Continuous Input Current
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In power electronics, achieving efficient and reliable DC voltage conversion from renewable energy systems is essential for various applications including portable electronic devices. This paper presents a novel Dual Switch Switched Inductor-Capacitor Network-based (DSSLCN) high-gain DC-DC converter topology that ensures continuous input current while reducing current stress through the switches. The proposed converter, comprising two inductors, three capacitors, three diodes, and two switches, achieves significant voltage gain and minimizes component current stress by operating with synchronized duty ratios for both switches. Theoretical analyses, including steady- state operation and parasitic effects, have been performed to derive an output voltage equation accounting for component characteristics. A hardware prototype of 400 V 200 W, 50 kHz, has been built, and the theoretical calculations are validated using the experimental results.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis of Grid Synchronization Enhancement in DFIG-Driven Wind System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The inherent variability of wind significantly impacts grid stability and diminishes power quality. Therefore, an enhanced control strategy is needed for grid-integrated DFIG-driven WES. The MSC utilizes an off-MPPT control mechanism to adhere to ESS limits, ensuring consistent power delivery to the grid under wind fluctuation. The ESS is incorporated across DC-link through BDC, facilitating charging, and discharging in alignment with system requirements during wind variation. It enables power smoothing and balancing, even with stochastic wind speed variation. Additionally, an Enhanced phase-locked loop control for the grid-integrated DFIG-driven WES, reduces DC offset, allowing both MSC, and GSC to operate efficiently despite various grid disturbances. The effectiveness of the presented PLL over conventional PLL is also presented. Furthermore, the proposed approach has been validated through tests conducted under sudden wind variations as well as different wind speeds. Additionally, outcomes confirm satisfactory system performance amidst sudden wind variability and grid disturbances.

articleTitle: Wide Duty Ratio DC DC Converter for Ultracapacitor Based EV Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Ultracapacitor-based electric vehicle storage systems are widely accepted owing to their attributes such as fast charging, high power density, and long charge-discharge efficiency over etc. Despite these advantages, ultracapacitors have severe reduction in terminal voltage while it discharges. To overcome this issue, an ultracapacitor-based storage requires a wide-duty high-gain DC DC boost converter as an interface between the UC bank and electric vehicle drive. In this study, a coupled inductor based novel high gain DC DC boost converter is proposed. The novel converter have the capability of boosting the terminal voltage with a wide variation in duty ratio (25-75%). A 100 W prototype of this converter is tested system and the results found satisfactory.

articleTitle: A Platform-less Voltage-Sourced Wind Energy Collection System for Offshore Wind Farms Using Single Active Bridge (SAB) Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The cost of installation of offshore wind farms (OWFs) can be reduced significantly if the large offshore platform can be eliminated. Thus, a platform-less series-connected DC offshore wind farm structure is adopted in this work, with single active bridges (SAB) acting as dc/dc converters on each wind turbine (WT). SABs are considered a suitable option for isolated DC-DC converters due to their compact size and galvanic isolation feature. Since wind turbines in a real offshore wind farm experience varying wind power inputs, the series-connected structure often faces the issue of voltage mismatch among the DC/DC converters. To address this, the inputs terminals of the series-connected SABs are connected in parallel in this work, and appropriate control strategies are developed to balance the output voltages of the SABs in spite of the variations in wind speed or failures in the wind turbines or converters. Unlike existing voltage balancing strategies, the proposed method does not require any fast communication between the wind turbines or between the onshore grid and the turbines. The effectiveness of the proposed structure and control strategy is validated through simulations and experimental results on a laboratory prototype.

articleTitle: Analysis of Integrated on-Board Charger for 400 V and 800 V EV Battery Using Dual-Mode Three-Leg LLC Resonant Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Electric vehicle technology is rapidly advancing to achieve higher power density and cost-effectiveness. On-board chargers (OBC) are evolving to support new power ratings and battery technologies, focusing on higher power and voltage capabilities to enhance power density and reduce recharge times. This paper proposes a novel three-leg LLC (TL-LLC) resonant converter for an On-board EV charger, designed to charge different EV models efficiently. By adopting a variable DC-link voltage as input, the converter tracks a wide battery voltage range, ensuring optimal efficiency. It operates in two modes: voltage doubler for 800-V charger and current doubler for 400-V charger at 10 kW power rating. MATLAB/Simulink simulations verify the converter's performance for both battery types at 10 kW power level.

articleTitle: Control of a Two Stage High-Frequency Isolated PV-Grid Integrated System with Improved Power Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Solar energy remains the predominant choice for renewable energy in residential and commercial applications. It is notable that residential PV-grid integrated systems are experiencing significant growth in recent times. The non-isolated PV-grid integrated systems encounter safety and leakage current issues. A novel two stage solar PV-single phase grid integrated system with galvanic isolation is proposed in the paper. The system consists of an LLC resonant DC-DC converter (LRDC) in order to provide galvanic isolation along with boosting of PV voltage and MPPT control. The LRDC employs zero current switching (ZCS) to reduce the switching stress, thereby enhancing the converter lifespan. Additionally high-frequency galvanic isolation makes the system more compact. A single phase voltage source inverter with second order generalized integral (SOGI) based grid integration control incorporated with power quality (PQ) enhancement is connected to the DC link. The performance of the proposed system is evaluated using matlab simulink model under different operating conditions.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization in Phase Shifted Full Bridge Converter Using Parallel Loop Shaping Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Phase-shifted Full-Bridge (PSFB) DC-DC converters are highly regarded for medium to high voltage and high power applications due to their ability to minimize switching and conduction losses. By utilizing Zero Voltage Switching (ZVS) through phase-shifted Pulse Width Modulation (PWM), these converters achieve significant reductions in switching losses during transitions, which enhances overall efficiency. The effective duty cycle in PSFB converters is crucial, as it directly influences the output voltage and power transfer capabilities. By carefully adjusting the phase shift between the switches, operators can optimize performance to maintain stable output voltages, even amid variations in input voltage, output current, or reference voltage. However, the non-minimum phase behavior of PSFB converters presents challenges for traditional control methods like Proportional-Integral (PI) and Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controllers, which may lead to stability issues. This paper proposes an effective control strategy to address these non-minimum phase characteristics by introducing a parallel control strategy, that integrates Voltage Mode Control (VMC) and Current Mode Control (CMC), enhanced by Type II and Type III compensators. VMC dynamically adjusts the duty cycle to regulate the output voltage, ensuring precise voltage control. Simultaneously, CMC improves transient response and provides overcurrent protection by continuously monitoring and regulating the output current. The Type II compensator enhances the steady-state response, while the Type III compensator improves transient performance and stability. This dual-mode control approach ensures optimal performance, stability, and responsiveness of the PSFB converter across diverse operating conditions, making it well-suited for demanding applications.

articleTitle: Restoration and Grid Integration of Unbalanced and Distorted Distribution System Using Inverter Based Renewable Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper deals with restoration and grid integration of an unbalanced and distorted distribution system, following a power outage (blackout). In this work, a new control strategy is proposed to enhance the restoration and grid integration capability of the grid forming based inverters consists of unbalanced and non-linear loads. Performance evaluation of grid forming based proposed control scheme is carried out during blackstart of an islanded distribution system. This system encompasses various type of loads like unbalanced and non-linear, as well as induction motor. The objectives are given as follows: (i) maintain the distortion less balanced voltage during restoration, (ii) restore all the loads without significant transient in current, voltage and power, (iii) whenever grid is available, re-synchronize with the grid as soon as possible for better reliability with respect to the loads and without instability. The entire distribution system along with the proposed inverter control is modeled using MATLAB/Simulink platform. The findings demonstrate improved ability of grid-forming inverters to initiate a blackstart and restoration operations, even with unbalanced and non-linear loads. The proposed controller ensures enhanced resiliency and reliability of an unbalanced and distorted distribution system with 100% inverter based renewable energy system during restoration and grid-integration.

articleTitle: Grid Emulator-based Testing of Power Factor Correction Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Power factor correction (PFC) circuits are employed as the front-end converters that convert AC power to DC power. These PFC circuits are connected to the ac grid that is prone to voltage sag, swell and distorted voltages. The PFC circuit behavior under these conditions has to be studied before connecting it to the actual ac grid. To emulate these conditions, power electronic converters based grid emulators are becoming popular because of their advantages in the testing and validation stage of hardware. Conventionally, grid emulators are realized with a back-to-back connected converter with a common dc-link, The output voltage of the DC-AC converter is controlled using closed-loop control to track the required output voltage reference. However, literature presents solutions for emulating grid using open-loop operation without an output LC filter for a three-phase grid-connected AC-DC converter. This idea of emulating grid voltage is extended to test a single-phase totem-pole power factor correction (TPPFC) circuit in this paper. The grid emulator hardware is tested with the TPPFC circuit as the converter under test, and performance of TPPFC is evaluated under conditions such as voltage sag, swell and distorted grid voltages.

articleTitle: Control of Single Phase Full Bridge VSI Using Modified Peak and Valley Current Control With Optical Isolation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a modified peak and valley current control of single-phase full bridge voltage source inverter with optical isolation. A constant switching frequency is guaranteed by employing a frequency-limited switching technique. The peak and valley limits of the inductor current is controlled either by the comparator or by the switching logic based on the nature of its slope. Also, the modification of the reference signal is a crucial element that enhances the quality of the output waveforms. The proposed approach offers a well-defined harmonic spectrum, fixed switching frequency performance, optical isolation and quick transient adaptability. The proposed method is validated with the simulation results.

articleTitle: AI Reduced Order Model of Induction Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Induction motors commonly used in electric drive, need precise efficiency calculations across various operating conditions from the early design stages. Electromagnetic finite-element analysis (FEA) offers high accuracy but is computationally demanding. Simpler models, like the T-equivalent circuit, are well-documented but challenging to determine due to dependencies on frequency, voltage, and slip. While reduced order models based on finite elements have been proposed, they often lack accuracy across different conditions. AI can be a good alternative but so far is primarily used for control and monitoring. This article presents a hybrid approach that combines FEA data with Reduced order Modeling leveraging AI, achieving a good compromise between accuracy and time computation.

articleTitle: Investigation of Inclined Coil Configurations for 3-Phase Dual Rotor Single Stator Winding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes different inclined coil config-urations for 3- phase dual rotor single stator winding. Unlike the conventional distributed windings which are placed in the peripheral slots, the proposed inclined coil configurations make use of additional slots placed symmetrically opposite to the peripheral slots. The use of additional slots gives rise to differ-ent configurations based on the coil crossover location. These different configurations are presented and investigated using ANSYS®Maxwell®. The results and findings are compared to report the best possible configuration.

articleTitle: ISTE and IST2E Based PID Control for Frequency Control of Shipboard Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Due to intermittent power injection of renewable energy sources in shipboard microgrids (SBMGs), it becomes extremely important to study their stability in the presence of varying loads. Load frequency control (LFC) plays a crucial role in maintaining the stability and power balance in SBMG. This study emphasizes LFC analysis for SBMG, implementing error performance indices methods (EPIm) for controller tuning. EPIms considered for tuning are integral square time error (ISTE) and integral square time square error (IST<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>E). Comparative analysis is performed based on responses of the frequency deviations obtained for SBMG without controller and with EPIm based controllers. For further supporting the obtained outcomes, comparison is further carried out on the basis of comparative analysis.

articleTitle: Performance of Distributed OPF Algorithm with ZIP Loads and Different PV Inverter Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: High penetration of inverter-associated renewable energy resources, especially solar photovoltaic (PV) panels, increases the number of controllable grid-edge devices in an electric grid. Optimal power flow (OPF) problems are often formulated to ensure such electric grids' economic, secure, and reliable operation. To overcome the scalability and computation challenges related to centralized OPF methods, distributed algorithms are adopted for medium and bulk distribution grids. However, the convergence of distributed algorithms is highly impacted by the network architecture and operating characteristics of the grid edge resources. Studies are abundant on the variation in network architecture, but no study has investigated the impact of load models and PV inverter operating modes on the performance of distributed OPF algorithms. To address this, in this article loads are modeled as both constant power and voltage-dependent ZIP loads, and PV inverters are modeled considering their four distinct operating modes viz. grid following (GFM), volt-var controlling (VVCM), volt-watt controlling (VWCM), and voltage control (VCM). The load and the PV inverter models are integrated with the consensus Alternating direction method of multiplier (ADMM)-based distributed OPF algorithm as constraints for minimizing total network loss for an unbalanced distribution network. The performance characterization is performed on the IEEE 123 bus test system concerning network loss values, solution time, and total number of required macro iterations.

articleTitle: Enhanced Power Management in a DC Microgrid Through Virtual Inertia Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This study explores virtual inertia-based power management in a grid-connected DC microgrid (DCMG) system. DCMG is formed of solar and wind-based renewable energy sources (RESs), electric vehicles (EV) as energy storage systems, a three-phase conventional grid, and a constant power load. There are numerous advantages of DCMG, however, it encounters obstacles like precise power distribution and voltage regulation of the DC bus. Additionally, RESs and EVs make use of power electronic converters, which result in decreased inertia support out of the DCMG system. Thus, in addition to DC bus voltage stabilisation, this work proposes a virtual inertia control technique for a bi-directional DC-DC converter in DCMG that attempts to increase inertia and regulate an EV's charge and discharge power as a function of its state-of-charge. A simulation-based experiment is conducted to evaluate the performance of the studied control strategy.

articleTitle: Grid Disturbance and Internal Voltage Source Saturation Impact on Power-Angle Curves of GFM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper investigates the effect of current limit constraints imposed by grid forming converter (GFM) on grid synchronization during and after the recovery from three-phase symmetrical faults. Saturation effects in GFM control due to factors such as internal voltage source, current reference and voltage sag on the power-angle curves significantly deviates from sinusoidal-based relationship and influences the transient stability studies. The approximation of internal voltage source to grid voltage is not valid for the case of grid disturbance in the case of symmetrical faults. The theoretical analysis includes these effects and provide a generalized expression for the case of prioritizing angle in current saturation algorithm. Simulation results validate the theoretical model for various system disturbances for stable and unstable cases.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Q-PLL and DSOGI with SMO Based Sensorless Control of PMSM Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents the comparative analysis of two different methods of Phased locked loop (PLL) with Sliding Mode Observer (SMO) for position estimation in a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) drive. The objective of PLL is to improve the position estimation in drive and the conventional Quadrature PLL (QPLL) unable to track accurate position and shows double frequency oscillations. In order to overcome this, and to remove the harmonics, Dual second order generalized integrator (DSOGI) is proposed with SMO and its performance is analyzed and compared with conventional QPLL at various speed and torque operating conditions. Simulation results shows the better harmonics rejection capability of DSOGI.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Novel Nine-Level Quadruple Boosting Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel nine-level quadruple-boosting multilevel inverter (MLI) that uses a single DC source and requires only ten power switches, one diode, and three capacitors. This design utilizes switched capacitors (SC) with a common ground (CG), achieving a four-fold voltage boost without needing an extra boost converter. The common grounding mitigates leakage current, making the system more efficient. In this proposed topology, the capacitors are self-balanced. The proposed inverter topology offers several advantages compared to existing nine-level inverters, such as significantly reducing leakage current due to common ground configuration, boosting capability, and using fewer components. MATLAB Simulink simulations demonstrate the superior effectiveness of the proposed nine-level quadruple-boosting MLI.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Voltage Support Control Strategy with Improved Active Power Deliverability of a DG During Unbalanced Microgrid Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Numerous control methods have been developed to support voltage during unbalanced microgrid faults. However, most of these methods focus on reactive power injection, which often results in active power curtailment, whether the microgrid is grid-connected or in islanding mode. This curtailment can cause an imbalance between power supply and load, leading to significant stability issues during islanding operations. To address this, we have developed a voltage support control strategy aimed at enhancing both voltage support and active power deliverability. The proposed control has greater flexibility of controlling three-phase-wise and single-phase-wise active and reactive power control with three current regulators only. Furthermore, it possesses current limiting capability during faults in compliance with voltage limits. The performance of the proposed control strategy was validated using a three-phase four-leg converter connected to a Thévenin equivalent microgrid with a Short Circuit ratio(SCR) of 3. Compared to conventional voltage support control, the results demonstrate the proposed method's superiority.

articleTitle: Hybrid Compensation System Using PVDSTATCOM and SVC for Enhanced Power Quality in Low Voltage AC Distribution Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: As electricity demand continues to rise, ensuring a stable and high-quality power supply becomes increasingly important. One major challenge that power systems face is maintaining power quality, which can be affected by issues such as voltage sags, swells, low power factor, and harmonic distortions. Integration of distributed energy resources like photovoltaic (PV) systems also presents challenges in maintaining the power quality of the grid. Effective mitigation of these issues is essential. DSTATCOMs are known for their ability to compensate reactive power and filter harmonics, but they are often associated with higher complexity and cost. On the other hand, SVCs offer rapid adjustment of reactive power, enhancing voltage stability and power quality with relatively simpler implementations. The integration of SVC and DSTATCOM technologies aims to combine their benefits and address their limitations. This involves using the dynamic response capabilities of SVC to provide reactive power and utilizing a PV-DSTATCOM to provide active power and harmonic compensation. The integration aims to reduce the overall complexity and cost of power quality management systems while ensuring a robust and stable electrical grid.

articleTitle: Optimized Power Quality Using Integrated Current and Voltage PFC for Energy Storage Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The integration of Power Factor Correction (PFC) techniques in DC-DC converters addresses critical efficiency and power quality issues in modern electronic systems. This paper a combined current and voltage control PFC technique is implemented to a novel buck topology with single inductor double capacitor buck configuration for energy storage applications. By employing a double capacitor network, efficient power transfer to the load is achieved through a single inductor, resulting in a gain ratio of 0.5D. The proposed converter's detailed steady-state analysis is thoroughly discussed. Also, the power factor and reduce harmonic distortion in the input current, is validated using the combined current and voltage control PFC technique. This approach significantly improves overall energy efficiency and power quality, making the converter highly suitable for energy storage applications. The simulation model has been created using MATLAB/Simulink, and the results obtained from the simulations confirm the effectiveness of the proposed topology and control approach.

articleTitle: PV System Dynamic Performance Maximisation Using a Novel Drift-Free MPPT Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Drift-free adaptive P&O and INC MPPT methods are proposed, which aims to improve the performance of PV system. In these drift-free methods, a change in current <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\Delta I)$</tex> and a change in voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\Delta V)$</tex> are incorporated to eliminate the right side drift. In addition, selecting a lower voltage threshold eliminates left-side drift in systems. A hardware prototype is developed for solar PV system by using DC-DC boost converter. The proposed algorithms are tested on 1.64 kWp laboratory setup for sudden change in irradiance level. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed methods are free from drift and show improved performance of the system.

articleTitle: Fault Detection in Autonomous Microgrid with Distributed Secondary Controlled DGs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The surge in renewable energy sources presents challenges in fault detection, particularly in autonomous microgrid operations where inverter-interfaced DGs contribute minimal current. This study proposes a fault detection method based on positive sequence angles of voltage and current, complemented by distributed secondary control for reactive power sharing among DGs during faults. The method ensures necessary reactive power injection into faulty feeders. Validation on a 5-bus MATLAB/SIMULINK model demonstrates effective fault detection for low-resistance and high-resistance faults. Also, it differentiates between faulty and healthy feeders, showcasing its applicability and reliability in microgrid operations.

articleTitle: Reconfigured Series Stacked Energy Buffer (SSB) for Voltage Drop Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)

articleTitle: Current Vector Oriented Control Scheme for Power Sharing in Open-End Winding Transformer Based Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A new control scheme for sharing of power between two energy sources integrated to form a microgrid using a transformer with open-end primary windings is proposed in this paper. The microgrid's power circuit, developed for the proposed scheme, consists of two three-phase voltage source inverters (VSIs), each connected to opposite ends of the open-end primary windings of a three-phase transformer. The transformer's secondary windings, arranged in a star configuration, supply power directly to the loads or feed it into the grid. The control scheme allows flexible sharing of both active and reactive power between the two inverters in any proportion, depending on the availability of power from the sources supplying the inverters. This flexibility is crucial for optimizing resource utilization and maintaining power balance. The power-sharing mechanism is based on a current vector-oriented synchronous reference frame, making it simpler and more efficient than conventional schemes used in microgrids. The effectiveness and validity of the proposed control approach are demonstrated through detailed simulations conducted in MATLAB Simulink, highlighting its practicality in managing power distribution in microgrids and enhancing system reliability.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning Enabled Voltage Control at Grid Edge Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The installation of distributed technologies such as variable renewable energy sources, energy storage system and flexible electric vehicle charging stations at edge of the distribution grid has increased drastically. Therefore, centralized management through distribution management system faces numerous operational challenges and control issues. Furthermore, highly dependent of communication system also make the grid vulnerable to cyber threats. Hence, an artificial intelligence-assisted voltage control strategy that relays on local measurements has been introduced. To develop the local control framework, the deep reinforcement learning (DRL) based artificial neural networks has been utilized. The proposed DRL-based local control works for grid edge technologies (GET) to support the voltage profile. The proposed DRL framework for voltage management has been validated through a modified IEEE 13 bus distribution test system connected with solar photovoltaics and electric vehicle charging station at edge of the grid. The simulation results of OpenDSS model interfaced with Python for the considered test illustrate that the proposed DRL framework able to control the voltage profile of GETs under uncertainties scenarios and transient events.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cyber Security in DC Microgrids with Intelligent Control Against False Data Injection Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Cyber security plays a major role in operation and control of the cyber physical systems (CPS). Various methods have been proposed in literature for securing the CPS from cyber-attacks. The adversary who has better knowledge of the system formulates an attack that manipulates the defence mechanism to achieve the objectives of adversary. These type of attacks are called as stealthy local overt attacks (SLCAs). They are far more dangerous as they are hard to detect. Any further delay in the detection and mitigation of these SLCAs lead to catastrophic failure of the system. In this article, an intelligent control mechanism is developed to detect and mitigate the stealthy local covert attack that is caused by false data injection (FDI) attack. The proposed algorithm is tested on a DC-DC boost converter which is an integral part of a DC microgrid. The proposed algorithm consists of two feed-forward-back propagation networks where one controller uses voltage information and the other controller uses the current information are modelled to generate the respective duties for the DC-DC buck converter. A decision block is placed in the path of the plant and controller that ensures correct duty is given to the converter that is free from the attack. The proposed control mechanism is initially tested in the MATLAB platform and later implemented on a real-time hardware setup.

articleTitle: Modelling and Identification of Lithium-Ion Battery Using Relay Feedback Response
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, attempts have been made to contribute a continuous-time identification approach for modelling and estimation of lithium-ion battery parameters. Considering a first-order RC equivalent circuit model (ECM) with a signal propagation delay for battery dynamics representation, a closed loop relay feedback test is to be an optimal choice for ascertaining the stable responses. Using a frequency domain analysis, an explicit set of analytical expressions for each of the unknowns in the considered system model is derived by using the important output measurements and relay settings. As the practical output is quite sensitive to measurement noise owing to the presence of erroneous current and voltage sensors, a noise-free waveform of the output is obtained by using a curve fitting method based on a Fourier series, and a point of relay switching instant is varied by an appropriate choice of hysteresis width. The proposed identification algorithm is validated by considering a benchmark example from literature, and its efficacy is demonstrated through an integral of the absolute error criterion and the step response plots.

articleTitle: State Space Mathematical Modeling and State of Charge Estimation of 18650 Panasonic Li-Ion Battery Using $\mathcal{L}_{2}-\mathcal{L}_{\infty}$ Observer Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This study focuses on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{L}_{2}-\mathcal{L}_{\infty}$</tex> observer design, which aims to enhance the accuracy of State of Charge (SOC) estimation in a 2RC (two resistor-capacitor) Li-Ion battery (LIB) model. Validation was performed using Hybrid Pulse Power Characterization (HPPC) for Panasonic (NCR-18650B) cells. The observer's goal is to accurately estimate the battery condition despite various uncertainties and disruptions, utilizing Lyapunov methods and linear matrix inequality (LMI) techniques. It employs observer gain to reduce disturbances and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{L}_{2}-\mathcal{L}_{\infty}$</tex> norms to ensure minimal error in steady-state performance. Integrating this observer allows the model to more accurately capture the battery's dynamic behavior, resulting in improved state estimation and reliable insights into battery performance under various operating conditions.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control of 3-Level T-Type Converter for Grid-Tie Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A finite control set model predictive control of 3Level T-type converter for grid tie application, with decoupled active and reactive power control with addition to dc link voltage balancing has been investigated and presented in this project. Also, one notable constraint associated with employing MPC is the variable switching frequency. This challenge can be mitigated by comparing the switching states with a carrier wave of constant frequency. Nevertheless, fine-tuning the weighting factors poses a formidable challenge, particularly as and when count of constraint to be included in designing of a cost-function rises. Consequently, in this proposed approach, the complexity of this tuning process is mitigated by adopting a MCDM technique, specifically VIKOR. Through simulation, the suggested predictive control algorithm is verified and demonstrates the ability to track and regulate the input unity power factor

articleTitle: Enhancing Voltage Stability in Bipolar Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This work proposes a solution for effectively integrating renewable energy systems into EV charging stations, focusing specifically on a bipolar DC microgrid framework to address increased loads. One of the main challenges tackled is asymmetrical loading within the bipolar DC network, which can lead to voltage drops at the neutral point. To address this, the paper examines a DC-to-DC converter with an integrated output voltage balancing method, eliminating the need for additional converters or control mechanisms. It also examines the design of a compensator for the closed-loop control of the DC-to-DC converter by developing a state-space model of the examined topology, obtaining a small-signal transfer function, and employing a k-factor method to design a compensator for voltage control. The proposed techniques and designs are validated through mathematical modeling and simulations using MATLAB/Simulink, supported by Typhoon HIL experimentation. The findings show significant potential for improving power transfer efficiency in practical EV charging station applications.

articleTitle: Extending the ZVS Range of Phase-Shifted Full-Bridge DC-DC Converters with a Variable Inductor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The objective of this study is to introduce a novel method for extending the soft-switching range of Phase-Shifted Full-Bridge DC-DC converters. Although these converters are renowned for their high efficiency, they face challenges in maintaining soft switching across a wide load range. The proposed approach incorporates a variable inductor, controlled by a low-power DC excitation, to reduce the current on power switches during mid- to full-load conditions and ensure adequate current to maintain soft switching under light-load conditions. Both the practical implementation of the variable inductor and the simulation of the converter confirm the feasibility of the proposed design.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Wide Voltage Range Battery Charger for Electric Transportation Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Existing electric vehicle (EV) battery chargers are currently facing significant challenges when it comes to operating across wide voltage ranges. The complexity arises from the diverse battery voltage architectures present in different EV models and existing chargers often lack the flexibility needed to adjust to these varying voltages effectively, leading to compatibility issues during the charging process. Through this paper, a new reconfigurable wide output voltage range battery charger for EV battery charging is proposed. The charger's ability to reconfigure over the wide voltage range of 250–1000 V with decreased voltage and current stress on switches makes it suitable for public EV battery charging applications. A new current control technique using a proportional resonant (PR) controller is designed, which maintains the unity power factor (UPF) with attenuation of lower-order harmonics in the input current. MATLAB/Simulink simulations are done in order to verify the performance of the proposed charger.

articleTitle: A Common Grounded ASISC High Gain DC-DC Converter with No Oscillation Across Switches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The DC-DC converter is an essential and integral part of fuel cell vehicles (FCVs). Active switched inductor/capacitor (ASISC) based converter is a desirable option for fuel cell vehicles because of its low switching voltage stress, current stress, and straightforward design and control. Although the capacitance and inductance values of the switches of an active switched inductor (ASI) network have a significant impact on the voltage stress in the switches. Because the ASL network's parameters are inconsistent, the switch's inductors and drain-source capacitors form a resonant circuit. This leads to voltage fluctuation across switches, which ultimately results from a sharp increase in switching voltage stress. The converter experiences higher power losses as a result of the voltage oscillation across the switches. In this paper, a new hybrid structure of a DC-DC converter was developed that combines an active switched inductor and a switched capacitor (ASISC). The proposed converter offers a high voltage conversion ratio, reduces voltage stress by mitigating voltage oscillation across switches, and also establishes a common ground between the source and load ends. In this manuscript, the converter's key waveform, fundamental principle, comprehensive steady-state analysis, and design equations are provided. The voltage conversion ratio, current stress, and voltage stress have been calculated and compared with the existing ASISC converters. Finally, a prototype of a 300 W converter with 35V input and 300V output is developed and demonstrated.

articleTitle: Current Ripple Analysis of 72° Phase-Clamping PWM Techniques for Five-Phase Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The appeal of multiphase systems has led to their widespread adoption in medium and high-powered drives. Effective operation of these systems necessitates the implementation of pulse width modulation (PWM). This paper focuses on the modulation technique for five-phase voltage source inverters using advanced PWM (ADPWM) methods. ADPWM employs specialized switching sequences that enable a clamping duration of 72°. Additionally, variations in the space vector timing yield additional PWM techniques. The clamping duration plays a crucial role in reducing switching energy losses. The proposed technique is subjected to simulation, and the results are meticulously analyzed.

articleTitle: Voltage Multiplier Cell-Based Enhanced Quadratic Buck-Boost DC-DC Converter with Reduced Switch Current Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a novel high gain quadratic DC-DC buck-boost converter which have extended boost region compared to its buck region counterpart is proposed. This topology is configured from a conventional topology by a novel arrangement of a switched inductor and a voltage multiplier cell. This novel arrangement helps to reduce voltage and current stress across switches and diodes compared to some of the conventional converters. This reduced stress enhances reliability of the devices. Furthermore, this topology facilitates continuous input current, non-inverted output voltage and self-voltage balancing across the switches. Steady state analysis and impact of parasitic elements on the efficiency of the converter are examined. The comparison between the proposed and similar conventional topologies is depicted in this paper. The experimental analysis has been conducted for a 200 W and 50 kHz hardware prototype of the converter with 48 V input voltage and 400 V output voltage, and the results are presented.

articleTitle: A Bi-level Decision Support System for Home Energy Management in Smart Homes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Effective home energy management requires addressing user preferences and the operational needs of household appliances with minimal human intervention. This paper presents a dedicated decision support system (DSS) for managing time-shiftable and controllable appliances. The system minimises energy costs and thermal discomfort by optimising the operation of appliances like washing machines (WM), dishwashers (DW) and air conditioners (AC). The complexity of managing appliances at different times is tackled using a bi-level DSS, incorporating particle swarm optimisation (PSO). In level 1, WM and DW's operation time is shifted to minimise the operating cost. In level 2, the AC power is adjusted in real-time to minimise both the cost paid to the upstream network and the thermal discomfort of the users. The proposed method is tested on a smart home dataset and observes an energy saving of 22.29kW h and bill saving of 287.65cents compared to uncontrolled operation and also maintains the room temperature variations within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 2^{\mathrm{o}}C$</tex> from the user choice.

articleTitle: Staircase Modulation for 17-Level Packed E-Cell Multilevel Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper introduces a staircase modulation technique for a single-phase 17-level Packed E-Cell (PEC) Multilevel Inverter to balance capacitor voltages, improve efficiency, and reduce total harmonic distortion (THD) without a filter. The inverter prototype contains two symmetric DC sources, eight switches, one bidirectional switch, 9 gate driver circuits, two capacitors, and two voltage sensors. The proposed modulation technique is implemented on a Raspberry Pi Pico W Microcontroller. Experimental results demonstrate that THD of 4.7 % for voltage and an efficiency of 99 % tested at 470 W. This research contributes a simple control algorithm that enhances inverter performance using low switching frequency for renewable energy applications.

articleTitle: Battery-Powered Current Regulated Automotive LED Driver
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This Paper describes battery-powered wide input voltage range automotive LED drivers which are used in modern lighting applications like automobiles. It has to provide stable illumination despite fluctuations in input voltage. The main objective is to develop and implement such a driver with an ability to regulate LED current for a wide input voltage range. The proposed driver circuit combines buck-boost and LC series resonant converter configurations. This design is integrated with a hybrid modulation technique that utilizes both PWM (pulse width modulation) and PSC (phase shift control) or PWM and PFM (pulse frequency modulation), to enable effective regulation of LED current for different variations of input voltages. The proposed work is implemented using MATLAB-SIMULINK and results are tested with hardware implementation. This work aims for compact and efficient solution for driving LEDs in automotive lighting applications

articleTitle: Experimental Method for Accurate Measurement of High Frequency Bridge Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Accurate measurement of power loss in a half-bridge circuit is essential for evaluating the performance of power converters. However, due to the fast-changing nature of voltages and currents in wide bandgap devices like SiC MOSFETs, measuring high-frequency bridge loss using traditional methods is challenging. The initial analysis of a buck converter presented in this article gives an insight of the important parameters to be considered for measurement. This article presents an experimental method to measure high-frequency bridge loss accurately. It requires a precision ammeter in addition to standard laboratory equipment like an oscilloscope and voltage probes with sufficiently high bandwidths. The accuracy of the presented method is validated experimentally using a buck-converter laboratory prototype upto 1.8kW with 1200V SiC MOSFETs. An accuracy of 98.5% is achieved in measuring high-frequency bridge loss using the proposed method.

articleTitle: MPC Based Phase Angle Adjustment for Optimal Power Transfer in Neutral Point Clamped Dual Active Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: For high-voltage applications, neutral point clamped-based dual active bridge (NPC-DAB) converters are commonly used. In literature, different fixed phase shift control methods like double phase shift control (DPS), triple phase shift control (TPS), etc., are used to reduce losses in NPC-DAB converter. In this paper, a variable phase shift method is proposed to reduce the losses in the converter. This variable phase shift angle is obtained by utilizing a power loss minimization function in a model predictive controller (MPC). The simulation result shows that MPC based variable phase shift control reduces power loss and improves transient performance in the NPC-DAB system in comparison to PI control based fixed phase shift control.

articleTitle: A Regenerative Weak-Grid Emulator for Distributed Generation Test Benches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a weak grid emulator intended for distributed generation test benches. The paper briefly de-scribes the different types of weak grid emulation techniques using Voltage Source Converter (VSC), which is based on current-in voltage-out method. It systematically arrives at the causal capacitor-based method for inductive impedance emulation and highlights the disadvantages of the same. A Second-Order Low-Pass (SOLP) filter-based band-limited inductive impedance emulator is suggested as an improvement for accurately emulating the weak grid in the range of frequencies of interest. The mathematical analysis of the same is presented along with a discussion on the effect of placement of the filter corner frequency on impedance emulation. Simulation results performed using the switching model of the inverter for balanced linear and non-linear load conditions is presented. Validation of the analysis and the emulator's effectiveness is demonstrated using experimental results on a hardware lab prototype.

articleTitle: Knowledge Inference Concept of Control Sharing - Mitigation of Power Quality Disturbances in Grid Tied PV Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a study on a Unified Power Quality Conditioner (UPQC) designed for grid-tied PV systems, combining distributed generation and active power filtering. Advanced control methods for UPQC are explored, including SRF theory with sliding mode control for dynamic response to voltage sag/swell and novel ANN control algorithm for cost-effective performance enhancement. Simulations in MATLAB/Simulink compare THD in load and grid voltage/current under different conditions, along with response times and performance under unbalanced loads. This research paper highlights a novel control sharing method for mitigating extreme sag and swell values in grid-tied photovoltaic (PV) systems. Leveraging knowledge domain principles, this approach integrates two Unified Power Quality Conditioners (UPQCs) into the system. Operational parameters of both UPQCs are stored in a knowledge domain, determined by sag and swell values. The primary UPQC, controlled by sliding mode control (SMC), manages operations under mild sag and swell conditions, while the secondary UPQC supplements the primary UPQC during instances of extreme sag and swell. Results indicate enhanced system performance, particularly under non-linear and unbalanced loads, showcasing superior efficacy compared to single UPQC systems in grid-tied PV applications.

articleTitle: A list of three novel dissimilar voltage multi-input isolated high gain DC-DC converters supplying multiple outputs with widely varying characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper explores three novel isolated Direct Current- Direct Current (DC-DC) converters with high gain and varying characteristics, fed from two unequal battery voltages. The two degrees of freedom in terms of the per unit duty cycle and the turns ratio <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> of the High-Frequency Transformer (HFT) help in providing a high gain isolated output voltage in Continuous Conduction Mode (CCM) with varying characteristics of derived Boost and Buck-boost. The isolated port output voltage for one of the converters is independent of Vin2 while for another it is the enhanced gain non-inverting buck-boost for a source voltage equal to an average of Vin1 and Vin2. The input current continuity of the converters (for possibilities of seamless renewable integration e.g. Solar Photovoltaic Array) and the OFF-state voltage stresses for all the power electronic switches in the converters are comparatively investigated. Steady-state CCM mode analyses for all the converters are presented in detail and the voltage gains at all output ports are derived respectively. MATLAB® SIMULINK Simulation platform is used to simulate the converters to validate the theoretical analysis. An average closed-loop current controller is designed and its efficacy is verified using step load changes. In summary, a list of three novel isolated DC-DC converters fed from dissimilar input battery voltages are presented in this paper which cater to enhanced gain buck-boost and boost characteristics and can cater to widely varying applications.

articleTitle: Adaptive Random Search Algorithm Based On-Board Charger for WPT Based EV Battery Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The recent advancements in the EV charging infrastructures, different new charging scenarios are being adopted, one of them is the wireless power transfer (WPT) charging system. It gains its importance because of the absence of physical cables and making the charging procedure sophisticated. Apart form its easiness to its user it got its challenges while charging due to the misalignment's occur during Inductive WPT charging. Hence a very smart control strategy should be implemented for the reliable charging of the EV battery. So, in this paper focused on a Heuristic Algorithm based controller which maintains a constant DC voltage at the battery terminals irrespective of the misalignment's condition of the coupled coils. This paper adopted Adaptive Random search (ARS) Algorithm for optimizing the controller parameters for different scenarios of misalignment's and a detailed detailed closed loop operation of the controller is analyzed.

articleTitle: Dynamic Stator Resistance Adaptation in Sensorless Direct Torque Control of SynRm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Direct torque control (DTC) method controls the electromagnetic torque and flux in AC machines, directly. This method is though immune to machine inductance variations but do get affected by stator resistance changes. Ignoring the stator resistance variation can lead to unstable motor drive operation. This paper proposes a new sensorless direct torque control (sDTC) method for a Synchronous reluctance motor that adapts to stator resistance variation. This is accomplished by adapting to changes in the error between the estimated and reference angles of the current and the stator flux vectors. Importantly, it completely obviates the need of any speed sensor. With the present estimation proposal, the sDTC is made to dynamically adjust to the changes in stator resistance ensuring proper motor performance under different operating conditions involving disturbances. The proposed sDTC approach manages to improves the torque and actual stator flux in the SynRm unlike existing DTC approach that greatly struggles under stator resistance variations and results in unstable operation. The performance of the SynRm with the envisaged sDTC with stator resistance change proposed in this paper is compared with the existing DTC method for a close one-to-one comparison and easy appreciation. Besides, ruggedness of the proposed approach for the SynRm is tested under stator resistance changes, motor speed changes and load disturbances.

articleTitle: Extendable Multisource Multilevel Boosting Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A new switched-capacitor based multisource multilevel inverter for high-frequency AC applications is proposed in this article. The proposed topology can generate 13-level output voltage by utilizing only 11 switches, two diodes, one capacitor, and two asymmetrical dc sources with inherent polarity reversal. The proposed topology and its extension has several advantages such as high voltage gain, less total blocking voltage, less component count, less total harmonic distortion, and higher number of voltage levels. Further, the capacitor is self voltage balanced without any extra balancing circuit. PLECS simulation and laboratory prototype results are presented to verify the operability and feasibility. Finally, a comparative study is also presented to validate the beneficial features of the proposed topology.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Inductor Current Prediction in HD-SPWM-Controlled 3-Level DAB Converter for Fast EV Charging Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The rapid proliferation of electric vehicles (EVs) has led to the emergence of the need for efficient and fast charging systems. This paper addresses the development of an artificial intelligence (AI) based model to predict the optimized peak inductor current in a high-definition sinusoidal pulse width modulation (HD-SPWM) controlled 3-level dual active bridge (DAB) converter for a fast charging electric vehicle application. Although the DAB converter topology has numerous advantages, which can be used for various power distribution systems due to the bidirectional power flow and high-power density, the DAB converter's performance level is significantly dependent on the performance of the model since the inductor current should accurately be predicted. The proposed AI-based model, with a novel long short-term memory (LSTM) approach, can predict the inductor current accurately based on the anticipated input parameters. The MATLAB/SIMULINK simulation platform has been used to train the model, indicating that the model can be robust under a wide arrangement of operating conditions. The error-free inductor current prediction would significantly affect the controller with excellent precision, minimal losses, and high-speed charging of the electric vehicle. A series of simulation tests has been executed to expose the promiscuity of the proposed AI-based model with conventional line-up.

articleTitle: Utilization of Master and Smart Meter Readings for Pin Pointing Electricity Theft Using Correlation Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The electricity becomes the economical backbone of any country. The energy theft becomes a major concern, since its directly affecting the countries economy. The power consumed by each customer is recorded continuously by the smart meters which are connected to the individual home. Also, the overall data is measured by a master meter. Most of the existing work focuses on the similar attack in all the houses and hence it can be considered as a linear attack. In this work, 3 different attacks have been considered, i.e. the consumer manipulate their readings in 3 different ways. Based on the data, the power theft could be identified and the particular non-honest consumer can be identified easily. In this work, spearman correlation is utilized for detecting the energy theft. Several experiments have been conducted for the real time dataset of various homes.

articleTitle: Design of Solar Photovoltaic System for Domestic Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper deals with design and benefits of twointerleaved bidirectional phase-shift (TI-BPS) based buck-boost dc to dc converter in terms of fast load transient response, half output overall ripple current and half current stress on switches is to maintain dc bus voltage for an inverter during unavailability of grid. While grid is available, it charges battery energy storage (BES). With addition of a 5 kVA off-grid solar home inverter system, this architecture eliminates line-frequency transformer, and improves overall system performance like, light weight, efficient, comparatively higher power density. During absence of grid, a H-bridge dc-ac inverter directly feeds ac power to domestic loads. While grid is available, it also works as pulse width modulated (PWM) bridge-less ac-dc front end converter, which maintains dc-bus voltage at nominal as input for battery side TIBPS dc-dc converter. Another, two-interleaved phase-shift (TIPS) buck dc-dc converter is also incorporated to extract maximum power from PV array, which inherently makes PV array nominal maximum power point voltage (Vmpp) two times more than BES voltage level and current lower than half to reduce PV array wiring losses and cost. TI-PS dc-dc converter doubles ripple frequency than switching frequency and each inductor runs at maximum of half rated output current, which helps to use smaller and lighter LC and EMI/EMC noise filter, reduced by half current stress in both switching devices per switching cycle, and faster load transient regulation. Performance of proposed system is evaluated at reduced number of batteries from conventional 20 to 15 numbers of 12V batteries in series as BES, connected with 5 kW solar panel with open circuit voltage of 450Voc each, for maximum ripple suppression factor upto -80db at 50% duty cycle.

articleTitle: Full Order Discrete Time Modelling of High Gain Switched Capacitor Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: High gain switched capacitor converters are quite popular for integrating low voltage storage devices to the high voltage dc link of DC Microgrids. One of the major challenge for switched capacitor circuit based topologies is to develop accurate dynamic model, as the conventional state space averaging methods can not be applied for these topologies due to the discontinuous nature of the capacitor voltages. In this aspect, discrete time based modelling approaches have been widely used for SC based topologies as it does not involve small ripple approximation. But specifically for SC converters system matrices may become singular for one or more states which can make DT modelling method ineffective. Though some of the existing literature have addressed this issue, but they suffer from different limitations such as reduced system order, loss of information and accuracy. In this paper, a generalized full order discrete time modelling technique for switched capacitor derived high gain topology is proposed considering matrix singularity problem with capacitor charge redistribution. A step by step large and small signal dynamic model is developed for a ladder SC circuit derived bidirectional high gain topology. Further, the dynamic modelling and controller design is validated through experimental results performed in a 500W, 220V laboratory prototype.

articleTitle: A Novel Five-Level Double-Boost Inverter with Reduced Spike Current
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel five-level double-boosting multi-level inverter (MLI) that uses a single DC source and requires only six power switches, one diode, and one capacitor. This design enables soft charging of the capacitor by integrating a charging inductor, which helps minimize or completely avoid large inrush or spike currents in the charging pathway. In this proposed topology, the capacitor is self-balanced. The proposed inverter topology offers several advantages compared to existing five-level inverters, such as significantly reducing inrush current, boosting capability, lower total standing voltage (TSV), common ground configuration, higher efficiency, and using fewer components. MATLAB Simulink simulations demonstrate the superior effectiveness of the proposed five-level double-boosting MLI in terms of reducing spike current.

articleTitle: Minimum Switch Double Boost Switched Capacitor Inverter with Phase Disposition PWM Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This work introduces a minimal switch double boosting Switched Capacitor Inverter (DBSCI) that is intended to resolve critical concerns associated with rising usage of capacitors, DC sources, and semiconductor switching. Leveraging a DC source, eight switches, and three capacitors, the suggested DBSCI makes a nine-level resulting output. It demonstrates an inclination to increase the output voltage by a factor of two. Furthermore, the DBSCI implements a phase disposition (PD) pulse width modulation strategy to improve the overall quality of the voltage it produces and increase the resulting voltage. Utilizing MATLAB-SIMULINK, the paper evaluates the viability and efficacy of the DBSCI with respect to a variety of modulating indices.

articleTitle: Sensorless Speed Control of Brushless DC Motor Using Artificial Neural Network Predicted Back EMF
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Electric Vehicles (EVs) are increasingly preferred over Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) vehicles due to their eco-friendliness. Brushless DC (BLDC) motors are ideal for EVs because of their efficiency and low maintenance. Traditional BLDC motor control uses position sensors, which are expensive and complex. Sensorless control, which does not rely on these sensors, is more desirable. A typical sensorless technique is to detect the Back Electromotive Force (BEMF) in the motor phase, but this is difficult at low speeds and sensitive to noise. The suggested method is a Sensorless Speed Control for BLDC motors using an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) to analyze BEMF. The ANN learns the correlation between BEMF zero crossing signals and the hall sensor's equivalent emf. This aids in precise rotor position and speed determination, leading to correct motor drive signals. This method's benefits include noise resistance, the absence of extra sensors or circuits, and effective operation at all speeds. TI Motor Control Board is used for testing and MATLAB Simulink is used for comparative analysis. The torque and current ripples are significantly reduced by using ANN BEMF method, and the speed regulation is improved.

articleTitle: Triple Active Bridge Converter for Solar PV-Assisted EV Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a systematic analysis and control of an isolated Triple Active Bridge (TAB) converter designed for solar PV assisted electric vehicle (EV) charging. The TAB converter features three distinct full-bridge ports that can be connected to different sources and loads. A high-frequency multi-winding transformer interconnects all ports providing the isolation and facilitating efficient energy transfer between sources and loads and isolation. The study includes a detailed mathematical analysis of a decoupled control technique, solar PV MPPT, and voltage source converter control. The proposed decoupled control enables independent power flow control between the sources. Simulation results for a 10 kW system validate the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Brushless PM Motor with Less-Rare-Earth Mixed Grade Segmented Poles for UAV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
