abstract: Brushless Permanent Magnet (PM) motors have been the obvious choice for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) owing to their high torque and power density. The motors employed for this application generally use radially magnetized arc shaped rare earth PMs in the outer rotor configuration. This paper presents a outer rotor brushless PM motor using less-rare-earth mixed grade segmented poles. The proposed motor, employing a mix of expensive rare earth and inexpensive ferrite PM segments on each pole, is compared against the conventional brushless PM motor. This pole arrangement produces more torque per rare earth magnet volume thus leading to a reduction in magnet usage. Additionally, the proposed motor demonstrates an improved torque quality with a satisfactory overall efficiency.

articleTitle: A Resonant Reset Forward Converter with Ultra-High Conversion Gain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes the implementation of a high-gain resonant reset forward converter and validates its performance. A differential transformer is used in the implementation, to achieve ultra-high conversion gain. The transformer design achieves this high voltage ratio with minimal leakage unlike a conventional transformer. The technique alleviates the duty cycle limit problem associated with high conversion gain converter design. A 600 V to 9 V, 150 W experimental prototype validates the effectiveness of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Advanced Control and Modeling for Enhanced BLDC Motor Efficiency and Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents an enhanced sensorless control strategy for Brushless DC Motors for low-powered electric vehicles, incorporating iron loss modeling. It addresses critical issues such as torque ripple and drive inefficiency through a Discrete Terminal Sliding Mode Control-based sensorless Field-Oriented Control (FOC), and comparison with traditional FOC-based control. By integrating robust control mechanisms and reducing iron losses, the strategy significantly improves motor performance. Comprehensive simulation results validate the efficacy of the presented methods, demonstrating robust and accurate performance under various load conditions. The system accurately tracks reference speeds, maintains stability amidst fluctuating loads and speeds, and accounts for iron losses. The results found satisfactory torque ripple reduction in the discrete TSMC approach.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of RLS-Based Torque Estimation for Control of EV Traction PMSMs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper addresses the critical need for accurate torque estimation in Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines (PMSM), particularly relevant in the context of the growing elec-trification of automobiles. Focusing on both Surface Permanent Magnet Machines (SPMSM) and Interior Permanent Magnet Machines (IPMSM), the paper proposes a Recursive Least Squares (RLS) based estimator to identify machine parameters for precise torque estimation. This method requires minimal prior knowledge of machine parameters and is analytically shown to be effective for torque estimation with practical levels of parameter uncertainty present in the motor. Simulation studies are presented to verify the concept. Experimental validation on an in-house developed IPMSM supports the accuracy of the proposed method, highlighting its potential for enhancing electric vehicle control and safety.

articleTitle: Agricultural Photovoltaic Water Pumping System Performance During Partial Shading Condition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) water pumping assemblies powered by sensorless vector controlled induction motors are gaining popularity in various applications. Partial shading conditions (PSC) pose a challenge for classical maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithms like perturb and observe (P&O). This paper proposes integrating modified invasive weed optimization (MIWO) with P&O to dynamically optimize PV power output under PSCs, ensuring maximum power extraction even in rapidly changing weather conditions.

articleTitle: Chaotic Behavior Assessment of Switched Reluctance Motor in Dynamic Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This study examines the impact of chaos on the dynamic performance of a hysteresis current controlled Switched Reluctance Motor (SRM). Firstly, the occurrence of chaos in the SRM for various parameter changes is analysed through computer simulations. The time series plot of dynamic characteristics of the motor such as speed, current and torque are observed. The behaviour of chaos with change in system's nonlinearity is analysed. Their behavior is characterized as periodic or chaotic using nonlinear techniques such as phase portraits, bifurcation diagram and Lyapunov exponents. A quantitative analysis of magnitude of oscillations of these characteristics are reported for different reference speeds as the operating behavior changes. Also the control of chaos in SRM is implemented. The observations obtained can be used to establish a relation between the performance and occurrence of chaos in SRM.

articleTitle: A Critical Analysis of Flywheel Energy Storage Systems' Technologies, Applications, and Prospects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The penetration of renewable energy sources (RES) is going to increase day by day in the existing grid to fulfill the increased demand. According to Central Electricity Authority CEA report, India is going to install 361 GW by 2030 in the existing grid. Due to the stochastic nature of renewables (solar and wind), smoothing them is a challenge. For smoothening the renewable, an energy storage system (ESS) is required. Flywheel energy storage (FES) has been proven to be a good alternative to standard EES (such as batteries, thermal storage, etc.) for smoothing the use of renewable energy sources because of its extended energy storage capacity, high specific energy, and high maximum power output. This paper represents an overview of the present and future status of RES in India, a brief discussion of different ESS, FES, and various applications of FES in power systems. Challenges and future scope of FES for smoothing renewables are also discussed.

articleTitle: Symmetrical ASL Hybrid DC-DC Converter with Low Voltage Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Active switched inductor (ASL) DC-DC converters utilize parallel charging and series discharging of inductors, which improves the voltage gain. In practice, the inductors often have unequal values, leading to variations in instantaneous currents when switching from parallel charging to series discharging. This leads to an increase in voltage stress across the switches of ASL cells. This paper proposes a symmetrical ASL hybrid DC-DC converter, providing a current path of the inductor currents when circuit configuration changes from parallel charging and series discharging of inductors, lowering the voltage stress. The operating principle, design equation, and device stress are analyzed. Finally, a laboratory prototype (22/308V) generating 430W is developed and tested to validate the analytical analysis.

articleTitle: Load Matching in Single-Stage Constant Power Series-Parallel Compensated Inductive Charging with High Voltage Gain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Inductive charging can alleaviate the drawbacks of the traditional conductive charging methods. It is well known that a inductive charger achieves optimal efficiency at optimal load conditions. However, during charging the load varies substantially which degrades the efficiency. Thus, load matching is required to achieve optimal efficiency. Further, a constant power (CP) has a better performance than the constant current (CC) charging stage due to its faster charging speed and reduced thermal design in comparison to CC. Within a CP charging, a high voltage gain is required for applications such as EV charging where charging voltage levels are considerably high. In this paper, a single-stage CP inductive charger is presented. The proposed charger adopts a current controlled semi active rectifier to achieve load matching and CP output simultaneously at higher values of voltage gain. The proposed charger is based on fixed frequency operation and control is entirely done on the secondary side thereby eliminating the wireless feedback communication. The simulation results are included to show the effectiveness of the proposed charger.

articleTitle: Practical Considerations and Error Estimation in Hall Effect Current Sensors using 2D-FEMM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Hall based current sensors are widely used in AC and DC high current sensing. Current in busbar generates magnetic field which is directed to hall sensor using a surrounding magnetic core. This paper describes practical considerations while designing the core based current sensor and estimation of errors due to various factors. Effect of airgap, effect of Non-linear magnetic material, busbar and sensor displacement has been demonstrated. Effect of returning busbar in proximity impacts current measurement. Effect with various spacing and placement of returning busbar are presented. Comparison of analytical design and simulation results using 2D FEMM (Finite Element Method Magnetics) is presented.

articleTitle: Fixed Frequency-Based Oscillation Mitigation Technique for Solid State Circuit Breaker in DC Microgrid Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper investigates instability issues in a 380V/20A Solid-State Circuit Breaker (SSCB) employing a variable frequency Pulse Width Modulation-Current Limiting (PWM-CL) technique. To enhance the SSCB's protection and to reduce the oscillatory nature of the SSCB, an improved Control Scheme is introduced with fixed frequency-based PWM-CL mode with an Artificial Ramp Compensation (ARC) technique. The proposed ARC control technique produces a Periodic Falling Slope Ramp Reference (PFSR) which eliminates the output oscillations and relationship between the PWM-CL time which in turn depends on the loading condition and perturbation. The effectiveness of the proposed control technique is validated through a 7.6KW SSCB integrated Buck Converter using MATLAB Simulink. The output response of the proposed control scheme illustrates the improvement in the operating condition of the buck converter during soft-start. Furthermore, it enhances differentiation between inrush and short circuit (SC) currents, leading to more accurate fault detection in the SSCB.

articleTitle: Estimation of Transmitter Coil Separation for Enhanced Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Dynamic Wireless Charging (DWC) systems provide a promising solution for electric vehicle (EV) charging on the move, enabling continuous replenishment of the vehicle's battery while in motion. The infrastructure for dynamic charging can either be a single long track or a segmented track consisting of multiple transmitter coils. One of the critical aspects of segmented DWC systems lies in the spacing between adjacent transmitter coils, which directly influences the charging efficiency and effectiveness of the system. An analytical approach has been developed to determine the distance between transmitter coils necessary for transferring the propulsion energy required by a moving EV per kilometer. This analytical method uses the mutual inductance profile of the transmitter and receiver coil to compute the power and the energy transferred from the transmitter coils to the receiver coil along the track to calculate the optimal transmitter parameters. This paper aims to optimize dynamic EV charging infrastructure by investigating how varying transmitter and receiver coil dimensions and air gaps affect distances between coils. The coils used for the analysis are rectangular, and both mathematical method and finite element analysis (FEA) using Ansys Software are employed

articleTitle: Electrolytic Capacitor-less Isolated Resonant Converter-fed BLDC Drive for Solar Water Pumping Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The electrolytes used in electrolytic capacitors (ECs) dries out with time due to heating, voltage stress and humidity leading to the degradation of the ECs. To address this concern, this paper presents a DC link electrolytic capacitor-less (ECL) isolated resonant converter-fed brushless DC motor drive for solar water pumping applications. For DC-DC converter operation, an isolated LLC-based dual half-active bridge resonant converter is used. The resonance in the isolated DC-DC converter (IDC) provides soft-switching operation to reduce the switching losses at high-frequency and isolation restricts the flow of the leakage current caused due to the capacitive path formed between the panels and the ground. For the analysis of the IDC, fundamental harmonics approximation has been used. The output film capacitor of the secondary half-active bridge is used as a DC-link capacitor. A three-phase voltage source inverter has been utilized for the electronic commutation of the BLDC motor. A 120° conduction scheme with the H-PWM-L-ON method has been adapted for the smooth operation of the BLDC motor. A 500 W laboratory prototype of the proposed drive system has been built and tested for the steady-state operation.

articleTitle: Shipboard Microgrid Frequency Control Using Error Performance Criteria
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The rapid advancement of renewable energy technologies and strict regulations imposed by the marine pollution protocol have significantly increased interest in integrating renewable energy sources into marine vessel power systems. But this gives rise to deviating frequency due to irregularities in generation from renewable energy sources. This study primarily focuses on the frequency regulation of shipboard microgrids implementing PID controller. The study employs error performance criteria, namely integral square error (ISE) and integral square time error (ISTE), for fine-tuning the PID controller parameters. The frequency analysis of shipboard microgrids with controllers based on ISE and ISTE methods, are presented and discussed in the research. To improve comprehension of the results, a comparative study is carried out, presenting time domain specifications for shipboard microgrids with and without controllers.

articleTitle: Audio-Susceptibility in Peak Current Controlled CI-SIDO Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The current trend towards miniaturizartion of consumer electronics have led to, rapid adoption of single input multi-output (SIMO) class of DC to DC converters. SIMO class of converters are fast replacing the single input single output(SISO) class of converters. SIMO DC to DC converters are capable of providing multiple regulated voltage levels, for various auxilliary units present in consumer electronics. This paper introduces a specific SIMO converter: the coupled inductor based single input dual output(CI-SIDO) buck converter. The input voltage fluctuations fed to CI-SIDO buck converter affect the output voltages of these converters. This phenomenon is called audio-susceptibility. As, CI-SIDO converters, need to have strictly regulated output voltages. The effect of input voltage fluctuations need to be studied extensively, for proper design and operation of CI-SIDO buck converters. Peak current mode(PCM) control is a commonly used controller in regulated DC to DC converters. The two control loops that make up PCM control are the outer voltage loop and the inner current loop. Current literature lacks investigation of the inner current loops effect, on audio-susceptibility of CI-SIDO buck converters. This paper develops a complete small-signal(SS) block diagram model of PCM controlled CI-SIDO buck converter. The effect of PCM control inner loops on audio-susceptibility of CI-SIDO buck is investigated using the developed model. The audio-susceptibility due to PCM inner loops, are shown using MATLAB Simulink, and the open-loop audio-susceptibility is used to compare the outcomes.

articleTitle: Advanced Discrete-Time Modeling and State Feedback Control of an Interleaved Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Onboard DC micro grids in electric transport is a demanding application that requires high quality steady-state and transient performance of the power converters and their control. To address this, a three-phase interleaved DC-DC converter together with an advanced observer-based control scheme are used in this paper. To enable implementation of this control, a practical discrete-time model of the converter is proposed that reduces a fourth order system to a second order, without a significant loss of accuracy. The proposed model provides closedform solutions for all associated coefficients and gains. Based on this model, observer-based state feedback control is tested in this paper by simulation and shows superior performance to PI control. Experimental validation in underway.

articleTitle: A Self-Sustaining Photovoltaic Power System with High-Gain Boost Converter for DC Nanogrid Equipped with Hybrid Storage Unit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents the design and control of a high gain boost converter (HGBC) for a stand-alone solar photovoltaic system supported by a battery-ultracapacitor (UC) based hybrid storage unit (HSU). It achieves a higher voltage conversion ratio compared to a conventional boost converter by stepping up the input voltage, which is especially useful when the solar panel output voltage is low or when specific output voltages are required for various applications. This extended voltage range provides more flexibility in system design and allows for compatibility with a wider range of devices. The implementation of maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithms play a crucial role in accurately tracking the maximum power point (MPP) and effectively responding to dynamic changes in environmental conditions. This PV system with HSU is integrated to the DC bus through two bidirectional converters for regulating the grid voltage to the desired value using a filtration-based dual-loop control strategy. The entire nanogrid power management along with bus voltage regulation is achieved under irradiance and load change scenarios. This system stands out because of its simple design, enhanced efficiency and substantial gain to achieve higher output voltages without the need of isolation stages. The uniqueness of the complete system can be a promising solution for PV-based water pumps and EV charging stations.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of a Hybrid Renewable Energy System with Different Storage Technologies for an off-grid Rural Household
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: As a result of urbanization and population expansion, energy consumption in the residential sector of India has been rising at a significant rate in recent times. In this regard, this study focuses on creating a hybrid energy system based on solar PV and energy storage to electrify a rural household on Lakshadweep Island. The primary goal of this research is to maximize the homeowner's financial gain while meeting the practical limitation of the reliability index. Different energy storage technologies like battery and hydrogen storage are considered in this paper. To optimally design the energy system, the seasonal fluctuation of the home load is accurately assessed, whereas the power generation of the solar PV system is estimated based on historical data. A computationally efficient rooted tree optimization (RTO) technique is utilized to determine the optimal size of the system components. Moreover, a comparative performance analysis is carried out between battery and hydrogen storage to investigate the most suitable storage option for a rural household. Further, the impact of the reliability index variation on the system components' optimal sizing is also thoroughly analyzed.

articleTitle: Generalization of Multiple Series-Connected Three-Level Boost Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: For modern high-power applications such as fast-charging EV stations, data centers, etc., direct connection to the medium voltage (MV) grid is crucial. Many topologies employ AC/DC front-end converters where these are connected in series to enhance their voltage blocking capability, enabling direct MV grid connection. One such converter is the three-level boost (TLB) based power factor correction (PFC) AC/DC converter, which is well-suited for MV applications due to its reduced inductor size, lower voltage stress and higher efficiency. Multiple TLBs are connected in series to meet the required voltage blocking capacity. While existing literature typically covers configurations with three series TLB units, the actual number needed depends on the MV grid level and the blocking voltage of each switch. Additionally, increasing the number of units introduces multiple regions with varying voltage & duty range, possible states and different equations crucial for proper functioning and control operation of the converter which are not discussed in the literature. This paper analyzes a four and five TLB series-connected converter across different region and possible states, and generalizes regions and equations for multiple series connected three-level boost (MSTLB). The study verifies its findings through simulations, demonstrating the scalability and validity of the proposed generalization.

articleTitle: PHIL Study on Fault Ride-Through Performance of Photovoltaic Converter in Active Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: As power electronic converter-based renewable energy sources, such as solar photovoltaics and wind turbines, become more prevalent in the grid, many nations are suggesting grid codes to ensure the efficient operation and stability of power systems. One such requirement outlined in these grid codes is the fault ride-through operation of renewable energy sources, which stipulates that they must remain connected during grid fault situations and provide reactive power to support grid stability. Conducting fault ride-through tests in the actual field is expensive and requires bulky equipment. Therefore, a scaled-down photovoltaic converter with the same control can be utilized to assess the network integration of the actual converter using power hardware in loop (PHIL) testing, offering a more cost-effective and alternative approach. This paper presents PHIL test setup to investigate the fault ride-through operation of a photovoltaic converter under both symmetrical and asymmetrical faults cases in the lIT Roorkee distribution network. This PHIL test setup requires a Wavect controller based on FPGA, a Real-time Digital Simulator (RTDS), an inverter, and a power amplifier.

articleTitle: Experimental Study and State of Charge Estimation of A123 Li-Ion Cylindrical Cell Using Passivity Observer in Different Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Accurate estimation of State of Charge (SoC) in lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) is vital for effective energy management, particularly under varying temperatures. This study develops a temperature-dependent passivity observer for SoC estimation using the Lyapunov and linear matrix inequality (LMI) approaches, applying passivity theory for the first time. Using a thermal chamber, SoC measurements were taken at 0°C, 25°C, and 50°C. By integrating temperature effects into the observer framework, we significantly improved SoC estimation accuracy. Extensive simulations and experimental validation demonstrated superior performance over traditional methods. This advancement promotes more efficient and reliable battery management systems (BMS), optimizing LIB usage in various electric vehicle (EV) applications.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Dual-Input Single-Output High-Gain DC-DC Converter for Renewable Energy Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents the design and performance evaluation of a novel non-isolated Dual-Input Single-Output High-Gain (DISOHG) DC-DC converter tailored for renewable energy applications, including fuel cells and solar photovoltaic systems. The DISOHG topology integrates two input sources, achieving higher voltage gain and improved system reliability while maintaining a common ground between the input and output terminals. The converter architecture employs two inductors, three capacitors, three diodes, and two MOSFETs to effectively step up the input voltage to a higher output level. Designed for a 200 W power rating, an output voltage of 350 V, and operating at a frequency of 50 kHz, it supports dual input sources with voltage levels of 48 V and 72 V. A detailed steady-state analysis in Continuous Conduction Mode (CCM) is carried out using analytical waveforms. Experimental results obtained from a prototype developed in the laboratory confirm the converter's effectiveness and performance.

articleTitle: Disturbance Model for the Integrated PSFB and Inverter System in Grid-Tied PV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A phase shift full bridge (PSFB) converter, working as an MPPT tracker, integrated to an inverter working in grid connected mode for photo voltaic(PV) applications is considered in this paper. This paper proposes disturbance models describing the response of the system to irradiation variations. These models are useful in designing the control loop of inverter DC bus voltage in grid connected mode(current injection). Irradiation to solar panel voltage transfer function derived finds use in designing the input PV voltage control of PSFB converter for maximum power point tracking(MPPT) during grid tied mode. The proposed models are validated by comparing the magnitude and phase of derived models with the fast fourier transform(FFT) result of the switching circuit model. The validation is done in the simulink environment.

articleTitle: Design of High-Frequency Current Transformer for Capacitive Wireless Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Capacitive wireless power transfer systems operate near their resonant frequency, typically in the MHz range, with high-quality factor (Q) ensuring sinusoidal currents in the passive elements. High-Frequency Current Transformers (HFCTs) are ideal for sensing such high-frequency currents. However, designing an HFCT for a specific measurement bandwidth presents challenges due to the influence of various design parameters on its performance. While there are advanced commercially available current sensors with high bandwidth, such as Tell-i current sensors and Combinational Rogowsky coils, these options are prohibitively expensive. This paper proposes a methodology for designing a low-cost HFCT for high-frequency sinusoidal current measurement to address this research gap. The proposed procedure facilitates a quick and straightforward comparison of different magnetic materials based on their complex permeability (μ), enabling the selection of the most suitable material for the design and, ultimately, the design of the HFCT. The finalized HFCT is then used to measure the sinusoidal resonant current of a series RLC circuit, and the measurement results are compared with analytically calculated data.

articleTitle: Multi-arm MMC Analysis for Resolving Power Mismatch Issues
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a multi-arm topology of modular multilevel converters (MMC) which consists of multiple number of three-phase arms, each consisting of several halfbridge sub-modules (SM), unlike a conventional MMC that has only even number of arms (two). In this topology, there can be odd number of arms in an MMC (with half-bridge cells). The MMC does not have a central dc-link and is ideally suitable for integrating photovoltaic (PV) arrays into the SMs. Due to various factors, the PV output of each SM may vary, hence leading to various types of power mismatches in the system. This paper proposes solutions for power mismatch among the arms, or among the phases, which is essential to send balanced currents to the grid. The mismatch between arms is resolved by independent arm current control technique, wherein the currents shared by the arms are proportionate to the powers generated by them. The mismatch between the phases is resolved by introducing fundamental frequency zero sequence voltages (FFZSV). These methods of resolving power mismatch have the advantage of not involving the circulating currents among the arms.

articleTitle: Hotel Load Converters for Indian Railways
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Indian Railways aims to achieve 100% electrification transitioning from diesel generators (DGs) in end on generation (EOG) systems to hotel load converters (HLCs) in head on generation (HOG) systems to power hotel loads (HLs) on trains. AC-AC power converters are needed to convert 960 Vrms 1ph voltage from the traction transformer in locomotives to 750 Vrms phase-to-phase 3ph voltage to supply the local step-down transformers in respective coaches for these HLs. This paper presents the design and test results of 500 kVA Cummins-developed HLCs for HOG rail application. Firstly, key performance and safety specifications of the HLC are discussed. Next, major steps to design, test, and integrate the AC-DC rectifier and DC-AC inverter using 3.3 kV IGBT are presented. Finally, simulation and experimental results of pantograph bounce, IGBT DESAT, short-circuit, current THD, and phase-to-earth-feeder voltage limit are presented. The measured AC-AC efficiency was 96.35% at rated voltages and load.

Author Keywords: AC-AC and DC-AC Hotel Load Converters

articleTitle: DC Link Capacitor Loss Minimization for Medium Voltage High Power Railway Traction Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Railway propulsion system deploys three induction motors, each rated at 850 kW, on a single bogey. These motors are operated from three-phase two-level voltage source converters (VSI) connected across the same DC bus of traction converter. DC bus is usually regulated at a fixed voltage through parallel-connected single-phase front end converters. Switching frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(f_{sw})$</tex> of these motor drives is usually restricted below 500 Hz due to significant switching energy losses. Operation at low fsw results into high current ripple on DC link current which increases the loss in the DC link capacitors. Temperature rise on account of power loss in capacitor bank is curtailed by increasing the size of the DC bus capacitance. This paper proposes an interleaved carrier based method to minimize the ripple in DC link current for a multi motor drive operated traction system. Proposed method is validated on a 3 MW traction converter having 3600 V DC link which feeds three IM drive each rated at 850 kW, 2.2 kV and 65 Hz over simulation in PLECs software.

Author Keywords: which results in a high DC link current ripple

articleTitle: Three-Level Boost Converter for EV Charging in Bipolar Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The rapid expansion of microgrids, the surge in electric vehicle (EV) adoption, and the widespread use of renewable energy systems have created an urgent need for a state-of-the-art DC-DC converter with regulated DC bus voltage. To meet this demand and revolutionize power regulation in EV charging stations within bipolar microgrid environments, a three-level boost converter (3-L BC) has been devised. The three-level boost converter is a game-changing interface for bipolar DC microgrids and batteries, handling diverse power levels in positive and negative DC buses. The converter features a closed-loop control system and an incremental conductance-based Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) technique to control power flow adeptly across the DC link poles. A proportional-integral (PI) controller is designed for each operating point using the k-factor approach. A small signal analysis determines the output voltage to the duty cycle transfer function. The PI controller generates a control signal for any operating point using the feedback signals and MPPT technique, thereby balancing the DC bus poles. An electric vehicle (EV) battery is linked to the DC bus for charging and discharging. The converter's performance is assessed using MATLAB/Simulink, and the results emphasize its crucial role in improving voltage stability, facilitating reliable EV charging infrastructure, and promoting sustainable energy practices.

Author Keywords: Bipolar microgrid and DC-to-DC converter for EV's

articleTitle: A Multifunctional Current Fed Triple Active Bridge Converter for EV Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: On-board charger (OBC) and auxiliary power module (APM) are two major power electronic units in electric vehicles (EV). The OBC is the power electronic interface between the grid and the high-voltage (HV) battery. It has an AC-DC converter followed by an isolated DC-DC converter. The APM is an isolated dc-dc converter, is the interface between the HV battery and the low-voltage (LV) battery. The power density of such a configuration is poor due to the presence of multiple power electronic converters. In this paper, an integrated OBC and APM are designed to improve the power density. This solution employs a triple active bridge (TAB) converter, where the AC-DC converter is integrated as a current-fed structure within the converter. This current fed structure forms an interleaved boost converter which further reduces the size of the input inductor. Moreover, this converter has an in-built feature of second-order ripple power compensation (RPC) in the charge mode of EV, this reduces the number of power stages and improves the reliability of the converter. To analyze the performance of the proposed solution a 3.3 kW converter is designed and simulated using MATLAB/Simscape.

articleTitle: Active Disturbance Rejection Controller Approach for Boost Converter in PV Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A boost converter (BC) connects the PV modules and the inverter in a two-stage grid-integrated photovoltaic (PV) system. The interactions between the maximum power point tracking, BC, and inverter influence the system's performance. Active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) provides robustness against uncertainties and quick disturbance response. This paper explores Linear ADRC (LADRC) and Generalized ADRC (GADRC) to improve the PV system's transient response and track reference current from the MPPT controller under environmental and load disturbances, including grid frequency-induced sinusoidal perturbations. The GADRC method integrates any known plant information into the control system, whereas the LADRC method utilizes order and gain information. A dynamic model of the BC system is employed to extract plant information, including order and gain. Additionally, in the ADRC method, the extended state observer estimates the generalized disturbance and incorporates this estimation into the feedback control to quickly mitigate it. The dynamic performance of LADRC and GADRC for the BC system is assessed in terms of settling time, undershoot, overshoot, and steady-state oscillation across various operating conditions.

articleTitle: Analysis of Power Deployment Characteristics and Costs of Energy Storage Systems for Frequency Regulation in Renewable-Rich Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The implementation of renewable energy sources such as solar and wind for electricity production has picked up an enormous pace in recent years, which not only gives rise to a more sustainable process of electricity production but also minimizes carbon dioxide emissions. However, the intermittent behaviour of the sources coupled with the absence of kinetic energy contribution to the electrical grid introduces a negative impact on the frequency stability of the grid. Hence, the grid requires further reinforcements in its infrastructure, and one such promising solution lies in the usage of grid-connected Energy Storage Systems (ESS) as a source of Frequency Containment Reserve for Disturbance (FCR-D) ancillary service for frequency regulation in Europe. This paper presents an extension of our previous work [1] to realize ESS as a favourable candidate for FCR-D service. In our previous work, we showed the benefits of ESS in terms of performance and cost compared to hydro turbines. However, the extended research takes a deeper dive into the characteristics of ESS and shows how the deployment characteristics, such as delay and power level, affect the frequency trajectory of an electrical grid with variable renewable energy penetration (REP) levels after an N-1 disturbance. The research found that ESS adhering to FCR-D deployment characteristics for the same disturbance yields diminishing impact at higher peak power levels, and with an increase in delay of deployment, the peak level must be increased by around 0.8MW to 5.08MW for per second increase in delay as the REP level of the grid rises to 30%. The study also found that the deployment delay must be reduced by up to 33.33% to keep the same level of impact of the disturbance. Finally, the total cost of FCR-D support may increase by up to 148.8% depending on the FCR-D deployment and grid characteristics.

articleTitle: Enhanced Grid Stability Using Virtual Inertia Control Strategy for DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This study demonstrates the use of virtual inertia and its effects on DC microgrid (DCMG) operating under grid-connected mode. The DCMG is comprised of an inertia-less solar photovoltaic system, and a battery energy storage system (BESS) with a bidirectional DC-DC converter (BDDC). The system has AC and constant power loads. The DCMG fails to participate in inertia support due to associated poor inertia and power electronics interface. As per the present grid code, the DCMG in grid-connected mode should participate in inertia support. Therefore, the emulation of virtual inertia utilizing the control loop of BDDC in DCMG is addressed and simulated in this work. Consequently, the battery's life cycle will be enhanced by avoiding high peaks of the BESS caused by low inertia. The simulation result demonstrates that using the proposed virtual inertia concept on BDDC would increase the inertia of DCMG and prolong the lifespan of the battery bank while maintaining the stability of the DC bus voltage. In order to assess the effectiveness of the suggested control strategy, a simulation-based experiment is implemented within the MATLAB/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Power Flow in Direct AC/AC SST with Selective Harmonic Elimination and Pulse Density Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Solid state transformers (SSTs) are integral in interfacing conventional grid to microgrid, any AC/DC source to the conventional grid, any kind of load to conventional grid and microgrid to microgrid. Direct AC/AC SST is a single stage SST with no electrolytic capacitors. It presents the advantages of high efficiency, power density and reliability over multi-stage SSTs. Bidirectional power flow is an essential functionality of any SST topology. With four-quadrant switches, the direct AC/AC SST is capable of bidirectional power flow. Bidirectional power flow in direct AC/AC SST is available in the literature using the space vector based synchronous PWM strategies. However, these synchronous strategies for direct AC/AC SST lead to non-sinusoidal current in the high frequency transformer (HFT) windings. This limits the switching frequency of the SST due to the HFT leakage inductance. The asynchronous PWM technique with selective harmonic elimination (SHE) and pulse density modulation (PDM) removes this limitation by making the current in HFT windings sinusoidal while also removing LC filter associated resonance in HFT voltage and current. bidirectional power flow using the asynchronous PWM strategy with SHE and PDM has not been discussed in the literature. This paper proposes a bidirectional power flow strategy for direct AC/AC SST between two grids of same or different frequencies using the asynchronous PWM strategy consisting of SHE and PDM to bridge this gap. The proposed strategy is verified through simulations in MATLAB Simulink.

articleTitle: Universal Three-Phase On-Board EV Charger Using Bridgeless Non-Isolated Boost-Buck Converter Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel three-phase non-isolated on-board charger for electric vehicles with wide range of voltage. The charger is compatible with the three-phase AC voltage input and is composed of two-stage circuits. The proposed charger is based on switching control of three-phase six-switch power factor correction (PFC) circuit in each phase. The switching control is so designed such that the front end cascade topology of a totem-pole PFC circuit acts as boost circuit while the rear end controls the buck mode with the help of a toggle-able LC tank circuit. The proposed control scheme relies on individual phase control. The control algorithm is simple and the input current and voltage present less distortion. MATLAB/Simulink platform has been used to carry out the simulation and the results have been presented.

articleTitle: Analysis of Control Methods for BLDC Motors in Electric Vehicle Powertrain Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The operation of an electric vehicle (EV) necessitates the use of a motor that is extremely durable, has a high-power density, and is very efficient. Because of its high power-to-weight ratio, the Brushless DC (BLDC) motor meets the quality standards set by the EV application. The effective control approaches will aid in matching the BLDC motor to the current requirements and applications. In this paper, a brief review of BLDC motor control techniques is presented. Further, mathematical modeling is used to develop proportional-integral-derivative (PID) control and self-tuning fuzzy logic PID (FLC-PID) control methods on the MATLAB-Simulink platform. The comparative analysis based on speed regulation, voltage behavior, current distortion, and energy consumption are presented for the two control techniques. It is found that the FLC- PID controller offers a robust and efficient solution for BLDC motor control in EVs, showing superior performance.

articleTitle: A Two-Stage PV-Battery Grid Forming Control with Current Limitations on Both AC and DC Side
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Integration of distributed generation (DG) has seen an exponential rise thanks to the presence of renewable sources. Most DG's employ a two-stage topology to transmit the generated power to grid or feed its local loads. In most of the literature the strategies developed for grid connected operation of a single DG or parallel operation of DGs have been developed considering a stiff DC source. However due to intermittencies in renewables and limited reserves from storage, a stiff DC source cannot be guaranteed. Thus, it would be evident to consider non stiff nature of DC source to imitate a much practical study. To ensure a stable operation on the AC side of the grid connected system, it must be guaranteed that the DC side dynamics are well within bounds. Also it must be guaranteed that the semiconductor based switching devices are not under stress. This paper focuses on the dynamics associated with the DC link and proposes a control scheme that can help mitigate them by improving the co-ordination among sources.

articleTitle: Optimized Switched Inductor-Capacitor Architecture for High Voltage DC-DC Conversion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: To develop a sustainable environment, power generation plans are shifting towards renewable energy sources (RES). However, voltage level mismatch makes it difficult to integrate these sources into loads directly. Traditionally, a boost converter is used to integrate, Yet the voltage gain is not very high. The switched inductor and switched capacitor technologies are introduced to improve the voltage gain of the traditional boost converter. So, in this paper, an optimized switched inductor-capacitor architecture for a high-voltage DC-DC (SICHV) converter is proposed. The functioning of the SICHV converter is elucidated by employing equivalent circuit models and mathematical expressions. To demonstrate the benefits of the suggested SICHV converter, a comparison is made, which demonstrates that the SICHV converter uses a single switch to generate a large voltage gain with less voltage stress across it. To confirm the theoretical assertions, a simulation study is carried out with components designed for specifications of output voltage of 400 V and power of 500 W.

articleTitle: PSFB Converter Based Programmable DC Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: High-frequency power electronic topologies such as phase-shifted full-bridge converters (PSFBs) are widely used in various applications including power supply products. The PSFB converter comprises of four switches that together create a full-bridge structure, a high-frequency transformer, a diode bridge structure, and a suitable control circuit. Since the PSFB converter can operate at high frequencies, it can be used to build compact power supplies. In this work, a 100 kHz switched PSFB converter is designed and developed for a programmable DC power supply requirement. The design aspects of such a programmable power supply based on the PSFB converter are discussed, and its performance is analyzed. The control performance is validated for various time-varying reference profiles, thus emulating a programmable power supply. The converter performance is validated through simulation studies using MATLAB and experimental studies on the developed hardware prototype.

articleTitle: Effect of Input Voltage Unbalanced Harmonics on DC bus Capacitors of Adjustable Speed Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Imbalance (unbalance) and harmonics (background distortion) in the supply voltage are major threats to the DC bus capacitor in an Adjustable Speed Drive (ASD). These disturbances create different frequency components other than the six times supply frequency component in the capacitor current which increases the losses in the capacitor and reduces its lifetime. It is identified from the Power Quality (PQ) survey the harmonics in the three phases are not balanced. This paper analyses the impact of these unbalanced harmonics on the DC bus capacitors. The magnitude of extra frequency components apart from six times the supply frequency component in the capacitor current varies based on the magnitude of unbalance in the harmonics present in the supply voltage. As a result of the analysis, the study proposes an index to assess the impact of unbalanced harmonics.

articleTitle: Control of a Microgrid Integrated PV-Assisted EV Charging Station for Active Power Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a power management strategy for a microgrid-connected electric vehicle (EV) parking lot, which incorporates photovoltaic (PV) power support. The concept of EV-to-grid (V2G) technology is utilized to manage the microgrid power demands by discharging EV batteries when available, with customer consent. The PV arrays charge the EV batteries, while the microgrid power supplements this when PV power is insufficient and microgrid power is available. An algorithm for this power management strategy is derived, featuring an advanced novel grid integration method which enables the system to withstand adverse microgrid operating conditions. This system not only meets the microgrid power demands but also maintains grid power quality. The Hermite interpolation-based maximum power point tracking (MPPT) control ensures optimal utilization of the PV arrays, and the grid synchronization method ensures system stability during grid disturbances. System performance is validated using the MATLAB/Simulink platform, demonstrating effectiveness under varying solar irradiance and grid-side power demand conditions. The results confirm the robustness and effectiveness of the proposed power management strategy in maintaining reliable and high-quality power delivery.

articleTitle: Bootstrap Gate Driver for GaN-Based Solar Inverter: Design Challenges and Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper focuses on gate driver design for Gallium-Nitride (GaN)-based H6 solar inverter topology. Wide bandgap devices such as GaN offer lower on-state resistance and faster switching, leading to improved performance of the converters, such as high efficiency and power density. Bootstrap-based gate drivers are preferred over isolated supply and gate drivers due to their low cost and size. Nevertheless, bootstrap-based solutions present numerous issues that are examined and addressed in this paper. Firstly, the H6 inverter requires multiple cascaded bootstrap circuits in contrast to a full bridge inverter due to the presence of six switches. This increases the complexity of charging the bootstrap circuit during startup of the inverter. The bootstrap capacitors must be pre-charged to a sufficient voltage to ensure the proper functioning of the gate driver. In addition to that, the bootstrap capacitor voltage at the far end of the bootstrap ladder decreases below the desired value in a cascaded structure. Additionally, the voltage of the bootstrap capacitor fluctuates with changes in the duty cycle of the switches. Finally, the reverse conduction properties of the GaN switch might overcharge the bootstrap capacitor, potentially resulting in device failure due to gate over-voltage. The paper highlights the pre-charging of bootstrap gate driver circuits for the inverter operation. It also addresses the challenges related to bootstrap-based gate drivers for GaN devices and presents solutions to mitigate them. The simulation and experimental prototype is developed to validate the bootstrap-based gate driver and its solution for the associated challenges.

articleTitle: High Step-Down Gain Bridgeless Cuk PFC Converter for Battery Charging Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a bridgeless Cuk converter topology, designed with a better stepdown capability, suited for Electric Vehicle (EV) charging applications. The proposed topology puts forward a switched capacitor network merged with bridgeless Cuk configuration to offer notable advantages including higher stepdown gain, reduced current stress and enhanced efficiency. Design and operational analysis are derived under Discontinuous Inductor Current Mode (DICM) operation. DICM mode facilitates natural alignment of supply voltage and current utility side, therefore, eliminating additional controlled converters to achieve unity power factor operation. The presented topology is particularly well-suited for on-board battery charging in light EV applications. This paper presents a comprehensive design, modelling and simulation analysis for a proposed topology rated for 600W at 60V. With a switching frequency of 20kHz, the converter demonstrates harmonics-free input current, well in coherence with IEC 61000-3-2.

articleTitle: Minimization of DC Bus Side Current Ripple in DFIG Supported DC Micro Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Integration of solar PV power plants, battery storage systems and DC loads through DC microgrid (DCMG) has become very popular. Due to absence of additional DC to AC power conversion stage, DCMG based systems have been proven to be efficient and reliable compared to AC grid-based systems. Type IV wind turbines can also be connected to DC microgrid due to the topological flexibility. In this paper, a type IV wind turbine consisting of, dual voltage-source inverter (VSI) fed doubly fed induction generator (DI-DFIG), is used for supporting DCMG having solar PV, battery storage and EV charging station. DC bus of both VSIs are connected to DCMG directly and DFIG is operated in super-synchronous generating mode. Synchronous sine-triangle (SST) pulse width modulation (PWM) technique is used for operating both VSIs. A carrier interleaving based technique is proposed in this paper for minimization of current ripple on the DC bus. Optimized interleaving angles are determined over complete range of turbine speed. Current ripple on DC-bus is found to be reduced significantly. The same is validated through simulations on a 250kW DFIG.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Performance Degradation Prediction of PEM Fuel Cell using Bi-GRU
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) is recognized as one of the clean and sustainable energy solutions for industrial, residential and commercial applications. However, reliable and and accurate prediction of PEMFC health degradation is vital for ensuring their efficient and reliable operation. The performance degradation prediction of PEMFC can be helpful in increased durability, effective utilization and contributes in risk management and maintenance. Deep learning techniques are identified as powerful techniques for prediction as they can learn about features, especially if the data involved in the prediction process is complex and large. Therefore, this study evaluates a data driven performance degradation prediction of a PEMFC using Bi-directional gated recurrent unit (Bi-GRU). Results obtained using Bi-GRU are compared with other approaches, such as,Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), Long Short Term Memory (LSTM), Bi-LSTM, Gated Recurrent Network (GRU). R2 score and other performance indices such as MSE, MAE, MAPE, and RMSE are used to verify the results. From the results, it is elucidated that Bi-GRU predicts PEMFC degradation with the highest R2 score of 0.9993, and the outcome values of MSE, MAE, MAPE, and RMSE are 0.0006, 0.0176, 0.0498, and 0.0255, respectively.

articleTitle: Finite Element-Based Inter-turn Fault Analysis in Closed Loop Induction Motor Drive Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This work utilizes machine learning techniques to investigate the finite element method-constituted stator phase winding inter-turn short fault in an induction motor (IM) operated in a closed-loop speed-controlled approach. One of the biggest challenges for electrical machine researchers is diagnosing inter-turn problems that involve fewer than 5% of turns. Due to the machine's varying speed and fluctuating load, diagnosing such defects becomes more complicated when the machine is regulated from a PWM inverter in a closed-loop speed-controlled technique. In this framework, ANSYS Maxwell finite element tool is utilized to simulate a 7.5 kW IM with several inter-turn fault situations, such as 30T (12.5%), 15T (6.25%), IOT (4.2%), and 5T (2%) and is integrated with ANSYS Simplorer for power source and loading configurations. In order to conduct a realistic simulation, a closed-loop controlled PWM inverter is designed in MATLAB and cosimulated with ANSYS Simplorer. Subsequently, machine learning methods are utilized to analyze the stator current data collected for different levels of fault severity. The outcome shows that ensemble bagged trees achieved a maximum accuracy of 90% across different algorithms. The number of faulty samples in the stator current histogram increases with the severity of the fault.

articleTitle: Improved Phase-Clamping PWM Techniques with Space Vector Approach for Five-Phase System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The most of the researchers are increasingly their favor of the adoption of electric vehicles to mitigate the environmental threats posed by the widespread use of fossil fuel-powered vehicles. Multi-phase drive systems offer distinct advantages for electric vehicles due to their superior power density. Effectively implementing pulse width modulation (PWM) is essential for driving multi-phase drives. This paper focuses on the five-phase voltage source inverter and explores various modulation techniques within a space vector-based approach. The paper introduces a novel switching sequence designed to enhance phase-clamping PWM techniques, incorporating different clamping durations. This improved phase-clamped PWM (IPCPWM) technique demonstrates superior performance in terms of harmonic spectrum and current ripple reduction. Furthermore, the study evaluates the switching energy loss associated with these techniques. The proposed PWM techniques is simulated and analyzed the results.

articleTitle: Optimal Charging Station Locations for Different Battery Sizes of Electric Vehicles in a Road Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) have become increasingly active in the public transportation system. To run an EV uninterruptedly, the location of the charging station (CS) is important. This paper proposes the use of two distinct charging cord levels to meet the charging demands of EVs with varying battery sizes throughout the day. There are two types of charging cords that need to be installed to fulfil the charging demand for EVs. The objectives of this paper are to minimise station installation costs (SIC) and EV travel costs (EVTC) by optimally placing CSs in the considered area. The cuckoo search algorithm (CSA) is used to find the best optimal locations for the considered road network. The results show that the proposed method finds the optimal CS for EVs.

articleTitle: Active Power Decoupling for Reduced-Switch Current-Fed Switched Inverter with Enhanced Gain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The recently developed Reduced-Switch Current-Fed Switched Inverter (RSCFSI) is attributed with key features such as continuous input current, greater ac output voltage, simultaneous operation with ac and dc loads, shoot-through immunity, and so on. The low-frequency (LF) oscillation study of RSCFSI reveals that they are also plagued by both fundamental and second-harmonic oscillations. To address this LF oscillation problem, an active power decoupling (APD) approach for RSCFSI is found in the literature, in which an ancillary capacitor is added to the RSCFSI and the ac output filter inductor is split into two without increasing the total inductance. As a result, the dc-link capacitor needed is substantially lowered without the use of any additional switches. However, the dc-ac voltage gain is remarkably reduced compared to that of RSCFSI. As a solution, this paper provides an alternative APD approach, in which the dc-ac voltage gain range is enhanced, and the voltage stresses on switches and passive components are diminished. A closed-loop control scheme is also elucidated, which assimilates output voltage regulation as well as LF oscillation mitigation. The paper also exhibits an experimental verification of the benefits of the proposed APD approach.

articleTitle: Analytical Prediction of the Unsaturated Inductance Profile of a Switched Reluctance Machine Using a Flux-Tube-Based Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The unsaturated inductance profile of a switched reluctance machine (SRM) is an important characteristic for performance evaluation and simulations. The complete inductance profile can be accurately predicted using inductances at three specific rotor positions, in addition to the aligned and unaligned inductances. This paper presents an analytical method to accurately predict the unsaturated inductance at these three rotor positions in terms of the machine dimensions and the unsaturated permeability of the magnetic material. A closed-form expression for the air-gap permeance is derived for each of these rotor positions, following a flux-tube-based approach. Unlike other analytical methods, this approach can incorporate the impact of rotor pole height, which is essential in high-speed SRMs. Additionally, the proposed method yields accurate results for SRMs with significantly different stator and rotor pole arc angles. The obtained permeances are validated through finite element analysis (FEA)-based simulations. The superiority of the proposed method is demonstrated by comparing it with two existing analytical methods that provide closed-form solutions. Finally, the inductances obtained by incorporating iron reluctance, as well as the derived complete inductance profile, are validated through FEA simulations and experiments performed on a 7.5 kW, 30,000 rpm, 3-phase switched reluctance machine prototype.

articleTitle: Model Order Reduction of a Single Area Power System Using Direct Truncation with Mihailov Criteria Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a single-area power system (SAPS) model is reduced to lower-order (LO) model. A mixed model order reduction (MOR) method is applied to obtain reduced order model (ROM). Direct truncation (DT) approach is applied for order reduction of numerator polynomial, where as, Mihailov criteria technique adopted to obtain reduced order denominator polynomial. The eleventh-order SAPS is taken into account as a numerical example to obtain second-order model. The validity of ROM is tested by plotting time and frequency responses, and comparing the time domain specifications. Also error indices including integral square error (ISE), integral absolute error (IAE), integral time absolute error (ITAE), and integral time squared error (ITSE) are utilized for performance comparison of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Grid Forming Control of PHC Based STATCOM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Voltage stability, power quality, and reactive power support are critical in modern power systems, particularly with increasing renewable energy integration and distributed generation. Static synchronous compensators (STATCOMs) are vital for addressing these challenges. Utilizing modular multilevel converters (MMCs) as STATCOMs enhances reactive power compensation and voltage management. Among various MMC-STATCOM topologies, the parallel hybrid converter (PHC) configuration is preferred because of its smaller capacitor size, reduced component count, and lower switching losses. Traditional PHC-STATCOMs operate in grid-following (GFL) mode, which is inadequate under weak grid or isolated operation due to dependency on grid for obtaining the phase angle. Grid-forming (GFM) control, emulating synchronous generators, provides autonomous voltage and frequency regulation, essential for grid stability with high renewable energy penetration. Implementing GFM control in MMC-based STATCOMs, particularly PHC-STATCOMs, poses challenges such as voltage modules (VMs) balance, stability during disturbances, and fast dynamic response. This paper explores GFM control implementation for PHC-STATCOM, addressing aforementioned challenges under different test case scenarios like balance/unbalance grid, unbalance load etc. Finally, a hardware prototype of 370 V/± 5 kVAR, 7-level 3-phase PHC-STATCOM has been developed to verify the proposed GFM control.

articleTitle: A Novel Passive Islanding Detection Strategy for DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The application of DC microgrid (MG) is extensively increasing in the modern power grid, because of the improved efficiency and reduction in the conversion stages, use of distributed generation which provides DC output, and DC loads. Unintentional islanding detection is a vital concern in both the DC and AC MGs. The research in islanding detection (ID) in AC MGs is well established. But ID in DC MGs is still in its initial stage. Therefore, the aim of this work is for the development of a novel passive ID methodology based on the rate of change of ripple voltage (ROCORV) for DC MGs. The proposed method works adeptly in distinguishing islanding from non-islanding conditions. It also detects islanding conditions adeptly during zero power mismatch conditions. The effectiveness of the proposed methodology is tested for various islanding and non-islanding detection (INI). The intended work detects islanding within 0.102 s.

articleTitle: A Reduced Footprint Extended Arm Thyristor Leg Converter: A VSC with Enhanced Power Handling Capacity for HVDC Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: LCCs (line commutated converter) & VSCs (voltage source converter) have their own advantages and limitations. The use of thyristors & IGBTs together in a converter station to blend in the properties of LCC & VSC would develop a hybrid converter with higher efficiency, superior control flexibility, higher power handling capability, fault tolerance capability etc. This paper relates to an interface arrangement, extended arm thyristor leg converter (EATLC), between an AC power system & an HVDC power system. EATLC has hybrid series-parallel chain-links which introduces current sharing among them. The on-state drop of thyristors is less than IGBTs and therefore major portion of current is made to flow through thyristors. The significant reduction of current in chain links reduces rating of devices and size of capacitors to be used. The advantages of both these converters, LCC & VCC, obtained in EATLC are carefully examined this paper. The results showcase the capability of EATLC to provide independent active and reactive power control despite presence of thyristors. The operation of EATLC for various circumstantial conditions such as standalone and grid connected are verified using PSCAD/EMTDC.

articleTitle: Design of a Multi-Mode DC-DC Converter for High-Power Wireless Charging of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The design of high-power wireless power transfer (WPT) systems has been the subject of substantial research due to the increasing demand for fast, efficient, and effective battery charging methods for electric vehicle (EV) customers. This paper proposes a DC-DC converter capable of operating in three distinct modes. It incorporates an H6-Bridge inverter, which can be configured as half bridge-half bridge (HB-HB), half bridge-full bridge (HB-FB), and full bridge-full bridge (FB-FB), and is connected through LCC-Series networks to a dedicated H6-Bridge configuration. This innovative design enables efficient charging of EVs with battery voltage classes ranging from 400V to 800V without affecting the current ratings of the converter's components. Furthermore, the paper presents an analysis of an equivalent circuit WPT system for battery packs with output voltages of 400V, 600V, and 800V. To validate its effectiveness, a 7.2 kW power converter with a 600V input and a variable output range from 400V to 800V was simulated, achieving an impressive maximum efficiency of 94.2% across a wide spectrum of output voltages.

articleTitle: Closed Loop Controller for Bi-Directional Weinberg DC-DC Converter for Space Satellite Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a non-isolated bi-directional Weinberg circuit topology for battery charge-discharge in space satellite applications is presented. In order to provide a better dynamic response to the DC bus voltage regulation during the discharge mode of operation, a double loop control is employed in the analog domain. Adding an additional switch to operate in synchronous mode mitigate thermal stress on the switches, thereby enhancing the converter's performance and efficiency. To verify the performance of the converter and its control scheme in the discharge mode of operation, simulation was carried out in PSIM and the results are provided. Finally, the experimental results from a 500 W prototype are provided in order to validate the design.

articleTitle: Enhanced Control Structure for Servo Drives with Adaptive PWM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The PWM switching frequency significantly impacts the performance and power dissipation of electrical servo drives. In many fields of application, such as industrial automation, static PWM frequencies are typically used. The novel adaptive PWM approach dynamically adjusts the PWM frequency according to process requirements of manufacturing processes. By adapting the PWM frequency, switching losses and the overall energy consumption of servo drives can be reduced. Changing the PWM frequency at runtime requires enhancements to the control structure for dynamic parameter adjustments and a stable operation of the controllers. To validate the enhanced control structure, an experimental evaluation of the performance at different, dynamically changing PWM frequencies is presented. It is shown that the controller operates with the expected behavior at different frequencies but that there are disturbances at the moment of adjusting the PWM frequency. Non-linearities are identified as a major source, including those caused by IGBT-deadtimes. A simple compensation mechanism is integrated in the enhanced control structure as a proof-of-concept, resulting in an almost complete cancelation of disturbances at the moment of adjusting the PWM frequency.

articleTitle: Enhanced Finite Control Set Predictive Current Control for Modular Multilevel Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The forward Euler integration method has been widely adopted in the development of discrete-time models of modular multilevel converter (MMC) for the implementation of finite control-set predictive current control (FCS-PCC) methods. The use of forward Euler method-based models in FCS-PCC leads to high switching frequency operation, while minimizing the reference current tracking error. However, the high switching frequency operation leads to significant switching losses, which undesirable in high-power MMC applications. Furthermore, these models affect the controllability of submodule (SM) capacitor voltages, leading to a higher voltage ripple. To address these problems, this paper proposes Heun's integration method-based FCS-PCC for an MMC, which aims to reduce the switching frequency and SM capacitor voltage ripple, while maintaining high-quality output waveforms. The proposed approach consists of predictor and corrector stages, which help to reduce computational errors caused by mathematical models inaccuracy at large sampling rates while predicting control variables. The discrete-time models of an MMC are developed by using Heun's integration method and employed in the proposed FCS-PCC implementation to control the MMC. The performance of an MMC with the proposed FCS-PCC has been validated through MATLAB simulations and is further compared with the forward Euler method-based FCS-PCC method.

articleTitle: A Multi-Port Converter as an Onboard Electric Vehicle Charger: Enabling 800V Battery Charging from 400V EVSE
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) face challenges in reducing the charging time and managing the power efficiently. Increasing the charging power can significantly reduce the charging time for the EVs. Current DC fast chargers operate at tens to few hundreds of k W which is insufficient to achieve charging times equivalent to conventional refueling. Advancing to ultra-fast charging above 500kW requires higher battery voltages, such as 800V, to reduce current and hence, the conduction losses. However, compatibility issues arise with existing 400V charging stations, necessitating a power electronic converter to boost the voltage. This paper analyzes the Dual-Transformer Triple Active Bridge (DT-TAB) as an onboard multi-port converter solution. The DT-TAB topology, an extension of the Dual Active Bridge, utilizes two transformers to mitigate power coupling issues and achieves zero-voltage switching (ZVS) across wide voltage ranges, minimizing switching losses. This study focuses on the design, simulation, and closed-loop control of a 22kW DT-TAB implementation, resolving the charging compatibility issue for present EVs.

articleTitle: Design of Stand-Alone PV System for Interior Village of Mizoram
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: To improve living circumstances, rural people in developing nations sometimes lack access to inexpensive, dependable, and sustainable energy sources. In contrast to renewable energy sources, many communities rely on extremely pollutingfuels like kerosene and diesel to meet their demands. In place of that, we should move towards renewable energy sourcesystems. Among them is sun-oriented PV power. According to the research, when an electronic converter is properly controlled, the perturb and observation (P&O) MPPT follows, the procedure and performs better. For its purposes, aboost converter is utilized. This technique yields better results than less regulated electrical converter MPPT modules. In this paper, we are designing a stand-alone PV system of 500 KW using a P&O MPPT controller for an interior village of Mizoram.

articleTitle: Novel Line-Start Rib-Less PM-Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Motor for Submersible Bore-Well Pump
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The presence of radial and tangential ribs adversely affects the electromagnetic performance of a Synchronous Re-luctance Motor. However, they are necessary from the viewpoint of the structural stability of the motor. This paper proposes a novel line-start rib-less permanent magnet-assisted synchronous reluctance motor that improves electromagnetic performance by eliminating ribs/bridges/posts in the rotor structure. In the absence of ribs, the structural integrity of the rotor structure is maintained by the cage winding bars and end rings. The cage winding bars and end rings, which are used to facilitate the self-starting of the motor, are slightly modified to serve the additional role. The efficacy of the cage bars in imparting structural integrity is verified using structural simulations. The resulting rib-less motor has superior performance characteristics in terms of efficiency, power factor, and torque density compared to similar-sized motors that have radial and/or tangential ribs. These claims are substantiated through electromagnetic time-stepping 2D Finite Element Analysis, and the simulation results so obtained are presented.

articleTitle: Advanced Structures of Modern Electrical Machines for Electric Transportation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a review of the development and structural classification of modern electrical machines employed for electric transportation. It highlights the back-EMF characteristics and excitation techniques of various machines by classifying them according to the placement of the Permanent Magnets (PMs) and the type of stator winding. This also includes Hybrid PM Machines (HPMM) where the magnets are magnetized in the same direction.
