With an emphasis on thermal issues, demagnetization, and manufacturing issues, the study particularly reviews stator-PM machines and presents a novel Doubly Salient Parallel Path Magnetic Motor (DS-PPMM) which offers reduced cogging torque, less torque ripple, and more sinusoidal back-EMF waveform in comparison with other doubly salient concentrated wound machines.

articleTitle: Particle Swarm Optimization-Based Sensorless Active Power Decoupling for Active-Front-End Impedance-Source Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The low-frequency harmonics (LFH) problem has been inherent to single-phase Active-Front-End Impedance-Source Inverters (AFE-ISI). The power density and reliability of such inverters have been poor, as large electrolytic capacitors and bulky inductors become obligatory in the active-front-end network (AFEN). In literature, alternatives are researched in the form of Active Power Decoupling Networks (APDNs), in which Boost-type APDN (BAPDN) has attracted a lot of attention for its simple operation and circuitry. The BAPDN consists of two switches, one storage capacitor to store the LFH energy and one transfer inductor for energy transfer from the AFEN capacitor to the storage capacitor. Generally, the implementation of the control loops of BAPDN requires two sensors: one current and one voltage sensor. The current sensor is utilized for the measurement of the LFH current passing through the transfer inductor so that it can be compared with a reference LFH current. The voltage sensor is essential for the measurement of the voltage across the storage capacitor so that the over-voltage protection loop can be constructed. In this paper, a sensorless mechanism is applied to BAPDN, where both sensors can be removed. For the parameter selection of the sensorless controller, the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm is utilized. Finally, with the help of a BAPDN-integrated AFE-ISI hardware prototype, the proposed mechanism is validated with experimental results.

articleTitle: Addressing Fault Ride-Through Challenges in DC Microgrids via Supercapacitor Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Due to the increasing penetration of power electronic converter-based distributed energy sources in the grid, countries suggest grid codes for the proper operation and stability of power systems and their components. One of such grid code requirements for power electronic converter is to remain connected under grid fault conditions and provide reactive power to support grid stability. As the DC microgrid is connected to the grid through a bidirectional power electronic converter (BPEC), its compliance with the grid code is mandatory. When a fault occurs on the grid side of the BPEC, the DC microgrid faces high voltage fault (HVF) and low voltage fault (LVF) events in the DC link voltage, which can risk the operation of the DC microgrid. Thus, to avoid the HVF and LVF events and simultaneously provide maximum reactive power support, this article proposes an integration of supercapacitor in the DC microgrid to remain connected with the grid and ensure grid stability during fault events. Various simulation case studies have been carried out in the Real-Time Digital Simulator (RTDS) platform to validate the efficacy of the proposed control strategy,

articleTitle: A Reduced Stage Half Bridge Based Isolated Interleaved Totempole Unidirectional AC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1}-\phi$</tex> unidirectional half-bridge isolated interleaved totem pole (UHBIIT) ac-dc converter, providing a regulated dc voltage. The proposed converter comprises fewer conversion stages than traditional converters, which enhances its efficiency and simplifies the system's complexity. A basic closed-loop current regulation ensures a high power factor. The source current's total harmonic distortion (THD) is below 5% under the IEC-61000/3-6 standard. The interleaved structure reduces the ripple in the source current. In addition, the half-bridge circuit guarantees that zero-crossing spikes are eliminated because of the body diode's reverse recovery and the sudden shift in the modulation index at the supply's zero crossing. Furthermore, the half-bridge capacitor leg provides a bypass path for the voltage spikes during high switching frequency and simultaneously a return path for the source current. The converter incorporates four controlled active switches, providing uniform thermal distribution. A two-winding transformer is used, which provides galvanic isolation to meet the standard IEC 61851. Simulations are performed in PLECS for a 3.5 kW, 400 V dc load to validate the theoretical analysis. Thermal analysis is also conducted in PLECS simulation by selecting the actual switch model, and the peak efficiency is found to be 98% at an input power factor of 0.995.

articleTitle: Secondary Side Control of Multi-Vehicle Inductive Charger by Using a Semi-Active Bridge Rectifier for Constant Power
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a Multi-vehicle (MV) Inductive Charger (IC). It uses a multileg-inverter instead of a single-phase full-wave inverter to charge multiple vehicles concurrently and individually according to their SOC conditions without cross-regulation. In the literature, constant current (CC) and constant voltage (CV) are very familiar methods of EV charging. A new method of constant power (CP) followed by CV is used in this article to charge the multi-vehicle system. A CP method helps to achieve fast charging for the vehicle and reduces the battery's thermal problem. A semi-active rectifier (SAR) is used in the secondary side to control the voltage and current to achieve constant power. It also helps in impedance matching for maximum efficiency. A MATLAB simulation has been performed for the multi-vehicle Inductive Charger system to verify the result.

articleTitle: Efficient Load Frequency Regulation of Islanded Microgrids with Fractional-Order PI Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This article focuses on load frequency regulation of islanded microgrid <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(I\mu \mathbf{G})$</tex>, which consists of various distributed generation sources like photovoltaic cells, wind turbines, microturbine, biodiesel engine generators, and biogas turbine generators with energy storage systems such as the battery, flywheel, ultracapacitor, and electric vehicles. To eliminate undesirable frequency deviations and errors of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(I\mu \mathbf{G})$</tex>, a fractional-order proportional-integral (FOPI) controller is utilized. Fine-tuning of FOPI controller gains is performed through a rule-based method. To prove the efficacy of FOPI controller in stabilizing frequency response, various simulation-based studies are conducted and compared. Moreover, comparative frequency response, with and without controller and transient specifications, underscore the importance of FOPI controller in stabilizing microgrid frequency.

articleTitle: Satellite Tumbling Control Using Magnetorquers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: One tool for managing a satellite's tumbling, attitude, and stabilization is a magnetorquer. A number of things can cause unintentional tumbling of satellites, such as external forces, imbalances in the distribution of mass, or modifications to the satellite's attitude control system. The satellite's orientation, or attitudinal position, is measured by sensors and fed into a comparator. Next, the detected signal is compared by the comparator to a predetermined reference value. The comparator produces error signals if there is a difference between the measured signal and the reference value. The satellite's orientation is adjusted as needed using these error signals. Devices known as magnetorquers apply torque to a satellite using magnetic fields in an effort to regulate its direction and lessen tumbling. The electromagnetic torque principle underlies the operation of magnetorquers. The torque produced when a magnetic field is created or affected by an external magnetic field can be utilised to adjust the satellite's orientation. The satellite's sensors record its orientation continually and send the information to a comparator. The intended reference orientation is compared to the existing orientation using a comparator. In the event of a discrepancy, it produces error messages so that the satellite's orientation can be changed appropriately.

articleTitle: Virtual Synchronous Generator Based PV-Battery System with a Current-Fed Switched Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In a two-stage photovoltaic (PV) system, batteries are typically connected to the DC-link via a boost converter, while the PV source is connected through another boost converter to operate at maximum power point tracking (MPPT). Virtual Synchronous Generator (VSG) control is popularly used in these systems due to its ability to provide inertia support and primary frequency regulation. Additionally, an inverter with high step-up and step-down capabilities, single-stage conversion, and shoot-through immunity is desired for reliable, versatile, and low-distortion AC inversion. While a current-fed switched inverter exhibits desirable qualities, it lacks inertia support and frequency regulation. The proposed approach in this paper implements Virtual Synchronous Generator (VSG) control in a current-fed switched inverter to meet all the aforementioned requirements by enhancing the performance of the PV-battery system. The effectiveness and advantages of the proposed strategy are validated through MATLAB simulations.

articleTitle: Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference-Based Control of Parallel Connected DC-DC Converters for DC Microgrid Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: DC microgrid has been popular in recent years, because of its excellent features such as decentralized design, environment friendly, and easy integration with renewable energy sources. In a typical DC microgrid, multiple DC-DC converters are connected in parallel for reliable operation. But in this parallel connection, accurate current sharing among converters and DC bus voltage regulation is not as desired. To overcome the inaccurate current sharing and DC voltage regulation problem, a novel Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) based control using the backpropagation training algorithm is proposed. The training efficiency of the proposed system is around ≈ 99.8%. The simulation results demonstrate that the ANFIS-based strategy has lesser oscillations during the sudden change in load conditions and is damped out in less time in comparison to conventional proportional-integral control.

articleTitle: Digitally Controlled PWM Rectifier for Harmonic Reduction and Bidirectional Power Flow
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In particle accelerators, magnet power supplies play a crucial role in controlling particle beams using electromagnets. Various types of power supplies are used in accelerators, including DC, ramping, and pulsed supplies. DC power supplies are typically employed in transport lines and storage rings, while ramping and pulsed power supplies are used for particle energy boosting and beam injection-extraction respectively. However, most of these power supplies, whether utilizing conventional rectifiers (uncontrolled / controlled) as pre-regulators or main regulators, suffer from poor line harmonic distortion and low power factor. To address these challenges, a Pulse Width Modulated Rectifier (PWMR) can be used as a utility interface, significantly improving performance at the cost of additional control and power electronic circuitry. This paper presents the simulation, digital controller implementation, and experimental demonstration of PWMR aimed at reducing line-side harmonic pollution, enhancing input power factor, and enabling bidirectional power flow. Control loop simulations of the PWMR were conducted to understand its dynamics, and Proportional-Integral (PI) controller parameters were tuned to achieve optimal control. An experimental demonstration of the digitally controlled PWMR was carried out using Digital Signal Processor (DSP). The experimental results from the prototype PWMR (100 V, ±5 A) align well with the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: A Novel Signal Processing and Deep Learning Approach for Fault Diagnosis in Grid Integrated AC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A novel approach for microgrid (MG) protection, utilizing Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) and Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNN), is proposed to enhance fault detection for improved reliability and safety. The method applies EMD to decompose the raw signals into distinct intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) across various frequency scales, followed by signal reconstruction based on key IMFs that capture transient characteristics. These reconstructed signals are transformed into 2D scalogram images, which serve as input to the DCNN, allowing the model to extract both temporal and frequency-based features for comprehensive fault analysis. By combining EMD with DCNN, the proposed EMD-DCNN method achieves improved accuracy and reliability in detecting shunt and series faults in grid-connected microgrids, with simulations carried out in the MATLAB/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: A Novel Sampling Mechanism for a Digital Average Current-Mode Controlled Buck Converter Under Leading-Edge Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Uniformly sampled digital average current mode control often employs dual-edge modulation to capture the average inductor current accurately. However, this technique fails to capture noise-free samples for converters that operate with a wide range of duty ratio. This happens due to the placement of the sampling clock only at interval-1 or interval-2 for the entire duty ratio range. This paper proposes a novel sampling mechanism that can capture noise-free samples by shifting the sampling clock position. With duty <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D\geq 0.5$</tex>, the technique will produce the sampling clock in interval-1; otherwise, it will produce the sampling clock in interval-2. Thus, the proposed sampling technique can be used for capturing noise-free samples in converters that operate with a wide range of duty ratios. The proposed mechanism can also be used in other digital average current-mode controlled DC-DC converters.

articleTitle: Development of Multi-Pulse Rectifier System Based on Multi-phase Conversion and Phase Displacement Technique for Medium Voltage Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a sixty-pulse rectifier for medium voltage drive applications. At all load situations, it is meant to fully optimize performance of a medium-voltage induction motor drive system across whole speed range, from standstill to rated speed. The phase displacement and multi-phase conversion techniques are used in construction of suggested multi-pulse rectifier system. There are three sets of multi-winding transformers in proposed multi-pulse rectifier setup, where primary of these multi winding transformer is designed for adopting three-phase supply from grid while secondary windings are designed for delivering five-phase power supply. Here, modular unit of transformer operates as twenty-pulse rectifier while entire system operates as sixty-pulse rectifier because primary winding is designed with phase displacement technique. Apart from this, a hybrid seven-level inverter is designed and developed to overcome the issue at drive end of medium voltage drive system. Major advantages of presented power converter include simple structure, modular structure, high reliability, and low-harmonic input/output waveforms, without a need of filter element. Practicality of system is confirmed by simulation results using a 4.16 kV, 1250 hp induction motor drive. The viability of innovative circuit and related control method is also confirmed by experiments conducted on a downscaled prototype of 415 V, 7.5 kW.

articleTitle: A Generic Load Flow Solution for Droop-Controlled AC Microgrids Considering Electric Vehicle Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Microgrids (MGs) have become more unpredictable due to integration of renewable generation sources. Several methods are used to solve load flow problems in MGs. Load flow analysis is a complex problem for islanded MGs due to the absence of slack bus and dependency of active power generation of droop-controlled DGs on frequency. In this paper, a Modified Newton Raphson (MNR) approach is used to perform load flow analysis of isolated MGs considering various types of electric vehicle (EV) loads. The presented method has been validated on 6-bus and 38-bus test systems of the islanded microgrid to give an accurate and simple approach for computing the load flow solutions.

articleTitle: Advanced Modulation Control for Three-Phase Single-Stage DC-AC Conversion with Optimized Filter Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The present article introduces a single-stage threephase DC/AC converter that incorporates an optimized filter design, aiming to simplify the power conversion process. Conventionally, to generate three-phase pure sinusoidal waveforms, three-power conversion stages are involved: a DC-DC converter, DC-AC inverter and a filter circuit. The term “single-stage” highlights the integration of these functionalities into a single conversion stage, which significantly reduces the system's complexity and size. Compared to the state-of-art approaches, the converter operates with a quantized sinusoidal modulation technique (QSMT). With an inherent filtering property, the QSMT is able to generate sinusoidal output waveforms, thus reducing the additional filter requirements. The operation of three-phase converter topology along with the suggested control scheme is thoroughly examined mathematically. Further, a brief discussion on the parametric design of passive components is presented with the investigation of filter size reduction compared to other modulation strategies. A comparative analysis with existing literature demonstrates the advantages of the proposed QSMT in terms of filter type, size, device count and harmonic distortion. The provided simulation results illustrate the operations of the converter topology using the control scheme.

articleTitle: An Isolated High Gain Quadratic DC-DC Boost Converter for Fuel Cell Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: An isolated high gain quadratic DC-DC boost converter for fuel cell application is proposed in this paper. The proposed converter has several advantages over other isolated and non-isolated DC-DC converters such as having relatively higher voltage gain at comparatively lower operating duty ratio. This not only helps to prevent the core saturation, but also lower the required turns ratio for a certain voltage boosting which prevents the drop in converter efficiency due to higher turns ratio. In addition to the aforementioned advantage, this converter has lower voltage stress on the active switches and diodes. The operating principle of the proposed converter has been explained and the relation between voltage gain in term of duty ratio is derived and presented in brief. Further, the expression for voltage stress across the active switches are presented. A control strategy of the proposed converter to control the load voltage of it only is also explained in brief. In order to validate the working of the proposed converter, a MATLAB Simulink model of it has been prepared, and exhaustive simulation study has been performed. The parameter of the proposed converter which are selected for the simulation study are as follows: input DC voltage: 24 V, load voltage: 400 V, operating duty ratio: 0.42, transformer turns ratio: 2, output power: 500 W.

articleTitle: Grid Forming Control of THSSC Under Unbalanced Grid Condition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Static synchronous compensators (STATCOM) are utilized in power systems to improve power quality, such as voltage support, reactive power support, harmonic mitigation, and flicker mitigation. Compared to the conventionally used hybrid series converter (HSC) based STATCOM, the transformer-less hybrid series static compensator (THSSC) has distinct advantages such as lower dv/dt stress, decreased energy storage requirements, fewer capacitors needed for submodules (SMs), fewer switching devices, and transformer-less functionality. However, its control system uses a phase-locked loop (PLL) for grid angle detection, which can be disrupted by grid disturbances. To address this issue, this paper implements a grid forming control (GFM) for THSSC. GFM is a control strategy that allows the THSSC to actively regulate the grid voltage and frequency, thereby maintaining grid stability even under unbalanced grid conditions. Key challenges while implementing the GFM strategy, such as capacitor voltage of modules, dynamic stability, and fast response, are investigated. This paper shows the impact of GFM on the performance of THSCC under different test cases. Finally, hardware results are presented under a balanced and unbalanced grid to verify the proposed GFM control.

articleTitle: Net Zero Energy Consumption for MW Scale Solar PV Supported Network Through Utility Grid Based Banking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Electrical networks are often connected with AC and DC loads for fulfilling the industrial and domestic requirements. The ever-growing energy demand must be satiated through utility grid supported by various power generating sources. Power Electronic converters are interfaced to match AC network load demands through renewable power generating plants. Instantaneous power and average energy demand for the loads connected to a common network can be fulfilled through the combination of traditional grid power and power-electronic converter interfaced solar PV plant. Thus, solar PV plants should be designed to not only meet the peak-load demands but also achieve net-zero energy consumption from utility grid. This paper proposes design of solar PV plant for supporting a DC load rated at 100 kW and AC load rated at 400 kW at 0.8 pf towards net-zero energy consumption. The proposed structure utilizes the DC link, regulated through the active front end converter, of solar PV plant to connect the DC Load without any additional power converter. On the other hand, AC load is connected to the utility grid in traditional way. A detailed design of solar PV system including sizing and control of power converters is presented in this paper. Computational validation based on irradiance data of Jodhpur region is performed for net-zero energy consumption. AC power converters, connected in parallel, are operated with carrier interleaving for reducing the distortion in grid-side line current. Performance of complete system is extensively validated through simulations for various operating conditions.

articleTitle: Adaptive Sliding Mode Controlled on-Board Dual Stage EV Charger with Enhanced Power Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents an Onboard Dual-Stage EV Charger (ODEC) with a boost Interleaved Power Factor Correction (IPFC) unit integrated with Capacitor-Inductor (CLLLC) resonant Dual-Active Bridge (DAB) converter. Onboard Chargers (OBC) are expected to enhance power quality on the mains supply side while maintaining compactness, high power density, and robustness against zero-crossing impulse currents. Proportional Integral (PI) control exhibits decreased robustness with parameter changes, non-linearities, limited eigenvector placement, and nonminimal phase elements. Double-Integral Sliding Mode Control (DI-SMC) circumvents these shortcomings, and thus a PI-based hybrid dual-loop DI-SMC control technique is proposed, in this paper. The hybrid control includes a PI-based dual-loop DI-SMC control loop, where the outer loop regulates a DC link voltage and inner loops regulate the boost inductor currents. CLLLC DAB includes a phase control loop that regulates the output charging port voltage. It is observed that the PI-based dual-loop DI-SMC implementation of IPFC is a PI dual-loop structure with additional active feed-forward compensation improving the input current quality. Further, a Second-Order Generalized Integrator with Phase Locked Loop (SOGI-PLL) is used to track the grid angle for unit vector template generation for IPFC reference currents. Validation of the proposed technique has been done in simulation and hardware, and the results are discussed.

articleTitle: Grid Voltage Sensor-Less State-Observer based OSS-MPCC for Grid-Tied Inverter with LCL Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents an enhanced reduced-sensor Optimal-Switching-Sequence Model-Predictive-Current-Control (OSS-MPCC) algorithm for grid-tied inverters with LCL filters, using only injected grid current measurements. The OSS-MPCC algorithm relies on four signals: estimated symmetrical components of grid voltage from a virtual flux observer, state estimates from Kalman Filter based estimation, reference positive sequence grid current from SOGI-QSG symmetrical voltage estimations, and inverter switching states for predictive current tracking. The proposed algorithm offers multiple benefits: it limits the switching frequency spectrum of the inverter voltage, reduces sensor count from nine to three, maintains low grid current THD even with voltage unbalance, and its computational time is comparable to previous OSS-MPC algorithms. Numerical validation has been conducted through MATLAB simulations.

articleTitle: Voltage Stabilization of a SEIG-Based Micro-Hydro System Using Static Synchronous Series Compensator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The Self-Excited Induction Generator's (SEIG) voltage regulation degrades with increased loading. This article attempts to use a battery-supported static synchronous series compensator (SSSC) to construct, simulate, and enhance the SEIG performance. The compensator used is a series operated, IGBT based voltage-controlled voltage source converters (VC-VSC), which is sinusoidal pulse width modulation (PWM) operated. The performance of SSSC is faster and accurate than that of the series capacitor approach. The SEIG modeling was done using a d-q reference frame. A decoupled control strategy is developed for the SSSC to manage the power flow between the SEIG and load. The evaluation of the harmonic spectra of the generator and load side voltage and current is another technique used to evaluate the power quality of the SEIG-SSSC system, which is done in this work. The entire model is developed using Matlab/Simulink environment and verified using OPAL-RT 4510 simulator.

articleTitle: Battery-Ultracapacitor fed Parallel Active Interleaved Bidirectional Converter Controlled BLDC Motor for E-Bike Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper explores the design aspects and control of the parallel active configuration of battery and ultracapacitor (UC) controlled BLDC motor drive for E-bike application. Since both the battery and UC have limitations in terms of power and energy density respectively, their combined use offers an optimized energy storage solution. The battery is interfaced to the BLDC motor through a non-isolated interleaved bidirectional converter (IBDC) and the UC is connected at the DC bus through another BDC. The interleaved architecture improves the power handling capacity and reduces the ripple current of the battery at the input port. It enables current sharing across different phases, which decreases the size of the filter inductor as well as the input and output capacitors, thus increasing the power density of the converter. The incorporation of battery-UC based PA-IBDC for the BLDC motor drive helps in efficiently storing energy regenerated from the motor during braking, thus enhancing energy utilization. Additionally, UC supports the battery during acceleration/braking phases which eradicates the negative effects of frequent battery discharging/charging. The effectiveness of the entire system is verified through simulation in MATLAB/Simulink under different operating scenarios. This research demonstrates significant potential for the future ad-vancement of EV technology. Therefore, this work can be further extended to optimize the complete system performance with real-time validation in different practical scenarios.

articleTitle: Seamless Mode Transition of a VSI in a 3-Phase Standalone Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: During transition of an incoming Voltage Source Inverter(VSI) from current to voltage-controlled mode in a standalone micro-grid, any instantaneous mismatch between these mode reference voltages causes a significant current transient which could lead to cascaded tripping of the operating units. Reported mode transition strategies either focus on grid-interactive systems or do not provide any insight about appropriate handling of the mode reference voltages during this transition. This paper proposes a compensation technique to the input voltage reference that includes synthesizing a current reference for equal power sharing, a synchronization loop and a proportional controller for equalization of the mode reference voltages. Mathematical analysis is presented in this paper to show that the aggregate of proposed compensations can eliminate any instantaneous mismatch between the mode reference voltages, thus allowing for zero transient mode transition. The proposed method is validated by experimental results obtained from a 22.5 kVA, 3-phase standalone micro-grid, comprising 3 VSI-s of identical rating connected in parallel.

articleTitle: A Unique Z-Source DC-DC Converter with Reduced Stresses on Passive Components
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: DC-DC converters play a critical role in various applications, such as electric vehicles (EVs) and photovoltaic (PV) systems, where there is a need to either step up or step-down the voltage levels. Among the various topologies, Z-source DC-DC converters have gained attention due to their ability to achieve higher voltage gains compared to conventional converters. This paper introduces a novel Z-source DC-DC converter topology that significantly reduces the voltage stress across passive components, thereby allowing the use of devices with lower voltage ratings. This reduction in stress contributes to improved efficiency and potentially lower costs. Comprehensive simulations of the proposed converter have been conducted, and the results align well with the theoretical analysis, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed design.

articleTitle: A Novel Six-Switch Three-Output DC-DC Converter with Isolated Buck Characteristics and its Derivation from a Novel Four-Switch Two-Output Non-Isolated DC-DC Converter with Modified Boost and Complimentary Buck Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a novel isolated DC-DC converter with six switches and three output ports is presented. The isolated output port observes the characteristics of an isolated buck converter in the Continuous Conduction Mode (CCM) whilst the two non-isolated output ports observe modified boost and complimentary buck characteristics respectively. The isolated topology is derived from the cascaded connection of a novel four-switch non-isolated DC-DC converter possessing the above-mentioned modified boost and complimentary buck outputs at the input side and a flyback branch at the output side. CCM steady-state analysis of the converters is presented and MATLAB® SIMULINK simulation platform is used to simulate the converters to validate the analyses. Closed-loop current controller dynamics are investigated and the efficacy of the designed controller is validated against step changes in load. In summary, a novel four-switch two-output port non-isolated DC-DC converter is presented and it is used to derive a novel six-switch isolated buck converter retaining the characteristics of the said non-isolated output ports as well.

articleTitle: Investigating Temperature Variations in AC Impedance with an Indigenously Developed EIS Test-Bed
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) is increasing rapidly, necessitating improvements in vehicle performance, reli-ability, and safety. The battery pack plays a crucial role in an EV, and thus, its performance should be monitored and enhanced. However, the performance of a battery pack is affected by multiple factors, one of which is the changing environmental conditions of the area where the vehicle operates. Ideally, it is targeted that the battery pack output exhibits minimal variations with changes in climatic conditions. Impedance in battery is one of the commonly analysed parameter to determine the performance of pack. Analyzing impedance variations under diverse operating conditions is essential for understanding pack behavior. This paper presents a detailed electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) analysis of lithium-ion cells of different manufacturers at different temperature conditions, ranging from −10°C to 50°C, across a frequency range of 20 mHz to 10 kHz. The study offers insights for the research community and OEMs (Original equipment manufacturer) to identify cell chemistry and manufacturers that exhibit minimal variation with changes in temperature.

articleTitle: Modular Three-Phase Matrix-Based Single-Stage High-Frequency Link Bidirectional PFC Converter for EV Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel modular three-phase matrix-based single-stage isolated high-frequency link (HFL) bidirectional AC/DC power factor correction (PFC) converter for fast EV charging applications. The proposed configuration consists of current-fed matrix converter (CFMC) with each of three-phases at AC side and the three-phase full-bridge converter at DC side via HFL, which is an optimal choice for a single-stage with galvanically isolated for EV charging application. The proposed soft-switching modulation technique attains zero current switching (ZCS) at AC-side switches and zero current turn-on at DC-side devices without active clamp or snubber circuit, which results into significantly reduced the switching losses, hardware, and cost. The implemented control method and novel modulation method ensure bidirectional power flow throughout operation with soft-switching technique. The paper demonstrates the steady-state operation and analysis, simulation results using Altair PSIM 11, and hardware experimental results.

articleTitle: Assessment of Unbalance Factor in Line Currents During Fault Tolerant Operation of Five Phase Induction Motor-Drive System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This research article aims at assessment of unbalance factor in line currents during fault tolerant operation of five phase induction motor (FPIM) drive system. Multiphase machines have gained more popularity because of their appreciable features like fault tolerance, high torque density, reduced torque ripple and reliability. These features make them more suitable for industrial applications like electric vehicles, electric ship propulsion, aircrafts etc. Five phase induction motor is chosen because of its simple and robust nature. The stator of FPIM has three possible configurations, star, pentagon and pentagram. An open phase fault is modeled using back-EMF approach and an appropriate fault tolerant control technique (FTCT) is applied to compensate for the unbalance and distortion that occur due to open phase fault. The phase currents are free of distortion and unbalance after the applied strategy, nevertheless, line currents do not reflect the same. It is worth noting that the applied strategy can lessen distortion in line currents but unbalance still exists in line currents. The amount of unbalance present in the currents is accounted by unbalance factors. Here, unbalance current factors are calculated using the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) standard definition. The aforementioned strategy is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink environment and the simulation results are discussed assiduously.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Wide Bandgap device based DAB Converter for EV On-Board Chargers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper focused on design and simulation of 3.3 kW, 400V DC output, Gallium nitride high electron mobility transistors (GaN-HEMT) based Dual Active Bridge (DAB) DC-DC Converter for EV On-board Chargers (OBC). An optimized design of converter with high power density and high efficiency is proposed. GaN-HEMT and Planar Transformer are selected to achieve high power density due to its compact size and high switching frequency. Proposed GaN based converter design, overall component selection, modes of operation and control strategies are discussed in details. The simulation of proposed converter is carried out in Plexim software. The performance analysis of GaN based DAB and SiC based DAB are presented in Plexim software. The overall device losses of both converters are compared and presented.

articleTitle: Switched-Capacitors Based Five-Level Boost Common-Ground Type Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A switched-capacitor-based five-level common ground type inverter is proposed in this article. The proposed inverter achieves two-fold voltage gain using two switched capacitors (SCs), each rated for half of the inverter's peak output voltage, and both SCs are self-voltage-balanced. As a result, the voltage stress on semiconductor devices is reduced, as is the cost and complexity of control. Because of the common ground feature, the proposed inverter eliminates ground leakage current. Furthermore, the circuit description and operational modes are described in indepth detail. Further, the circuit description and operational modes are explained in detail. The several simulation experiments demonstrate the practicality of the proposed inverter, and results are presented for grid-connected mode. Finally, a detailed comparative analysis is performed to highlight the key figure of merits of individual inverters.

articleTitle: A Modified T-Type Based Single-Stage 3-Level Isolated Bidirectional Off-Board Charger for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Traditional AC-DC isolated converters typically follow a design approach by integrating the two stages. The primary stage involves an AC-DC power factor correction (PFC) stage. The Secondary stage is a resonant converter with regulated output DC voltage. Existing topologies mainly comprise the boost-PFC stage which is integrated with either side of the switch network of the resonant converter, with the benefit of 25% reduction in switching devices. These topologies allow for soft switching at high frequencies, enabling the use of smaller magnetic components and capacitors for higher power density. Despite that, they are unipolar voltage-fed resonant systems with unidirectional power flow (AC-to-DC) and high switch voltage stress. To embark on the drawbacks of conventional converters, this paper proposes a novel 3-level T-type isolated bidirectional AC-to-DC converter. The voltage generated across the secondary side of the resonant tank corresponds to the proposed converter is bipolar in nature, which leads to advantageous G2V and V2G operation. It is an extended version of the T-type 3-level converter. Simulations and experiments demonstrate successful power transfer (6.6 kW) at a 126 kHz switching frequency, with a 415V AC input grid and 800V DC battery.

articleTitle: Vulnerability Analysis of Torque Controlled PMSM Drives Against Sophisticated Data Integrity Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) have become more intelligent and smarter with the incorporation of electronics and software which depends on sensor signals and networks. For better performance of the connected and autonomous EVs, several sub units have to be controlled in a centralized manner. However, this has made it more vulnerable to malicious cyber-attacks, since the sensors and networks are more prone to cyber-attacks. In this paper, the impact of various sensor data integrity attacks on torque controlled permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) based electric drive system (EDS) has been studied through MATLAB simulations. Different sensor data integrity attacks are modelled and analysed with the help of predefined performance metrics for PMSM-based EDS under different torque control strategies. The simulations and analysis can help in understanding the impacts of sensor data integrity attacks on EDS and hence can pave way for its effective mitigation through predictive control approach.

articleTitle: D-Axis Disturbance Injection and Wavelet Transform based Islanding Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The unplanned islanding formation is needed to be detected and subsequently the distributed generators (DG) required to be de-energized. This becomes essential to safeguard the maintenance personnel and the electrical equipment. In this work, a hybrid islanding detection strategy is proposed based on d-axis current disturbance injection and subsequent analysis of the voltage by the wavelet transform. The proposed strategy is efficient to detect the islanding event, and also classify the non-islanding events precisely even though the measured voltage or frequency magnitudes are out of its operating zone. Thus the proposed strategy allows the DGs for the ride through capability. The proposed strategy is corroborated using MATLAB/Simulink 2024a

Author Keywords: hybrid islanding detection and d-axis current disturbance injection

articleTitle: Robust PID Controller for DC-DC Boost Converter Feeding CPL
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Power electronics converters with constant power loads (CPL) exhibit negative incremental impedance characteristics, which can affect the converter regulation performance and may cause instability. A robust QFT approach is proposed in this paper to improve the regulation performance and maintain the robust stability of the boost converter system with CPL. Loop shaping technique is employed to design a robust PID controller with disturbance dynamics in the QFT approach. The advantage of the proposed QFT based design is demonstrated by the means of simulations of a boost converter supplying a CPL

articleTitle: An Islanding Identification Strategy based on Disturbance Injection and Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The continuous advances in the power electronics technologies, assisted the renewable energy resources to be connected to the distribution electrical network effectively. It provides several advantages and a few challenges like islanding detection. It is vital to detect the accidental islanding formation to protect the electrical component and the working personnels. In this work, an accidental islanding identification strategy is proposed to detect the island formation based on current disturbance injection and wavelet transform. The proposed methodology identifies the islanding formation within 200 ms, and allows the distributed generator (DG) for the fault ride through. The proposed strategy is verified and validated in MATLAB/Simulink 2024a.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control of a New Common-Mode Current Free EV Charger with a Wide Output Voltage Range
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Non-isolated electric vehicle (EV) chargers are gaining popularity due to their enhanced efficiency, power density, reduced cost and smaller footprint. However, the lack of an isolation barrier in the charging system poses challenges such as the generation of a large common-mode (CM) current and touch current hazards, which cause serious safety concerns for the end-user. On the other hand, an EV charger should have a wide output voltage range to support different EV battery pack voltages. This paper presents a new non-isolated EV battery charger that minimizes CM current and ensures compatibility with a wide voltage range of EV battery packs. The proposed topology comprises two stages: an AC-DC converter stage for power factor correction (PFC) and a DC-DC converter stage for charging the battery at its nominal voltage. The AC-DC converter stage consists of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{3}-\phi$</tex>, four-wire full-bridge converter with a split DC-link, whose midpoint is connected to the mains neutral. This provides very stable potential at the DC-link rails. The DC-DC converter stage consists of a three-level (3L) buck converter. The discrete-time model of the proposed charger is derived and employed in the model predictive control algorithm to control the charger effectively. The simulation results are presented to verify the operation and performance of the proposed charger.

articleTitle: Design of a Single Phase Twenty Five Level Grid Connected Inverter for Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Galvanic isolation is a crucial component of grid-connected solar PV systems. Despite the increasing adoption of multilevel inverters (MLIs) for grid-connected applications, the literature lacks sufficient discussion on the isolation of these inverters. This paper introduces a 25-level isolated multilevel inverter topology that utilizes only fourteen switches. The proposed configuration incorporates three transformers, each connected via a combination of three bidirectional switches and two H-bridges. This single-phase isolated inverter efficiently generates a 25-level AC output voltage with a voltage gain of 6 while requiring fewer switches. The design of the proposed converter is compared with state-of-the-art multilevel inverters described in the literature. Simulations conducted using MATLAB software demonstrate that the proposed MLI delivers high-quality power, even under dynamic conditions.

articleTitle: Optimized Voltage Harmonic Injection Strategies to Mitigate Speed Fluctuations in PMSM EV Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The growing demand for efficient and reliable electric vehicles therefore requires minimal speed and torque variation, which provides them with precise, smoother control and an enhanced user experience. Therefore, this paper presents the enhanced SSA-optimized voltage harmonic injection strategies to mitigate speed fluctuations in Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (IPMSM) based EV drives. Furthermore, comprehensive analyses, speed harmonic extraction, and system performance assessments for validation are provided under various operation conditions. This study enhanced the optimized amplitude and phase-based control strategy to enhance the EV user experience, and lifespan of the motor. The optimized control is tested with and without speed harmonic suppression which improves user experience. The outcome validates that the optimal voltage harmonic method effectively reduces speed harmonics and speed ripple in an IPMSM-based EV drive system.

articleTitle: Model Reference Adaptive System Based on Ultra-Local Model for Induction Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Induction motors' longevity, ease of use, and relative affordability have contributed to their widespread adoption across various industries and application domains for their low cost and high efficiency. Model Reference Adaptive Systems (MRAS) have been widely used to obtain high performance at a reasonable cost. MRAS typically uses two models, the Reference and Adaptive, which rely heavily on motor characteristics. This reliance can impair performance in extreme environments, such as deep mines. This work describes a new Ultra Local Model-based MRAS (MRAS-ULM) that eliminates rotor parameter dependency in the adaptive model of standard MRAS. The performance and application of the MRAS-ULM Speed Sensorless Induction Motor drive are evaluated under various conditions. Experimental results confirm the efficacy and superiority of the suggested approach for induction motor applications in demanding conditions, such as HVAC systems.

articleTitle: Modified MTPA Controlled Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Drive for Electric Vehicle Application Considering Magnetic Saturation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper investigates the performance of an Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (IPMSM) drive under Maximum Torque Per Ampere (MTPA) control, taking magnetic saturation into account. Practical drive systems are susceptible to magnetic saturation, particularly under heavily loaded conditions. This study proposes a method to integrate saturation effects into MTPA control and evaluates the motor's performance with and without saturation through extensive simulations. MATLAB/Simulink is employed to model and simulate a three-phase voltage source inverter (VSI)-fed IPMSM drive using Sinusoidal Pulse Width Modulation (SPWM). Additionally, a laboratory prototype is developed, and the modified MTPA control is tested on a scaled version of the IPMSM used in simulations. The drive's performance is assessed under various load and speed conditions to show its effectiveness for Electric Vehicle Application.

Author Keywords: Maximum Torque Per Ampere (MTPA) and Flux Weakening(FW)

articleTitle: Implementation of Microgrid System and Its Operation Under Line to Ground Fault Condition in Grid Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Microgrid is a collection of distributed energy sources such as solar PV, wind energy, fuel cells as well as energy storage systems.It usually runs synchronously with the grid, but it can be disconnected from the grid to operate in island mode. One of the major challenges under such conditions is the implementation of the transition from Islanded/Standalone to Grid connected mode of operation and vice versa, under Line to Ground fault/post-fault conditions. This study introduces a decentralized control structure for a Microgrid that incorporates a Battery and a PV Source. The proposed control architecture implements a smooth transition from Islanded/Standalone to Grid Connected mode and vice versa under normal and unbalance (Line to Ground fault) Grid Voltage condition. The performance of the proposed control strategy is validated by experimental results in a Hardware in Loop (HIL) System.

articleTitle: Integrated Speed and Current Control with Adaptive Sliding Mode Based Deadbeat Predictive Strategy Considering Uncertainties for In-Wheel PMSMs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive sliding mode control (ASMC) combined with deadbeat predictive current control (DPCC) is developed to enhance current tracking precision and improve speed robustness in in-wheel permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM), particularly under uncertainties such as parameter mismatches and external disturbances. These uncertainties are modeled as lumped disturbances within the PMSM drive system. First, the ASMC is developed to enhance speed tracking, while the adaptive reaching law is employed to mitigate chattering and expedite the rise time, ensuring fast convergence to the desired speed. Next, the DPCC is applied to further improve current regulation performance. Additionally, disturbance observer is designed to estimate the lumped disturbances and provide compensation in the speed and current control loop, thereby improving the drive performance robustness. The effectiveness of the proposed ASMC-DPCC method is demonstrated through simulations on in-wheel PMSM motors, showing improved tracking accuracy and disturbance rejection.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Dual-Input DC-DC Converter for Ultra-Capacitor/Battery HESS in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Due to the limited life cycle of the battery in Electric Vehicles (EVs), nowadays, HESS (Hybrid Energy storage systems) are in demand (As the number of charges/discharges increases, the life span of the battery will decrease). Therefore, a new ultra-capacitor (UC)/battery HESS is proposed. As the energy density of the battery is higher than that of UC and the power density of UC is higher than that of the battery, combining these properties will achieve better overall performance. Four modes (low power mode, medium power mode, high power mode, and regenerative braking mode) of the proposed converters are described. In these modes, UC has preferred frequent charge and discharge so that the battery is limited in use, which will improve the lifetime of the battery. The control scheme is presented to achieve higher efficiency by establishing maximum direct power flow between input and output, and soft switching techniques such as MOSFET switches are used. The advantages of higher efficiency lead to higher power density, low-temperature rise and converter of smaller size and weight. The proposed converter system is verified with simulation studies.

articleTitle: Asymmetrical Low Switch Count 15-Level Multilevel Inverter with Multi-Carrier PWM Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This study investigates the performance of an asymmetrical 15-level multilevel inverter topology featuring four half-bridge modules and three input DC voltage sources. The voltage sources ratio is 1:2:5. A multi-carrier level-shifted PWM control strategy is employed to generate the required gate pulses of the proposed inverter. The inverter operation is simulated using MATLAB/Simulink software. The research assesses the inverter's performance under varying load conditions and modulation indices, aiming to validate its effectiveness in industrial and renewable energy applications.

articleTitle: PSO-Based Optimised Type-III Controller for Dual-Input Bipolar Triple-Output Coupled Inductor Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper explores the modeling and design of a voltage mode control (VMC) for a magnetically coupled dual-input bipolar triple-output (DITO) buck converter. The small-signal model of the converter is developed using the state-space averaging method. The compensator design is based on the model. A Type-III compensator is selected, and its parameters are optimized using particle swarm optimization (PSO). The PSO-based compensator design technique enhances dynamic performance and addresses cross-coupling and cross-regulation issues inherent in coupled-inductor dc-dc converters. The proposed method provides designers with flexibility in trading off various closed-loop performance parameters. The designed controller is capable of simultaneously regulating three voltage levels: 3.3 volts, −3.3 volts, and 6.6 volts. The proposed methodology demonstrates improved transient responses compared to existing design techniques, with simulation results validating the effectiveness of the approach.

articleTitle: Design and Experimental Investigation of Battery Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Increasing energy demand is promoting the use of batteries in Energy Storage System (ESS). A battery management system (BMS) is used to mitigate the risks associated with over-charging, over-discharging, cell unbalancing and potential hazards in battery energy storage systems (BESS). The BMS is responsible for monitoring, state estimation, cell balancing, diagnostics, and fault detection to ensure the safety and durability of battery packs in stationary energy storage. Lithium-ion batteries are widely used today in a variety of applications due to their high energy density, low self-discharge rate, and relatively low cost. They are still relatively unstable and have a restricted operating range, so careful supervision is required to ensure optimal use. A precise battery model is an inevitable requirement for battery management systems for forecasting battery performance and parameters under a variety of charging and discharging scenarios. Since the lithium-ion batteries are being widely adopted for grid ancillary services, the BMS needs to be incorporated with continuous monitoring of the voltage, current and temperature of individual battery cells connected in series. This paper discusses various BMS topologies, battery modeling, simulation and experimental implementation of a master-slave topology for ensuring the safe operating voltage inside the battery pack.

articleTitle: An Auxiliary Circuit for Improving Torque Per Ampere of Switched Reluctance Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Switched reluctance motors are one of the potential candidate to challenge the popularity of BLDC/PMSM motors in the EV and aerospace applications due to absence of rare earth magnetic elements. One of the major limitation of switched reluctance machines (SRMs) as compared to the BLDC motors is the lower value of torque per ampere (TPA). TPA is lower because positive torque cannot be obtained at all positions of the rotor (θ) around the stator but only for a limited range of values of θ. The challenge is to utilize the torque producing values of θ to the maximum extent. In this paper, a technique to enhance the value of TPA is proposed using an auxiliary converter to maximize the utilization of torque production region in a rotational cycle. The proposed auxiliary converter applies a voltage in series with the main converter voltage to increase the rate of rise and fall of current to effectively utilize the torque producing capability of the machine. This helps to obtain the same torque using low value of current, thereby increasing TPA and reducing the conduction loss. The proposed technique is validated using simulations and is found to increase the motor torque for a particular current reference by 22%. Some of the results are presented here.

articleTitle: Hybrid Model-Based and Heuristic Optimal Parameter Estimation for a PV-Fed DC-DC Converter with Maximum Power Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Precise estimation of photovoltaic (PV) parameters is crucial for extracting the Maximum Power Point (MPP). Heuristic MPP extraction methods suffer from the power oscillations phenomenon, whereas the model-based MPP results in convergence issues due to errors in estimated or measured parameters. In this article, a hybrid model-based and heuristic MPP extraction technique is proposed, where the heuristic approach for MPP extraction compensates for a reduced sensor estimation errors and oscillations in the model-based MPP extraction. The proposed methodology implements an iterative model-based PV parameter estimation to mitigate the above-mentioned drawback. The proposed algorithm estimates the PV equivalent circuit parameters at STC using the iterative technique with an initial guess. It is followed by estimation of irradiance and temperature and updating PV parameters. PV MPP voltage and current extraction is done using model-based iterative Guass-Seidel analysis and a dual-loop boost converter PI control loop. Higher-order polynomial approximation of the transcendental I-V equation is done for plotting PV curves using the estimated values and PV MPP voltage. Heuristric PV curves-based MPP extraction is aided with model-based MPP extraction to compensate for the errors. Simulation-based analysis is carried out for a PV module with a boost MPP converter, and the results for MPP extraction with sensorless estimation is provided for different loading conditions. Further, a prototype of 200 W boost converter is developed and validated for various irradiance and temperature profiles. Simulation and experiment results show the efficacy of the proposed technique for a Boost MPP converter.

articleTitle: Volt/Var Control of Smart Transformer fed Active Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this article, model predictive based centralized control strategy is proposed to manage voltage variations and line congestions in smart transformer (ST) fed distribution networks with electric vehicles (EVs) and photovoltaic (PV) generators. ST is a power electronics-based transformer that exhibits intelligent features in control and communication fields. The proposed control scheme deals in coordinating the fast power electronics interfaced devices, such as EVs, ST and PVs in the low voltage (LV) side to maintain voltages as well as line congestions. The ST provides the voltage control in the LV side by setting the voltage reference at the source of the feeder in a similar manner a conventional transformer with on-load tap changers. Simulations are performed in a 38-bus distribution network to validate the efficacy of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: High-Performance SRM Drive for Household Appliances
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In current scenario, SRM drive fed with a diode bridge rectifier has several demerits as low power factor (PF), high current total harmonic distortion (THD), and high cost. To mitigate these challenges, a high-power quality (PQ) front-end converter is presented in this paper. A modified SEPIC dual output with a totem pole structure is derived for a midpoint converter-based SRM drive for an efficient cost-effective low power solution. Balanced split output voltages are generated and varied by a voltage controller for wide range speed variation of SRM. Additionally, front-end PFC converter is accountable for ensuring grid-side unity power factor along with managing DC link voltage. Moreover, discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) is recommended for energy efficiency and economic viability. A 500 W, SRM drive is simulated at rated and dynamic conditions. DC link voltage is controlled from 100 V to 300 V for varying motor speeds. Simulated results validate converter performance enhanced power quality at grid side with SRM control.

articleTitle: An Optimal Design and Control of Dynamically Re-Configurable DC-DC Converter for Off-Board Charger Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes an optimal design and control of a dynamically re-configurable DC-DC converter with a minimal ripple current content at its output for electric vehicle (EV) off-board charger application. Off-board chargers must support a wide output voltage range i.e. 200–1000 V DC, to meet the charging requirements of various EVs available globally. By exploiting the requirement of a wide output voltage range, this paper proposes an intelligent control algorithm that reduces the filter inductance value to 50% of the one used in a conventional interleaved converter. It maintains the minimum ripple at the output by thoughtfully varying the input voltage by adjusting the converter duty cycle with proper coordination with the current ripple cancellation factor. Reduction in the filter inductance size offers the dual advantage of higher converter power density and reduces the cost of the off-board chargers. In addition, high power efficiency is achieved throughout the range of load variations by properly selecting the optimal number of interleaved phases and dynamically allocating the appropriate interleaved angle between the phases that dynamically manage to cancel the ripple current effectively. The proposed algorithms in this paper are first simulated in MATLAB/Simulink and experimentally verified using the TMS320F28335 DSP-based control hardware on OPAL-RT based Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) system.

articleTitle: Torque Enhancement of BLDC Motor Considering Iron Loss: Modeling and Compensation Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper explores the effects of iron loss on Permanent Magnet Brushless DC motor (BLDCM) performance and compares two of the most popular compensation techniques to improve torque. Iron loss significantly impacts the efficiency and performance of BLDC motors, particularly in high-speed applications. By incorporating iron loss into a detailed motor model, the study aims to accurately predict performance and develop effective compensation strategies. Simulation results validate the comparison of the proposed methods namely Model Predictive Control (MPC) and Field Oriented Control (FOC) based on improvements in torque output. The findings demonstrate the robustness and accuracy of the Model Predictive Control (MPC) system over conventional Field Oriented Control (FOC) under varying load and speed conditions. This research underscores the importance of considering iron losses for optimizing BLDC motor efficiency, especially in electric vehicle applications.

Author Keywords: Iron Loss modeling. Model Predictive Control (MPC)

articleTitle: Soft Switched Common Ground Transformerless Single Phase PV Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Soft-switching techniques are employed in compact photovoltaic transformer-less inverters (TLIs) which operates at high switching frequencies. Inverters which comply to recent technical standards like IEEE1547 needs to have a greater power factor operation range so that it can support the utility grid during sag and swell conditions. However, many of the existing soft-switched TLIs are meant to work at unity power factor only. Some of the recently proposed H-bridge derived TLI topologies which support full power factor (FPF) operation is built with more number of auxiliary switches and this increases the complexity of the inverter. In this paper a zero-voltage transition (ZVT) common ground (CG) transformer-less inverter is proposed where soft-switching is achieved for FPF operation with only four additional auxiliary switches. This scheme ensures zero voltage turn-on and turn-off for the main switches and zero-current turn-on for the auxiliary switches.

articleTitle: A Novel Design of Switched Reluctance Machine Using the Rotor of Synchronous Reluctance Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a new design of Switched Reluctance Machine (SRM) has been proposed, where the rotor of a conventional SRM has been replaced by the rotor of a Synchronous Reluctance Machine (SyRM). The new design is named SRM-SyRM. It has been shown that this machine can function as a SRM. The presence of flux barriers on the SyRM rotor serves the purpose to create the difference in inductance between the aligned and the un-aligned positions for SRM operation. Variation of torque and torque ripple have been studied for changes in number of barriers and rib width of the SyRM rotor.

articleTitle: Optimal DG Placement and Sizing for Multi-Objective Performance Enhancement of Radial Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Optimizing the allocation and sizing of distributed generators (DGs) in distribution networks is a significant challenge. The research aims to address this by using the Slime Mould Algorithm (SMA), a novel population-based optimization technique, to reduce active power losses through strategic DG integration. Additionally, the study presents a multi-objective approach that simultaneously minimizes active power losses (APL), enhances the voltage stability index (VSI), and improves the voltage profile (VP). This comprehensive optimization strategy seeks to holistically enhance the efficiency and reliability of distribution systems by effectively integrating distributed generations. The multi-objective problem is addressed using SMA in conjunction with the fuzzy decision-maker approach and the weighted sum technique. The performance of the applied method is evaluated on a 69-bus system, and the results are compared with those of different evolutionary approaches to demonstrate SMA's computational efficiency, convergence speed, and user-friendliness.

articleTitle: Harmonic Profile of Various Loads Used in Distribution System of Qatar Utility
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive investigation of the harmonic profiles and total harmonic distortion (THD) of individual Qatari household loads, both dominant and non-dominant. The study analyses the harmonic characteristics of major appliances such as refrigerators, air conditioners and televisions. It reveals a significant THD of 65.12%, indicating significant harmonic contributions from these dominant loads. At the same time, a more modest THD of 13.71%, indicating a comparatively cleaner harmonic signature, is shown for non-dominant loads such as LED lamps, washing machines and hairdryers. The paper also looks at the specific harmonic components generated by each load, shedding light on the distinctive nature of their harmonic distortions. Highlighting the collective influence of both dominant and non-dominant loads on overall power quality, the cumulative THD for all domestic loads is measured at 30.36%.

articleTitle: Impedance Distortions Based Interturn Fault Diagnosis in PMSM Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Interturn fault (ITF) is a commonly occurring fault in permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM). The propagation of the ITF could cause damage to the entire electrical machine if it is not detected in time. In this proposed technique, second order harmonic components in dq-reference frame impedance distortions are used for ITF detection in field-oriented controlled PMSM drive. The dq-reference frame impedance distortions are obtained from the voltage distortions and current distortions by using the Luenberger observer, and also by healthy and faulty analytical models of PMSM. These dq-reference frame impedance distortions are transformed to negative-sequence reference frame. Then the magnitude of dc components obtained from negative-sequence dq-reference frame impedance distortions is defined as fault index. Further, the comparison with the dq-reference frame current residuals ITF detection technique shows the superiority of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Design and Development of 10kA 1kV Synchronized Thyristor Based Static Switch for Evaluation of Breaking Performance of Low Voltage Circuit Breakers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The Point On Wave (POW) switching of a Make Switch (MS) is a prime requirement for short-circuit (SC) testing of various electrical equipment. The circuit closing shall occur at voltage zero to establish maximum asymmetry, which decides the dynamic peak current during short-circuit testing. In the case of Circuit Breakers (CB), the SC current will be limited considerably below its prospective value. The breaking capacity tests on Miniature Circuit Breakers(MCBs), as per IEC 60898–1 [1], demand that the MS be fast enough to close at different closing instances of the sinusoid input voltage waveform. Inconsistency in MS operation leads to improper closing angle for the test, thus invalidating the test. Hence, to evaluate the breaking performance of MCBs, a 10kA 1kV synchronized thyristor-based static switch is designed and developed in this research work. This work is the first attempt to develop such a static switch indigenous. This paper also discusses the effect of breaking current characteristics due to the variation of closing angle (initiation at which the SC occurs) through real-time experiments on 240V ac C6A 10kA Single Pole (SP) MCBs. This paper also analytically attempts to analyze the closing angle at which maximum energy occurs for the given fault level, further validating the significance of POW closing. From the overall analysis, this research investigation signifies the positive effects of mechanical force under short-circuit conditions.

articleTitle: Detection of Stator and Rotor Winding Faults by Monitoring Air-Gap Flux Spectrum of Slip-Ring Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In the literature, the detection of winding faults using flux analysis is found more suitable as compared to classical techniques, like current signature analysis. The detection of inter-turn winding faults, by using external stray flux sensor is reported by most of the researchers. The induced emf in the external stray flux sensor is the function of the position of the sensor. Also, the amount of induced emf in millivolts. To overcome these problems, the air-gap flux sensor (AGFS) based technique is recommended. In this technique, the AGFSs are made up of copper coils of few turns. In the stator core, the AGFSs are placed in addition to stator winding (coils). This paper deals with, the detection of inter-turn faults in stator and rotor windings. It also, detect the unbalanced supply voltage in the three phase wound rotor induction motor (WRIM). The asymmetry in the supply voltage and inter-turn faults in stator and rotor windings lead to the variation in the air-gap flux thereby, induced emf in AGFS. By analyzing flux spectrum of induced emf in all AGFSs, the type of abnormality is identified. Also, in case of stator winding fault the exact fault location is identified. The proposed technique is a new technique as, AGFSs are placed internally for the detection of proposed abnormalities in the wound rotor induction motor.

articleTitle: A 25-Level Hybrid Cascaded Multilevel Converter with Capacitor Voltage Balancing Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Multilevel converters (MLC) have attracted significant attention in both industry and research due to their increased power capacity, reduced output harmonics, and minimized commutation losses. However, their adoption is impeded by increased complexity, necessitating a larger number of power devices, passive components, and intricate control circuitry, especially as voltage levels increase. This paper introduces a hybrid 25-level MLC topology with a capacitor voltage balancing scheme. The proposed configuration consists of two power cells per phase, each consisting of six uni-directional, two bidirectional switching devices, and two capacitors. In this study, the switching scheme, capacitor voltage balancing, and selection of switched capacitors are studied. In simulation studies, 25 levels of the proposed configuration are achieved with a total harmonic distortion (THD) of 4.57% in the leg and 2.75% in line voltage waveforms.

articleTitle: A Simple Triple Phase Shift Control to Minimize Inductor RMS Current Maintaining ZVS for Dual Active Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach for triple phase shift control (TPS) of dual active bridge (DAB) converter using frequency domain-based fundamental harmonic analysis (FHA), which is more convenient and straightforward.
