The proposed algorithm features the calculation of optimal control points that offer minimum inductor RMS current while maintaining soft switching at different output power levels. The closed loop control architecture features a PI controller and two look-up tables, offering precise and efficient control. The PI controller controls the external phase shift ratio based on the desired output power level. The look-up tables control the internal phase shift ratios of the twin H-bridges to modify the shape of the AC inductor current. A 3 kW DAB converter with input and output voltage ratings of 280 V and 300 V respectively verifies the proposed TPS control algorithm. The results also verify the effectiveness of the closed loop control strategy for the proposed TPS control. The control scheme is implemented in MATLAB Simulink.

articleTitle: Low-Frequency Common Mode Voltage Mitigation in Si/SiC Based Ten-Switch Neutral-Point Clamped Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Power converter switching actions generate undesirable common-mode voltages (CMVs) and cause premature motor failure in drive applications due to voltage stress on the winding insulation system. The low-frequency CMV also brings challenges in CM inductive filter design for transformer-less solutions in grid integration of renewables. Through parasitic elements, CMV may also produce electromagnetic interference (EMI). This paper proposes methods for eliminating low-frequency CMV in a three-phase ten-switch neutral point clamped converter (TS-NPC). The converter is a low-cost alternative to existing three-level inverters such as NPCs and T-type converters, among others. However, the modulation methods available in the literature for TS-NPCI are not appropriate for reducing low-frequency CMV. The proposed modulation scheme of TS-NPC uses combinations of existing voltage vectors to generate a new set of zero CM voltage vectors (ZCVVs), The output voltage waveforms are produced using these ZCMVs following the voltsec balancing principle. The modulation also does not alter the inherent ability to balance the split capacitors' voltages of TS-NPC. An adequately designed switching sequence will allow for fewer switching events with no direct jump between the top and bottom DC links in the pole voltage waveform. Simulation results and comparisons with existing methods are provided to validate the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Real-Time Experimental Validation for Assessing Efficiency of On-Board Chargers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The effectiveness of the on-board chargers (OBCs) has a significant impact on the powertrain's ability to optimise energy consumption and extend the range of electric vehicles (EVs), This paper focuses on the experimental validation of unidirectional OBC operating in single-phase mode (7.5kW) and three-phase mode (22kW) using a real-time Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) simulator. The proposed OBC architecture includes a front-stage AC-DC converter representing the totem-pole bridgeless power factor correction (PFC) arrangement, and a rear-stage isolated DC-DC converter providing zero-voltage switching (ZVS) capability reducing the ripples in the DC bus voltage. The novelty of the paper involves the system design with the experimental validation of the proposed architecture using the dSPACE as HIL simulator. The plant model is developed based on the test system with a real-time executable code embedded into the simulator. In the real-time simulator, the pertinent variables are defined for assessing the OBC efficiency for both single-phase and three-phase system. The OBC efficiency is estimated in the test system using MATLAB/Simulink based on the system design parameters. The efficacy of the test system is substantiated in the real-time simulator, dSPACE SCALEXIO. The approach for evaluating the OBC efficiency with the use of real-time simulators helps in accomplishing higher efficiency without restricting the output voltage range, making it widely applicable in the automotive industry.

articleTitle: Control Strategies for 3L-T-Type Inverter in Islanded and Grid-Tied Modes Using Controller-Hardware in the Loop
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents the closed-loop control of a three-level T-type (3L-TNPC) inverter in both islanded and gridtied modes, with a focus on optimizing control strategies using a digital signal processor (DSP) microcontroller in conjunction with controller-hardware in the loop (C-HIL) through space vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM). The study leverages C-HIL to validate control algorithms in a realistic environment. It progresses to a comprehensive simulation phase in MATLAB/Simulink, utilizing proportional-integral (PI) control mechanisms to regulate the converter's operations. Furthermore, a 67 kVA power-rated inverter is evaluated through a C-HIL experimental setup in Typhoon HIL, an advanced real-time simulation platform. The performance of these methodologies is validated across various load types, both linear and nonlinear. The model is also tested in grid-tied mode, delivering 67 kVA of power to the grid at unity power factor (UPF). Additionally, total harmonic distortion (THD) is observed for both modes.

articleTitle: A Non-isolated Step-up DC-DC Converter Based on Modified Quadratic Boost and Cuk Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel non-isolated high-gain DC-DC converter engineered for optimal efficiency. This converter boasts a remarkably simple structure and employs a minimal number of components. Its standout characteristic is its wide duty ratio range, which significantly enhances adaptability to suit the diverse requirements of renewable energy sources (RES) and electric vehicle (EV) applications. The proposed converter integrates the quadratic boost and modified Cuk converter designs to obtain enhanced gain and performance. Additionally, this converter offers the advantage of utilizing just one switch, leading to simplified circuitry and reduced complexity. Furthermore, the voltage stress across the switch is maintained at a low level, contributing to improved reliability and reduced cost. A brief analysis and simulation results are presented to validate the efficacy of the proposed converter.

Author Keywords: Modified Quadratic Boost and Cuk (MQBC) Converter

articleTitle: A Fault Tolerant Multilevel Inverter for Preserved Rated Power Output During Post-Fault
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper introduces a fault-tolerant converter by incorporating a resistor switch circuit (RSC) into a T-type multilevel inverter (MLI). The proposed converter offers fault tolerance while maintaining rated power when subjected to various switch faults on single and multiple phases. Additionally, it includes a feature for capacitor voltage balancing during the post-fault period. The fault tolerance ability and operation of the proposed converter are validated using MATLAB SIMULINK, and corresponding simulation results are presented for healthy operation, fault scenarios, and post-fault duration, which are discussed in detail. Leveraging its robust fault tolerance capability with preserved rated power, the proposed converter shows promise for use in remote and emergency load applications.

articleTitle: Design of Input and Output Filter Capacitors of a DC-DC Dual Active Bridge Converter with Time-domain Analysis of Voltage Ripple
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Ahstract-A dual active bridge (DAB) converter is widely used in isolated DC-to-DC topology due to its attractive features, such as bidirectional power flow capability and the ability to attain soft-switching transitions over a wide range. The design of input and output differential-mode filter capacitors is critical for high power-density and low-cost applications. Peak-to-peak allowable voltage ripple and the ripple current RMS flowing through the capacitor are two important factors that determine the value and size of the capacitors. Conventionally, the peak-to-peak voltage ripple is analyzed in the frequency domain after considering the total ripple current RMS is concentrated in one frequency, leading to the over-design of the capacitors. This article analyses the voltage ripple of one of the operating modes of the DAB converter in the time domain after considering the actual ripple current waveforms in the input and output DC rails. It also provides analytical closed-from expressions of the capacitance value and the RMS current for given specifications of input and output voltages, power, and allowable voltage ripples. The theoretical design is validated through simulation and experiments performed on hardware at 425 V input, 40 V and 55 A at the output, and switching frequency of 250 kHz.

articleTitle: Dynamic Surface Sliding Mode Control Scheme for Load Frequency Control of Multi-Area Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This work introduces a dynamic surface sliding mode control technique for load frequency control (LFC) in interconnected power systems which is capable of handling both parametric and matched disturbances. The design involves a first-order low pass filter to the virtual control stage to eliminate the “explosion of terms” present in the backstepping and other SMC techniques. LFC under two cases (matched and unmatched disturbances) are considered to illustrate the superior performance of the proposed DSMC and the required asymptotic stability condition is proven based on the Lyapunov stability criteria.

articleTitle: A Novel Hybrid Virtual Synchronous Control Strategy for Enhanced Grid Resilience in Renewable Energy Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A dominant rise in renewable energy (RE) mix into the power grid instigated prominent challenges in grid synchronization and power system stability. Inertia inherited rotational machines play a vital role in grid resilience, which is becoming deficient due to the advent of converter-based sources (CBS) into the grid. Hence, robust converter control strategies are to be implemented to take over the challenges of grid synchronization (GS) and stability. Unlike the conventional phase locked loops (PLL) for GS which intrude on severe disturbances during transients and have slower recovery, the proposed novel hybrid virtual synchronous control (HVSC) incorporates the synthetic torque parameters to the synchronous generator features emphasising an optimal stable system during both transient and steady states, delivering a stable frequency response for seamless grid synchronization. Furthermore, the performance and robustness of the proposed HVSC method are examined by implementing it on the grid-connected voltage source converter (GSC).

articleTitle: Small Signal Modeling of LLC Converter based on Time Domain Analysis and Equivalent Circuit Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Resonant converters, notably LLC resonant converters, are gaining popularity and are being used in various applications due to their inherent soft-switching ability. In existing literature, various modeling methods have been derived based on the extended describing function, which uses the first harmonic approximation. This first harmonic approximation-based small-signal model provides accurate results in terms of gain and phase when operating at the resonant frequency. However, operating away from the resonant frequency yields inaccurate results, particularly in gain. This paper presents an accurate small-signal model derived from time-domain analysis for gain determination and circuit reduction techniques for pole location determination. The accuracy of the proposed analytical model has been confirmed through validation using MATLAB/Simulink and experimental verification.

articleTitle: ITAE Index Based Control Design Strategy to Mitigate Frequency Deviation of Renewable Integrated Islanded-Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This work addresses the frequency stability issue of microgrids and eliminates frequency errors by incorporating a proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller. PID controller mitigates frequency error by deriving controller gains with the help of integral time absolute error (ITAE) index as a key design criterion. To validate controller efficacy, various analyses are conducted. The results indicate that ITAE assisted-PID controller achieves good settling time, rise time, and requires minimum controller magnitude. The ITAE-PID controller provides a better frequency response of considered microgrid model.

articleTitle: Optimized Design of the CUK Power Converter Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, the CUK converter topology has been designed by optimal parameters, operating characteristics and control strategy for performance improvements to become a competent charge controller unit for rechargeable batteries. An ample assessment with the high switching frequency CUK regulator has been simulated by the software platform to be commercial success. So, optimized design of CUK converter is the best option when it is assessed by other converter circuits

articleTitle: Grid Forming Control of Delta-H Bridge Module Under Unbalanced Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Static synchronous compensators (STATCOMs) are essential in power systems for improving power quality by providing voltage regulation, reactive power support, harmonic reduction, and flicker mitigation. Two widely used topologies for STATCOMs are the star H-bridge module (S-HBM) and the delta H-bridge module (D-HBM). The S-HBM usually requires a higher DC bus voltage due to the need for zero-sequence voltage injection, while the D-HBM operates without this requirement, making it a more voltage-efficient alternative. However, the D-HBM commonly uses a phase-locked loop (PLL) for grid angle detection, which is sensitive to grid disturbances and can degrade system performance. To address these limitations, this paper introduces a grid-forming (GFM) control strategy for the D-HBM. GFM control enhances the system's ability to balance capacitor voltages, maintain dynamic stability, and deliver fast response times. A detailed analysis of these challenges is provided, demonstrating the improved performance of GFM-controlled D-HBM under various operating conditions. Experimental results highlight the robustness of the proposed GFM method, showing stable operation in both balanced and unbalanced grid scenarios. These findings confirm the GFM-based D-HBM as a reliable and efficient solution for STATCOM applications in real-world power systems.

articleTitle: Review and Comparison of Modulation Schemes for Inductive Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) technology eliminates physical connectors and cords, providing electric vehicle (EV) owners with a safe and user-friendly charging experience. Despite the apparent simplicity of the circuit, an inductive power transfer (IPT)-based EV charging system imposes high requirements on the control system, including modulation schemes, which can be implemented in many ways. To illustrate this and recommend further research, this paper will provide a comprehensive review and evaluation of the most popular distinct modulation techniques employed in IPT systems. The investigation is based on a 3.3 kW IPT configuration to evaluate the comparison between these modulation schemes. Finally, the merits and demerits of each modulation scheme are discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Coded Power Transfer for Power Electronic Converter System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Information exchange between the load side and the source side allows the power electronic system to adjust its operation to match the load requirements dynamically. This paper presents a mechanism for the transfer of power and data between the load and the source sides of the power electronic system. The system utilizes the coded information in the switching signals adopting coded power transfer. The data to be transmitted is converted into a binary fixed point number and is superimposed on the switched voltage to transfer the information. The coded power transfer is implemented on a buck converter system. The conversion of data from the analog domain to the digital domain and vice versa is explored. The simulation results are obtained from MATLAB/Simulink software and Hardware-in-loop validating the sequential transmission of data and power.

articleTitle: A Four Switch SiC Solid State Relay with Inrush Current Protection for High Voltage and High Power Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a new four-switch configuration for a solid-state relay (SSR) with an inrush current limiting feature for high-voltage and high-power converters. A solid-state relay is a non-mechanical circuit breaker with no moving parts. It is used to disconnect a power electronic converter from its source in case of any faults or during normal shutdown. Conventionally, a solid state relay is made up of two back-to-back connected semiconductor switches like MOSFETs for bidirectional control of power. The new proposed arrangement of four N-channel MOSFETs, along with a resistor for a solid state relay, provides a 25% reduction in conduction losses compared to the conventional two MOSFET arrangement. It also charges the capacitor bank of the converter during startup with a limited peak inrush current value without any additional pre-charge circuit. Thus a converter using the proposed arrangement for a solid-state relay would be more reliable, compact, cost-effective, and efficient when compared with a conventional setup using a two MOSFET solid-state relay and a separate pre-charging circuit. A thermal model of a 1200V SiC MOSFET from Infineon was created in PLECS software, and compared with the conventional arrangement of the MOSFETs for the solid-state relay. An 800V 35KVA three-phase voltage source inverter was used to compare their performance and losses.

articleTitle: Approximation of Higher Order Fuel Cell System Employing Error Minimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this presented research work, the higher order (HO) hydrogen fuel cell (FC) system is approximated to lower order (LO) model. The oxygen excess factor (OEF) is one of the important criterion which maintains the flow of oxygen in FC stack, specifically in case of proton exchange membrane (PEM) type FCs. Similarly, FC output is also dependent on developed FC stack voltage. The OEF and stack voltage, need efficient controller for FC operation. The presented research proposal provides the approximated order FC model for eighth order FC system. The approximation is done with the help of minimization of errors between time moments and Markov parameters of HO FC system and its desired second order FC model. The optimized coefficients of unknown second order FC model is obtained by employing jaya optimization (JO) algorithm by ensuring the stability and zero steady state error conditions for better FC model. In the support of proposed FC model, comparative analysis of responses and tabular data are also done against the models ascertained using other approximation approaches.

articleTitle: On the Development of an FCS-MPC Based Power Amplifier for Power-Hardware-in-the-Loop Tests
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Power Hardware-in-the-Loop (PHIL) has emerged as a highly effective tool for testing and validation of hardware before being deployed in the field. Since full-fledged hardware testing may not be possible in a lab environment, PHIL provides a balance between cost and fidelity in testing and therefore plays an important role in renewable energy integration. The power amplifier is one of the main components which facilitates these PHIL tests. Thus, it becomes necessary to develop a robust, dynamic and efficient power amplifier. This work proposes a finite control set model predictive control based power amplifier. The proposed approach demonstrates high dynamic response in addition to high tracking efficiency. The proposed approach is able to emulate voltage sags, swells, distortions and frequency deviations. The efficacy of the proposed approach is validated through exhaustive time-domain simulations in MATLAB/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode Current Control in Multiple Batteries Based DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This article presents a variable structure model for a DC microgrid system, comprising photovoltaic (PV) and multiple batteries connected to a DC bus. It includes a brief overview of Sliding Mode Control (SMC), covering the existence condition, hitting condition, and switching law for the system under study. The article also discusses a comprehensive control scheme, featuring an outer voltage PI controller and a reference current generation module that distributes the current demand among the batteries based on their state of charge. SMC is used for inner current control. The performance of the SMC is compared with that of a PI controller for inner current loop. Simulations are conducted in MATLAB/Simulink under varying irradiance and load conditions.

articleTitle: Determining Power Loss of Motor Controller at Different Torque and Speed for Electric 2-Wheeler Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: With the given specifications, for optimum design and selection of devices, accuracy in power loss analysis is required. The power loss analysis becomes more reliable and closer to experimental results after considering all types of power loss, converter operation and device parameters. The accuracy can be increased by using the data given in the datasheet and updating it for the required operating conditions and taking load impedance into consideration. With the updations mentioned, an analysis is made with BLDC motor load with different speed and torque conditions for designing an inverter and then tested in lab with dynamometer. The results are promising for the MOSFET parameters updations and the circuit operation with load.

articleTitle: Performance Characteristics Assessment of Dual Rotor Single Stator Five-Phase Surface-Inset PMSG for Hydroelectric Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper investigates the characteristics of the Dual Rotor Single Stator Five-Phase Surface-Inset Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (DRSSFPSI-PMSG) for hydroelectric systems. The dual rotor configuration includes two-sets of eight magnetic poles, while the single stator features two-sets of balanced five-phase windings. This distinctive rotor- stator design and the multi-phase system enhance power density and reliability of the generator. For design and performance assessment, both magnetostatic and transient analyses are employed. Key parameters such as generated voltage, voltage versus speed, output voltage versus current load, and efficiency versus load current are thoroughly analysed for the DRSSFPSI-PMSG. The comprehensive evaluation indicates that the proposed generator exhibits robustness, reliability, and significantly higher efficiency. These advantages make the generator particularly well-suited for hydroelectric applications.

articleTitle: An Improved Maximum Power Point Tracking of PV Source Using Parametric Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Traditional MPPT methods often rely perturbations based on fixed algorithms to track varying characteristics of Photovoltaic (PV) modules due to climatic conditions, which generate significant ripple in PV voltage and current. Proposed parametric esstimation allows for real time adjustment of control parameters based on the actual operating conditions of the PV Module. The work presents on the extraction and formulation of unknown parameters of PV Module with help of known parameters (irradiance, temperature, open circuit voltage, short circuit current) to create a Single diode PV Model. The identified unknown parameters are then utilized within an MPPT control algorithm to dynamically adjust the operating point of the PV module. The unknown parameters are solved using iterative method and Voltage reference for PI controller to operate at maximum power point at different irradiance, temperature computed, which is given as the reference to a PI controller. Proposed methodology contributes better results, which was tested in simulation environment. Further, a data driven model is also developed for PV Module using regression-based AI technique and compared with proposed method.

articleTitle: Enhancing Ancillary Grid Services with Integrated PV System under Unbalanced Load and Weak Grid Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The paper introduces a grid-connected ancillary photovoltaic (PV) system that supplies power to the grid and a nonlinear load. It employs a Third Order Generalized Integrator Quadrature Signal Generator (TOGI-QSG) control for a D-STATCOM type Voltage Source Converter (VSC). In comparison with conventional control algorithms, it ensure symmetrically balanced grid currents, unity power factor correction, and harmonic mitigation, even under conditions such as unbalanced nonlinear loads, fluctuations in solar irradiation, and disturbances in grid voltage. The Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm, based on Perturb and Observe (P&O), is utilized to maximize power extraction from the solar photovoltaic array. The real-time performance of the system is evaluated using the Opal-RT OP4510 simulator across diverse operational scenarios, including load imbalances, sudden changes in solar irradiance. The work adheres strictly to revised harmonic control standards such as IEEE std. 519 and IEC std. 62109.

articleTitle: Sustainable Maritime Transportation Through Modular Wireless Shore-to-Ship Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The maritime transportation sector, heavily reliant on fossil fuels, significantly contributes to global greenhouse gas emissions, posing environmental and health risks. According to the International Maritime Organization, approximately 90% of global trade is carried by marine transportation, necessitating the electrification of ships and shore-to-ship charging infrastructure. While existing literature emphasizes conductive charging for shore-to-ship charging, wireless charging aspects are often overlooked. This paper provides a holistic review of wireless charging modalities, covering power converters, compensation mechanisms, and couplers. The study examines the practical implementation of wireless charging for maritime vessels, utilizing a case study of a 1 MW charging system for the Motored Ferry (MF) Ampere to promote sustainability in maritime transport.

articleTitle: A Seven Level Symmetrical Reduced Switch MLI for Grid-Tied Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Multilevel inverter (MLI) is attaining popularity for medium and high power application for renewable energy (RE) based grid connected system. The article presents a new seven level reduced switch MLI with grid tied application. The inverter uses nine unidirectional switches with less total standing voltage and cost function. SPWM is used to produce gate signal to trigger the switches. The proposed topology is represented for symmetrical mode of operation. DC sources are used in place of RES for simulation. The proposed inverter is also performed for grid-tied system. The performance of the proposed inverter is analyzed in MATT.AB/Simulink

articleTitle: Digital Evaluation of Li-Ion Cells: Impact of concentration Based Diffusivity on P2D Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Every EV manufacturer is focused on using an energy storage system which provides exceptional energy density, long cycle life and weighs as low as possible. With an increase in the research and development of different battery materials, there is a plethora of battery chemistries which can quickly adapt to the fast-moving world of electric mobility. While the EV industry or more importantly the battery industry is still booming, a lot of focus is shifted towards understanding the internal phenomenon of a cell which governs its working. The equivalent circuit models simplify the representation of an electrochemical system by using resistors, capacitors, inductors and other electrical components, however electrochemical models such as the pseudo-2-dimensional model enables us to understand the internal phenomenon that govern the performance of the cell. This work highlights the importance of incorporating concentration dependent diffusivity in P2D models and compares the impact of concentration dependent and concentration independent diffusivity models on terminal voltage at higher Crates.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Single-Phase Five-Level Transformerless Solar PV Grid-Connected Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In recent years, the development of alternative, sustainable, and pollution-free renewable energy sources such as solar has increased on account of a significant reduction in the cost of solar photovoltaic (PV) panels. The adoption of transformerless solar PV inverters has become increasingly important because of their high power density, efficiency, cost-effectiveness, and small size. However, the formation of parasitic capacitance between the PV array and the ground provides a closed path for leakage current to flow, leading to the degradation of the panel's life and several electromagnetic interference (EMI) issues. Several three-level solar PV inverters have been developed to overcome this problem, however the output power quality has been compromised. This study conducts an extensive review and comparison analysis of a few promising five-level transformerless solar PV inverters. Simulations for 2.5 kW PV inverter systems are carried out in MATLAB and PLECS environments. The performance of each inverter topology, including the leakage currents, voltage and current harmonic contents, common mode voltage (CMV), and semiconductor power losses, are thoroughly evaluated. The study also highlights the merits and shortcomings of inverter topologies.

articleTitle: A Simplified Primary Side Control Strategy for Resonant Inductive Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative primary side indirect control strategy for the Resonant Inductive Power Transfer (RIPT) system, which eliminates the need for secondary side communication and additional weight, leveraging mathematical relationships to control the primary side inverter. The proposed method ensures efficient CC-CV charging of Li-ion and LiPo batteries while simplifying the system architecture. The controller design is validated through both simulation and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) testing, demonstrating robust performance in regulating battery voltage and current under varying conditions. This innovative approach offers a scalable solution for enhancing UA V autonomy and can be adapted for broader RIPT applications.

articleTitle: Inductor Current Feed-Forward Based Single-Loop DQ Control Scheme for Standalone Inverter System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: With the influx of nonlinear loads into the power system, there is a need to mitigate the effects of harmonic current drawn by the loads under standalone inverter systems. Filters are ineffective in mitigating lower-order harmonics. Hence, improve-ments in control schemes have to be implemented to improve the voltage quality. In this paper, an Inductor Current Feed-forward (ICF) based single-loop dq (SLdq) control scheme is proposed to suppress the effects of the harmonics. The proposed controller is developed through dq frame modelling and is compared with the existing SLdq control scheme. It is shown through simulations and hardware experimentation that the ICF-based SLdq control scheme is superior to the SLdq control.

articleTitle: Dual Configured SEIG-Based WES Using Modified SVM Technique for Three Level Back to Back Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of a Selfexcited induction generator (SEIG) based wind energy systems (WES)-fed three-level back-to-back frequency converter (3LBBFC) and two-level back-to-back frequency converter (2LBBFC). The indirect vector control (IVC) technique with modified space vector modulation technique (MSVMT) is proposed to control load-side connected frequency converter (LSCFC) and the IVC technique with sinusoidal pulse width modulation (SPWM) technique is used to control machine-side connected frequency converter (MSCFC). IVC with MSCFC is used to control torque ripples, active power, and reactive power of the generator, and IVC with MSVMT is used to control DClink voltage, active power, and reactive power of the load or grid. Proposed techniques are implemented in Matlab/simpower system and real-time simulator (RTS) environments respectively.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Impact of Holes on the Performance of Multilayer Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Multilayer interior permanent magnet synchronous machines (IPMSMs) are preferred options for high-speed operations among the different configurations of IPMSMs. Different flux barriers in multilayer IPMSMs can also help in changing the shape of the air-gap flux, which can enhance the performance of the motor by reducing core losses or by reducing torque ripple. While reducing core losses improves efficiency, torque ripple reduction enhances the health of the shaft and bearing by reducing noise and vibration. Different methods to minimize torque ripple exist in literature (e.g., skewing, changing the magnet orientation and shape). This work deals with the impact of the location and size of holes on the performance of multilayer IPMSM. Holes on the rotor and stator core bear the potential of altering the shape of air-gap flux and, therefore, creating an impact on the performance. Therefore, different possible combinations of holes placed on the stator and rotor have been considered in this work. Simulation studies have been conducted using FE Simulation software, and the results have been reported.

Author Keywords: Multilayer interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (ML-IPMSM)

articleTitle: Recovering Below LVD Li-ion Batteries for BMS Based Rechargeable Electrical Appliances
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (Li-ion) stand as the foremost choice for energy storage in today's industry. Commonly, the south Asian countries import those Li-ion batteries from abroad and store those in warehouse for manufacturing rechargeable electronics devices. In our industry, Li-ion batteries ranging from 4.2V HVD to 2.8V LVD are commonly used. Storing Li-ion batteries for a long time reduces the voltage of the battery below LVD rendering the integrated recharging circuit ineffective, as the battery management system rejects below LVD batteries. To address this issue, a charging method is proposed in this paper incorporating TP4056 IC to facilitate forced charging, accompanied by comprehensive protection measures such as overcharge, over-discharge, and overcurrent protection. Results indicate that these batteries can be efficiently recharged within a 240-minute forced charging cycle, providing backup for more than 180 minutes, again can be recharged using device incorporated charging circuit in charging second cycle and still demonstrate a healthy backup time in discharging second cycle. Additionally, the paper examines the temperature profile during both charging and discharging processes.

articleTitle: Common-Mode Voltage Mitigation in 3-Phase 3-Level VSI with Dc-bus Midpoint Switching
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Common Mode voltage (CMV) is the prime source of EMI issues in 3-phase electric drives. Different approaches to reduce the CMV are reported in the literature. In this paper a simple and effective switching scheme for 3-phase, 3-level inverters is proposed to mitigate the CMV. In the proposed method, a new topology for 3-level inverters with multiple DC bus capacitors is presented and the proposed switching scheme results in zero CMV with suitable switching of DC bus mid-point for each switching state. Available methods in literature for CMV reduction use modified PWM switching schemes [3], [4], which are suffering from poor THD of voltage waveform. Proposed switching scheme leads to zero CMV without compromising with the quality of the voltage waveform.

articleTitle: Hexverter Based Medium Voltage Fast-Charger with Medium Frequency Isolation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Fast-charging infrastructure is required for smooth transition from fossil fuel-based mobility to electric mobility where the power rating of the charger can be as high as few hundred kW. This work proposes a medium voltage medium frequency isolated Fast-charging architecture to cater to the need of high-power density charging station in congested cities. The architecture interfaces the medium voltage AC distribution grid and the charger outlet through a Hexverter and active rectifier with medium frequency transformer in-between. The suitability of the converter architecture and its energy management strategy is verified through simulation in MATLAB/Simulink platform for a 50 KW, 400V rated charging outlet.

articleTitle: Adaptive Proportional Integral Regulator for the PV-Shunt Active Power Filter Under Stochastic Solar PV System Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper investigates the problems of regulating a 2-stage photovoltaic (PV)-based Shunt Active Power Filter (SAPF) under distortion grid supply and stochastic PV system behavior. This paper proposes to solve this problem by using a new adaptive proportional integral (API) regulator for DC-link voltage regulation, with adjustable API parameters based on the error voltage at the DClink side, to achieve high and low bandwidth depending on the appetite for disturbance rejection or dynamic performance improvement. The proposed API's accuracy is evaluated using time and frequency domain analysis. The performance of the PV-SAPF system under various grid situations utilizing the suggested control algorithms is then proven using simulation and real-time hardware. The suggested API regulator shown encouraging results in terms of improving system performance under internal/external disturbances when PV-SAPF is used, and the overall harmonic distortion of the grid current is sianificantly within IEEE Std 519–2014 limits.

articleTitle: Fault Signal Formulation for Fault Analysis in DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: With increasing demand of electricity and depleting non-renewable resources, the rising demand of energy is fulfilled by renewable energy sources (RES). Microgrids in power system integrate various RES, convectional grid and various type of loads. This leads to the progressing interests of scholars towards DC Microgrids (DCMG). Power system control, energy management, fault analysis, power quality and reliability are major area of concern in DCMG as these are extremely significant in power distribution sector. Study on various methods for Fault Diagnosis are being carried out by identifying different type of Fault Signatures. This paper focuses on extracting harmonics from inductor voltage during faults at various locations within the DCMG system and identifying the fault type and location based on the harmonic signatures.

articleTitle: Enhancing System Performance with Wind Farm Using Fuzzy Logic Coordination between AVR and PSS Controllers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Given the pervasive deployment of Doubly-fed Induction Generator (DFIG) in power grids, ensuring optimal operation during faults is crucial, particularly addressing transient stability. This study focuses on enhancing the system's stability by integrating DFIG-based wind farms and coordinating Automatic Voltage Regulators (AVR) and Power System Stabilizers (PSS) of synchronous generators via fuzzy logic. The fuzzy coordinator mitigates detrimental AVR-PSS interactions, optimising their gains for fault conditions. This coordination improves active power flow, reduces DFIG reactive power demands, and mitigates the deviation of system parameters. It is established based on the IEEE-9 bus system to validate the approach, showcasing superior performance compared to individual methods. The results underscore the robustness and reliability of FLC coordination, ensuring enhanced system stability.

Author Keywords: Automatic Voltage Regulators (AVR) and Power System Stabilizers (PSS)

articleTitle: Unified Active Disturbance Rejection Control Strategies for Time-Varying Disturbances: Case Study on a DC-DC Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: For time varying disturbances, it is reported that cascade extended state observer (CESO) as well as generalized proportional integral observer (GPIO) based active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) strategies yield satisfactory disturbance rejection whereas a linear extended state observer (LESO) fails to do so. Furthermore, including poles of the desired dynamics into the nominal model results in a simple and easy-to-implement reduced order observer. Also, manual tuning of ADRC parameters fails to provide optimal closed-loop system response. Motivated by the above facts, unified structures of CESO (UCESO) and GPIO (UGPIO) are proposed in this work and convergence analysis of the closed-loop system is presented based on the above mentioned control strategies using Lyapunov stability criteria. Additionally, particle swarm optimization (PSO) based optimal control strategies in the framework of above said ADRC schemes are also presented. Case study performed on a DC-DC boost converter illustrates superior disturbance attenuation, regulatory performance and reference tracking of the proposed control strategies.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis of Quasi Z Source Resonant Converter at Fixed Frequency Phase Shift Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A single-stage conversion topology called a quasi-z source resonant converter (QZSRC) was designed for dual port charging to overcome multistage power conversion in the conventional multiport resonant converter. Using varied magnetizing inductance ratios, the suggested QZSRC work analyzes power sharing and efficiency for even and uneven voltage levels. The proposed converter can charge two batteries at a fixed frequency with a conventional PWM. However, the overall efficiency is affected by conventional PWM. This employed fixed frequency phase shift modulation (FFPSPWM) to the quasi z source resonant converter-based dual port charger to solve this problem. The proposed converter steady state analysis has been discussed, and experimentally testing a 400 W laboratory prototype on both chargers yielded a 91.8% efficiency.

articleTitle: Performance Study of a Three-Phase SEIG Feeding Single-Phase Non-Linear Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The single-phase operation of a three-phase self-excited induction generator (SEIG) is an atypical way of generating single-phase power for remote off-grid areas in small scale, from renewable resources like: wind and hydro. The current paper focuses on the performance study on a hydro-driven 2.2 kW three-phase SEIG, that supplies single-phase non-linear resistive (R) loads. The single-phase operation of the generator is performed using a newly developed capacitor-based scheme. The result indicates that, at a fixed speed (1500 rpm) of the generator, the capacitor scheme can maintain the generator voltage and current balanced, supplying the single-phase non-linear loads. Further, it is observed that with the increasing non-linear load impedance, the generator voltage remains almost constant, while the stator current after decreasing almost tends to be constant. Finally, the SEIG voltage and current total harmonic distortion (THD) due to supply of non-linear loads, are observed which are found to be exceeding IEEE std. 519–2014.

articleTitle: Transformer Current Stress Minimization Using Voltage Matching Control in a Solar PV Fed Grid Tied Dual Active Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Dual active bridge is a popular DC/DC converter topology for solar PV microinverter applications due to its high frequency isolation. However, they suffer from high transformer current stress when the voltages on the primary and secondary of the transformer are mismatched, and this lowers the efficiency. Current stress can be reduced if the amplitude of the voltage at the transformer primary and secondary windings are matched. Control techniques that reduce current stress under changing operating conditions generally involve complex calculations and require accurate values of system parameters. In this paper, a control scheme for a current fed dual active bridge (CF-DAB) converter injecting power into a single-phase grid is proposed where the voltages at the two ends of the transformer are matched to reduce the current stress. The aim here is to reduce the current stress under varying operating conditions while performing MPPT of the solar PV source without requiring complex calculations and accurate knowledge of system parameters. The CF-DAB is followed by a DC/AC inverter regulating the DC link voltage, which is the amplitude of transformer secondary voltage. The primary voltage is matched with the reflected secondary voltage through phase shift control. The input PV source is operated with MPPT. The transformer primary voltage is independent of the PV voltage, which achieves voltage balancing under different conditions of MPPT voltage, depending upon irradiation and temperature. The proposed scheme is validated using simulation in PLECS and those results are presented.

articleTitle: Active Gate Driving Technique for the Voltage Balancing of Series Connected GaN Devices for Higher Voltage Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: GaN switches have better power density and lower switching/conduction loss than SiC switches. However, their acceptability is restricted due to their lower blocking voltage capability (maximum 650 V). Connecting two devices in series is the simplest solution to this problem. However, there is an issue of unequal voltage distribution even in well-matched switches, which leads to non-optimal utilization of the devices or, even worse, device failure. This voltage unbalance may either be due to gate pulse propagation delay or due to the presence of non-uniform parasitic capacitors across switches. This paper proposes an active gate driving method to balance voltages across two series-connected GaN switches with minimal voltage overshoot even in the presence of moderate loop inductances, parasitic gate capacitances, and gate pulse propagation delay. The simulation model for the proposed method has been developed and verified using LTspice incorporating commercially available GaN device GS66508T for a 900V DC link for two series-connected switches. To verify the technique's operability for other GaN devices too, a simulation was also conducted for two series connected EPC2304 for a DC link of 300 V. Voltage balance with minimal overshoot was obtained for both cases.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Novel Multi-Functional Onboard Battery Charger for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents the design and analysis of a dual-stage onboard electric vehicle charger utilizing an interleaved totem pole AC-DC converter at the front end and a synchronous buck-boost DC-DC converter at the back end. The proposed onboard charger supports two operational modes. One is grid-connected mode (GCM), where the main battery inside the EV is charged from a single-phase AC supply. There is also a possibility of feeding power back to the grid from the main battery in the deregulated environment. The second is the driving mode (DM) when disconnected from the grid, where the main battery supplies power to the auxiliary battery and other auxiliary loads rated at 12/24V within the EV without requiring an additional DC-DC converter. This is achieved through the optimal utilization of components in the charger, ensuring maximum power factor and minimal harmonic distortion in the input current during the grid-connected mode, aided by independent control loops. This paper provides a comprehensive operational overview and presents simulation studies of a 10-kW onboard charger in grid-connected mode and a 2-kW charger in driving mode.

articleTitle: A Novel Reconfigurable Inductive Power Transfer System with Pulse Density Modulation for Constant Current and Constant Voltage Charging Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Owing to the dependence on coil characteristics, loading profile, and operating frequency in inductive power transfer (IPT) systems, it is difficult to design a charger that provides the electric vehicle (EV) battery with the required constant current (CC) or constant voltage (CV) efficiently over a pre-defined charging profile. Furthermore, existing IPT systems that use CC-CV charging cause power loss due to hard switching or require additional reactive power due to variable frequency control. Recently, automotive manufacturers have moved to 800 V battery pack architectures due to significant EV weight reduction and shorter charging time. To address these concerns, this paper introduces a novel reconfigurable IPT system that charges 400 V and 800 V battery packs with enhanced efficiency and a smooth CC-CV charging profile. It only uses three coils and two relays that can be switched to series series-series (SS-S) topology for CC output and inductor-capacitor-inductor-series (LCL-S) compensation for CV output with relay 1 and a reconfigurable system to charge the 400 V and 800 V battery packs with configuration of relay 2. Additionally, pulse density modulation (PDM) is adopted for this topology to increase IPT's efficiency by achieving the soft switching capability over a wide voltage range. Simulation studies are carried out on a designed 3.3 kW IPT charging system under CC and CV charging profiles at 400 V and 800 V to verify the feasibility of the proposed reconfigurable topology with the PDM method.

articleTitle: Enhancing Efficiency in Dual-Motor Four-Wheel Drive Electric Vehicles via Power Sharing Optimisation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Energy efficiency is the critical parameter for extending the driving range of electric vehicles (EVs). This paper introduces a novel dual-motor differential 4-wheel drive (D4WD) system based on OEWIM. The study focuses on optimizing the torque distribution to minimize the drive system power loss. The proposed D4WD drive and direct torque control strategies were validated through simulations using the FTP-75 driving cycle. The results demonstrate that the optimized torque distribution model significantly enhances energy efficiency, contributing to improved vehicle performance and extended driving range. This research provides a comprehensive approach to achieving high efficiency in D4WD EVs through effective torque management.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of State-Observer Algorithms for Mitigation of False Data Injection Attacks on Automatic Generation Control System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents the performance comparison between Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) and Particle Filter (PF) to maintain the data integrity of a Three-Area Thermal Automatic Generation Control (AGC) system against False Data Injection Attack (FDIA). Simulation study shows that both the state-observer algorithms provide a good estimate of the AGC system states in the presence of FDIA. However, the EKF outperforms PF in terms of reduced computational burden and response time which is crucial to ensure the security of the AGC system data against FDIA.

articleTitle: Bayesian Inference Framework for Probabilistic Power Flow Analysis for Microgrid Uncertainty Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The intermittence of renewable sources of energy and uncertainty in power system calls for the development of algorithms which can include uncertainty. In the probabilistic power flow (PRPF) analysis methods, injected powers have been considered uncertain, however there is also uncertainty associated with state variables. To take into consideration that uncertainty, Bayesian inference have been proposed for the microgrid. This involves specifying the prior and likelihood to find out posterior using Bayesian inference. Hamiltonian Monte-carlo (HMC) has been used as likelihood based Bayesian simulator. The method has been simulated using R-Stan for a 6 bus microgrid system.

articleTitle: Modelling of Cross-Saturation in a PMa-SyRM Using Emperical Polynomial Reduction Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The impact of cross-saturation effects on the performance of a permanent magnet assisted synchronous reluctance motor (PMa-SyRM) is investigated in this paper. Usually finite element (FE) analysis is used to model the effects of non-linearity due to core saturation. However, FE analysis is very time consuming, especially when modelling SyRMs due to a large number of FE meshes and nodes at the rotor ribs. Therefore, a MATLAB-based model incorporating the effects of non-linearity is presented in this paper. The model takes into account the cross-saturation effects using a polynomial reduction method. Further, from the simulations, the non-linear inductance variation due to the cross-coupling and saturation effects are presented. It is found that there is a reduction of 34.6 % rated torque in the proposed MATLAB-based model considering the cross-saturation effect.

articleTitle: Maximum Torque per Ampere Control of Interior PMSM and BLDC Motor Using Co-Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of the control performances of interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) and surface-mounted brushless dc (SM BLDC) motor drives using co-simulation. The 2-D finite element (FE) model of both the motors are modelled using the Simcenter MagNet software, and the control strategies are implemented using MATLAB/Simulink. A field-oriented control (FOC) with the maximum torque per ampere (MTPA) technique for an interior PMSM and a simple hysteresis current control for a BLDC motor are implemented using co-simulations. An interface block from MagNet software is used to link the motor models with the drive control scheme developed in MATLAB/Simulink. It is claimed that, for the co-simulations a complex look-up table for calculations of inductance considering the non-linearities of the material is not required. Further, the results obtained from co-simulations of both motors are compared and presented. From the simulations, it is concluded that, though time-consuming, the accuracy of the co-simulations is higher compared to a complete motor and drive model developed in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Simplified Average Model of Voltage Source Inverter for Controller Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The paper introduces a simplified average model of Voltage Source Inverters (VSI), suitable for practical analysis in circuit simulators. By circumventing the mathematical complexities of traditional small signal analysis, this model enables rapid frequency sweep analysis, streamlining stability assessment and controller design. A detailed derivation of a current controller using the proposed average model is presented, with simulations demonstrating robust performance under various disturbances. Experimental validation on a real hardware setup further corroborates the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The results underscore the practical viability of the derived controller in tracking reference current amidst changes in circuit parameters, thus contributing to the advancement of current control methods for single-phase inverters. This paper offers valuable insights for engineers working in power electronics, particularly in the domain of renewable energy systems.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Correlation Between Axial Force and Movement of a Rotor Magnet in a Four-Layered Stack Structured Permanent Magnet Bearing Using the Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The study focuses on the design and performance evaluation of a passive magnetic bearing system for horizontal rotation, utilizing repulsive magnetic technology. This involves designing and analyzing the performance of the permanent magnet (PM) bearing system intended to rotate on a horizontal axis. The proposed PM bearing is based on passive magnetic technology, and its performance is evaluated by using both analytical solution and finite element analysis. The results indicate that the maximum force is experienced by the rotor magnet at specific axial movements, with minimal force at the origin position. The force varies with radial movement and stack height, with greater stack heights resulting in increased force. The polynomial equations provide a mathematical model for predicting axial force based upon axial movement, aiding in control and understanding of nonlinear dynamics. Understanding these relationships is crucial for designing flexible and optimized bearings.

articleTitle: Design of Compact Si-IGBT Module Based Power Converter Fed Vector Controlled IM Drives for EV Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The global concern over pollution and greenhouse gas emissions has accelerated the electrification of vehicles, including automobiles, locomotives, and aircraft. EVs, powered by electric motors and reliable electricity sources, offer several advantages over traditional internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles. These benefits include reduced air pollution, zero tailpipe emissions, and lower operating costs due to cheaper electricity. EVs find applications in low-power (E-rickshaws, E-bikes, E-scooters) and high-power (E-cars, E-buses) vehicles. Designing compact power converters for EVs is essential. These converters serve as traction inverters, controlling motor speed and torque. Challenges include managing switching losses, optimizing thermal models, and reducing heat sink size. Integrating multiple circuits and utilizing integrated power modules (IPMs) contribute to compactness. Therefore, the objective is to present the design and development procedure for a three-phase two-level converter integrated with diode rectifiers, choppers, and controlled AC-DC converters. Additional components include voltage sensors, current sensors, gate drivers, microcontrollers, and auxiliary power supplies. The presented configuration is simulated in MATLAB/SIMULINK environment and then the simulation result is validated from experimental results.

articleTitle: Detection of Wind Turbine Induced Forced Oscillations using Periodogram and DEF Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive method for forced oscillation (FO) source identification on wind turbine system (WTS) integrated 4-generator 11-bus power system. Identifying FOs, especially those originating from wind turbines, is essential due to their potential to introduce variability and instability into the power grid. These periodic disturbances can arise from WTS due to various reasons, including aerodynamic forces, mechanical imbalances within the turbines, and control system malfunctions. The proposed methodology utilizes the periodogram method to evaluate the FO frequency. PMU data is then filtered based on this estimated frequency. To accurately pinpoint the location of the FO sources, the Dissipating Energy Flow (DEF) technique is subsequently applied to the filtered signal. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is rigorously evaluated through multiple scenarios, demonstrating that the DEF technique can precisely and reliably identify the origin of FOs, even when they are generated by wind turbine systems (WTS).

articleTitle: Optimized Dual Phase Shift Control for Dual Active Bridge DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The Dual Active Bridge (DAB) converter is widely recognized for its applicability in high-power applications, offering features such as high-power density, inherent soft switching, modularity, galvanic isolation, bi-directional power flow, and high-frequency operation. Typically, the DAB converter is controlled using the traditional Single-Phase Shift (SPS) method. However, this control method can lead to a peak inductor current when there is a voltage disparity across the inductor, negatively impacting the performance of the converter. To address this issue, an optimized Dual Phase Shift (DPS) control technique has been introduced. This optimized DPS control not only minimizes the peak inductor current required to achieve the desired power but also reduces the RMS current flowing through the magnetic components, thereby enhancing the overall performance of the converter.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Intelligent Power Module based Power Electronics Learning Kit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A configurable power electronic learning kit based on the intelligent power module (IPM) has been presented which can be used for understanding the working of multiple power electronic circuits. The kit developed is capable of operating in four different modes, namely buck, boost, single-phase inverter and three-phase inverter mode. Each of these modes is operated in closed loop using digitally implemented proportional and integral (PI) controller. In this paper, the design of the kit and the hardware results corresponding to all the modes has been presented. The kit also has the facility to upgrade individual boards and reconfigure software program as per the user's requirement. This kit is intended for people from all aspects of academia and industry for their prototype testing.

articleTitle: Dual LUT-Based DTC Strategy for Optimized Energy Efficiency in Electric Vehicles Powertrains
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a refined Direct Torque Control (DTC) strategy for Open-end Winding Induction Motors (OEWIMs). The scheme combats torque ripple and flux demagnetizing with dual Look-Up Tables and a novel five-level hysteresis torque controller. It strategically employs zero voltage vectors for enhanced torque performance at high speeds. The result has lower Total Harmonic Distortion (THD), reduced switching frequency, and better efficiency while maintaining the core advantages of traditional DTC. Comprehensive experimental findings demonstrate the usefulness of the proposed DTC technique.

articleTitle: Dynamic Power Sharing Between Charging Guns in Off-Board Chargers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Automobile manufacturers are adopting different charging standards for their electric vehicles (EVs), which vary geographically. Hence, off-board chargers/wayside DC fast chargers must be equipped with multiple charging guns to cater to various requirements of EVs that pertain to particular geographical areas. Recently, most EVs have been equipped with large-capacity batteries to cover more distance on a single charge. The charging infrastructure needs to be upgraded to charge these high-capacity EVs in a shorter time, which calls for a huge investment. This paper proposes a dynamic power-sharing algorithm for off-board chargers to reduce charging time by effectively utilizing the existing charging infrastructure. Without any interruption in the EV charging process, the power rating of the off-board charger can be re-configured according to the charging requirements and the availability status of the other charging gun. The proposed algorithm is experimentally verified and tested on an indigenously developed 122kW fast charger.

articleTitle: Learning-Platform for Mixed Domain Control of Power Electronics Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Mixed (analog and digital) domain control is preferred for fast transient response of high frequency power converters. A matching signal processing and conversion circuitry along with digital communication is required for this purpose. A student of power electronics needs to understand the intricacies of such complex provisions in context of modern power electronics equipment and control. A mixed domain control platform is developed for the ease of learning modern control schemes for high frequency power electronic converters. In this platform, a combined FPGA-DSP (Field programmable gate array - Digital signal processor) based controller is used along with an interface PCB (printed circuit board). The interface PCB comprises of the circuits for signal conditioning, serial/parallel analog to digital and digital to analog converters (ADCs and DACs), Pulse width modulation (PWM) gating signal and protection etc. This paper presents the control platform design requirements, hardware details, module based learning methodology, and the preliminary results of control scheme implementation.

articleTitle: Precision Power Amplifier with Enhanced Current Capacity for Characterization of Magnetic Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Direct-coupled multistage linear power amplifiers serve as a low cost power source to provide DC-biased alternating excitations for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex>-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex> characterization of magnetic materials. The voltage and current capacity of amplifier should be adequate to produce the desired value of B and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex> in the test sample. The current capacity of such amplifiers is often limited due to temperature rise of the current-carrying device in the output stage, rather than the rated current of transistor. This work presents the design of the output current gain stage of a precision power amplifier having multiple current-carrying transistors in parallel. The required number of transistors in parallel is evaluated using thermal circuit analysis to safely achieve a peak inductive current of 10 A with a bias rail voltage of 75-0-75 V. The design of the base drive stage for paralleled current-carrying transistors is performed. The designed amplifier is fabricated and tested with inductive load to ensure a safe temperature rise. The capabilities in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex>-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex> characterization are demonstrated through tests on a 0.35 mm thick Si-Fe steel at multiple frequencies ranging from 10 Hz to 5 kHz.

articleTitle: Diode Assisted High Gain DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel diode-assisted high-gain DC-DC converter for electric vehicles, microgrids, and household applications. It efficiently utilizes power from energy storage systems to meet varying demands. Initially designed for DC-DC conversion and further it was extended for hybrid applications. The converter efficiently boosts input DC voltage to high output voltage with a small duty ratio, featuring low input ripple current. Its switched capacitor topology is optimized for diverse applications like uninterrupted power supply, energy storage, and battery charging. Focused on reducing power losses and enhancing power density, it ensures high efficiency crucial for electric vehicles/microgrids. Theoretical analysis clarifies operational principles; experimental validation confirms voltage boost across loads, minimizing power losses.

articleTitle: Development of FPGA-based Interface Card for Power Electronic Converter Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Multilevel topologies, back-to-back converter systems, solid-state transformers, etc., require many analogue signals for their control. To implement digital control in these systems, a custom interface circuit for digital processors needs to be developed. This paper presents a systematic design and development of an interface card for the digital control of such power elec-tronic converters. The proposed design consists of two daughter cards (signal conditioning card and analogue-to-digital converter (ADC) card) connected to Zedboard development board. An ADC driver is developed and discussed as a state machine. A total of 40 analogue signal intakes is provided, along with 40 general-purpose input/output (GPIO) pins and communication features like serial peripheral interface (SPI), campus area network (CAN), and universal asynchronous receiver/transmitter (UART). The ADC card printed circuit board (PCB) is simulated in Ansys SIwave for direct current internal resistance (DCIR) analysis. The signal conditioning circuit is analysed with a frequency response that considers the circuit parasitic. Lastly, hardware results are showcased, verifying the proposed solution.

articleTitle: The Use of Power Factor Optimisation to Improve Harmonic Performance of Matrix Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Matrix Converter (MC) is a compact and power efficient alternative to the traditional two-step AC/DC/AC conversion. MC typically provides closed-loop control of the output current and unity power factor at the input side. When supplied from a distorted voltage source, it is desirable that MC does not transfer harmonics to the load and does not contribute to the harmonic distortion at the input. However, it has been found that the MC harmonic mitigation and power factor correction are contradictory objectives. This paper presents a detailed study of the dependence of the MC harmonic performance on the input power factor. It optimises the power factor with the view of harmonic minimisation. Simulation results presented in this paper demonstrate the effect of the proposed optimisation. Experimental validation is underway.

articleTitle: Mitigating Subsynchronous Resonance in DFIG-Based Wind Farms Using a Robust Terminal Sliding Mode Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a robust terminal sliding mode controller (TSMC) is proposed for doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG)-based wind farms to mitigate subsynchronous resonance (SSR) induced by series-compensated transmission lines. Here, the controller governs the rotor-side converter (RSC) of a DFIG, utilizing a new exponential reaching law that is specifically designed for damping the SSR. The controller's robustness against external disturbances is thoroughly evaluated by incorporating them within the dynamic model of the RSC, while considering the impacts of series compensations. The stability of the entire DFIG-based wind farm, including the series compensator, is rigorously analyzed using the Lyapunov stability theory. The performance assessment of the proposed approach in mitigating the SSR is conducted, and results are presented, along with comparisons against a fractional-order SMC (FOSMC).

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of an Asymmetrical 21-Level Multilevel Inverter with Reduced Switch Count
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposed an asymmetrical 21-level multi-level inverter comprising eight switches and three different rating voltage sources having a ratio of 1:2:7. The three voltage sources are used in different additive and subtractive manners to produce 21 output voltage levels. The level-shifted multi-carrier PWM technique generates gate pulses for the inverter. The theoretical analysis of the inverter is verified using MATLAB/Simulink software. The inverter is simulated under different load and modulation indices under steady-state and dynamic conditions. The inverter produces 5.68 % total harmonic distortion in the output voltage.

articleTitle: Binary Search-Based Adaptive P&O MPPT Algorithm for TLBC-Based Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: With the drive to safeguard the environment for future generations, there is a need to incorporate Renewable Energy Sources(RES) into the electrical power grids. Among the prominent RES, the solar photovoltaic (PV) system is of utmost importance for the Indian subcontinent. One drawback of the PV system is the intermittent nature of the PV energy source. In order to extract the maximum available power from the PV system, maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithms have to be implemented that are fast and can track the maximum power point (MPP). Conventional MPPT algorithms suffer from a jittering effect near the MPP, whereas newer methods are faster but require complex implementation procedures and reset algorithms to work. This paper aims to present a new binary search-based adaptive Preturb and Observe (BSAPO) MPPT algorithm that has a faster convergence speed compared to conventional schemes and minimum jitter near the MPP. The developed algorithm is tested and compared with the conventional Perturb and Observe algorithm experimentally on a Three-Level Boost Converter (TLBC)-based PV system.

articleTitle: Design and Testing of Coordinated Controller for PV Assisted Municipal Solid Waste Fueled EV Charging Station
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a PV assisted, energy-efficient electric vehicle charging station (EVCS) powered by hybrid energy sources in a grid-connected mode. The EVCS facility is equipped with a bi-directional AC/DC converter for interfacing with the distribution grid, a dual active bridge (DAB) converter for EV charging, and a multi-phase interleaved boost converter for rooftop solar panels. An energy recovery technique is used for municipal solid waste energy conversion plants coupled with a turbine genset to supply power as a main source to the EVCS which reduces the grid power dependency for EV charging. The syn gas-operated turbine coupled with a salient pole wound field synchronous generator controlled through a converter-fed to extract generated power.
