A coordinated controller is implemented considering power generation, and intermittency of photovoltaic (PV) to maintain the power availability at the charging facility and also to limit the charging power requirement from the grid. The test cases are developed to evaluate the EVCS effectiveness and performance of the proposed control algorithm in a common DC bus. EVs of different battery capacities with different states of charge are modeled in MATLAB/Simulink 2023b.

articleTitle: A Novel Six-Switch Isolated DC-DC Converter with an Isolated Port Providing DC Transformer Gain and Two Non-Isolated Ports Serving Reciprocal Non-Inverting Buck-Boost Voltage Gain for EV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel isolated DC-DC converter with six switches comprising one isolated port subscribing to pure DC transformer action and two non-isolated ports with reciprocal non-inverting buck-boost operation. The Continuous Conduction Mode (CCM) voltage gain at the isolated output port is reliant only on the secondary-to-primary turns ratio <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> of the High-Frequency Transformer (HFT) and not on the per unit duty cycle of the converter, hence providing a pure DC transformer action. The two non-isolated output ports are complimentary to each other and provide buck-boost characteristics with CCM voltage gain at the ports as mathematically inverse in magnitude to each other. Detailed steady-state CCM analyses are portrayed and MATLAB® SIMULINK simulation waveforms are presented. Closed-loop current controller is designed and its efficacy is tested using step changes in load.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analyses of Single-Phase Grid-Tied Bidirectional Electric Vehicle Charger
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This work proposed a dual control technique that uses predictive power control (PPC) on the rectifier side and new predictive duty cycle control (PDCC) on the dual active bridge (DAB) side to improve grid power quality (PQ) and charge electric vehicles (EVs), respectively. Additionally, it features an EV charger that supports bidirectional power flow. The proposed bidirectional electric car charger works in grid-to-vehicle (G2V) and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) modes. In G2V mode, also known as charging mode, the vehicle's battery receives electricity from the utility grid. In V2G mode, also known as discharging mode, the battery delivers power back to the grid. The proposed bidirectional EV charger (BEVC) exhibits a rapid dynamic response attributed to the efficient management of the battery current. Regulating the transformer winding current peak value is essential for maintaining symmetry. Furthermore, a voltage estimation scheme is integrated into the PPC algorithm, enabling sensorless operation for grid voltage. This regulation of the current minimizes the DC bias present in the transformer current. The BEVC is designed and simulated for a peak power of 0.5kW. Simulated results from MATLAB are presented for the G2V and V2G modes of operation of a 48V, 80 Ah battery.

articleTitle: The Study of Opttimizing Profit for Solar-Energy Integrated Battery Swapping Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In response to growing environmental concerns, the widespread adoption of Electric Vehicles (EVs) is imperative, particularly given the transportation sector's significant reliance on fossil fuels. However, successful integration of EVs necessitates an efficient charging and swapping infrastructure to mitigate long charging times and alleviate range anxiety. Battery swapping stations offer a solution akin to traditional gasoline refilling stations by enabling the swift exchange of depleted batteries for charged ones. Beyond customer convenience, this infrastructure also benefits the power system by bolstering grid stability during peak load conditions through battery-to-grid (B2G) functionality. Moreover, batteries can be charged during off-peak periods through grid-to-battery (G2B) mode, leveraging Day-ahead pricing and incorporating solar energy to optimize operations. To address these complexities, we present an optimization model designed to schedule battery charging and discharging based on Day-ahead market prices, integrating considerations such as solar energy availability, battery degradation costs, and customer incentives. This model aims to maximize profits for Battery Swapping Stations (BSS), enhance grid stability, and ensure customer satisfaction. The model is verified in Matlab using Gurobi solver in Yalmip optimizer.

articleTitle: Robust Sliding Mode Observer Based Speed Sensorless Control of FPIM for Wide Range of Speed Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In sensorless speed control, the conventional speed estimation techniques often encounter challenges such as chattering and convergence issues, especially at low speeds, leading to potential performance degradation or instability. In contrast, sliding mode observers can significantly enhances the system reliability under harsh operating conditions. The present paper introduces a Continuous Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Observer (CFT-SMO) based speed estimation technique for five-phase induction motor (FPIM) drive. An adaptive gain mechanism is included to offer rapid convergence and robust speed tracking across a broad operating speed range, ensuring stability and precise tracking even at very low speeds. The proposed CFT-SMO is incorporated with Indirect Field Oriented Control (IFOC) scheme to leverage the observer's capabilities to the fullest under extreme system dynamics. The stability of the observer is rigorously validated through Lyapunov stability theory. The performance of the combination of IFOC with the proposed observer is evaluated in MATLAB/SIMULINK. It ensures optimal performance and reliability of the control system under varying operating conditions. A hardware prototype is developed in laboratory and typical hardware result is presented.

articleTitle: An Optimized Hexagonal Geometry Magnetic Coupler for Floor-Mounted Electric Vehicles Wireless Charging System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Electric Vehicles (EVs) are rapidly gaining popularity as a sustainable mode of transportation. Wireless charging technology is a convenient and efficient way to recharge EVs, and the design of the charging pad plays a crucial role in the efficiency of the charging process. A novel implementation of a Double LCC compensated wireless power transfer (WPT) system with hexagonal coils can provide stable and reliable output under various operational conditions, including load variations and misalignments, for wireless charging systems. The proposed WPT system employs a Double LCC configuration with hexagonal coils to maintain a stable output current despite misalignments and load variations. The stability of the output is achieved by carefully designing the system parameters, particularly the denominator parameter a, which is the sum of two factors aA and aB that exhibit opposite trends under misalignment conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that the system can maintain a stable 13.5A output current with minimal fluctuations when the load varies between 5.2Ω-4.8Ω and the misalignment ranges up to ±120mm in the Y-axis and 60-100mm in the Z-axis. The proposed system with hexagonal coils is more straightforward, easier to implement, and does not require complex control algorithms or additional communication modules.

articleTitle: Reduced Order Modeling of Higher Order Fuel Cell System for Electric Vehicle Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This study proposes the reduction of an eighth-order fuel cell system (FCS) using truncation reduction method (TRM) and Routh approximation method (RAM) for electric vehicle (EV) applications. The eighth-order EV's FCS is approximated into its comparatively lowered order approximated order (AO) models. The AO numerators of desired fuel cell models (FCMs) are derived by truncating the numerator coefficients of the eighth-order FCS using TRM. Additionally, RAM is employed to determine the AO FCMs' denominators of FCS. The effectiveness of derived FCMs is evaluated through qualitative and quantitative analyses. Qualitative analysis involves plotting step response, impulse response, Bode diagram with magnitude and phase plots, and pole-zero map. Quantitative analysis presents time-domain specifications (TDSs) and error indices (EIs) in tabular form to assess the performance of proposed FCMs.

articleTitle: Seamless Dispatchable Grid Integration of an FPPT-Controlled PV System with Limited Local Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: With the proliferation of the photovoltaic (PV) power generation, dispatchability of the PV system is highly desirable to maintain the grid security. There is a requirement of the large local energy storage for the dispatchable grid connection of a maximum power point tracking controlled PV array. In contrast, no such local energy storage is, in principle, required in the case the maximum power point tracking is replaced with flexible power point tracking. However, since there may always be a power tracking error on the PV side because of the duty ratio quantization problem, it is not advisable to fully exclude the local energy storage so as to prevent the above power tracking error from propagating to the AC side. Instead, a low capacity local energy storage system may be used with an appropriate mechanism for its state-of-charge control. In the earlier control coordination methods for the above system configuration, the voltage-source converter was used to control the DC-link voltage, leading to unnecessary oscillations in the AC-side power output. In order to avoid the particular problem, the possibility of the DC-link voltage control by means a battery converter with very limited local energy storage is investigated in the present paper.

articleTitle: A Simple and Accurate Analytical Approach for Calculation of Air-Gap Flux Density in PMSM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Permanent magnet (PM) synchronous motors (PMSMs) are being used to drive a number of electric vehicles be it mid-motor or hub-motor. They have high torque density, high efficiency, and a wide speed range. This paper presents a simple, fast and accurate analytical technique for calculating the PM characteristics such as flux density, demagnetizing force, PM energy product and motor characteristics like the air-gap flux density, back-emf, and torque-constant of arc-magnet PMSM. The PM characteristics are represented by a lumped magnetic equivalent circuit when the thickness and width of the PM are increased for the same volume. In this paper, PM characteristics and motor characteristics of Surface-mounted PMSM(SPMSM), Inset PMSM, Interior-magnet PMSM(IPMSM) and Outer-rotor PMSM(Hub Motor) are analytically calculated by the proposed method and then, are compared by finite element analysis(FEA).

articleTitle: A Fault-Tolerant Multilevel Inverter Topology Configured with Three Sources with Improved Performance in Post-Fault Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel topology for fault-tolerant multilevel inverters featuring three sources with improved performance in post-fault conditions. The conventional three-source topology has a total of eight switches, and anyone switch's failure severely impacts output voltage and harmonics. A fault analysis has been carried out for the conventional three-source topology, which has led to the development of a novel fault-tolerant MLI. For the proposed fault-tolerant topology, the number of levels and output voltage improve in the post-fault conditions for different modes of operation. For the proposed topology, a detailed fault analysis, along with the power quality assessment that has been carried out for open-circuit faults to every switch, has been provided in this paper. Finally, the simulation results have been provided to validate the proposed topology.

articleTitle: Torque Ripple Reduction in Delta Connected FPIM Under Double Phase Fault With EV as Load
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The main objective of this research article is to present a model comprising of electric vehicle propelled by five phase induction motor (FPIM). Electric vehicles are garnering attention as a dependable alternative in transportation applications because of their environmental-friendly nature. Multi phase machines have become potential contenders because of their advantages over three phase counterparts. The stator of five phase induction motor has three possible configurations, namely, star, pentagon and pentagram. The connections pentagon and pentagram are termed as delta connected windings. A mathematical model of a double phase fault is proposed employing back-EMF approach. A customized drive cycle representing Indian road driving conditions is used as reference signal for closed loop operation of FPIM. As the fault occurs, the currents become unbalanced and distorted due to the presence of third harmonic components, which further result into surge in torque ripple. A suitable compensation strategy is applied to produce a balanced rotating magneto-motive force (MMF) which successfully mitigates the torque ripple. The simulation results presented for FPIM operating under a double phase fault in MATLAB/Simulink environment validate the mathematical model developed.

articleTitle: A Bridge-Structured Switched-Capacitor Voltage Equalizer for Li-Ion Battery Strings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A bridge-structured switched-capacitor (SC) equalizer (BSSCE) is proposed to increase the balancing speed and to improve the efficiency at different cell voltage distributions. The proposed BSSCE can transfer energy simultaneously among cells with more optimal balancing paths by using minimum components, which allows the equalizer to achieve improved balancing speed, efficiency, size, and cost. Also, the topology minimizes the effective resistance at slow and fast switching limits, which allows the equalizer to draw high currents to enhance the balancing speed. A simulation model for four series-connected battery cells with different switching frequencies is set up to validate the feasibility of the proposed equalizer. Simulation results and effective resistance analysis show that the proposed BSSCE can achieve any cell-to-cell equalization automatically concerning different switching frequencies. The proposed equalizer can achieve high balancing speed and efficiency.

articleTitle: Power Electronic Implementation of Adjustable Finite Bandwidth Constant Power Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Power electronic loads are increasingly being adopted in various applications. Tightly regulated load converters act as constant power loads (CPLs) in a multi-converter cascaded system. The dynamics of a closed-loop controlled load converter make it behave as a finite bandwidth CPL. So, the availability of such a CPL is beneficial to evaluate the performance of a source converter in the laboratory. However, a provision for user-programmable bandwidth is typically unavailable in commercial CPLs. In this paper, a CPL with adjustable bandwidth is developed based on a synchronous buck converter (SBC). Closed-loop control implementation on an FPGA platform is explained using timing diagrams that are critical for its implementation. Practical considerations for number format selection for digital controller implementation are highlighted. Analytical estimations of settling times under step-change in power levels are validated using experimental measurements. The significance of an anti-windup scheme during closed-loop control implementation is shown experimentally.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis of EV Charging System on Grid with and without Solar PV Integrated System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This research article investigates the impact of Electric Vehicle (EV) charging systems on the traditional three-phase power grid, comparing scenarios with and without the integration of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems. In the present condition, the exponential rise in EV usage has significantly increased load demand, leading to imbalances in the distribution system. The presented article discusses the different impacts of EV charging systems which affect the grid stability, energy demand, and peak load periods. Additionally, it explores the potential advantages of integrating solar PV systems to mitigate these impacts, enhancing grid resilience, and promoting sustainability. This research article also discusses the comparative analysis of impacts in both conditions and the simulation results show the analysis of each impact in different conditions. Further, the MATLAB/Simulink environment is used to model and analyze the different impacts of EV charging station on the three-phase traditional power grid. By integrating grid and solar PV, the article aims to offer a thorough understanding of how solar PV systems can be leveraged to support the growing adoption of EVs, ensuring a stable and sustainable power grid.

articleTitle: Sinusoidal Amplitude Integrator-based Harmonic Extraction for Active Harmonic Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The substantial increase in demand has also posed a threat to utilities due to nonlinear loads. A recent example is the cluster of EV charging stations with a front-stage rectifier unit followed by passive LC filtering to generate the DC link. These practices lead to power quality issues in the grid because of the nonlinear current extraction. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an Active Harmonic Filter (AHF) incorporating a Sinusoidal Amplitude Integrator (SAI) for harmonic extraction. AHF injects the high-harmonic current components into the Point of Common Coupling (PCC). Thus, the source current is drawn to be of acceptable quality. Traditionally, in synchronous reference frame control techniques, harmonic currents in the grid current are extracted through a low-pass filter. Unbalances in the voltages can lead to synchronization issues and potentially slow down the detection of harmonic currents. Fast and precise harmonic detection can be achieved using SAl-based harmonic detection. The instantaneous power theory-based Phase-Locked Loop (PLL) is implemented to achieve seamless and reliable synchronization. Simulations and experiments are carried out to verify the proposed control.

articleTitle: A Novel Hybrid Harmonic Estimation Technique Based on Recursive Least Square and Artificial Protozoa Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Harmonic estimation in renewable energy integrated power systems is crucial for ensuring power quality and system reliability. This paper presents a novel hybrid harmonic estimation technique that combines the Recursive Least Squares (RLS) method with an Artificial Protozoa Optimizer (APO). The proposed method leverages the adaptive filtering capabilities of RLS and the robust optimization properties of APO to accurately estimate harmonic components under varying operating conditions. The APO mimics the foraging behaviour and adaptive movement of protozoa, enhancing the convergence speed and estimation accuracy of the hybrid technique. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in dealing with the non-linarites and uncertainties inherent in renewable energy sources, outperforming traditional estimation methods. The hybrid approach shows significant improvements in terms of accuracy, convergence time, and robustness, making it a promising solution for real-time harmonic monitoring in modern power systems.

articleTitle: Pre-Processing Measurement Data for Computing Internal DC Resistance with Anomaly Detection Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A significant concern in using electric vehicles (EVs) is the range variability, despite vehicles being from the same manufacturers and driven under similar conditions. This vari-ance often stems from cell-to-cell impedance variation within the battery pack. Since the impedance is a very small value ranging in milliohm (mΩ), the measurement requires precise signal generation and measurement, followed by data post-processing to ensure accurate outcomes. The focus of this paper is to propose the use of anomaly detection techniques in preprocessing the raw data to ensure reliable results are obtained when using the data. In this study, three anomaly detection methods were examined and their precision and limitations in preprocessing measured data were assessed. Based on the evaluation and conclusions drawn, the best method among these three was chosen for anomaly detection during preprocessing. Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) is employed on the healthy data of the internal DC resistances to explore patterns in the variation with respect to manufacturers.

articleTitle: Optimized Super Twisting Sliding Mode Based Direct Torque Control for BLDC Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This work explores a refined Direct Torque Control (DTC) using super twisting sliding mode (STSM) controllers to drive BLDC motors under various operating conditions. The proposed control model includes the regulation of dc-link current to achieve precise speed and torque responses despite changes in the power supply. The effectiveness of the suggested methodology is assessed along with established techniques. Additionally, the design of the STSM controller is incorporated, and a PSO methodology is developed to update its parameters. Implementation of the proposed methodology is carried out using OPAL-RT modules to demonstrate diverse outcomes of the hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) process.

articleTitle: Three-Phase Decomposition-Based PWM for CMV Elimination in Dual Inverter-Fed Six-Phase Motor Drive Supplied from Single DC Source
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A three-phase decomposition-based pulse width modulation (PWM) scheme with bus-clamping for a dual inverter-fed symmetric six-phase motor drive is proposed in this paper. The proposed PWM scheme facilitates elimination of common mode voltage (CMV), a major issue in the inverters operated at high switching frequencies in applications such as propulsion motor in electric aircrafts. This scheme also nullifies the resultant CMV generated across the two three-phase stator winding sets on an average basis, enabling a single battery to supply all the inverters in the system without resulting in circulating currents through the motor windings. Furthermore, the proposed scheme significantly enhances the stator voltage for a given battery voltage compared to a single VSI-fed six-phase drive. The proposed scheme is validated by performing simulations under different operating conditions.

articleTitle: Soft Switching Range Extension of Bidirectional DC-DC Converter for Applications Demanding Wide Voltage Gain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Bidirectional DC-DC converters have an important role in low-carbon technologies during power flow control and energy management. The galvanic isolation in these converters also help in meeting the necessary safety standards. However, they fail to achieve soft-switching conditions during varying voltage gain operations resulting in higher switching losses and reduced efficiency, necessitating higher thermal management. This paper considers the operation of a dual active bridge (DAB) DC-DC Converter during varying input voltage. A method is proposed to achieve soft switching conditions in an extended range with wide voltage gain. A conventional DAB and the proposed one were simulated in MATLAB/Simulink and the soft switching conditions were verified.

articleTitle: A VUF Constrained Neutral Current Reduction Strategy for 4-Leg Grid Forming Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The landscape of power distribution networks is undergoing a significant transformation with the increasing penetration of distributed energy generators (DGs). These DGs include single phase solar and wind based generator. While this integration offers environmental and economic benefits, it also introduces challenges related to unbalanced load conditions. The inherent unbalance in distribution networks is further exacerbated by integration of single phase inverters, leading to excessive neutral currents. These high neutral currents pose significant challenges, including overloading of distribution feeders and transformers, common mode noise, flat-topping of voltage waveforms, and potential wiring failures. To address this critical issue, three-phase four-leg (3P4L) grid-forming inverters (GFMs) offer a promising solution. The fourth leg in these inverters can be employed to actively regulate the neutral current while maintaining grid codes. This paper delves into the control strategy for a 3P4L GFMs and proposes a novel neutral current reduction (NCR) control algorithm. The proposed control strategy demonstrates a significant reduction in neutral current, achieving up to 34% decrease compared to a scenario without any reduction mechanism. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is further validated through simulations conducted on a benchmarked low voltage CIGRE test network and in scenarios with multiple DGs supplying power. These results showcase the adaptability and flexibility of the proposed control approach in practical grid configurations.

articleTitle: Ultra High Gain DC- DC Converter With Reduced Voltage Stress for DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: DC microgrids gained popularity due to integrating renewable energy (RE) sources like solar photovoltaic (PV) cells and fuel cells. The lower output voltage of these renewable sources requires a reliable, highly efficient, high-gain DC boost converter to connect them with DC microgrids. A three-switch configured non-isolated high-efficient DC-DC converter is proposed in this paper to achieve ultra-high voltage gain at a lower duty ratio with less voltage stress on the switching devices. The operating principle, derived equation, switch stress, and diode stress are analyzed in continuous conduction mode (CCM). The efficiency, switch stress, and diode stress are presented. To validate the proposed converter topology, a 460 W converter with a 40V input and 600V output, running at a 40 KHz switching frequency is simulated in MATLAB. The simulation result demonstrated that the converter maintains an efficiency at full load.

Author Keywords: Voltage Stress on switches and diodes

articleTitle: Smart Utility Interface for Solar PV Fed Vector Controlled Induction Motor Drive for Water Pump Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a smart utility-interfaced solar photovoltaic (PV) system designed to power a pump load through a vector-controlled induction motor drive. Unlike conventional systems, this design addresses challenges posed by fluctuating solar irradiation by enabling dynamic management of surplus and deficit power. This is achieved through the innovative use of a bidirectional active power flow mechanism, enabled by a single-phase, voltage source converter linked to the DC bus. The front-end active converter (FEAC) topology used in this system, allows active power exchange between utility and DC link but also ensures optimal system performance under varying irradiation conditions. This guarantees that the pump system consistently operates at the best possible operating point. Furthermore, as induction motor is operated in vector controlled mode, the system dynamics gets enhanced. The proposed system is mathematically modeled, designed and simulated in a discrete-time frame in MATLAB environment using simulink and sim power system toolboxes. The simulation results affirm effectiveness of the control strategy designed for the system, demonstrating robustness and practical viability in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Loss Comparison of GaN, SiC, and IGBT Based Inverters for Low Voltage High Current Two-Wheeler EV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Currently, most of the EV technology either uses Si or SiC devices. With GaN becoming cheaper and more readily available, there is a need to explore the possibility of using GaN-based devices in EVs, especially two-wheelers, because of their low voltage and high current demand. This paper presents a comparative loss analysis (switching loss, conduction loss, and total loss) of various GaN (EPC 2302, EPC 2304 & GS61008), SiC (C3M0025065K), and Si IGBT (IKW50N60H3) based 2-level and 3-level (ANPC and T-Type) inverters fed motor load of 10kW, 120VL-L, 60A load. The loss analysis of the different switches and converter topologies was done in MATLAB/SIMULINK and PLEXIM software. The study reveals that 3-level topologies with GaN devices are much superior to other topologies. Compact packaging of GaN devices, in addition to reduced losses and hence lesser heat generated, will reduce the requirement for heat sinks, which can further result in a significant reduction of the inverter space requirement for EV applications.

articleTitle: Design of Ferrite Magnet Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Motors for Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In general, motors are widely used in various consumer and commercial applications like Electric Vehicles (EVs). One of the most popular motor considered is Neodymium based Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM), thanks to their high-power density. But Neodymium (NdfeB), being a rare earth material, PMSM's in general are not suitable for the long term sustainability. Now, this is where Synchronous Reluctance Motors (SynRM) are becoming popular. However, one of the disadvantages is their relatively low power density and power factor. To solve these problems, this paper explores the insertion of Ferrite magnets in the flux barriers of rotor to increase the power factor and also to get the interaction torque as well along with reluctance torque. This paper presents the design of four SynRM motors with power ratings of 3 kW, 5 kW, 12.15 kW, and 30 kW, detailing initial specifications, design processes, power and torque profiles, and power densities. Also, the detailed discussions on 2D model designs, slot plot combination, and output performance analysis will also be presented.

articleTitle: Pole Number Optimization and Closed Loop Control of an Outer Rotor BLDC Motor for UAV Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper describes the performance study and design optimization of a medium speed antigravity type brushless DC (BLDC) motor featuring an outer rotor configuration. This motor is commonly employed in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) applications, with a particular focus on agricultural drones. The pole number optimization technique is used for such motors to lower the cost by reducing the number of permanent magnets needed while simultaneously increasing the efficiency. The present analysis uses the ratings and design specifications of a typical antigravity-type outer rotor BLDC motor employed in UAVs as a baseline. The design is optimized to achieve the highest efficiency with reduced magnet costs without compromising the performance. All the electromagnetic performance and structural analysis of the finally designed motor is verified in finite element method (FEM)-based simulation software. Following this, a closed loop control algorithm is presented to show the overall performance of the motor drive in MATLAB (Simulink) software.

articleTitle: A Practical Approach for Estimating State of Health of Li-Ion Batteries in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Accurately estimating the state-of-health (SOH) of rechargeable batteries is crucial to ensure the safe and depend-able performance of electric vehicles (EVs), consumer electronic products, and other systems powered by batteries. We propose an optimized and practical solution for accurate capacity-based SOH estimation that does not necessarily require full charge and discharge. The battery parameters related to SOH are identified in runtime using the forgetting factor recursive least square algorithm (FFRLS), followed by capacity estimation based on the identified parameters. The online update of capacity into an extended Kalman filter-based state-of-charge (SOC) estimation has improved the accuracy of the estimation. Using only partial discharge during normal driving conditions, less than 1.98 % maximum absolute error for the test scenarios has been achieved for SOH estimation. The proposed method has increased the accuracy of SOC and SOH estimation, and can maintain the computational complexity from an embedded constraint point of view by making use of relations among the states. The scheme is validated on real-time aging data to show effectiveness and practicability.

articleTitle: PV-Solar based Hybrid Telecom Power Plant for Roof-top Mobile Towers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The exponential growth in smartphone usage over GSM networks has significantly increased the energy demands of expanding telecom infrastructure. Concurrently, the adoption of green energy from renewable sources has become a key trend in the telecom industry. This paper presents the design and implementation of a hybrid PV-solar/Grid powered Telecom Power Plant (TPP) suitable for operation at modern roof-top mobile base stations. The conventional grid-powered telecom hardware is efficiently modified to operate on PV-solar power during daylight hours. The proposed TPP supports three rectifiers, each with a 2 kW capacity giving overall power of 6 kW, connected in parallel with hot-plugging features for redundancy, flexibility, and ease of maintenance. The power supply automatically switches between the PV source and the grid supply, based on the available voltage at the PV panels. The Power Factor Correction (PFC) stage in grid-mode is optimized for PV integration using Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) control via a synchronous boost converter. The system employed by PFC stage, followed by an LLC resonant converter topology for a 400V to 54V DC-DC converter with synchronous rectifiers at the output. A multi-mode digital control system, implemented on a DSP controller, regulates the output voltage and current. This system utilizes pulse frequency modulation to meet the dynamic energy requirements of the telecom load over a wide current range, including boost-charging of the battery in Constant Current/Constant Voltage mode. A prototype 2 kW system was designed and implemented using Silicon Carbide power MOSFETs for most power switches. It was tested with a 3.3 kWp polycrystalline PV solar panel array and a 100Ah 48V Sealed Maintenance Free battery pack, supporting a 48V/60A 5G mobile-tower base-station. The proposed system operates at around 94% efficiency, utilizing an average 12–15 kWh of green energy per day.

articleTitle: A Hardware-in-the-Loop Approach to Enhanced Harmonic Suppression in Grid-Connected Inverters Using LCL Filters with Trap Branches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Harmonic suppression in grid-connected inverters is critical for maintaining power quality and ensuring the reliable operation of electrical systems. While traditional LCL filters are widely used for their superior harmonic attenuation capabilities, they often struggle with resonance issues. They are inadequate for suppressing higher-order harmonics under varying grid conditions. This paper presents a novel approach to enhancing harmonic suppression in grid-connected inverters through an optimized LCL filter design incorporating a trap branch. The proposed filter significantly reduces Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) and improves overall power quality by tuning the trap branch to the third harmonic. The effectiveness of the design is validated using a Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) simulation, which replicates real-world operating conditions with varying DC link voltages and current references. The results demonstrate a substantial THD reduction to 2.99% and the delivery of purely active power characterized by in-phase inverter current and grid voltage. This work advances the state of LCL filter design and offers a practical solution for improving power quality in modern renewable energy systems.

Author Keywords: Power quality and Total Harmonic Distortion (THD)

articleTitle: Optimizing DC-Link Capacitor Size in Ten-Switch Neutral Point Clamped Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The paper presents a new modulation strategy for reducing the DC-Link capacitor size in ten-switch neutral point clamped converters (TS-NPCs). The TS-NPC, like the NPC, has a split DC-link but uses only ten switches rather than twelve. Low-frequency oscillations at three times the fundamental frequency is also present because of load current flowing through the neutral point (NP) during TS-NPC operation. The low-frequency capacitor voltage ripple in the DC-link is not addressed by the TS-NPC modulations currently available in the literature. Therefore, the DC link capacitors are sized to reduce the effect of voltage deviation due to this large third harmonic NP current. Furthermore, the multiplexed nature of the DC link causes TS-NPC to produce fewer switching states than NPC. In contrast to the existing modulations for TS-NPC, the proposed modulation guarantees the zero average NP current in each switching cycle and thereby eliminates the effect of low-frequency oscillations in the capacitors' voltages. This will enable the use of smaller DC-Link capacitors resulting in more compact passive components and high-power dense designs. Simulation results and comparisons with existing methods are provided to validate the proposed strategy to optimize the DC-Link capacitors size.

articleTitle: A Fault Tolerant N-Level Isolated Inverter Topology to Handle All Open Circuit Switch Faults Using Output Voltage Deviation Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, an isolated cascaded H-Bridge (ICHB) is reconfigured to create a fully fault-tolerant (FT) topology, where one leg of the H - Bridge operates as the active leg and the other serves as the FT leg. The proposed topology can function under single, multiple, or fully faulty conditions without increasing the device count compared to conventional FT ICHB structures, thereby incurring no additional cost. Additionally, the FT technique operates independently of switching methods and requires only two sensors (output voltage and current). The performance of the proposed method is evaluated against existing techniques to demonstrate its superiority. The effectiveness of the proposed topology is validated through real-time simulations using MATLAB and OPAL-RT.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of High Torque Toroidal Motor for Low-Speed Spacecraft Actuators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Spacecraft actuators are the focus of the fast-growing space industry as they are a key functional element in space systems. The desired features of these actuators are - long life, high reliability, high power density, high efficiency, reduced size under deep vacuum and extreme temperature environments, etc. A slow-speed scanning and imaging system intended for spacecraft application traditionally uses either torque motors or concentrated winding PMBLDC motors. As a better alternative, a permanent magnet toroidal winding BLDC motor is proposed in this paper, and its suitability is explored. For the toroidal winding BLDC motor, novel design aspects, such as the concept of phase isolation through flux barriers and stator spacers, are analyzed. Configurations of toroidal winding motors are investigated in this paper to achieve improved torque density and specific power. Considering various variants, the design of the Toroidal Winding - Dual Rotor PM Brushless Motor (TW-DRPMBLM) is carried out using Finite Element (FE) simulation analysis and its performance indices are compared with the slotless Concentrated Winding PMBLDC motor (CW-PMBLDC) for showcasing the superiority and usefulness of the proposed TW-DRPMBDM for the slow-speed scanning and imaging spacecraft application.

articleTitle: Modified Field Oriented Control Based Kramer Drive for Wound Rotor Induction Motor with Sinusoidal Machine Current and Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents Field Oriented Control (FOC) of modified Kramer drive with back-to-back SCR based converters in rotor side of an asymmetric WRIM. The rotor side SCR converter is operated to ensure proper current control in rotor side. The line side converter is operated to maintain DC link current constant (based on load torque demand). A two level VSI is connected on rotor side to compensate current harmonics to make rotor currents sinusoidal and inject reactive power for the thyristor commutation. The proposed drive can be operated in both sub-synchronous and super-synchronous speed range. Proper modelling of each unit of the proposed system along with their control is shown in this paper. Due to sinusoidal current and voltage at machine terminals the efficiency of the drive increases and promising improvement in torque profile can be obtained. To validate the proposed topology MATLAB/SIMULINK environment is used.

articleTitle: Deadbeat Controller for Current Injection Circuit based Front-End Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Diode bridge rectifiers are used as the front-end rectifier due to high efficiency and reliability. However, it needs big passive components at the dc-side and requires electrolytic capacitors. To reduce the size of the rectifier circuit, small dc-link capacitors may be used. With such a circuit, there is a possibility to maintain the unity power factor at the input current. However, to get this functionality, a current injection circuit is required. This paper focuses on a current injection-based front-end converter. This converter needs a single current controller but the current to be controlled is not dc and has a frequency of 150 Hz. To track a time-varying reference signal, the paper proposes the use of a deadbeat controller. The design of the controller is explained in the paper. The performance of the controller at the limit of the controller output is discussed, and a simple approach to improve the performance is discussed. The controller performance is verified using simulation results.

articleTitle: Power Quality Comparison of Even and Odd Number of Levels with Active Neutral Point Clamped Configured Topologies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The number of levels is crucial in the design of a switched-capacitor-based inverter topologies. The number of levels plays an important role in the power quality of the output parameters, which also signifies the size of the filter. In this paper, four different multilevel inverter topologies have been discussed for a different number of levels. First, a four-level topology is discussed, followed by the five-level, six-level, and seven-level topologies. A power quality assessment of output voltage and current has been carried out for different filter sizes as well as carrier frequencies for all four topologies. A comparative study of all four topologies has been carried out regarding component count and harmonics. Simulation results have been provided for all four topologies at the same operating conditions for a better decree of the topologies.

articleTitle: A User-Friendly Reconfigurable Testbed System and Method to Test and Validate the Power Electronics Circuits for Educational and Research Purposes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This study discusses a reconfigurable testbed system that is easy to use and tests circuit and power electronic converter systems in power engineering research. Features of the reconfigurable power electronics testbed system include hardware protection against failures such as sudden overvoltages, undervoltages, and overcurrents. The testbed has six voltage and current sensors available to sense the circuit's voltage and current. The voltages and currents detected by the sensors are displayed on the sensor's voltmeters and ammeters that are attached to the sensors. The testbed has input and output voltmeters to show the measured input and output voltages of the completed circuit. The user has the flexibility to create a variety of power electronics circuits thanks to the availability of IGBT switches and passive circuit components like capacitors and inductors. By creating an external electrical connection, all topologies that call for a minimum of 1 switch, a maximum of 12 power electronics switches, constant or variable inductors, and capacitors in the specified voltage and current range may be made possible. Users can utilize the testbed's internal controller or add their own external controller to create a variety of circuits. In this paper, an example with synchronous boost and synchronous cuk converter is shown.

articleTitle: A Passive $\frac{dv}{dt}$ Filter for Integrated Induction Motor Drive Fed from 3-Phase 2-Level GaN Based Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In recent times, the Si-IGBT switches are being replaced by the WBG devices (SiC, GaN) in the next gen EV drive train as the WBG devices exhibit inherent advantages like higher switching frequency, better efficeincy as compared to Si-IGBTs. On the other hand, between SiC MOSFETs and GaN, the GaN exhibits superior performance when compared with SiC in terms of efficiency. Moreover, GaN is found to be smaller size as compared to SiC. Because of these advantages, GaN is being used widely in next gen EV drive drain as the switchingdevice of inverter. However, this GaN devices exhibit higher <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac{d v}{d t}$</tex> at the inverter terminal (approximately 40 V/ns) and because of that uneven distribution of voltage occurs in the motor windings. As a result, the life span of motor winding is degraded. To overcome this problem, passive <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac{dv}{dt}$</tex> filter is used. On the other hand, the loading effect of motor impedance is not considered while designing the passive <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac{dv}{dt}$</tex> filter. As a result, the accuracy in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac{dv}{dt}$</tex> at the motor terminal is missed. In this paper, a novel passive LC based <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac{dv}{dt}$</tex> filter designing algorithm is proposed considering the loading effect of motor impedance. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac{dv}{dt}$</tex> at the motor terminal is maintained at 0.5 V/ns. The propose-passive <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac{dv}{dt}$</tex> filter is applied on a 120 V, 2.2 kW induction motor. The simulation and experimental results illustrate the accuracy in designing LC based <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac{dv}{dt}$</tex> filter.

articleTitle: Fractional IMC-PIDA Control Technique for Mitigation of Time Delay Attack in Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This article proposes a fractional filter internal model control (FFIMC) based proportional integral derivative acceleration (PIDA) control technique for mitigating the time delay attack (TDA) in a single-area power system (SAPS). The uniqueness of the proposed method is that the parameters are tuned for minimum value of integral errors. The rapid development of power systems and cyber-physical systems (CPSs) makes them highly vulnerable to cyber threats due to information sharing through the open communication channel. This article focuses on the load frequency control (LFC) issue of SAPS in the presence of the TDA. The LFC issue arises because of the unanticipated load requirements. The function of LFC is to regulate the frequency in the specified limit, whereas the presence of TDA, along with sudden load demand, severely affects the whole system, resulting in destabilization. Therefore, to mitigate the TDA from SAPS and improve performance, the proposed technique FFIMC-PIDA is used in addition to the Smith predictor approach. Finally, the efficacy of the proposed method is analyzed based on integral error indices and compared with existina techniques,

articleTitle: Implementation of Current Sensorless Level Shifted PWM Strategy for Modular Multilevel Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, the implementation of the current sensorless level-shifted PWM algorithm for a modular multilevel converter is proposed. The algorithm is tailored for MMC with N submodules (SMs) per arm, resulting in its universal feasibility. Furthermore, the algorithm does not require arm-current signals, reducing the cost even more. The pole voltage may have two possible voltage levels: N+1 or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\mathrm{N}+1$</tex>. The phase difference between the upper and lower arm carriers determines the specific level. The paper provides an extensive description of the mathematical structure of the technique and includes a flowchart to facilitate a better understanding. The cogency of the proposed algorithm is initially tested through single-phase MMC simulations in MATLAB/Simulink and then subsequently verified on an experimental setup.

articleTitle: Dynamic Droop Control for Optimal Power Sharing in Renewable Rich Hybrid Islanded Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A stepwise optimal droop control method is designed in this paper to enhance the integration of renewable energy sources (RES) and ensure economical power sharing among dispatchable sources. This novel control strategy prioritizes the use of RES, thereby promoting a cleaner and more sustainable energy mix. Following this prioritization, the method utilizes an incremental cost droop control mechanism to optimize power and decrease the generation cost of the overall system. Additionally, an adaptive gradient parameter is introduced in cost-based droop control to fully exploit the potential of dispatchable sources while maintaining system frequency stability. This adaptive feature ensures the system's stability even if any dispatchable source reaches its maximum capacity. It dynamically removes that source from the incremental cost droop control, allowing the remaining sources to continue following the equal incremental cost criteria. This adaptive feature allows the system to respond dynamically to fluctuating demand and supply conditions, ensuring optimal performance and reliability.

articleTitle: Study and Performance Evaluation of Design and Control Methods for CC/CV Based EV Charging in WPT Topologies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper comprehensively studies different designs and controls of several wireless power transfer (WPT) topologies for battery charging. Generally, most WPT topologies exhibit inherent constant voltage (CV) or constant current (CC) output characteristics. The paper systematically studies many WPT topologies to find these natural CC or CV characteristics, where topologies like LCL/S, S/LCC, S/LCL, PS/SP, etc., are studied for the first time. The battery requires combined CC and CV charging. Hence, many works related to different WPT topologies exhibiting two or more resonant frequencies while achieving the CC and CV charging profile at two distinct frequencies are thoroughly studied. Further, a sensitivity analysis compares the performances and robustness of different topologies' natural CC or CV characteristics when the WPT coil and compensation circuit parameters have ±10% tolerance. Finally, a 500 W lab prototype is built to verify the generalized study for CC and CV-based design for the PS-SP topology.

articleTitle: Frequency Response Assessment of Inverter Dominated Power System Under Grid Abnormalities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The increase in renewable sources equipped with power electronic converters can pose a serious threat to power system stability. This paper presents the grid frequency response observed after integrating inverter-based resources into the dynamically focused synchronous generator-based IEEE 9 bus system. The inverter current and voltage control strategies of the grid following mode is implemented, and the inverter response to grid disturbances such as faults, phase jump, voltage sag-swell, and harmonics are observed. The rate of change of frequency, inertia, voltage stability, and transient stability are examined with different inverter penetration levels. The effect of load power factor on the power voltage curve is also analyzed. The data from MATLAB-SIMULINK is utilized to evaluate the performance of inertia estimation and various stability methods.

articleTitle: Effect of Rotor Core Shapings and Ribs on the Performance of Reduced Rare Earth Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Multilayer interior permanent magnet synchronous machines (IPMSMs) are preferred for high-speed operations and reducing rare earth magnet materials. The use of a hybrid magnet arrangement in the rotor structure is made possible by the use of multiple layers in the rotor structure. This is particularly significant as the price of rare earth materials is increasing globally. The reduced use of rare earth topologies in the IPMSM is in growing demand. However, challenges associated with the design prospect to meet the required torque-speed characteristics are the same as those of rare-earth-based IPMSM, as well as high efficiency and less core loss. Typically, the air gap is uniform in the case of an IPMSM. This work deals with the effect of rotor core shaping in the stampings of the rotor along the d-axis, q-axis, or both axes in the U-shaped double-layer rotor topology of IPMSM. Further improvement of the performance of the motor impact of rib thickness has also been investigated. Therefore, different possible combinations of rotor core shaping on the rotor have been considered in this work. Simulation studies have been conducted using FE Simulation software, and the results have been reported.

Author Keywords: Multilayer interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (ML-IPMSM)

articleTitle: Planar Litz Inductor Design for High-Frequency Soft-switched PWM Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The power density consideration of high-frequency soft-switched PWM converters demands highly efficient magnetic components. This paper presents a detailed procedure for designing a planar litz inductor carrying significant high-frequency AC current using a printed circuit board (PCB). The significance of the appropriate selection of copper thickness and trace width for planar windings is explained. Four different winding strategies based on the number of strands, routing, and placement of vias are evaluated. The impact of staggered and sandwiched traces in a multi-layer planar litz winding on inter-winding capacitances is highlighted. The core and copper losses are estimated using analytical models for a non-sinusoidal excitation condition. Analytical core loss is compared with SIMPLIS MDM simulation. The current density of different winding strategies is evaluated using Ansys Maxwell 2D. Inter-winding capacitances are extracted using Ansys Q3D. Five different inductors, one based on Litz winding and the other four based on PCB windings have been fabricated and tested in the laboratory. An estimation of the parasitic capacitance based on terminal measurements using a network analyzer is discussed.

articleTitle: Power Control Technique of a Multiport Converter for Low Voltage Standalone Solar PV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper introduces an approach to the power control technique of a non-isolated DC-DC multiport converter for low voltage standalone solar PV (photovoltaic) applications, incorporating a single inductor. The system utilizes an advanced time-sharing voltage-mode control strategy to manage power distribution between the PV array, rechargeable battery, and DC load. This control strategy maintains a stable DC load voltage and simultaneously achieves the optimal Global Maximum Power Point (GMPP) for the solar PV system with or without partially shaded. The design of the converter is such that it can operates at four different modes such as dual input buck mode (DIBuM), dual output boost mode (DOBoM), dual output buck-boost mode (DOBuBoM) and buck converter with battery charge control mode (BCBCCM). The comprehensive implementation details of this the converter and control scheme are thoroughly explained in this paper. Design and the simulation results for all four modes with dynamic mode changing are shown with varying irradiance and DC load demand.

Author Keywords: buck converter with battery charge control mode (BCBCCM)

articleTitle: Use of Artificial Neural Network to Predict Duty Ratio in Two Sub-Modes of CI-SIDO Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper focuses on the coupled inductor single input dual output (CI-SIDO) boost converter, a variant of SIMO topology. The CI-SIDO boost converter operates in continuous conduction mode (CCM) and discontinuous conduction mode (DCM). In CCM, the duty ratio depends only on input and output voltages and is sector-independent. In DCM, however, the duty ratio involves complex equations with load current, input and output voltages, inductances, and coupling coefficient, varying across sectors and sub-modes. There are 21 sub-modes in 9 sectors when one boost operates in CCM and the other in DCM. The narrow load range for each sub-mode in DCM makes duty ratio determination challenging using conventional methods. This paper proposes to determine the duty ratio in DCM for CI-SIDO boost converter using an artificial neural network (ANN). Existing literature has limited applications of ANN in power electronic converters and none for DCM operation in CI-SIDO converters. This study fills that gap by proposing an ANN model to determine duty ratios, considering frequent sub-mode and sector changes under varying loads. Using the feed-forward and back-propagation algorithm, the ANN is trained for two sub-modes in one sector by varying the duty ratio, output voltage, and current in the converter in DCM while keeping the parameters of the converter in CCM fixed. After training, the ANN predicts the duty ratio for the converter in DCM based on reference output voltage and current. The predicted duty ratio is applied to a MATLAB/Simulink model of the CI-SIDO boost converter to verify output voltage and current. The predicted duty ratio is also compared with theoretical values for the same sub-mode and circuit conditions.

articleTitle: Disturbance Observer-Based Sliding Mode Control of Boost-Flyback Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a disturbance observer based sliding mode control of single-input double-output Boost-flyback dc-dc converter. The converter supplies two outputs i.e. flyback side output and boost side output through common magnetic path of flyback transformer. The power flow through common magnetic path poses the challenges of cross-coupling and crossregulation at line and load transient operations of converter. In this paper, these challenges are alleviated using sliding mode control approach. Moreover, a disturbance observer is also designed to alleviate the effect of cross-regulation at the load transients. The performance of proposed control technique is validated using simulation results.

articleTitle: Enhancing Drive Performance using Mixed-Order Flux Observer driven Sensorless Control of PMSM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper addresses the widespread adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) and the importance of efficient control, cost-effectiveness, and resilience performance. Therefore, sensorless motor control is used, which relies on a flux observer to estimate position and speed without a physical sensor. This paper presents a novel approach to enhancing the performance of electric drive systems by implementing sensorless control using a Mixed-Order (MO) Integral-based rotor Flux Observer. Traditional electric drives require sensors for performance monitoring and control, adding complexity, cost, and potential points of failure. The proposed MO-based flux observer offers a viable sensorless control solution that improves reliability and reduces position-tracking errors, even in the presence of DC offsets. The effectiveness of second, third, and mixed order-based flux observers are presented. Simulation results demonstrate significant improvements in system performance, validating the effectiveness and finding satisfactory system response.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of Frequency Modulated LLC Resonant Converter for Deeply Depleted Battery Charging Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents the variable frequency LLC resonant converter for charging the On-Board Electric Vehicle (OBEV) battery in a normal and deeply depleted state. Based on the battery's State of Charge (SoC), the presented charging circuit has three modes of operation Half Bridge Normal Mode (HBNM), Full Bridge Normal Mode (FBNM), and Full Bridge Voltage Doubler mode (FBVD). Both HBNM and FBNM modes are operated in deeply depleted states with end voltage ranges of 13.5 V and 24 V respectively. The FBVD mode is operated in the normal charging mode of a deeply depleted battery with an end voltage range of 42 V. A control logical circuit has been implemented to change the operation modes based on the battery's voltage range. The proposed converter is simulated in PSIM software with 36 V 12.5 Ah battery specifications, and the mathematical model is also implemented in MATLAB Simulink software.

articleTitle: Effect of Harmonics Due to Grid Integration of Electric Vehicles: Case Study and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Due to the widespread adoption of EVs, the demand for charging infrastructure for electric vehicles is on the rise. EV chargers, which are non-linear loads, generate harmonics, which may affect power quality adversely. Simultaneous charging of huge number of EVs can, thus, strain distribution grids. Therefore, understanding the effect of integrating various EV chargers on the power distribution network is essential. Level 2 15 KW and 25 KW EV chargers are often used for three and four-wheeled vehicles and are the best suited options for charging in a variety of locations, such as workplaces, residences, commercial and public areas. This research examines the effects of installing 15 and 25 KW DC chargers at commercial and public charging stations connected to the power utility network.

articleTitle: Reverse Conduction Loss and $\left(\frac{d v}{d t}\right)$ Induced False Triggering Protection of GaN-HFET Based Power Converter for EV Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Enhancement mode GaN (e-GaN) and cascode GaN HFET both are capable of 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> quadrant operation where e-GaN HFET has zero <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${Q}_{{r}{r}}$</tex> and cascode GaN HFET has small <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${Q}_{{r}{r}}$</tex> (less than MOSFET). These makes negligible switching loss using these devices in power converter (PC) but larger threshold voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({V}_{{t}{h}}\approx-6{V}$</tex> for e-GaN and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${V}_{{t} {h}}\approx-2{V}$</tex> for cascode GaN HFET) in 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> quadrant and higher reverse resistance creates extra reverse conduction loss. Again, bootstrap capacitor-based driver for both these devices creates <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left(\frac{d v}{d t}\right)$</tex> induced false triggering at high side e-GaN-HFET with increased loading and dead time. In this work reverse conduction loss comparison is performed on both MOSFET (V≈0.7 V) and GaN-HFET based 600W LLC resonant converter used for EV charging. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left(\frac{d v}{d t}\right)$</tex> induced false triggering prevention method is also proposed.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Frequency Deviation in MPS Utilizing Demand Response Techniques for Irregularity Between Sources and Load
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This article describes the utilization of a Demand Response (DR) technique for enhancing the Frequency deviation of a modern power system (MPS). The power system under study integrates three different power sources-gas, hydro, and thermal-in each control area with several real-time nonlinearities, including governor dead band (GDB), boiler dynamics, and generation rate constraint (GRC). The renewables sources (solar and wind plant) are penetrated in area-1 and area-2 respectively. A self-adaptive fuzzy-PID (SA-FPID) controller is suggested for investigated MPS model. The effectiveness of existing controller is compared with several existing controllers. An Opposition based Sea-Horse Optimization (OSHO) is designed to get optimum settings of various deployed controllers. A more complex automated generation control (AGC) approach of a hybrid DR technique appears in the integration of intrinsic communication delay into the DR loop. All system physical constraints are taken into account together with DR with step delay to assess the stability of the investigated MPS. Additionally, an analysis is conducted on the test system's steady state error evaluation. The results show that the proposed control algorithm works significantly better than other control strategies. For the system under study, the clearly raised results support the frequency deviation technique with DR that is proposed.

articleTitle: Modelling of Coupled Inductor-Based Single Input Triple Output Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Multiple levels of regulated DC voltages are crucial for power modules in various applications. Electric vehicles (EV s), portable electronics, IT and telecommunications, aerospace, and renewable energy are some of the applications requiring multiple voltage levels. Traditionally, multiple voltage levels are provided by several parallelly connected single input single output (SISO) DC-DC converters. However, the need for size reduction has led to the use of single input multiple output (SIMO) DC-DC converters. This paper introduces a specific SIMO converter: the coupled inductor-based single input triple output (CI-SITO) boost converter. Accurate modeling of CI-SITO boost converter is essential for designing control guidelines and predicting performance. However, current literature lacks precise mathematical models for CI -SITO boost converters. CI-SITO converters are compact but suffer from cross-coupling and cross-regulation due to the coupled inductors present in it. Existing research does not analyze the effect of cross-coupling and cross-regulation, on steady state operation of CI-SITO boost converter. This paper develops a mathematical model, state-space average equations, and a small-signal model (SSM) for a CI-SITO boost converter using the state-space averaging method. It also analyzes the effects of cross-coupling and cross-regulation on steady state operation. The model is verified using results from MATLAB/Simulink environment and its derived transfer function model.

articleTitle: Modular Multilevel Converter Control by Using Sorting Algorithm and Smoothing of ARM Inductor Current
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The modular multilevel converter (MMC) is a revolutionary design that has shown potential for high-voltage applications. The MMC consists of many identical sub modules(SM's). Each SM may be regarded of as a controlled voltage source that must keep the capacitor's voltage at a specified level in order to work effectively. Furthermore, limiting the circulating current (which does not flow to the load) is critical to the MMC's consistent and effective functioning. This paper proposes a new sorting algorithm to balancing capacitor voltage, and eventually balance the load current with minimal total harmonic distortion (THD). It aims to equalize the capacitor voltages for each SM contained in the MMC one at a time using a new sorting approach. The analysis is based on a low-power case study of single-phase with eight SM's in one arm of MMC, but it may be expanded with a larger number of cells. The low power five-level MMC has been verified by mathematical and theoretical studies, in addition to data from simulations.

articleTitle: Minimization of Simple Payback Time through Reactive Power Injection & kVA Billing in MW Scale Solar PV Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: MW scale renewable power generation through solar PV plants is promoted strongly to curtail down the CO2 emission in power sector. However, high installation cost of solar power plant results into a long simple payback time due to limited utilization factor of solar PV plant. This paper provides a methodology to improve the utilization factor of solar PV plant through injection of reactive power to the utility grid during no Sun hours. It is proposed that kVA billing of total energy injected to utility grid would effectively improve the utilization and bring down the simple payback time. The design and implementation of a 2MW scale solar power plant, consisting of DC-DC converters connected to active front-end converters is studied in the paper. The system involves LCL filter for better power quality and feeds power to 33 kV grid through a step-up transformer. An analysis is presented in the paper to suggest the reduction in simple payback time due to injection of reactive power in different proportions. The penalty imposed by utility due to poor power factor is also considered in the simple pay back time computation. A suitable proportion is proposed for minimization of simple payback time for the MW scale solar PV power plant. MATLAB/Simulink based model of the solar power plant is developed and performance of the same is presented during various operating conditions.

articleTitle: Transient Stability Enhancement of a Synchronous Generator Using DFIG Considering its LVRT Capability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The high penetration of doubly fed induction generators (DFIGs) to the grid may affect the stability of the synchronous generators (SGs). The dedicated control of the DFIG can enhance the transient stability of the SG. This paper proposes a transient control technique for DFIG, which enhances the rotor angle stability of the SG. The proposed control technique operates the DFIG in motoring mode during a fault, by modulating the electromagnetic torque considering the PCC bus voltage and low voltage ride-through (LVRT) capability of DFIG. In order to appropriately realize the practical behavior of the DFIG under a fault scenario, the standard LVRT capability of the DFIG is also incorporated along with the proposed technique. To avoid the post-fault instability of the system, a rate limiter is used to allow the smooth recovery of the DFIG. The real time digital simulator (RTDS) is used to analyze the performance of the proposed technique in a modified IEEE 9-bus system.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of IPMSM with Modular Stator Structure for Electric Vehicular Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Traditionally, interior permanent magnet synchronous machines (IPMSMs) with non-modular stator structures are widely used in electric vehicles (EVs) owing to higher power and torque density. However, it occupies more space, less efficient and unable to operate under phase faults. To address the aforementioned concerns, this paper introduces IPMSMs with a modular stator structure for EV applications. The proposed stator structure improves electromagnetic torque and efficiency of IPMSM. To validate these features, modular IPMSMs with different slot/pole combinations (12-slot/10-pole and 12-slot/14-pole) consisting of flux-gaps in alternate stator teeth and single-layer concentrated winding is investigated. As a result, it enhances the slot filling factor, output torque and power density. To find the suitability of these machines, a 2-D finite element (FE) analysis is carried out using Ansys-Maxwell software. The performance of these machines is holistically evaluated in terms of phase back-EMF, on-load torque, torque ripple, core losses, copper losses, and efficiency by varying the slot/pole number and flux-gap widths. Finally, the performance of these modular IPMSMs is compared with that of non-modular IPMSMs.

articleTitle: A Control Technique for Achieving ZVS and Minimum Conduction Loss in DAB by Varying Input DC Link Voltage for EV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Isolated DC-DC converters are essential in electric vehicle (EV) applications. For power ratings exceeding 5kW, the Dual Active Bridge (DAB) converter is often preferred due to its lower conduction losses than resonant converters. However, DAB converters suffer from higher switching loss, particularly under light load conditions which adversely affects system efficiency. The wide voltage variation in EV batteries makes it challenging to maintain the DAB's voltage gain within the ZVS range when the turns ratio is fixed. This paper proposes a control technique for a DAB converter that maintains the voltage gain ratio within the ZVS range, even under light load conditions, while also minimizing conduction losses. A comprehensive loss analysis of a 6.6kW DAB converter is conducted across various DC link input voltages for EV charging applications. The analysis covers an output voltage range of 300-500V. The study demonstrates that maintaining a voltage gain ratio near unity is crucial for achieving ZVS and minimizing conduction losses.
