Further, also explores the relationship between battery voltage variations and the corresponding optimal input DC link voltage to reduce switching and conduction losses and is carried out using the PLECS Blockset integrated with MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Optimal Reactive Power Control in Standalone Hybrid Power System by Using Harris Hawks Algorithm Tuned Statcom Tilt Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The intermittent nature of renewable energy sources and load disturbances may lead to an imbalance of reactive power, which can further affect the stability of the system. In order to achieve dynamic voltage support and reactive power control, the implementation of flexible AC transmission system (FACTS) devices is necessary. This paper discusses the reactive power control and improvement of stability in a standalone micro-hydro wind diesel hybrid power system (SMHWDHPS) using a novel Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO) algorithm tuned STATCOM tilt-integral second-order double derivative controller (STATCOM-TIDD<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). A comparison of results is made with different controllers and algorithms.

Author Keywords: Standalone micro-hydro wind diesel hybrid power system(SMHWDHPS)

articleTitle: A Variable Duty Cycle Based Method for High Resistance Connection Fault Detection in BLDC Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: High-resistance connection (HRC) is a common issue in motor drive applications. These connections occur between the motor and inverter terminals, leading to voltage drops across the junction connectors and increased copper losses. HRC can create asymmetry in motor drive systems, degrading the motor's performance in terms of speed and torque. Therefore, reliable detection is crucial for implementing the mitigation techniques before the fault escalates and impacts the performance of the target application. This work proposes a new technique for detecting HRC faults in Brushless DC (BLDC) motor drives. In this technique, the DC link voltage across the motor terminals is varied for a fixed duration in an electrical cycle by adjusting the duty of the buck converter. This variation introduces a DC signal into the stator currents. By extracting the DC components from stator currents, it is possible to estimate the line resistances. Also, the severity of the fault is assessed using symmetrical component transforms. The proposed method is immune to variations in inductance and symmetrical variations in resistance. The above claims are supported by analytical expressions and experimental results obtained from a 36 V, 500 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex> BLDC motor drive.

articleTitle: A Flying Capacitor Based Neutral Voltage Balancing System for Three Phase Four Wire Inverter with State Feedback Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper addresses the important problem of the neutral point voltage equalisation in three-phase four-wire standalone inverters employing a state feedback control technique. The neutral voltage balancer functions independently, and state feedback gains can be obtained utilising optimal controller design methodologies. The suggested state feedback control approach is immune to parameter changes and keeps the neutral voltage very close to zero under diverse dynamic loading scenarios. This paper also proposes a flying capacitor-based switch network that significantly reduces the neutral link inductor current ripple. A MATLAB-based simulation analysis is performed to illustrate the efficacy of the suggested method in providing balanced neutral voltage distribution with reduced oscillations, hence improving the overall stability and performance of the inverter system. Simulation results shows the neutral voltage equalisation with balanced and unbalanced DC link capacitors. This work, using a state feedback control method and a flying capacitor-based switch network, provides a potential choice for enhancing the robustness of stand-alone inverter systems under unbalanced loading conditions.

articleTitle: Common-Ground-Type Dual-Source Switched-Capacitor Multilevel Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A novel common-ground-type dual-source switched-capacitor multilevel inverter (CGT-DSSCMLI) for grid-connected application is proposed in this article. The proposed CGT-DSSCMLI topology can generate 11-level output voltage by utilizing only eight switches, three diodes, three capacitors, and two asymmetrical dc sources. The proposed topology has various advantages such as: high voltage gain, less total blocking voltage, less component count, less total harmonic distortion, higher number of voltage levels, and zero ground leakage current. Further, the capacitor is self voltage balanced without any extra balancing circuit. PLECS based simulation results are presented for verification of operability and feasibility. Additionally, a comprehensive comparative study is conducted to validate the advantageous features.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Optimal PV Array Reconfiguration Under Partial Shaded Condition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The integration of photovoltaic (PV) systems for various applications has significantly increased due to their potential as renewable energy sources. However, PV array performance is substantially impacted by partial shading caused by obstacles such as trees, buildings, or dust accumulation, which leads to uneven current distribution. This results in mismatch losses, increased temperatures, potential hotspots, compromised efficiency and lifespan of PV modules. Assessing PV efficiency under partial shading is crucial for developing effective mitigation strategies and optimizing system performance. The main objective of this paper is to compare and validate the performances of various shade dispersion techniques for maximizing Global Maximum Power Point (GMPP) of PV array under partial shaded conditions. In this paper, a 9x9 Total Cross Tied (TCT) configuration of PV array and four different shading patterns are considered for comparative analysis. TCT configuration is considered because it combines series and parallel connections which is proved to be performed better in mitigating shading effects than conventional series or parallel configurations. Furthermore, in addition to the analysis of optimal dispersion of shaded PV panel by altering electrical connections, this paper also addressed the other goal of minimizing losses associated with cable resistance. Performance metrics, such as mismatch percentage, shading power loss, and wiring losses, were meticulously analyzed to assess the efficacy of different dispersion methods in mitigating shading effects. Techniques like optimal Su Do Ku, conventional SuDoKu, and meta-heuristics algorithms such as Harmony Search Algorithm (HSA), Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Grasshopper Optimization Algorithm (GOA) were taken into consideration for the comparative analysis in this paper.

articleTitle: Diamond(m-switch) Converter Topology for Four-Phase Switched Reluctance Motor(SRM) Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents Diamond converter(m-switch converter) topology for four-phase switched reluctance motor(SRM) drives, which reduces the number of switches to half when compared to Asymmetrical bridge converter(AHB) and does not have any additional capacitance when compared to split capacitor(SC) converter. At the beginning operation principle, and electrical equations are analyzed based on an SRM with double-phase excitation. Diamond converter is comparatively investigated with a both AHB and SC converter with a four-phase SRM. Steady-state and transient performances of the converters are discussed and compared by the means of simulations. Further, Direct Instantaneous Torques Control(DITC) has been implemented to control the speed of SRM using this novel converter.

articleTitle: A Novel 7-Level Triple-Boost Common-Ground Switched Capacitor Based Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Multilevel inverters (MLIs) with a common ground (CG) feature have gained significant popularity in transformer-less grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) systems. In this paper, a novel switched capacitor (SC) based common ground type seven-level inverter topology with triple voltage boosting capability has been proposed. The common ground feature of the proposed inverter bypasses the PV stray capacitor, resulting in zero leakage current in the stray capacitor of the PV system. The proposed inverter topology requires two capacitors, rated at the source voltage and twice the source voltage, respectively, reducing overall cost and improving reliability and power density. The pulse width modulation (PWM) scheme balances the voltages across the SCs, which eliminates the need for the sensor for capacitor voltage balancing. The proposed inverter's circuit description, its operating states, PWM scheme, and control scheme for closed-loop grid-connected operation are discussed. Further, a detailed comparison with the CG-type seven-level triple-boost inverter is presented in terms of capacitor voltage rating, component count, cost factor, total standing voltage, total conducting devices per level, and maximum blocking voltage, which demonstrates the improved attribute of the proposed inverter topology. The pro-posed inverter is simulated in MATLAB Simulink environment for various steady state and dynamic conditions, which validate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed inverter.

articleTitle: An Improved Power Quality EV Charger Using a Modified Bridgeless Cuk Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)

articleTitle: Bidirectional Proportional Multi-SOGI Based OCC for LV PV-STATCOM with Trapezoidal Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper focuses on an improved controller configuration for active filter with its LV DC-bus directly connected with PV-modules. The power circuit consists of two full bridge inverters connected with a transformer and LC filter. The first full bridge is modulated with trapezoidal modulation to reduce the switching losses in the converter. The second full bridge is controlled through modified one cycle controller (OCC) for achieving grid voltage sensor-less operation. An proportional Multi-SOGI controller within one cycle controller ensures bidirectional active power exchange between PCC and grid, excellent grid current quality irrespective of the presence of non-linear and reactive load at the point of common coupling (PCC) and the additional harmonics generated by the trapezoidal modulation. However, the determination of phase angle information of the trapezoidal modulating signal and the adjustment of the resonant peaks at appropriate frequencies for Multi-SOGI controller requires the information of grid voltage. The grid voltage sensor-less operation is ensured through a proposed grid voltage estimator. A conventional PV-MPPT algorithm ensures the required DC voltage reference for the converter. The detailed simulation study of the proposed solution and experimental verification from an scaled down active filter prototype are presented.

articleTitle: Mitigation of Circulating Currents in Parallel-Connected Solar PV Inverters: Real-Time Implementation and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The integration of multiple solar photovoltaic (PV) inverters in parallel configurations holds immense potential for enhancing power generation efficiency and system reliability. However, the parallel connection of inverters introduces challenges such as high-frequency circulating currents, which can adversely affect system performance and component longevity. This work presents a comprehensive study focused on real-time implementation, analysis and mitigation of circulating current issues in parallel-connected solar PV inverters. Through detailed analysis and experimental validation, the work identifies key problems associated with inverter paralleling and explores various strategies for mitigating of circulating currents. The findings provide valuable insights for improving the operation and reliability of parallel-connected solar PV systems, thereby facilitating the widespread adoption of renewable energy technologies.

articleTitle: Soft and Hard-Switched Synchronous Buck Converter Comparison for USB Power Delivery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The widespread adoption of USB Power Delivery (PD) has revolutionized portable electronics charging, offering fast, efficient, and flexible power transfer solutions. Hard-switched synchronous buck converters (SBC) are widely used for this application. But this topology suffers from high switching losses. Zero voltage switching synchronous buck converter (ZVS SBC) mitigates these issues and could potentially serve as an alternative solution for USB PD application. This paper presents a comparative loss analysis of ZVS SBC against the traditional SBC in the context based on GaN semiconductor switches. The variation in switching, conduction, and core losses with varying input voltage and load conditions are highlighted. The impacts of fixed, variable, and step -varied frequency modulation techniques on power losses of ZVS SBC are analyzed. Experiments are carried out to evaluate the performance of ZVS SBC with different modulation techniques and corresponding power loss breakdowns are presented.

articleTitle: A Multi-Objective Approach for Energy Management of Data Center Microgrid Considering Carbon Emission and Operational Cost
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Increase in global digitization, increases the demand for data centers and to provide a flexible and reliable service to end users its continuous operation is utmost priority. The continuous operation of data centers involves three major challenges such as rising bills for electricity, power outages and carbon emissions. Data center microgrids are effective choice to enhance reliability and energy efficiency for electrical services but, its optimized operation considering both operational cost and carbon emission needs to be addressed. Therefore, this paper proposes an energy management approach for data center microgrid considering energy storage system, renewable sources, and generation units. Consequently, a multi-objective optimisation problem is then formulated to optimize the operational cost and carbon emission. Five different metaheuristic optimization approaches are adopted to minimize the objective function. It is elucidated that grey wolf optimizer (GWO) outperforms among other used algorithms and obtained results give optimized operational cost and carbon emission as 34928.91 ($) and 150155.30 (Kg) respectively. Furthermore, a scenario for fixed price is investigated and obtained values of the operational cost and carbon emission are 71850.13 ($) and 204023.28 KG respectively.

articleTitle: Complex Vector Disturbance Observer for Syn-RL Motor with Speed Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a model based sensorless technique for estimation of active flux (AF), speed and position. It focuses on complex vector disturbance observer (CVDO) for AF estimation and adaptive enhanced quadrature phase locked loop (AE-QPLL) technique for speed and position estimation. Complex vector observer is used to mitigate negative fundamental frequency components in estimated active flux and DC offset followed by disturbance observer for estimation of errorless active flux. CVDO method also eliminates a use of extra filters for extraction of fundamental AF. For improving dynamic speed and position error, AE-QPLL technique with forward compensation is used. Effectiveness of presented system is validated in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Advanced Driver System for Enhanced Efficiency in Emergency Led Lights
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper represents an optimized driver circuit for emergency LED lights providing higher wattage, featuring battery management system (BMS) and intelligent power failure detection. The driver circuit has been designed to support an 18W emergency bulb and the battery capacity of this light was increased to 3600mAh. The primary objectives of this research are to ensure that the driver supports higher output, a high-power factor with high efficiency, adaptability to rough electrical conditions and an efficient BMS. The proposed system integrates multiple sections, including a buck regulator constant current IC, an LC filter, a joule thief circuit, and a battery protection IC. This ensures persistent performance, over charging protection, over discharging protection and swift errorless power outage detection. Testing results show a higher efficiency up to 89.8% with a power factor of 96.3% and lower current and voltage harmonic distortion of 26.6% and 0.2% respectively. Also to demonstrate the battery efficiency the driver shows a backup duration over 180 minutes. The driver is also able to charge at high and low voltage condition. Photometric tests verified stable lumen output in both AC connection mode and emergency DC backup mode. This integrated system satisfies the performance goals.

articleTitle: Harmonic Optimization in a Nine-Level Cascaded H-Bridge Inverter: Leveraging Support Vector Machine Algorithm with LSPWM Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach that integrates a support vector machine (SVM) regression model with a nine-level cascaded H-bridge multilevel voltage source inverter triggered by LSPWM. The objective is to optimize low-frequency odd harmonics in the output voltage while achieving a uniform output current, thus improving the power quality of the inverter. Specifically, the focus is on predicting the fifth, seventh, and eleventh order harmonics from the phase voltage and optimizing their amplitudes. The innovative SVM-based LSPWM technique predicts the best-fitted amplitude range of odd harmonics under variable modulation indices and switching angles using simplified low-order equations, offering an alternative to complex nonlinear equations. Simulation and experimental results closely align with theoretical analysis, affirming the adaptability of the proposed work for industrial applications.

articleTitle: Traction-Braking of an EV in Mountainous Terrain with Hybrid Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper discusses the advantages of upgrading the existing battery electric vehicle (BEV) with the proposed configuration of a hybrid energy storage system (HESS). A simple and low-cost configuration for a HESS in an electric vehicle (EV) is analyzed and presented for hilly-driving regions. The performance of the energy storage system (ESS) during hilly terrain traction/braking is enhanced by leveraging the electrical property of each source i.e. Li-ion battery and ultracapacitor (UC). The simulation results show that the UC acts as a source/sink for all the transients during acceleration/deceleration conditions in the hilly driving pattern. Further, the experimental results in this paper show the high electrical stress on the battery that needs to be taken care of during the vehicle traction/electrical braking. Also, there is higher energy recovery when UC is used along with a Li-ion battery in the simplified configuration.

articleTitle: A Versatile Reinforced Inverter Station Control Strategy for Hybrid HVDC-Based Offshore DFIG Wind Farm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A straightforward and effective power control approach for a hybrid-HVDC system linked to a DFIG-based offshore wind power farm that feeds a weak onshore grid is proposed. Real power generated from the wind farm is controlled by an LCC rectifier station at the sending end. It is efficiently transmitted to another VSC inverter station through the HVDC line under nominal onshore grid voltages. Nevertheless, the abnormalities in onshore grid voltage make the inverter station control tedious, as the power converter suffers from huge harmonic grid currents and power pulsations beyond permissible limits. To efficiently extract power from offshore DFIG and regulate active/reactive power at the onshore grid, a dynamic current control approach at the VSC inverter station via compensating current injection while minimising power oscillations, HVDC link capacitor voltage ripples and THD in the grid current instigated by voltage deviations in the onshore grid is proposed here. The performance of the hybrid HVDC system integrated offshore DFIG wind farm is validated for a 100km, 100kV HVDC link coupled to a 100MW DFIG wind farm via simulations on PSCAD/EMTDC software.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based State of Charge Estimation and Real-Time Battery Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Accurately estimating the state of charge (SOC) is essential for the safety and longevity of lithium-ion batteries in electric vehicles (EVs) but is challenging due to nonlinear battery dynamics, especially with online methods. With rising EV demand, efficient and consumer-friendly battery monitoring is needed. This work uses voltage and current sensors and an ESP32 development board to monitor terminal voltage and load current, displaying SOC on mobile phones via Bluetooth. However, SOC can not be displayed directly, as it can not be measured directly. To estimate battery SOC, terminal voltage and load current must be accurately estimated. The measured data is used to estimate battery SOC accurately using the Random Forest Regression (RFR) algorithm. The estimated SOC using the proposed method has been compared to the Simulated results to validate the estimation results. The results demonstrate that the SOC estimator provides sufficient accuracy and surpasses traditional artificial intelligence-based methods to create an affordable, user-friendly system for remote EV battery monitoring, enhancing performance and supporting wider EV adoption.

articleTitle: A Three-Winding Based Triple Active Bridge Converter for Multipurpose Electric Vehicle Charger
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) have zero emissions only if the batteries are charged by renewable energy sources. These days, a smart micro-grid is connected to the main grid and different types of renewable energy sources (such as solar, wind, and other energy sources) to reduce the load demand in peak times. Such a system enhances the quality of electricity, promotes renewable energy, and prevents pollution of the environment. Therefore, to balance and regulate power flows among renewable energy sources, electric vehicles (EVs), and the grid, an isolated hybrid multi-port converter is needed to charge EVs from a smart micro grid. A novel isolated multi-port triple active bridge (TAB) converter with multidirectional power flow control is proposed which is validated using PLECS Simulink-based platform. In this system, the solar PV operates at maximum power point tracking (MPPT) and continuously develops maximum power without a dedicated boost converter for MPPT. The PLECS/Simulink software environment is used to model the EV charger. A comprehensive discussion covering the modeling, implementation, and results is provided in this paper.

articleTitle: Fractional Order Relaxation Model for Supercapacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The suitability of Fractional Order (FO) models for representing the nonlinear charge/discharge dynamics of supercapacitors (SC) are well discussed in the literature. However, modelling of the rest time voltage variation due to charge redistribution and leakage with FO models are not addressed. The major challenge is the high computational burden associated with modelling the complete rest time dynamics with FO model. Conversely accurate characterization of a limited operating range can be possible with simple FO models. In view of this, a simplified FO relaxation model for characterizing the rest time voltage variation of SC is proposed. The model is derived considering all the nonlinearities associated with the voltage, current dependence, and residual charge effects. Further, it is simplified with various approximations derived from the operating range of typical applications and validated with experiments on several commercial SCs.

articleTitle: Shunt Active Power Filter Using Asymmetric Cascaded Multilevel Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Power quality conditioning is a critical issue in the current scenario due to the continuous increase in the proliferation of non-linear loads. This work presents an asymmetric cascaded H-bridge multilevel inverter for active power filter applications. In this topology, three H-bridges per phase are cascaded in series, with voltage sources in the ratio of 16:4:1. This voltage asymmetry results in a high-resolution output voltage, making it a promising converter for these applications. This topology has the potential to compensate low power factor and high harmonic load currents which makes it suitable for medium voltage and high-power applications. The reference current for compensation is calculated using the instantaneous p-q theory. The high-resolution output results in excellent performance in tracking the compensating current reference. A three-phase uncontrolled rectifier has been utilized as a non-linear load to introduce distortion in the grid current. Simulation results obtained from the MATLAB/Simulink environment demonstrate that the proposed topology has significant potential for active power filtering in medium-voltage and high-power applications.

articleTitle: A Single-Stage Grid-Following PV Inverter Featuring a Current Management System to Handle MPPT and LVRT with Fewer Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In order to guarantee stability and adherence to the rigorous grid protocols, the power grid requires improved grid support functionalities due to the growing integration of renewable energy sources, particularly solar photovoltaic (SPV) systems. This study introduces a novel single stage grid connected solar PV system (SSGCSPV) featuring a current control stage, designed to enhance low voltage ride through (LVRT) capability and optimize maximum power point tracking (MPPT) while minimizing the number of required sensors. The current management system (CMS) can be designed to adhere to any grid code requirements, ensuring stable and reliable grid integration even under fault conditions. Furthermore, the research explores and compares various MPPT techniques, evaluating their performances in terms of efficiency, settling time and reliability under dynamic environmental conditions under voltage control mode and current control mode. Results are presented with single stage converter operation with current control mode to improve the MPP efficiency, fast tracking avoiding the nonlinear DC link voltage control. Further, the DC link voltage is estimated instantaneously to cater the protection requirement of the converter under various fault scenarios.

articleTitle: Enhanced Canvasback Swarm Algorithm for Active Power Loss Diminution and Voltage Stability Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Enhanced Canvasback swarm (ECS) algorithm is based on the examining activities of the Canvasback and in order to expand the exploration capability, canvasback swarm algorithm has been integrated with gemsbok optimization algorithm. In the exploration section canvasback queuing around the food spring region and canvasback disperses in that specific region for searching the food. Canvasback completes the search after food springs are identified and canvasback will be positioned rendering to the accessibility condition of the food springs and fitness value computed in that location. Location changing during foraging and excavating behaviour of gemsbok has been considered in the design of the gemsbok optimization algorithm. Gemsbok has a high capability of tracking rain and identifies regions of vegetation in the foraging conditions. Gemsbok owns high skill in excavating to take rest in a particular place. Design of the algorithm exploration grounded on foraging procedure of the gemsbok and exploitation is modeled based on excavating ability of the Gemsbok. Enhanced Canvasback swarm (ECS) algorithm validated in IEEE 30, 57 systems.

articleTitle: Minimum Pulse Width Adjustment in Duties of SVPWM Technique for Synchronous Motor Drives Using a 3 Level NPC Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The following paper presents the analysis of the dynamics of the Synchronous Motor Drives (SMD) operated by the three level Neutral Point Clamped (NPC) inverter using the modified space vector modulation technique. The theoretical aspect of any PWM technique does not includes the time delay, rise time and fall time of the switching device involved in the process thus it fails to meet the minimum pulse width requirement of the switching device which is the minimum time required to produce the switching transition from one state to the other state i.e. ON to OFF and OFF to ON states. In Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation (SVPWM) technique as the dwelling time of each space vector can be calculated and the switches involved in the generation of that space vector can also be defined. Any switch whose duty time does not meets the minimum transitional requirement, a correction factor can be introduced in the duty of that switch to produce a successful transition from any state. This paper we introduce the modified SVPWM along with the basics of SVPWM to meet the minimum switching criterion, the application of this technique can be generalized to any drive or converter with solid state switches, here this technique is applied to the synchronous motor drives for the dynamics improvement.

Author Keywords: modified space vector pulse width modulation

articleTitle: Phase-Shift Control Analysis of a 25 kV DC Supply Utilizing Voltage Multiplier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper introduces an analysis of a phase-shift control technique for the generation of high DC voltage using a two-stage half-wave Cockcroft-Walton multiplier. In high-voltage applications, the phase shift technique edge over Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) due to its high voltage gain, ability to minimize switching losses with zero-voltage switching (ZVS), and capacity to generate a three-level voltage signal in contrast to PWM's traditional two-level signal. This approach effectively reduces stress on switching devices, enhances overall efficiency, and it also produces lower electromagnetic interference (EMI) due to smoother transitions. The stability under phase-shift control stability is challenging over the PWM method; however, its advantages make it suitable for high-voltage applications in air purification, microwave, and terahertz (THz) generation. The designed topology containing a five-stacked voltage multiplier is simulated to generate a voltage of up to 25 kV using a phase-shift controlled full bridge inverter circuit. The performance of the proposed phase-shift control strategy is verified on a miniaturized hardware prototype at a fixed load.

articleTitle: Impacts of Earth Fault on Neighboring AC Motor Drives in Isolated Neutral (IT) Grid Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to analyze the impact of earth fault in one drive on the other neighboring drives connected in a multi motor drives application supplied from an isolated neutral or ungrounded grid system. It has been found that if one drive has an earth fault on the motor side (named as ‘faulted drive’), the fault current finds a path to charge the DC link capacitors of neighboring drive (named as ‘victim drive’) through the coupling or common mode capacitors, especially if the drive is not enabled (i.e. idle condition). It is identified that this increase in the DC-link voltage (charge-up of DC capacitors of ‘victim drive’) depends on various parameters and operational conditions such as fault resistance, magnitude of supply voltage, switching frequency of faulted drive, common mode capacitance value, and capacitance of input cable. A detailed analysis and simulations have been carried out to understand the influence of these forementioned parameters on the DC-link voltage of the victim drive. A simple solution is also proposed to overcome the impact this earth fault on neighboring drives. The study has also been verified by an experimental test at system level.

articleTitle: Modeling and Design of Internal Energy Balance Controller with Circulating Current Suppression for Modular Multilevel Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper provides an in-depth investigation of the modeling and design of an internal energy balance controller for MMC in the context of a three-phase grid-connected converter. Given the inherent complexity of MMC's internal dynamics, this paper aims to address the critical challenges associated with the transient performance, including high circulating currents, which are prevalent under open-loop operation. The proposed energy balance controller has been designed to ensure that the energy distribution remains balanced across the submodules (SMs), thereby significantly enhancing the transient performance and reducing the circulating currents. A mathematical model of the energy balance controller has been developed, with a detailed analytical foundation for its implementation and design. The controller's performance is assessed through a simulation study in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Inertia Synthesis for AHO Controlled Converters in Smart Transformer Based Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The smart transformer (ST)-based low-voltage distribution systems have lower inertia, primarily due to the lack of rotating machines. This characteristic becomes critical when integrating high levels of renewable-based distributed generation (DG) units. The grid-forming (GFM) control mode in low voltage (LV) converters can apply either virtual synchronous generator or, droop control to coordinate with DGs. However, these control strategies are based on the phasor-domain, and synchronous steady-state needs to be well defined. On the other hand, the virtual oscillator (VO) control is a time-domain based decentralized GFM converter control technique and globally asymptotic stable. In this paper, a virtual inertia (VI)-VO control equipped with a proportional-derivative (PD) controller is pro-posed to generate a response comparable to that of a synchronous generator (SG) inertia. The impact of adjusting the equivalent VO control inertia constant is evaluated through simulation in MATLAB/Simulink software. The simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed VI-VO control enhances frequency characteristics like the rate of change of frequency (RoCoF) and frequency nadir.

articleTitle: Optimized DSSq Transmitter Coil-based Charging Pad Scheme to Mitigate Misalignment Issues for Wireless EV Chargers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The charging coils or pads are key components in inductive Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) technology. The offset between the transmitter and receiver pad positions causes a shift from the point of maximum flux linkage. This misalignment condition leads to a reduced coupling coefficient, thereby decreasing the power transferred to the battery load. To mitigate this issue, this paper proposes an optimised Double Set Square (DSSq) charging pad scheme for the transmitter. It is a combination of four right-angled triangular coils placed adjacent to one another. The first coil is connected to the third coil, and the second coil is connected to the fourth. The current excitation for the coils needs to be in quadrature to achieve an improved and wider flux profile around the charging pad, leading to enhanced tolerance for misalignment. An analytical formula to estimate mutual inductance and induced output voltage is derived for this design. Validation is performed using Finite Element Analysis (FEA) simulations on the Ansys Maxwell-3D platform. The proposed DSSq transmitter coil experimental design has been done and verified with simulated data. The coil has been designed for 80-90kHz operation and as per SAE-J2954 standards.

articleTitle: Coupled Inductor Based Regenerative Cascaded Multicell Converter for Drives with Reduced Transformer VA Rating and DC-link Capacitor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A regenerative cascaded multicell converter (CMC) is considered one of the most effective and reliable solutions for high-power medium voltage drives. In the existing regenerative CMC-based drives, multilevel voltage and high-quality current are achieved at the output side by connecting multiple cells in series. However, on the input side, the cells are effectively connected in parallel through the transformer, and their two-level operation results in a considerable amount of harmonics in the secondary winding currents, even with a filter inductor used in each cell. This increases the overall VA rating of the transformer. This paper proposes a modified regenerative CMC in which a three-phase active front-end rectifier (AFER) is used at the input side of each cell, and a coupled inductor is used instead of a normal inductor. The coupled inductor effectively suppresses the lower-order switching frequency harmonics from the secondary winding current while offering negligible reactance to the fundamental component. Hence, the overall size and cost of the transformer will be reduced. Due to the three-phase configuration, the cell capacitance is reduced. A simulation-based comparison study between existing and proposed regenerative CMCs is presented.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Driven Versatile Single In Dual Out NonIsolated Converter for Electric Vehicle Charging System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Grid-connected electric vehicles (EVs) are often powered by electricity from fossil fuels, which contributes to carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions during production. To promote a more sustainable approach, EV charging powered by renewable energy offers an environmentally friendly alternative to EV charging and transportation systems, known as “green mobility.” This research proposes a photovoltaic (PV)-assisted EV charging system using a non-isolated, single-input, dual-output electronic DC-DC power converter. It aims to provide a highly efficient and cost-effective charging solution by integrating renewable energy production directly into the EV charging infrastructure. This paper presents a novel design for a high-voltage gain, non-isolated DC/DC converter. This converter meets high conversion ratio requirements by combining a dual boost converter with a switched inductor configuration. The proposed converter operates in constant current mode (CCM) with an appropriate duty cycle and zero current in all switches and diodes. The proposed SIDO converter is designed in MATLAB/Simulink and tested in a laboratory environment with a hardware setup. This design offers many advantages such as a wide duty cycle range, low switching stress and losses, high efficiency, and high output voltage gain, making it suitable for a variety of applications.

articleTitle: Bidirectional DC-DC Dual-Active-Bridge Converter with Symmetric Bipolar Outputs Using Triangular Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This article presents a symmetrical bipolar output voltage-based DC-DC dual active bridge converter (DAB) using the triangular modulation (TRM) technique. In the proposed TRM, one arm of the high voltage (HV) side bridge is controlled using time-varying pulse width modulation (PWM), while the remaining arms of both the low voltage (LV) side bridge and the HV side bridge are controlled using time-invariant PWM. As a result of this switching strategy, the DC-DC DAB converter improves its soft switching performance, achieving 1) zero-current turn-on and turn-off for the devices operating on the LV side bridge. 2) zero-voltage turn-on for the devices on the HV side bridge operating with time-invariant PWM. 3) zero-voltage turn-on for the devices on the HV side bridge operating with time-variant PWM. The proposed TRM also ensures soft switching under all loading conditions with simple control, utilizing a single control variable that maintains a linear relationship with power. Simulation results, followed by experimental results of a scaled-down prototype of a 500 W system were developed using the TMS320F28335 for bidirectional electric vehicle DC charging system and EV-to-load applications, achieving an experimental efficiency of 94.7%.

articleTitle: Optimized Model Predictive Current Control for Enhanced Light Commercial Vehicle Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents the optimized Model Predictive Current Control (MPCC) for Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (IPMSM)-based Light Commercial Vehicle drives. This study enhances the conventional MPC approach by introducing a selection horizon of two control intervals, aiming to reduce the switching frequency in the TPTL inverter by maintaining optimal VVs across consecutive periods. The dual-framework MPC model efficiently controls motor variables while managing the trade-offs between dynamic performance and computational complexity. The efficacy of current THD in both conventional and enhanced MPCC is analyzed. The simulations are performed under torque and speed variations as well as regenerative braking scenarios. Finally, outcomes demonstrate notable improvements in system response and overall performance, validating the effectiveness of the enhanced control framework.

articleTitle: Two Stage Module Based Buck-Boost Converter for Cell Equalization of Series Connected Cells for Electric Vehicle Battery Pack Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a two-stage module-based active cell balancing circuit using a buck-boost converter is proposed. In this technique cell balancing is performed by considering the State of Charge as a balancing criteria. Further to explore modified buck-boost converter topology with inductor and switches being used for balancing adjacent cells. An existing work of two stage module based cell equalization topology is referred. Such topology is aimed at increasing balancing speed by targeting two cells simultaneously. The topology uses fewer components than traditional balancing circuit. Proposed cell balancing is simulated by MATLAB/Simulink. The efficiency and time required for balancing is evaluated. An SOC based control is proposed instead of voltage based control in the proposed topology. Further the efficacy of such circuit in dynamic condition i.e. charging and discharging is evaluated through simulation.

articleTitle: A Novel Control Technique for Dual Active Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel control technique for a dual active bridge (DAB) converter. The proposed controller is derived directly from the power expression without employing any averaging techniques. Conventional state-space averaging methods are challenging to apply to the DAB converter due to the zero integral value of the external inductor current over one cycle. This paper systematically develops a current controller specifically designed for the DAB converter. Simulation results for a 10 kW solar-based EV charging validate the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: FPGA Based Improved State-of-Charge Estimation Using Modified Coulomb Counting Method for Lithium-Ion Battery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A key feature for the protection and durability of electric vehicles is the State of Charge (SOC) monitoring. But the SOC can not be estimated directly. Inaccuracies in the battery model and parametric uncertainties are the issues that might result in inaccurate SOC prediction. Therefore, precise parameter estimation yields accurate SOC estimation. The Recursive Least Squares (RLS) estimation method has been employed to estimate the parameters of the battery, which has been used to model equivalent circuit model (ECM). An improved Coulomb counting method is used for SOC estimation of the battery. The Coulomb counting method has been improved by accurately estimating the initial SOC using the open-circuit voltage (OCV)-SOC relationship, and piece-wise linearizing the relationship increases estimation accuracy. The aims to develop and implement the proposed algorithm on a PYNQ-Z2 board for accurate and fast battery SOC estimation. The effectiveness of the proposed model in precisely estimating the SOC of lithium-ion batteries has been verified through simulations and real-time testing.

articleTitle: A Cyber-Resilient Control Scheme for AGC of Hydropower System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A cyberattack is designed to destabilize a system connected through a communication network. While ongoing research focuses on attack detection algorithms, it is crucial to have a robust control mechanism in place to address the possibility of undiscovered security compromise events persisting for a significant duration. Resiliency is particularly important for a controller engaged in automated generation control (AGC), since it must be able to function effectively even in abnormal conditions, without the option of shutting down operations. This research presents a novel method to assist hydrothermal power systems in dealing with network-related obstacles such as communication latency (CL) and attacks. We present a novel tri-parametric fractional controller (TFC) that combines the benefits of proportional-integral and proportional-derivative operations. This eliminates the requirement for extra control loops. The resiliency of suggested TFC is illustrated by performing simulation studies on benchmark attack models.

articleTitle: AC Short-Circuit Fault Detection and Isolation in Islanded Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper investigates AC short-circuit fault detection and isolation technique in islanded microgrid having grid-forming (GFM) and grid-following (GFL) converters. The study focuses on the impact of AC side faults on the DC side performance of the converters, analyzed through mathematical analysis and simulations. Asymmetrical faults induce second-order harmonics in the DC current, causing oscillations in it. During symmetrical faults, the DC side current experiences higher fault currents compared to an asymmetrical fault without oscillations. In case of GFL converter as operating in current control mode (CCM), it does not contribute to fault current, whereas the GFM converter handles the fault current independently due to voltage control mode (VCM). These results emphasize the potential for efficiently detecting and quickly isolating AC side faults using DC side current measurements, which simplifies fault management and enhances system reliability and resilience.

articleTitle: LCL Compensated Series Transmitter Array Based Inductive Wireless Charger for Multiple EV Charging Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a LCL compensated series connected transmitter coils array based wireless inductive charging system for multiple receivers which can charge several EVs simultaneously and independently. LCL compensation offers a constant transmitting coil current which neither depends on number of transmitting coil connected at its output nor on coupling and load resistance of a connected EV. A tuning capacitor is used in series with each transmitting coil to maintain resonance in the system. This makes system flexible to isolate the particular transmitting coil set which is not coupled with any receiving coil while other transmitting coils are supplying power to EVs. Relay switches are used to isolate the coil. This system adopts only a single inverter and common primary LCL compensation to excite all the series connected transmitting coil set which reduces number of passive elements in primary. Cross coupling of a coil with adjacent transmitter or their receiver coil is neglected. Simulation study is performed with an example of three transmitter system. Results shows that all channels are independent from each other. Output voltage and power from a channel is independent of coupling and load condition of other channels. The system operates at zero phase angle at input and transmitting coil current is constant irrespective of number of EVs connected in the system. To validate the system a scaled down experimental prototype is developed form 150V input to 75V output.

articleTitle: A Novel 9-Level Multilevel Inverter for Water Pumping System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In agricultural and residential applications where the grid power is unavailable, water pumping devices assisted by photovoltaic (PV) array are growing more popularity. The performance of a proposed multilevel inverter (MLI) fed induction motor water pumping system (WPS) is investigated in this research. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{V}/f$</tex> method is adopted for speed control of the induction motor in the single-stage WPS system. The proposed multilevel inverter with phase opposition disposition sinusoidal pulse width modulation (POD-SPWM) technique is employed to produce the reference voltage for the WPS system. Simulations are carried for the proposed system in MATLAB/Simulink platform. The system is tested under different test case conditions and are tabulated. The proposed MLI for water pumping is easy to use, needs less devices compared to traditional ones and produces optimal voltage and current waveforms with lower harmonics, which minimizes the need of filters.

articleTitle: Efficient Evaluation of Short-Circuit Faults in Active Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Short-circuit problems in unbalanced radial distribution networks have become more common as a result of distributed generation connectivity and smart grid advancements. An accurate and effective strategy for assessing these faults due to short circuits is presented in this study. In contrast to traditional methods, this approach uses relationship matrices that are created expressly to take use of distribution network's radial characteristics. Through the examination of variations in bus voltages, bus current injections, and branch currents during fault conditions, the suggested method formulates the analysis of various fault types. The accuracy of developed method has been validated on IEEE-123 bus modified test network by comparing the obtained results with PSCAD/EMTDC simulation results.

articleTitle: Optimizing EV Charging Power Quality with Enhanced PLL-Driven Active Power Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The widespread adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) globally, and their extensive integration into the distribution grid have led to major concerns regarding the quality of power and current in the system. An EV needs a charging station for its battery charging, and the harmonics created are due to the frequent use of power electronics devices. To overcome these harmonics and reduce reactive power, this paper implements a active power filter (APF) using a TPTL- NPC inverter with a dq method-based control strategy. Since APF has a highly sensitive to grid disturbances, raises the possibility of grid instability and power outages. Therefore, an enhanced PLL is used to continually monitoring frequency and phase angles and effectively suppresses dc-offset. Because its improved frequency tracking capabilities and mitigation of dc offset, allow reliable tracking of rapidly changing input frequencies, making it especially useful in dynamic situations. The system description, controller parameters for the APF, and system performance under various conditions are detailed. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the APF in compensating for reactive power and harmonics, demonstrating its utility in enhanced grid quality.

articleTitle: MRAS and $\alpha^{\prime}\beta^{\prime}-{}$ Framed SVPWM Based Modified FS-MPC for PMSM Drive Powered by Five-Level TF-Type Inverter for EV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The integration of space vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM) and finite set model predictive control (FS-MPC) is essential as it ensures precise motor control by improving voltage quality, reducing torque ripples, and enhancing the dynamic response of multilevel inverters (MLI)-based PMSM drives. However, the execution of SVPWM with a higher level is very complex due to the large number of space vectors and increasing complexity in dwell time calculations. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha^{\prime}\beta^{\prime}-{}$</tex> reference framed SVPWM is introduced to simplify the complexity and time burden by eliminating the necessity of trigonometric transformation and lookup table. Furthermore, it is simple and computationally efficient because the dwell time calculation is independent of voltage level. In addition, model reference adaptive system (MRAS) based sensorless control is employed for speed estimation to improve reliability and stability. The effectiveness of the proposed system is verified in various torque-speed scenarios on the MATLAB platform with a five-level TF-type inverter fed PMSM drive for sensorless speed control with MRAS and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha^{\prime}\beta^{\prime}$</tex>-reference framed SVPWM based modified FS-MPC. Finally, this hybrid control technique is functionally validated with a hardware prototype.

articleTitle: Double Boost Switched Capacitor Multi-Level Inverter with Modified PWM Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Switched capacitor-based multilevel inverters (MLIs) are increasingly appealing for renewable energy technologies because of their effective voltage amplification capabilities. The Double Boost Switched Capacitor (DBSC) approach attains the necessary voltage levels with less dependence on several DC sources by using capacitor voltage multiplication. Creating a high-gain MLI with a reduced number of components, such as fewer DC sources and switches, is a considerable technical challenge. This research presents an innovative nine-level inverter architecture using the DBSC principle, which substantially reduces the component count. The suggested architecture requires a single DC source, eight switches, and two capacitors to provide nine unique output voltage levels. The advanced inverter exhibits exceptional performance by producing high-quality voltage waveforms across diverse operating situations, enabled by an enhanced Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) approach. The Variable Frequency Alternate Phase Opposition and Disposition PWM (VFAPODPWM) method is used to improve operating efficiency. Extensive simulation evaluations are performed using MATLAB/Simulink to verify the efficacy of the suggested design.

articleTitle: Triple Active Bridge Converter for Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: To fulfill the growing demand for electric vehicles (EVs), new power conversion technologies are required to increase economy and performance. This study presents a novel Triple Active Bridge (TAB) converter intended for use in electric car applications. The TAB converter architecture exhibits significant gains in power density, efficiency, and control flexibility as compared to traditional single and twin active bridge converters. By combining three active bridges, the proposed converter allows for efficient energy management and bidirectional power transfer between the battery, auxiliary systems, and regenerative braking. The flexibility and convenience of switching between modes of operation of the converter enhance the system's overall dependability and adaptability. The converter's improved efficiency, lower switching losses, and improved thermal performance are shown by results from experiments and simulations. Sophisticated control techniques are employed to further improve power transfer, ensuring dependable and efficient operation under various load circumstances. The Triple Active Bridge converter has significant promise for future EV powertrains, furthering the cause of high-performance and ecologically responsible electric mobility, according to the study's findings.

articleTitle: An Effective Fault Detection Technique for Grid-Connected Electric Vehicle Charging Station
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The widespread integration of electric vehicle (EV) charging stations (CS) into the existing utility grid is giving rise to numerous power quality and protection challenges, significantly impacting load performance at both large and small consumer ends. This phenomenon is escalating as the transition from internal combustion engine (IC) vehicles to EVs gains momentum, driven by their inherent advantages. EV chargers utilize power electronics to convert AC power into DC power for battery charging from the grid. However, this conversion process, facilitated by high-frequency switching converters, introduces harmonics into the grid, consequently deteriorating the power quality of grid line currents. These injected harmonics lead to electrical and thermal overloading of distribution transformers, thereby compromising their lifespan. Additional issues include excessive current draw from the grid, imbalance between demand and supply, and voltage fluctuations. Apart from power quality issues, there is a need to develop a fast fault detection algorithm to protect the charging station supply equipment when a fault occurs either grid side or on the downstream DC side. This paper presents an instantaneous power-based fault detection algorithm to detect the fault in grid-connected EV charging stations for Grid vehicle (G2V) and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) mode of operation.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Approach with Optimizing Current Harmonic Regulation in IPMSM Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents the comprehensive analysis and effectiveness of the dead time effect of VSI, and digital control delay for IPMSM drives. Furthermore, investigates the decoupling of current harmonics and the compensation of initial phase angles of voltage harmonics. The influence of voltage harmonics on current controllers and the impacts of digital control delays via the use of sophisticated control methods. The presented current harmonic regulator suppresses the challenges of voltage harmonics and digital control delays in VSI-driven IPMSM drives. The simulations are performed under torque and speed variations as well as regenerative braking scenarios. Outcomes demonstrate significant improvements in system per-formance, validating the effectiveness and finding satisfactory system response under various operating conditions.

articleTitle: Predictive Phase-Shift Control of Interleaved Quadratic Buck Converter as the Power Supply of the Electrolyzer in Green Hydrogen Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a study on using the interleaved quadratic buck converter (QBC) to power an electrolyzer system for green hydrogen production. The interleaved operation of QBC offers several advantages, including high current output, reduced current ripple, lower input and output voltage stresses, and improved reliability, making it an excellent choice for high-power applications. The finite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) is proposed to control the QBC and regulate the system variable. FCS-MPC enables the control of the phase-shift required for interleaved operation, which is achieved through an extra term added to the cost function. Simulation results confirm the precise regulation of the output voltage and the reduction in output current ripple while effectively handling system disturbances.

articleTitle: A High-Voltage Bipolar Pulsed Power Generator Based on a Three-level F-type Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Bipolar Pulsed Power Generators (PPGs) have transformative capabilities in solving medical, residential, and industrial challenges by providing innovative and efficient solutions. This paper introduces a novel high-voltage bipolar PPG utilizing an F-type inverter integrating a front-side boost converter (FSBC). The proposed PPG produces output pulses with high voltage gain when operating at low input DC voltage. The operating principle and circuit structure are discussed in detail. The operation and performance of the proposed generator are presented in two different versions: single-module and multi-module. Multilevel pulses with higher voltage amplitude can be obtained using the multi-module version. The effectiveness of the proposed bipolar PPG is verified by simulation and real-time hardware-based examination of a scaled-down laboratory prototype.

articleTitle: Traction to Auxiliary Power Transfer in Modular EV Drivetrain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper eliminates vehicular auxiliary power module hardware by introducing a novel traction to auxiliary (T2A) power transfer topology for modular multilevel converter (MMC) based electric vehicle (EV) drivetrain. Utilizing neutral connection to the motor and implementing carrier phase shift sinusoidal PWM, the proposed system integrates auxiliary power transfer functionality directly into modular drivetrain by leveraging zero sequence subcircuit. It does not affect dq-axis operation of the motor. Key components added in the proposed topology are passive, including compensation capacitor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{C}_{\boldsymbol{r}}$</tex>, a diode bridge rectifier and filter capacitor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{C}_{\boldsymbol{f}}$</tex>. Simulation results showcase traction to auxiliary (T2A) battery charging.

articleTitle: Identification of Li-Ion Battery Parameters Using Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: There is an increase in the demand for Li-ion batteries particularly in Electric Vehicles (EVs). Identifying the Li-ion battery parameters will help in estimating the state of charge (SOC) accurately. In this paper, Li-ion battery is represented with one RC equivalent circuit. The charging/discharging behaviour of the generic battery in MATLAB-SIMULINK is used to get the relation between open circuit voltage and SOC. The circuit parameters are determined using neural network. The performance of the identified parameters is verified with the generic battery in MATLAB.

articleTitle: A Finite Control Set Based Model Predictive Control for Reducing Inductor Current Ripple in Dual Active Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Inductor current ripple in a dual active bridge (DAB) converter increases voltage stress, core loss, and electromagnetic interference (EMI). This paper proposes a finite control set-based model predictive controller (FCS-MPC) for reducing inductor current ripple in a DAB converter system. The FCS-MPC reduces the inductor current ripple by controlling the primary side switching with a sinusoidal reference current without affecting the power transfer requirement. It has several benefits like no modulator requirement, faster response, better transient and steady-state performance.

articleTitle: Active Balancing of LiFePO4 Battery Modules using Phase-Shift Type DC-DC Converter for High Voltage Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A battery management system (BMS) for electric vehicles is a crucial component that ensures optimal battery pack performance, safety, and longevity. Monitors and manages various aspects of the battery, such as the state of charge, state of health, temperature, and voltage, to prevent overcharging or over-discharging, which can damage the battery. By the estimation of SoC and/or the battery cell/module voltages, active balancing circuits with isolated DC-DC converters enable power exchange between the battery modules for battery balancing. This paper describes a hybrid active battery balancing procedure. The proposed balancing technique includes the implementation of dissipative passive balancing at cell-level and non-dissipative active balancing at the module level. This enhances efficiency while maintaining the cost-effectiveness of the overall battery system. The active balancing part of the proposed system includes an isolated multiport bi-directional half-bridge DC-DC converter with a closed-loop phase-shift control. The proposed phase control algorithm involves generating phase shifts based on the extent of module voltage imbalances, the largest voltage disparity, and the set value of the maximum phase shift. The proposed technique is validated using simulation and experimental analysis.

articleTitle: Peak Current Mode Controlled Phase Shifted Multi-Phase Buck Converter for 48V/72V EV Battery Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Multi-phase buck converters have applications in server power supply, telecom power supply, and electric vehicle (EV) battery charging. The present work is focused on implementation of peak current mode control of multi-phase buck converter with phase shift operation. Peak current mode control algorithm has been programmed in micro-controller TMS320F28379D using its comparator subsystem (CMPSS) and ePWM modules. Here, three individual buck converter are operated from same DC input with 120° phase separation between their current references. Inductor current has been sensed using hall effect current sensors to achieve peak current mode control. Light electric vehicles which uses battery bank of nominal voltage 48V/72V may require to be charged at higher charging current rate for short duration. The charging current rate will depend on battery voltage, state of charge and user's necessity. This work evaluates an IGBT based standard three phase bridge circuit which is used as multi-phase buck converter.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Drive-Cycle-Based Analysis of Hairpin vs Stranded Windings for EV
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Winding analysis is crucial for enhancing electric vehicle (EV) performance as it directly impacts motor efficiency, thermal management, and torque production. By examining different winding technologies, this study aims to identify optimal designs that improve overall motor performance and reliability. In this paper, a comprehensive analysis of hairpin and stranded windings for highway and urban drive cycles is conducted for two interior permanent magnet synchronous motors rated at 150 kW for EV. By integrating two distinct drive cycles, the research aims to provide a detailed assessment of efficiency, losses, and torque characteristics for each winding type. Additionally, the machines are evaluated at critical operational points, considering peak currents, and torque under the specified drive cycles. This drive cycle-based analysis provides a holistic view of the performance, reliability, and efficiency of hairpin and stranded windings, facilitating better design decisions.

articleTitle: A Four-Port Buck-Boost Converter with Dual-Input and Bipolar-Output
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This article explores a novel Zeta-derived four-port DC-DC converter circuit designed for hybrid energy integration. The proposed circuit offers substantial voltage gain and enhanced versatility, supporting both buck and boost operations in both power flow directions. Its bidirectional functionality and inherently balanced bipolar voltage output make the converter perfectly suited for integrating energy storage components such as batteries and ultra-capacitors with a neutral point clamped inverter in electric vehicle drive train or bipolar DC microgrid. Notably, there are no voltage restrictions for connections at the input port. The paper elaborates on the operating principles and provides steady-state simulation results to confirm the performance of the proposed topology across various operational modes.

articleTitle: Rule-Based Controller Design for Frequency Control in Islanded Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a Cohen-Coon rule-based controller designed for frequency regulation in islanded microgrids, crucial for maintaining stability during grid disconnections. The microgrid integrates diverse renewable and conventional energy sources, including PV panels, wind turbines, and biodiesel generators, alongside energy storage systems. The study focuses on transforming the microgrid's higher-order model into a simplified first-order plus dead time model and optimizing controller tuning using the Cohen-Coon method. Real-time simulations on Opal-RT validate the controller's performance under varying load conditions and intermittent renewable energy inputs. Results demonstrate the controller's effectiveness in minimizing frequency deviations, affirming its robustness for ensuring stable power supply in dynamic microgrid environments.

articleTitle: Switch Fault Diagnosis in Single Switch DC-DC Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In many applications, the dependability of the DC-DC converter's operation is essential. Thus, fault-tolerant converters are desired. Prior to fault tolerance, fast fault diagnosis is required. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a simple and new fault signature-based detection technique that can identify open-circuit and short-circuit switch faults in DC-DC converters. The suggested method for fault diagnosis is based on signal processing. It is demonstrated here that diode current contains significant information to identify switch faults. Fault detection is achieved by processing diode current as well as gate switching state information. The switch fault diagnosis technique utilizes the same sensors used for control, obviating the need for additional sensors. The fault detection is obtained in less than one switching time period. The obtained simulation and hardware results validate the suggested technique.

articleTitle: Adaptive Model Predictive Control of Dual Output Three-Level Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive model predictive control (A-MPC) strategy for a three-level dual output voltage (TLDOV) converter. The proposed control addresses the growing demand for robust, multi-objective control solutions in multi-output multilevel inverters. It has a fast transient response, straightforward implementation, and can handle non-linear constraints like finite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC). The proposed A-MPC is immune to performance degradation due to sensitivity to system model inaccuracies and parameter variations, which impacts the performance of FCS-MPC. A mathematical model of the TLDOV converter is developed, and A-MPC is utilized to control two output voltages independently while maintaining DC-link voltage balance, irrespective of load fluctuations. The system's performance is validated through Matlab/Simulink in constant and dynamic frequency conditions, with its robustness tested against sudden load changes.

articleTitle: Direct Hill Optimization for the Efficiency Maximizing Flexible Power Point Tracking of a PV Array under Partial Shading
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The flexible power point tracking (FPPT) is the recent trend to control the power output of the photovoltaic (PV) array as per a user specified power reference command. As the power reference line may intersect a multi-modal power-voltage curve at two or more operating points, the FPPT control under partial shading has to face an additional challenge of finding out the best operating point apart from avoiding the local peak blockage. The operating point at the highest voltage level is preferable as it reduces the thermal stress on the array converter by maximizing its power conversion efficiency. An efficiency-maximizing FPPT based upon a metaheuristic optimization algorithm was already proposed in the literature. However, as a metaheuristically implemented power tracking procedure leads to vigorous power oscillations. A direct hill optimization procedure to assist the conventional sweeping-based FPPT is proposed in this paper. The proposed direct hill optimization is similar to the global maximum power point search procedure, but is aimed at finding the hill that contains the most energy-efficient reference-line power point. Simulation results are produced to demonstrate the power tracking time improvement because of the direct hill optimization Instead of a metaheuristic power tracking.

articleTitle: An Improved Approach for Design of Inductors with Air Gaps
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Inductors play an essential role in the design of power electronic converters. Typically, the cores selected for high-current applications are built with air gaps. However, introducing an air gap results in fringing, making the design challenging. The extent of fringing depends on the air gap length and cannot be captured using a single equivalent circuit. This paper presents an improved approach for the design of inductors with air gaps. The proposed approach is based on a metric that signifies the accuracy in modeling the effect of fringing. In addition, the proposed approach also reports an optimization algorithm for the design of an inductor that accounts for different constraints. The inductance designed using this approach is compared with the existing methods and the models from the FEMM software. The proposed algorithm is validated experimentally using a small boost converter setup.

articleTitle: Wide Speed Range Operation of PMaSynRM for Electric Vehicle Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper discuss about the control algorithm of a PMaSynRM drive for wide speed range operation. The control technique comprises of Maximum Torque per Ampere (MTPA) operation to the base speed followed by flux-weakening operation, till the motor reaches the desired speed of operation. The chances of demagnetizing the air gap flux completely at higher operating speeds is also taken into account through the Maximum Torque per Voltage (MTPV) control during flux weakening.
