The non-linearity of the motor due to saturation effects are also incorporated in the control for superior performance. The performance evaluation of the proposed control is done in MATLAB/Simulink for dynamic changes in load and speed. A hardware prototype of the proposed MTPA control is also developed and results are evaluated.

Author Keywords: Permanent Magnet Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Motor (PMaSynRM)

articleTitle: A Transformerless Quadratic DC-DC Boost Converter Based on Switched-Capacitor Structure with Reduced Switch Voltage Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A transformerless Quadratic DC-DC Boost converter based on a Switched-Capacitor Structure (QBSCS) has been proposed in this paper. Due to the non-ideality of components, the duty ratio limitation of a conventional Quadratic DC-DC Boost converter (QBC) restraints the voltage gain. The QBSCS enhances the voltage conversion ratio while maintaining continuous input current and a common ground shared between the input and output. The switch configuration in the proposed QBSCS reduces the voltage stress across the switches while maintaining high voltage gain. A comprehensive mathematical analysis is presented for each mode of operation, assuming that the proposed QBSCS operates in Continuous Conduction Mode (CCM). The proposed converter has been compared with the existing converters based on the nature of input current, conversion ratio, switch voltage stress, and total component count. The QBSCS converter is simulated in MATLAB Simulink in closed-loop control and verified under various operating conditions, and corresponding simulation results are shown to validate its performance.

articleTitle: Comparative Effects of Gate Pulse Shifting on CCM/DCM Boundary Current in CI-SIDO Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The demand for various DC voltage levels has neces-sitated single-input multiple-output (SIMO) systems, efficiently replacing various single-input single-output (SISO) converters. Among these, single-input dual-output (SIDO) converters are notable. This paper focuses on coupled inductor single-input dual-output (CI-SIDO) buck, boost, and buck-boost converters. There are two distinct operating modes of DC-DC convert-ers: continuous conduction mode (CCM), where the inductor current stays above zero for the entire switching period, and discontinuous conduction mode (DCM), where the current falls to zero before the switching period concludes. Converters are typically designed for CCM, simplifying control by making the input-output voltage relationship load-independent. However, converters may enter DCM at light loads, making the voltage relationship load-dependent. Analyzing the CCM/DCM boundary is crucial for maintaining CCM operation. Existing methods for determining boundary conditions for SISO DC-DC converters focus on calculating CCM/DCM boundary conditions, where the average inductor current at this boundary determines the critical inductance needed for CCM operation. Lowering the boundary current value broadens the load range for CCM and reduces the required critical inductance. Relative gate-pulse shifting is introduced to minimize inductor current ripples in CI-SIDO converters by time-shifting gate pulses without additional circuitry. However, its effect on CCM/DCM boundary currents has not been explored. This paper investigates boundary inductor currents in CI-SIDO converters by relatively time-shifting gate pulses. The impact of gate pulse shifting on CCM/DCM boundaries in CI-SIDO buck and buck-boost converters is examined, and a comparison of critical inductances for the same boundary currents is presented for all three converters. The analysis is verified with MATLAB/Simulink simulation results.

articleTitle: Dynamic Inductance Model for Synchronous Reluctance Motor Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A dynamic inductance (DYI) model for sensorless control of Synchronous Reluctance Motor (SynRM) drive in low-speed regions is proposed. The model is analyzed in the abc frame and estimates the rotor position without using any mechanical sensors. The effectiveness of the DYI model in estimating the rotor position is validated through simulation results. The proposed DYI model addresses the challenges of rotor position estimation in low-speed regions.

articleTitle: A Seven-Level Triple Boost Common Ground Inverter Without H-Bridge
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In solar photovoltaic (PV) systems, inverters without transformers are extensively accepted because of their high-power density, decreased <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{dv}/\text{dt}$</tex> stress, affordability and enhanced performance. However, leakage current through the ground is a primary issue with transformer-less inverters. This study introduces a modified 7-level common-ground (CG) transformer-less inverter without an H-bridge and with a reduced number of components. It employs switched capacitors (SC) with a single source input to generate a seven-level output, achieving a threefold voltage gain and eliminating ground leakage current via the CG connection. The SC voltages are balanced naturally in each cycle, avoiding the need for sensors or complex controls. The inverter's performance is validated through MATLAB/Simulink simulations and experimental testing, including thermal modelling in PLECS to evaluate efficiency and power losses. Simulation and experimental results confirm the working of the proposed topology.

articleTitle: Experimental Studies on Speed-Dependent Vibrations of a 30,000 rpm Switched Reluctance Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The absence of current-carrying conductors or permanent magnets on the rotor makes the switched reluctance machine (SRM) a strong candidate for high-speed applications. This paper presents experimental vibration measurements on a 30,000 rpm SRM at various speeds under no load, conducted by mounting two accelerometers-one on the bearing housing and the other on the external housing. The SRM is run at speeds ranging from 1,000 rpm to 30,000 rpm, and the vibrations captured by the accelerometers are analyzed in the frequency domain to obtain the dominant frequencies at various operating speeds of the machine. The obtained dominant frequencies are related to the natural frequencies of the machine components, as well as the rotational frequency and the frequency of electromagnetic excitation (radial force). At lower speeds, the natural frequencies of the machine components are observed to be dominant, while at higher speeds, it is primarily the speed or radial force frequencies and their harmonics that prevail. The RMS acceleration increases with rotor speed, but the vibration is significantly higher at certain intermediate speeds when the natural frequencies of the machine parts–namely the stator, cooling jacket, and rotor assembly–are excited by speed or radial force excitation. The dominance of the rotational frequency component with increasing speed indicates the importance of proper dynamic balancing of the rotor in high-speed SRMs.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode Observer Based Predictive Torque Control of PMa-SynRM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This article explores the implementation and comparative analysis of Sliding mode observer (SMO) based Model Predictive Torque Control (MPTC) for Permanent Magnet Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Motor (PMa-SynRM) versus conventional Model Predictive Torque Control. The proposed SMO-based MPTC strategy aims to enhance the performance and efficiency of PMa-SynRM by eliminating the need for mechanical sensors, thus reducing system complexity and cost. The conventional MPTC method, while effective, relies on precise sensor data for optimal performance, which can be a limitation in specific applications. This paper presents an SMO-based sensorless control algorithm that leverages state estimation techniques to accurately predict and control the torque and flux linkage of the PMa-SynRM. Through extensive simulations, the effectiveness of the sensor-less MPTC in maintaining robust performance under various operating conditions is demonstrated. The results indicate that the sensor-less approach not only matches but sometimes surpasses the conventional MPTC in terms of dynamic response, efficiency, and robustness. This research underscores the potential of sensor-less control methodologies in advancing the performance and applicability of modern electric machines in Electric Vehicles.

Author Keywords: Permanent Magnet Assisted Synchronous reluctance motor

articleTitle: Non-Linear PID Based Power Quality Improvement Using Single-Phase Shunt Active Power Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a simple single-phase shunt active power filter (SAPF) control technique. The proposed control technique can improve power quality (PQ) issues like power factor (PF) and harmonics mitigation. The SAPF is comprises of a single-phase voltage source inverter with coupling inductance. Mostly, the PQ issues are related to load currents; hence, proposed control schemes utilize modified load currents under various loadings, and a hysteresis band comparator is used to generate a triggering pulse for SAPF. A nonlinear PID (NPID) controller has been used to regulate the DC voltage of SAPF. The system is tested for different types of loads, including linear load (LL), nonlinear loads (NLL) and a combination of linear and nonlinear loads (NLLL). Simulation is done in a Matlab/ Simulink environment, and the results are presented. The results validate with the lesser transient response time, PF correction and lower THD satisfying IEEE 519–2022.

articleTitle: Planar Magnetics Based Onboard Electric Vehicle Charger with Auxiliary Supply
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are equipped with a main battery pack (MBP) for traction purposes and an auxiliary battery pack (ABP) to power the onboard auxiliary systems. Traditionally, the onboard charger (OBC) charges the MBP, and via the auxiliary power module (APM) connected to the MBP, ABP gets charged. To minimize the size of passive components on the OBC, higher switching frequencies are preferred. A planar transformer, which can operate at these higher switching frequencies and has a lower profile, is chosen for improved performance. This paper explores a charger design in which a tertiary coil is inserted between the planar coils to charge the ABP. The evaluation was conducted through simulations.

articleTitle: Low Ripple Predictive Torque Control of MLI-Fed Induction Motor for Marine Propulsion Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents an improved model predictive torque control (MPTC) approach with reduced torque and flux ripples capability for multilevel inverter-fed motor drives in marine propulsion systems. The control strategy takes the average trajectories of the control variables in the prediction process to enhance model accuracy and minimize computational errors. This reduces torque and flux prediction errors, leading to decreased torque and flux fluctuations. Additionally, a Heun-based model is also developed for flying capacitor voltages to mitigate voltage ripples. Simulation studies are conducted on a four-level inverter-fed motor drive to validate the effectiveness of the proposed MPTC and its performance is compared with the existing MPTC method.

articleTitle: FPGA Based Digital Controller for Two Stage On-Board EV Charger
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) based digital control system of two stage (AC-DC; DC-DC) on-board Electric Vehicle charger for achieving boost power factor correction, constant current-constant voltage (CC-CV) and zero voltage switching (ZVS) operations with single stage voltage and current controller. Conventional on-board chargers, which are used for EV battery charging has serious issue of drawing peaky input AC current and extreme current ripples in battery charging current profile. Therefore, the conventional EV chargers have adverse effects on utility grid, low power factor, EMI effect and life hazard for the EV batteries. An on-board EV charger must have following characteristics such as unity power factor operation, galvanic isolation, CC-CV Charging Operation, fast charging, dynamic stability and low switching losses. In order to include these key features in an on-board battery charger, a two-stage charger design and various control operation using FPGA-based digital board are discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Commutation Torque Ripple Reduction in Open-end Winding BLDC Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This article introduces a two-level torque hysteresis-based direct torque control (DTC) strategy for a dual inverter-fed three-phase BLDC motor drive (BLDCMD) with open-end stator windings, incorporating a commutation torque ripple mitigation technique. The voltage space vectors generated while the inverters operate in 120-degree and 180-degree conduction modes are utilized to implement the DTC. An analysis of the torque ripple indicates that employing three-phase conducting voltage space vectors during the commutation interval in the DTC scheme substantially reduces commutation torque. Furthermore, the proposed method uses a unipolar-based switching scheme for torque control, which decreases dv/dt compared to a bipolar switching scheme. The motor's electromagnetic torque is maximized by utilizing a two-phase conducting voltage space vectors for torque control during the non-commutation interval. The proposed scheme is validated through simulations using MATLAB-Simulink software and experiment on a laboratory prototype.

articleTitle: Third Harmonic Injection with Carrier-Reassignment PWM for a Nine-Level Grid Connected CHB Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Carrier-based pulse width modulation (PWM) techniques are widely employed in cascaded H-bridge (CHB) multilevel inverters due to their computational simplicity and ease of implementation. However, the widely used level-shifted PWM (LSPWM) causes extreme power imbalance across the modules of the CHB inverter, leading to device over-stressing and premature failure. To address this issue, carriers can be re-assigned to different modules over one or multiple cycles in so-called CarrierReassignment PWM (CRPWM) techniques. In particular, a four-quadrant CRPWM technique (Type-A) results in near-perfect power balance across the CHB modules. In three-phase systems, third harmonic injection is a well-known technique to improve DC bus utilization, increase the number of levels in the line-to-line voltage, and enhance power quality by reducing the total harmonic distortion (THD). This paper presents the adaptation of the CRPWM techniques, combined with third harmonic injection, for improved DC-bus utilization and enhanced module power balance in a three-phase grid-connected CHB inverter. Analytical and simulation results show the superior performance of the Type-A CRPWM technique in achieving near-perfect power balance while optimizing DC-bus utilization. The paper also compares the performance of LSPWM, FIFO-CRPWM, and Type-A CRPWM both with and without third-harmonic injection, in a three-phase grid-connected nine-level CHB inverter operating at unity-power factor under closed-loop dq-controller.

articleTitle: Power Quality Enhancement of Five-Level Converter Using Floating H-Bridges of Voltage Ratio 4:1/2:1/4
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This work presents a way to improve the power quality of a three-phase five-level converter by cascading it with two floating H-bridges of voltage ratio 4:1/2:1/4. The proposed configuration enhances the power quality by producing a seventeen-level output voltage waveform and thirty-three levels in line voltage waveform. In this paper, the operation of the proposed converter is explained including various switching states and capacitor voltage balancing scheme. The performance of the proposed converter is assessed in simulation studies carried out in MATLAB/Simulink environment. The evaluation involves the use of a multi-carrier level-shifted PWM technique and a two-level hysteresis controller for voltage balancing of the capacitors.

articleTitle: Bi-Level Optimization Framework for Energy Management in Networked Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The global energy sector is transforming significantly, driven by the need for an efficient and sustainable generation with the goal of net-zero carbon emissions. Microgrids (MGs) have therefore risen to the challenge by facilitating the decentralization of power supply and consumption. This paper proposes a Bi-Level Optimization approach to promote optimal decision-making in Networked Microgrids (NMGs) by leveraging the real-time data processing capabilities of edge-fog devices. Furthermore, the study seeks to optimize both independent MG and NMG, in a bid to achieve cost optimization. To accomplish this, the framework utilizes two optimization strategies: an internal Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Programming (MINLP) optimizer within the microgrids to minimize costs and optimize energy source utilization at the MG level, and an external MINLP optimizer at the fog level to handle energy transactions between the MGs. The simulation analysis on Australian grid data demonstrates that this framework effectively decreases operational expenses by efficiently managing energy use inside and between MGs, improving cost effectiveness by 19.5%.

articleTitle: Transition and Fault-Tolerant Scheme for Single-Phase Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Being a critical component of modern systems and in many machine-critical applications, reliability of power electronic converters, particularly inverters is of paramount importance. The reliability in single-phase inverter can be improved by employing redundant leg, module, etc. Redundancy (leg/module) utilises additional switches and connecting devices to provide fault tolerance for semiconductor faults. However, in a conventional fault-tolerant inverter, the redundant leg is inactive during normal/pre-fault operation, indicating the under-utilization of the redundant leg. Thus, the conventional fault-tolerant inverter needs to be modified to utilize the redundant leg in the normal as well as the post-fault conditions. This needs a highly effective transition scheme which can transform the usage of the redundant leg on occurrence of a fault. This paper investigates the potential timings of fault occurrence and their impact on the transition scheme. The detailed analysis is implemented and tested on the hardware prototype of a single-phase inverter.

articleTitle: Dual Virtual Inertia Control of Interlinking Converter in Hybrid Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a dual virtual inertia control (DVIC) for the interlinking converter (ILC) in a hybrid microgrid (HMG). The AC and DC section control scheme includes primary and secondary controls. The primary control utilizes virtual synchronous generator (VSG) control, while the secondary control restores the frequency and voltages of the AC and DC sections via a proportional-integral (PI) controller. In the interlinking (IL) section, the proposed control incorporates virtually coupled emulated dual virtual synchronous machines (VSMs) on the ILC. These dual VSMs regulate the active and reactive power of the ILC. The proposed control enhances the frequency nadir and rate of change of frequency (ROCOF) on the AC side or the DC voltage nadir and the DC side rate of change of voltage (ROCOV), depending on the ILC virtual inertia value. The control also enhances the AC voltage nadir and ROCOV. Simulation studies are performed and compared with the traditional method to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control under transient conditions.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Linear Electromagnetic Actuator for Automobile Active Suspension System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The article presents a design topology of an electromagnetic actuator using Finite Element Analysis primarily for applications related to vibration control and linear motion in automobile suspension systems. This proposed topology features an innovative arrangement of three-phase windings and permanent magnet arrays to reduce ripple, enhance average output force, and improve efficiency and force density by optimizing the coil arrays and their sequence around the actuator axis. Geometrical modifications in the translator and stator iron, including flux guides and notches, efficiently utilize space and guide flux lines to prevent leakage and reduce the actuator's mass. Additionally, the shapes of winding slots and permanent magnet shields are optimized for better performance. The active suspension system with the designed actuator is analysed using the full vehicle model with 7 degrees of freedom. The designed electromagnetic actuator with look-ahead preview control can replace the vehicle's pneumatic or hydraulic, or conventional passive suspension system.

articleTitle: Fast Charging of Electric Vehicles Using a Multi-Winding Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A medium voltage grid connected fast charging architecture for electric vehicles is proposed in this paper. The proposed architecture uses a custom designed multi-winding transformer that has one primary winding and several isolated secondary windings. The secondary windings are connected in such a manner that they form two group. One group consists of a delta connected winding and two delta polygon connected windings such that the line voltages of these winding has a shift of ±20° with respect to line voltage of the primary winding. These three secondary windings are connected to three-phase bridge rectifiers, whose outputs are cascaded to form a necessary part of an 18-pulse converter. The cascade connection of DBRs forms a combined DC bus for fast charging of electric vehicles. Irrespective of number of charging vehicles, grid current drawn by this converter has a very low THD. The second group consists of delta connected secondary which is connected to voltage source converter. The voltage source converter is connected to large battery energy storage and allows bidirectional power flow between grid and battery energy storage,power flow from battery energy storage to vehicles connected to the combined DC bus. The proposed architecture provides a low cost fast charger that has bidirectional power flow capability and uses well-established multi-winding transformer for electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Supercapacitor Voltage Prediction Using a Dynamic Fractional Order Parameter Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The accuracy of the model for the analysis of supercapacitor dynamics is critical for its application. Traditional models often fail to capture supercapacitor's nonlinear dynamics and complex behaviors, such as charge redistribution and leakage currents. This study addresses these limitations by incorporating real-time parameter estimation during various operational phases, including the charging, discharging, and rest periods. The experimental setup included multiple SC cells and precise measurement tools to capture the terminal voltage under constant-current conditions. By utilizing only 10each stage, the model parameters were optimized, and accurate voltage predictions for the subsequent stages were achieved. The proposed methodology significantly reduces computational complexity while maintaining high fidelity in SC management, making it suitable for electric vehicles and renewable energy systems applications.

articleTitle: A Novel High-Gain Non-Inverted Voltage-Lift Switched-Capacitor DC-DC Step-Up Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper addresses a novel high-gain non-inverted voltage-lift and switched-capacitor (HGNIVLSC) based DC-DC step-up converter having a common grounding between the source and the load, a low inductor current ripple, and continuous input current benefits for integration with renewable energy sources (RES). The proposed topology steps up the low voltage of the photovoltaic (PV) array using voltage-lifting and switched-capacitor techniques with reduced device count, low voltage stress, and current stress. The proposed HGNIVLSC converter is analyzed in ideal and steady-state to determine the voltage gain, voltage stress, and current stress on power semiconductor devices in continuous conduction mode (CCM), as well as the boundary values of the energy storage elements. Finally, the proposed topology verifies its performance using the dSPACE1104 controller by hardware implementation, having the input voltage supply of 25V and regulated output voltage of 200V, having a nominal output power of 200W of the designed prototype.

articleTitle: Inspecting Cascaded Boost Configuration Linking LVDC and CDC Bus in DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: To enhance the reliability and uninterrupted power supply of direct current (DC) microgrid, a generic practise is to connect the low voltage DC (LVDC) bus of individual households to the community DC (CDC) bus using power converters with high voltage gain ability. The cascaded connection of boost converters is an apposite choice for this application. However, multiple switch sequence as well as switching frequency operation of the power stages make the modelling analysis ravel. Moreover, existence of right half plane zeros in the required transfer functions of control to output variables governs the controller design process. This paper makes an effort to simplify the design analysis by incorporating the averaged switch model in the modelling procedure. An averaged small signal model (ASSM) is designed for the cascaded power structure considering inductor ripple information and ramp compensation slope for the mixedsignal peak current mode control algorithm. The derived model is verified with simulink circuit model(SCM) considering different switching sequence and switching frequencies in operation. A detailed controller design process and stability analysis is practised on the power topology. A laboratory prototype is developed to analyse the functionality of designed controllers form the derived model with consideration of steady state and transient operating conditions of the converters.

articleTitle: Edge Computing Enabled Battery State of Charge(SoC) Estimation Using TinyML Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Redox flow batteries (RFBs) are electrolyte-based batteries that have become a research hotspot due to their modular nature and decoupled power-energy characteristics. Household and microgrid environments extensively utilize RFBs as storage systems. The nonlinear chemical nature of RFBs hinders the modeling process, estimation of critical parameters like State of Charge (SoC), and consequently, overall energy management. The current methods in the literature use computationally complex multi-physical models that are unsuitable for deployment at the edge. Therefore, this study focuses on developing a resource-optimized machine learning-based SoC estimation model fit for deployment on an ESP32-based edge device. The study also outlines and enumerates the experimental setup for two types of RFBs: vanadium-based (AVRFB) and zinc bromide-based (ZBRFB), its data preprocessing steps, and the edge deployment process. Additionally, model quantization has also been targeted to reduce computational requirements. Using a dynamically quantized model, the devised framework achieved a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^{2}$</tex> score of 0.975 for AVRFB, performing inference in 1.72 seconds. In the case of ZBRFB, the SOC estimation model achieved a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^{2}$</tex> score of 0.818 with the float32 quantized model, outputting inference in 3.18 seconds.

articleTitle: Modelling and Simulation Analysis of Innovative Offshore Wind Energy Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: India faces critical energy challenges and ambitious climate targets that necessitate innovative and sustainable solutions. This study explores the modeling and analysis for 10 MW offshore wind energy plant that integrates green hydrogen generating unit. By harnessing the synergy between these technologies, both energy efficiency and sustainability can be enhanced. This work focuses the modeling and detailed analysis of offshore wind plant considering pitch angle control with constant speed operation of permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) for varying wind speed. The simulation analysis of wind energy conversion system (WECS) has been carried out using MATLAB R2023a Simulink, in which various results are obtained. In this analysis, the feasibility of wind energy generation up to 10 MW capacity is explored which can be easily integrated with the electrolyser plant for green hydrogen generation. Finally, it is observed that the findings contribute to the development of more efficient and sustainable offshore wind energy systems, capable of meeting future energy demands while reducing environmental impact.

articleTitle: Control and Implementation Aspects of Totem-Pole Power Factor Correction Circuit in Digital Domain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A front-end power factor correction (PFC) circuit is usually employed in the ac to dc power conversion stage to maintain unity power factor. Digital signal processor (DSP) for controlling these circuits are becoming popular because of their advantages, such as flexibility, reproducibility, and fast development time. In digital implementation, delays such as sampling delay and modulation delay are present. In digital implementation, delays such as sampling and modulation delay are present. Sampling delay is caused by analog to digital (ADC) conversion, and modulation delay is caused by the uniformly sampled nature of the pulse width modulator. These delays can significantly impact the performance of the controller if not considered during the design stage. This paper designs the controller, including these digital delays. Also, the de-link voltage has a ripple with a frequency equal to twice the grid frequency, superimposed over the average de value due to a power mismatch between the ac and de sides. The controller should only respond to the average dc value, as fluctuations in the ripple voltage could impact the overall control performance. A digital filter eliminates this ripple voltage from entering the control loop. The totem-pole PFC circuit is fabricated to test the performance of the controller under various conditions, such as step change in de-link voltage reference and input voltage variations, such as voltage sag and swell.

articleTitle: Grid Forming Control of Star Connected Cascaded H-Bridge STATCOM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In modern power systems, maintaining voltage sta-bility, enhancing power quality, and ensuring reactive power support are crucial, especially with the growing incorporation of renewable energy sources and distributed generation. Static syn-chronous compensators (STATCOMs) are crucial for mitigating these challenges. Using modular multilevel converters (MMCs) as STATCOMs enhances reactive power compensation and voltage regulation. Among various MMC-STATCOM topologies, the star connected cascaded H-bridge (SC-CHB) is favored because of its simpler architecture, lower voltage stress, fewer components and cost-effectiveness. Traditional SC-CHB STATCOMs oper-ate in grid-following (GFL) mode, which is inadequate under weak/unbalance grid or isolated operation due to reliance on grid for phase angle acquisition. Grid-forming (GFM) control, mimicking synchronous generators, provides autonomous volt-age and frequency regulation, crucial for grid stability with high renewable energy penetration. Implementing GFM control in MMC-based STATCOMs, particularly SC-CHB STATCOM, poses challenges such as voltage balance across the H-bridge modules (HBMs), stability during disturbances, and fast dynamic response. This paper explores GFM control implementation for SC-CHB STATCOM, addressing aforementioned challenges under different test case scenarios like lag/lead reactive power compensation, unbalance load etc. Finally, a hardware prototype of 370 V/± 5 kVAR, 7-level 3-phase SC-CHB STATCOM has been built to validate the proposed GFM control.

articleTitle: Minimization of Torque Ripple in Dual Inverter Fed High-Power Wound Rotor Induction Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Dual inverter fed wound rotor induction motor (DIWRIM) has gained popularity in various medium voltage high power industrial motor drive applications. To cope with high switching energy losses in voltage source inverters, switching frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(f_{sw})$</tex> is restricted below <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$750Hz$</tex>. This results into high distortions on motor line currents which leads to high peak-peak ripple on electromagnetic torque. This paper proposes a carrier interleaving based technique for minimization of peak-peak torque ripple in DI-WRIM drive. The motor drive is operated with rotor flux oriented (RFO) and V/F control technique from stator and rotor sides, respectively. Both stator and rotor VSIs are operated with synchronized sine-triangle (SST) pulse width modulation (PWM) techniques having same pulse numbers. Optimized interleaving angle is determined and proposed for minimization of peak-peak torque ripple under full-load condition over complete range of fundamental frequency. Performance of motor drive is validated in terms of stator and rotor side currents under zero and optimal interleaving angles. Peak-peak torque is also computed under no- and half- load conditions at different interleaving angles to confirm the validity of proposed optimal interleaving angle. A <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$250kW, 400V, 50Hz$</tex> 4-pole, 1: 1, WRIM is used for validation of theoretical findings through simulations.

Author Keywords: Double Inverter Fed Wound Rotor Induction Machine

articleTitle: An Improved Model Predictive Current Control for Medium-Voltage Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: High current ripple leads to higher torque ripple in medium-voltage (MV) motor drive systems, and poses significant drawbacks like accelerated vibration and noise, increased wear and tear, and poor efficiency. This paper introduces an improved model predictive current control (MPCC) strategy to minimize the current ripple, thereby reducing torque ripple in multilevel inverter (MLI) fed MV motor drives. In the proposed method, the corrector stage is incorporated to enhance the prediction process, thus effectively minimizing computational errors. This approach further improves current harmonic performance and lowers flying capacitor (FC) ripples, leading to reduced torque fluctuations. To validate the efficacy of the proposed MPCC, simulation studies are conducted on a four-level inverter fed MV motor drive and its performance is compared with the conventional MPCC method.

articleTitle: Improved Boost Type-ANPC 5L Inverter Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This letter proposes an Improved boost type ANPC (IBT-ANPC-5L) Inverter topology combining a frontend dc-dc converter with a switched-capacitor module. The proposed topology is realized using switches of low voltage rating, unlike its existing counterparts. Design equations for the capacitors and inductors of the proposed topology are included in the paper, and a detailed loss analysis is performed. The proposed topology is compared in detail to a recently proposed one in terms of cost, component counts, and efficiency. Using a laboratory hardware prototype, the performance of the proposed topology such as modulation index, load variations, etc, is verified and validated at 400W with an efficiency of~97%.

articleTitle: Charging Area Based State of Health Estimation of Lithium-Ion Battery Pack For EV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This research paper presents an innovative approach for estimating the State of Health (SoH) of Lithium-Ion Battery Packs used in Electric Vehicle (EV) applications. The proposed methodology introduces the concept of Area between Capacity and Charging Time (ACCT) as a metric for quantifying battery degradation. By analyzing the area between the capacity and charging time curves obtained from battery testing data, the ACCT method offers a holistic assessment of battery health, capturing both capacity fade and aging effects. Through extensive experimental validation using real-world EV battery datasets, the effectiveness and accuracy of the ACCT method are demonstrated. The results indicate that the ACCT-based SoH estimation approach outperforms conventional techniques, providing valuable insights for battery management systems and facilitating the optimization of electric vehicle performance and longevity. This work extends the support to the long term beneficial change needed in the field of monitoring and the assessment of the Battery health, and hence supporting the development of sustainable and resilient electric transportation systems.

articleTitle: A Three-Port Converter for Integrating Solar PV-Battery Systems with DC Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a new three-port DC-DC converter circuit tailored for integrating solar PV and battery systems with DC loads, enabling single-stage energy conversion. The proposed design outperforms traditional non-isolated multi-input DC-DC converters by offering superior voltage boosting while utilizing fewer inductors. It operates flexibly as a single-input dual-output, dual-input single-output, or single-input single-output system, adapting seamlessly to varying energy flows between sources and loads. Additionally, it ensures maximum power point tracking for the solar PV source and maintains output voltage regulation through a multi-objective control architecture based on competitive mode selector. Steady-state and dynamic simulation results are provided to validate the performance of the converter across multiple operating modes.

articleTitle: A Combined Control for Efficiency Improvement of Integrated Three-Port Dual Active Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In conventional single phase shift (SPS) control for the dual active bridge (DAB), the efficiency at light load is poor. While operating in dual-phase shift (DPS) control, the light load efficiency improves to some extent, however, the current stress at heavy load becomes higher than in SPS control. Importantly, the DPS control suggested in the literature does not converge to SPS control near heavy-load conditions. This paper proposes a novel approach for a three-port DAB converter by synergistically combining the techniques of SPS and DPS. Importantly, it provides a clear demarcation between the SPS and DPS regions of operation to achieve a high-efficiency profile over a wide range of operations. It covers the detailed analysis of different modes of operation based on the zero-crossing instant of leakage inductor current. In addition, an efficiency and current stressed comparison is provided among the SPS, DPS, and combined control approach for various load conditions. The operation of the proposed technique is also validated with a 2.6 kilowatt prototype.

articleTitle: Grid Power Quality Management with SCR-Based CSI Fed Medium Voltage Induction Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a strategy for managing reactive power demand in grid-connected, Silicon-Controlled Rectifier-based Current Source Inverter (SCR-CSI) fed hybrid Medium Voltage (MV) induction motor drives. SCR-based CSI topologies are known for their reliability, cost-effectiveness, and high-power handling capabilities, making them useful in high-power drive applications. These drives are controlled by changing the firing angle of the rectifiers, which impacts the reactive power demand on the grid, particularly during low and mid-speed operating regions of the drive. The paper proposes a power quality management strategy that adapts with the speed of the drive, keeping the reactive power demand on the grid at an optimal level and ensuring a near-unity fundamental power factor across a range of operating speeds. In conventional methods, the maximum reactive power demand at the grid is 385 kVA in 1 MW drives, which has been reduced to 243 kVA with the employment of two rectifiers and 114 kVA with four rectifiers. The methodology based on theoretical and mathematical modelling is presented. The control strategies are validated through simulation on the PLECS platform.

articleTitle: DC-AC Conversion in PV Based Series Modular Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper explores a DC-AC photovoltaic (PV) based modular multilevel converter (MMC) aimed at optimizing solar energy conversion. With the increasing demand for renewable energy solutions, there is a pressing need for advanced conversion technologies that enhance energy output while ensuring system reliability. The modular multilevel converter architecture supports scalable and flexible configurations, effectively integrating multiple photovoltaic modules. By generating a multi-level output waveform, the converter minimizes harmonic distortion, improving the quality of the resulting AC voltage. The implementation of a derived MMC topology reduces the number of semiconductor switches required, leading to a more compact design and lower component count, which enhances costeffectiveness and simplifies maintenance. Real-time monitoring of capacitor voltages and arm currents enables dynamic adjustment of submodules, allowing the system to optimize performance in response to changing solar irradiance conditions. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate the converter's efficiency across various load scenarios. In summary, this DC-AC PV-based modular multilevel converter represents a significant step forward in solar energy conversion technology, offering enhanced efficiency, modularity, and reliability for future photovoltaic systems.

articleTitle: Design and Control of Three Phase Active Front End Converter fed Isolated Voltage Balancer for Bipolar DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: An efficient and reliable bipolar DC distribution system is gaining traction in a variety of DC microgrid applications due to the development of distributed energy systems and energy storage. This paper addresses voltage imbalances and power flow difficulties in a recently introduced Bipolar DC Microgrid (BDM). A novel control approach is introduced for an isolated full-bridge-type voltage balancing circuit fed by a three-phase active front-end converter. The subsequent section also includes design instructions. The inherent advantages of the proposed isolated voltage balancer using the Phase Shifted Full Bridge (PSFB) converter and the Buck-Boost Bipolar Balancer are the galvanic isolation and high voltage gain due to the transformer turns ratio, making it suitable for high voltage and high power applications. Moreover, soft switching is achieved by employing phase-shift control for the primary active bridge, thereby enhancing conversion efficiency. A dual loop PI control of the voltage balancing converter and a traditional dual loop <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$dq$</tex> control of the active front-end converter are presented to reduce voltage imbalances in a bipolar DC microgrid. The imbalance in bipolar DC buses in microgrids occurs due to uneven loading, unequal integration of renewable sources, and distributed energy storage elements. Extensive simulation studies have been conducted to validate the proposal in various disturbance scenarios.

articleTitle: Enhanced VSG-Based Control for Parallel Grid-Forming Converters in an Autonomous Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper introduces a virtual synchronous gen-erator (VSG)-based control scheme with governing action tai-lored for grid-forming converters within autonomous micro-grids (MGs). A comparative analysis is conducted between conventional droop control and the proposed VSG control. In autonomous mode, conventional droop control exhibits limited inertia and damping, leading to sharp changes in converter output frequency during load disturbances that may violate rate of change of frequency (ROCOF) regulations. In contrast, the proposed VSG controller is engineered to deliver superior performance. By incorporating governing action, the proposed VSG-based control introduces virtual inertia, effectively minimizing power oscillations and reducing settling time in autonomous MGs. This approach ensures smoother frequency transitions and enhances overall MG stability. Unlike conventional droop control, which employs a proportional controller with a low-pass filter, the VSG controller dynamically adapts its active power control loop to disturbances, closely emulating the behaviour of synchronous generators. Comprehensive simulations conducted in MATLAB Simulink R2023b validate the efficacy of the proposed VSG-based control. These results affirm that VSG-based control surpasses conventional droop control in managing frequency stability and fortifying the resilience of autonomous MGs.

articleTitle: Analysis and Experiments on a Lab-Fabricated Inductor of Improved Composite Material Core in a High Frequency Synchronous Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents the development and use of a magnetic composite material of low relative permeability (barium ferrite (BaFe)) in an inductor core of a GaN-based DC-DC Synchronous Buck Converter (SBC). The details of the core development from the commercially available BaFe powder are provided. Experimental and analytical investigations have been conducted to validate its performance. The estimation of parameters is presented as a part of the material performance validation exercise duly. The external characteristics (F <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B-H$</tex> loop) of the material are obtained from the internal characteristics <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(M-H)$</tex> through appropriate conversion. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B-H$</tex> characteristic is then used in finite element (FE)-based simulation. The inductor is tested for large ripple values over much smaller average current, while the converter output is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$12 V, 15W$</tex> (nominal), at 500 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$kHz$</tex>. The analytical and experimental results are found to be in good agreement.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization of FCL in DC Microgrid using Meta Heuristic Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The primary objective of this study is to simplify the complex model of a looped-type DCMG and conduct an indepth analysis to derive expressions for currents in the switching devices, specifically insulated-gate bipolar transistors (IGBTs), following the occurrence of faults. Additionally, the work aims to develop an optimization model for FCL placement. This model considers a multi objective function optimization goal involving the fault current as well as the inductance value. The optimization model that has been simulated using PSCAD operates within the constraints of resistance and inductance values of the FCL, while ensuring a balance between protective measures and operational efficacy within the DCMG.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Type I and Type II Buck-Boost Partial Power Converter for EV Fast Chargers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This work introduces a reconfigurable topology for AC-link partial power converters (PPC), intended for use as high-frequency transformerless regulated DC-DC converters in fast charging stations for electric vehicles (EV). This new topology allows an AC-link PPC to be reconfigured so that it works as a type I PPC during boost mode and as a type II PPC during buck mode. The converter is able to operate across a wide output voltage range, making it compatible with the different battery voltage configurations found in the electric vehicle industry. The converter is reconfigured using four additional switches. Depending on the operating mode, these switches can be turned on or off to achieve the desired topology. In a type I PPC configuration, the input is connected in parallel, and the output is connected in series with the battery. In a type II configuration, the input is connected in series, and the output is connected in parallel with the battery. This paper presents an analysis of converter operations and control for EV charging systems operating at 400 V and 800 V, incorporating both operation validation and efficiency metrics derived from simulations.

articleTitle: A Compact Low Cost and High Efficiency Switched-Capacitor Boost Multilevel Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Switched capacitor multilevel inverters (SC-MLls) are highly popular for their ability to produce high-quality output voltage with less total harmonic distortion (THD). The main feature of this topology is that it require a low number of power switches (seven switches) compared to the existing 5-level inverter topologies. Apart from the dual voltage gain, self-voltage balancing of capacitor voltage without any auxiliary control technique along with reduced voltage stress has been the main advantages of this topology. A comparative assessment of the recent published topologies with the proposed SC-MLI inverter is presented to emphasize the features of the proposed inverter. Finaly, The experimental results are obtained from a 1.0kW prototype setup. The proposed topology tested under various modulation index and load conditions.

articleTitle: Effective PLL-Based Control Technique for Seamless Transition from Islanded Mode to Grid-Connected Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This study presents a practical phase-locked loop (PLL) based control system that uses minimal PI Controllers to ensure a smooth transition from islanding mode to grid-connected mode for an AC microgrid. The developed controls are specifically designed for converters operating in droop control mode during islanded operation and grid following control mode when connected to the grid. The system also effectively manages transient issues on the connected load during the island-to-grid synchronization process. The paper provides a comprehensive design approach for the developed controls and demonstrates their practicality and effectiveness through simulation studies and validation using Control hardware in a loop system comprising a 500 kW Grid Forming converter and a 500 kW Grid Following Converter operating in parallel.

articleTitle: Anti-Resonant Tank-based Wireless Charging of EVs for Ultra-Wide Output Voltage Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Wireless chargers are becoming increasingly popular for charging electric vehicles (EVs) due to their autonomous potential, safety, and convenience. For the fast adoption of EVs, a wireless charger installed at public parking spaces should be compatible with different types of EVs (2-wheeler, 3-wheeler and, 4-wheeler) and support various battery voltages within the operating frequency range of 79–90 kHz. Conventional wireless chargers employ a three-stage topology to achieve a wide output voltage range, typically incorporating a buck-boost converter at the charger or battery side, which increases the system's cost. This paper proposes a single-stage topology utilizing series-series compensation with an LC anti-resonant tank-based wireless charging system for EVs, achieving an ultra-wide output voltage range from 150–900 V. The LC anti-resonant tank provides the ultra-wide output voltage range by nullifying the voltage gain at the anti-resonant frequency. Furthermore, the incorporation of an LC tank and frequency modulation control technique enables a wide zero voltage switching area throughout the voltage range, which reduces switching losses in the converter. The analysis and design of the proposed system have been conducted and verified through MATLAB simulation for the output voltage range of 150–900 V. Finally, a 3-kW prototype is developed to transfer power over a 15 cm air gap, achieving maximum efficiency of 90% in simulation and 87% in hardware.

articleTitle: A Voltage-Based Charge Balancing Algorithm to Mitigate the Charge Recovery Effect of Li-ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The design and control of the active charge balancing (ACB) architecture are essential functionalities performed by a battery management system (BMS) in lithium-ion battery (LiB) applications. In many applications, the charge balancing control of the battery packs is implemented using state of charge (SOC) estimation methods. A similar approach can be implemented for cell-level balancing operations. However, such SOC-based balancing control introduces the cost of additional hardware for the ACB circuit and more computational cost on the controller. Therefore, voltage-based charge balancing algorithms have been preferred in the literature to overcome the cost and complexity. A limitation is not considering the voltage recovery effect, a dominating phenomenon observed with a high charge rate of the balancing current. An efficient charge-balancing algorithm has been proposed in this study, considering the charge recovery effect of each series cell. The balancing operations are performed on a 4S8P battery pack configured using ICR 18650-26j commercial Li-ion cells. An experimental results are presented to validate the proposed balancing strategy.

articleTitle: Fault-Tolerant Operation of Hybrid Modular Multilevel Converter for MVDC Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The utilization of unipolar half-bridge submodules (HBSMs), remains the most cost-effective option to date, but they fail to block DC-side faults. Therefore, incorporating a combination of unipolar and bipolar submodules (full-bridge) can be advantageous, as this configuration not only effectively manages DC-side faults but also enhances operational performance. In this context, a Hybrid Modular Multilevel Converter (HMMC) is considered for medium-voltage direct current (MVDC) applications. Due to more switch count in MMC, it is more prone to faults. This paper proposes a fault-tolerant algorithm specifically designed for addressing open-circuit switch faults in a HMMC. The algorithm takes into account various open switch fault scenarios, including single switch fault, multi switch fault, single SM fault, and multi SM faults. In conventional MMCs, such faults increase the stress on SM capacitors. However, the proposed fault-tolerant algorithm allows the converter to operate under fault conditions without escalating the stress on the SM capacitors. This proposed algorithm ensures that the stress on SM capacitors remains consistent during both normal operation and fault conditions. The effectiveness of the proposed technique is validated through MATLAB simulation results.

articleTitle: Efficient Dual-Input DC-DC Converter Design for Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper examines integrating fuel cell stack and battery pack to power permanent magnet brushless DC motor (PMBLDC) motor in fuel cell electric vehicles (FCEVs) through various converter topology designs and performance evaluations. In the conventional FCEV power-train, a dual converter system is used that consists of a boost converter for the fuel cell and a converter with bidirectional capabilities for the battery in regenerative braking. The feasibility of employing a dual input single output(DISO) converter with bidirectional features is investigated in the paper to streamline power conversion. Different configurations of dual input single output converters and a few topologies with bidirectional features are examined, and a comparative analysis is conducted to assess their performance and compatibility with the BLDC motor. Subsequent simulations integrate the selected converter topology with the BLDC motor, utilizing fuel cells and batteries as energy sources. Performance evaluations are conducted under diverse operating conditions, including efficiency, reliability, and motor compatibility. The proposed converter enables increased compactness, extended driving range, reduced complexity, and reduced vehicle cost.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control of Solar PV and Battery Converters Using Droop Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a droop control based finite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) of a hybrid energy system. The hybrid energy system consists of a solar photovoltaic (PV) and a battery energy storage system (BESS) connected to a DC bus. The droop control is designed to control DC bus voltage depending on the state of charge (SoC) of BESS and load. When the BESS is not fully charged, the BESS converter regulates the DC bus voltage, while the PV converter operates at maximum power point tracking (MPPT). In case of BESS is fully charged and MPPT power is greater than load power, the PV converter regulates the DC bus voltage considering <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I-V$</tex> droop control. The proposed method provides good transient response to load power variation for single stage DC-DC converter. The simulation studies are performed in MATLAB/Simulink to show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Author Keywords: Finite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC)

articleTitle: Adaptive Harmonic Compensation Strategy Based Frequency Lock Loop for Grid Connected PV System Under Abnormal Grid Voltages
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This article presents a novel adaptive harmonic compensation strategy utilizing a frequency lock loop (FLL) for a single stage grid connected photovoltaic (SSGCPV) system under abnormal grid voltages. The proposed compensation strategy integrates an adaptive phase improved multiresonant (APIMR) current controller to effectively suppress grid current harmonics in the presence of distorted grid voltage caused by nonlinear loads. Moreover, an enhanced second order generalised integrator (ESOGI) FLL is integrated into the APIMR controller to enhance synchronization with the grid and eliminate frequency oscillations. The proposed compensation strategy not only addresses oscillations in active and reactive power during unbalanced grid faults but also enhances the frequency adaptability of the SSGCPV system in response to grid frequency variations. Furthermore, the proposed control strategy eliminates the need for parks transformation, thereby reducing the computational burden on the system. Realtime digital simulations using OPAL-RT OP4510 in a software in the loop environment for a 15 kW SSGCPV system are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed compensation strategy.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Controlled Level-3 Reconfigurable Battery Charger for Future Electric Transportation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The offboard charger signifies a pivotal advancement in electric vehicle (EV) growth, facilitating fast charging while offering flexibility and scalability. Nonetheless, existing off-board chargers encounter various challenges related to scalability and design complexity, degrading their performance over a wide voltage range. This paper presents a modular and reconfigurable offboard EV charger for charging a wide output voltage range of EVs. It is controlled through a new distributed finite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) architecture. The proposed charger can operate in star and delta configurations, optimizing the charging process for low-voltage and next-generation high-voltage battery pack vehicles. A key benefit of the proposed charger and its controller is the wide operating voltage range with allowable voltage and current ripple. The performance of the proposed charger and its controller is evaluated through simulation studies in the MATLAB Simulink platform. The results demonstrate the unity power factor operation and ability to charge from a single-phase power supply without compromising power rating in the absence of a three-phase supply, making it an efficient and scalable solution for future EV charging infrastructure.

articleTitle: Integral Dual Fractional Derivative Frequency Controller for Thermal Power Plant with Delay
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Time delays in power systems cause phase lag and impair closed-loop stability, which worsen the performance of load frequency control (LFC). So as to accomplish increased resilience, this work suggests an analytical design of an integral dual fractional derivative (IDFD) controller with a single tuneable parameter for an isolated time-delayed microgrid. The controller's sole tuning parameter is intended to accomplish a satisfactory trade-off between resilience and performance. The findings of the simulation confirm that the suggested design is more resilient than some of its counterparts. In the face of nonlinearities, abrupt changes in load, and uncertainties in system parameters, the competency of proposed controller is assessed.

articleTitle: A Modified Dual Switch High Gain Boost Converter with Control Liberty for PV Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This study introduces a dual-switch non-isolated boost converter (DSNIBC) which increases the voltage gain without operating non-isolated boost converter (NIBC) at high-duty ratios by adding a diode-switch pair and switched Inductor to NIBC. The insertion of an additional switch also rise the Liberty of Control (LoC) for both inductor current and output voltage simultaneously using control variables <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_{1}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_{2}$</tex>, in comparison to NIBC. A capacitor is also connected across the load to reduce the ripples. The proposed converter with continuous input current and low ripple is well-suited for renewable energy applications due to its ability to respond quickly to changes in input conditions. The characteristics of DSNIBC are supported by simulations and developed by mathematical derivations. For example, according to the simulation results, voltage gains rise from 5.67 to 15 when the duty ratio of the additional switch in DSNIBC goes from 0 to 0.1.

articleTitle: Estimation of Parasitic Inductances of a Two-Phase Interleaved Buck Converter with Coupled Inductors Through Detailed Experiments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents the experimental determination of parameters, especially the leakage inductance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(L_{lk})$</tex> of coupled inductors (CIs) due to the leakage flux of the CIs <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\phi_{lk})$</tex>, in a two-phase interleaved synchronous buck converter (ISBC) with a 200 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> input feeding a 75 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex>, 1.5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> load at a nominal rating of 110 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex>. The CIs have been designed to operate at a frequency of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$100\ kHz$</tex>. It is identified that the performance of the CIs are heavily influenced by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{lk}$</tex> and the coupling coefficient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(k)$</tex> of the CIs. A simple, yet novel method of determining <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{lk}$</tex> from the experimental waveforms has been proposed. Besides <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{L}_{l k}$</tex> of the CIs, the parasitic inductances <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(L_{pr})$</tex> in the actual hardware prototype contribute to the total inductance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(L_{uc})$</tex> that does not couple the two phases of the CIs. This distorts the voltage waveform across the CIs. An analytical exercise is carried out to evaluate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{pr}$</tex> from the experimental waveforms and then validated through circuit simulations. Further, the various losses in the CIs have been calculated from the experimental results as a part of the performance validation exercise. The experimental and simulation results are found to be in good agreement.

articleTitle: Trajectory Tracking Controller Design for a Ball-Plate Balancing System Using ANFIS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The Ball-Plate Balancing (BPB) problem is a widely known nonlinear control problem, and numerous control system solutions have been proposed to solve it. The BPB is a nonlinear system with the under-actuation characteristic that makes control harder to accomplish trajectory tracking objectives. Therefore, in this article, Adaptive Neuro Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) based closed loop controller is designed for precise trajectory tracking control objective by the ball, along with the dynamics model of BPB. In addition to the proposed controller, a comparison study is carried out with the existing conventional Proportional Integral and Derivative (PID) controller. In order to validate the proposed ANFIS-based controller, tracking simulations have been conducted using two distinct trajectories: a circular path and a Lissajous pattern.

articleTitle: A Non-Isolated Multiport Converter with Wide Input Voltage Range to Enhance Ultracapacitor Utilization for Electrified Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: To enhance the utilization of the ultracapacitor (UC) energy in a battery-UC based hybrid energy storage system (HESS) for electrified vehicles (EVs), the UC needs to be discharged up to its minimum operating terminal voltage, resulting in higher duty cycle operation of the power converter with excessive high current at source side. This tends to cause instability in the close loop control and necessitates high current rated magnetic and switching components of the converter. Addressing to this, a non-isolated bidirectional multiport converter is proposed, which is capable of ensuring deep discharging of UCs without increasing the operating duty cycle or component ratings of the converter. The proposed converter offers the unique feature of energizing the inductor co-operatively through both UC and battery in the same switching cycle, during certain transient events of peak power delivery or regenerative energy recuperation. This eventually facilitates in extending the range of UC operation, thereby ensuring improved dynamic performance of EV. The operation of the proposed converter is validated through simulation and preliminary experimentation performed in a laboratory scale hardware prototype.

articleTitle: Optimal Design and Performance Analysis of Model Predictive Control for EV Charging Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The proposed work mainly focusses on the implementation of finite control set based model predictive control technique for the second-stage OBC (On-Board Charger) to control the power flow from the main grid to an Electric Vehicle (EV) battery. Conventionally, Power converters can be controlled by certain traditional techniques, such as direct power control and proportional integral control. Although these conventional techniques exhibit satisfactory performance under steady state operation but heavily suffers during dynamic operating conditions. Therefore, in the proposed work a model predictive control (MPC) has been implemented where the switching states have been adaptably estimated as per the dynamic operating conditions. The design and performance analysis of MPC has been thoroughly presented and simulated in MATLAB/Simulink environment. The simulation results have been extensively presented under different operating conditions to validate the effectiveness of proposed control technique.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Novel Bi-Directional High Gain DC-DC Converter for Renewable Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Bidirectional DC-DC converters (BDCs) are of significant importance in applications involving batteries and this article presents a BDC arrangement with two inductors, four capacitors, and six switches. A comprehensive analysis of the proposed converter is presented, including the derivation of the voltage transfer ratio (VTR) during both Step-Up and Step-Down modes. Additionally, the lowered voltage stress on MOSFETs leads to reduced switching losses. The derived transfer ratios are validated through circuit-level simulations. The converter is specifically designed for a 300 W, 350 V high-voltage side and a 48 V low-voltage side, operating at a frequency of 50 kHz. Simulation results demonstrate the converter's performance, with a notable improvement in VTR compared to other converters employing quadratic VTR.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Automatic Synthesis of 2- DOF QFT for Unstable Maglev system
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper focuses on the position control of Unstable Magnetic levitation (Maglev) systems using Quantitative Feedback Theory (QFT) approach. The robust QFT controller and prefilter are obtained using enhanced simultaneous automatic synthesis (SAS). The proposed SAS design stabilizes the levitation of the steel ball in the air, precisely tracking the position of the ball in the presence of the system uncertainty. The simulation results is analysed and compared with the controllers in the literature like LQR-PID-Feed forward (FF), PIV-FF controllers, fractional-order enhanced model reference adaptive controller (FOEMRAC). The superiority of the proposed SAS design is shown by the better tracking performance and less controller effort.

articleTitle: An Agile Solution to Estimate the Capacity of Virtual Energy of Refrigerator Using ANN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Integrating a renewable energy source (RES) into a distribution network is challenging due to its intermittent nature. One of the methods to address the issue is a smart energy storage (SES) system, which is achieved by a stationary battery system (SBS). SES can be reached by using demand response management (DRM) when the loads work with long thermal constants. However, the SBS faces life cycle issues, unsteady charging and discharging, high cost, and sizing complexities. In lieu of SBS, temperature-controlled electrical loads (TCLs) like air conditioners, refrigerators, water heaters, and similar appliances with virtual energy storage (VES) capacity can be considered in the context of SES. During peak demand periods, VES and DRM are implemented to ensure the grid's stability and bring equilibrium between supply and demand. Utilizing artificial neural network (ANN) models to capture their energy capacity and self-discharge, residential refrigerators analogously hold promise in predicting energy consumption and performance. This research addresses while SBS energy capacity is insufficient to meet peak demand, by utilizing residential refrigerators as virtual energy storage systems (VESS), enabling more efficient and reliable energy management in the context of smart grid systems and the intermittent challenge of RES integration.

articleTitle: Detection and Discrimination Between Stator Winding Fault and Unbalanced Supply Voltage by Monitoring Rotor Bar Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In the literature, the detection of different faults in induction motors using current, voltage, shaft induced emf, power, partial discharge, surges, magnetic flux, electromechanical torque, angular frequency component, temperature, vibration, noise, different gasses are reported. In this paper, the rotor bar voltage is used to detect of stator winding inter-turn faults and unbalanced in supply voltage. It is very difficult to discriminate between stator winding fault and unbalanced supply voltage. In the proposed technique, the rotor bar voltage is able to discriminate between stator winding inter-turn fault and unbalanced in supply voltage. The proposed abnormalities lead to variation in rotating magnetic field and thereby, rotor induced emf. Therefore, the rotor bar voltage is changes with respective stator winding inter-turn fault severity and unbalanced in supply voltage. By analyzing frequencies components induced in rotor bar voltage, the type of abnormality and their level of fault is identified. Online detection of the fault is possible for the given technique. The proposed technique is the novel technique which is, not yet reported for the detection of any kind of faults in any motors.

Author Keywords: Stator winding fault (SWF) and Unbalanced supply voltage (USV)

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Accurate Small Signal Modeling of Resonant Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
