abstract: Due to advent of high switching frequency devices such as Sillion Carbide (SiC) and Gallium nitride (GaN) switches, the resonant converters have become a popular choice for modern switched mode power supply applications. The application of the resonant converters extend from high power EV charging to low power consumer electronics. The high efficiency and compact design of resonant converters are made possible by the resonance phenomenon, which also presents design and control challenges. There have been attempts to ascertain the small signal control to output dynamics for resonant converters, but they have either involved intricate mathematical calculations or have resulted in numerical solutions that don't offer much insight. This paper models the various stages of a series resonant converter using the Fundamental Harmonic Approximation (FHA). The perturbations in the inductor current envelope, that is caused by the small signal perturbations in the control variable (switching frequency), is analyzed in laplace domain. The control-to-output transfer function of a series resonant converter is then derived analytically using the current envelop. The validity of the model is then verified using simulation and experimental results.

articleTitle: Linear Phase-Locked Loop Based Hybrid Grid Synchronization for Grid-Forming Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The next generation grid-forming (GFM) inverter-based resources (IBRs) suffer from grid synchronization issues during their grid integration to a stiff grid or in the event of severe grid faults. Thus, this paper introduces an improved hybrid power and voltage synchronization scheme for a three-phase droop-controlled GFM inverter. During normal grid operation, Active Power Loop (APL) based synchronization is used. However, during grid connection (breaker operation), or transients such as voltage dip because of grid fault, linear phase-locked loop (LPLL) based voltage synchronization scheme is enabled to avoid high active and reactive power swings. To ensure smooth transition between the synchronization strategies, two frameworks are proposed. The first scheme is enabled by moni-toring only voltage magnitude and the second one rely on both voltage magnitude and phase-angle error during faults. The proposed schemes leverage the linearity of the PLL implementation and avoid the tradeoff-based bandwidth design of the classical synchronous referenced frame-based PLL (SRFPLL) depending upon grid conditions. The improved hybrid grid synchronization along with the two transition schemes is modelled, simulated and compared with the state-of-the-art hybrid synchronization scheme. It is observed that the GFM inverter achieves faster re-synchronization during both the inception and post grid fault event, facilitated by the proposed smooth transition-based hybrid grid synchronization.

articleTitle: A Dual Output High-Gain Flyback Converter for DC Microgrid Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The demand for electrical energy utilization is immense and continues to rise. The market for non-conventional, renewable energy sources is expanding rapidly to meet this growing demand. Among the various renewable energy resources, electrical energy generated from photovoltaic (PV) cells stands out as one of the most reliable and effective options for power generation. The increasing adoption of DC microgrids can be attributed to integrating renewable energy sources like solar photovoltaic systems and fuel cells. However, these DC power generators typically have low output voltages. To effectively connect them to the DC microgrid, there is a need for highly efficient, high-gain DC-DC converters that can boost the low input voltages to the required higher levels. The paper introduces a novel dual-output flyback converter topology that can be employed for various high-voltage applications. Conventionally, a flyback converter consists of one primary winding and one secondary winding. However, the proposed new topology incorporates an additional tertiary winding, which enables the generation of multiple outputs on the secondary side of the converter for bipolar DC microgrid applications. The proposed DC-DC converter is able to achieve higher gain at a lower duty ratio while providing galvanic isolation. The proposed high-gain converter topology is validated by MATLAB/Simulink platform simulations. The results obtained from this platform demonstrate the feasibility and sustainability of the proposed converter design.

articleTitle: A Grid Resilient Wide EV Segment Portable DC Charger with Seamless Phase Transition Adaptability Over Consistent Power Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Line or phase outage is a frequent occurrence, often accompanied by various grid abnormalities such as persistent voltage fluctuations, deviations in frequency or phase, particularly during high-demand hour. During power outages and abnormalities in grid voltages, both AC type-II and DC wall-mounted chargers are unable to function properly. This is owing to their control and protection unit design. This paper proposes a portable DC charging concept that is impervious to grid issues. In this case, a three-phase delta rectifier is employed for active front-end power conversion, while full-bridge LLC resonating converters are applied to control charging rate. The proposed approach involves a front-end converter that ensures a steady power flow even in the event of an interruption in any of the phases in a three-phase grid. Furthermore, it ensures consistency in the intermediate DC voltage notwithstanding any irregularities or interruptions in the grid. The wide EV segment battery voltage is targeted with full-bridge LLC converter with modified control approach. For this, the control approach is refined with a hybrid utilization of both pulse-frequency and pulse-conduction angle technique. Additionally, the intermediate DC link is regulated to provide a broad range of voltage conversion ratios. The proposed concept is validated by developing a 5kW hardware design that supports a battery voltage charging range of 72V−400V.

articleTitle: Enhanced Direct Torque Control Strategies for In-Wheel Switched Reluctance Motors: Evaluating Sector and Voltage Vector Selection Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In-wheel switched reluctance motors (IWSRMs) hold significant promise for the future of electric vehicles (EVs) due to their integration, which saves space, reduces overall vehicle weight, and enables more efficient packaging of the drivetrain components. In future autonomous vehicles, IWSRMs align well with the goals of enhanced efficiency, performance, and autonomy. The main challenge in IWSRMs is precise torque control and torque ripple issues. Therefore, this paper proposes enhanced direct torque control strategies to mitigate the torque ripples. To evaluate the performance of different voltage vector selection strategies using metrics such as torque ripple, flux ripple, current harmonics, and efficiency, this model designed 16/12 IWSRMs using finite element analysis. The developed mathematical model implemented different DTC techniques and strategies using MATLAB/Simulation. The performance analyzed motor drives in different drive conditions. Hardware-in-loop simulation enables real-time testing of DTC algorithms by interfacing with physical hardware emulators. The real-time hardware experimental analysis with WAVECT controller, using model-based design to reduce system complexity and mitigate the torque ripple effectively.

articleTitle: Single Cell Development Platform for SOC Estimation of Li-ion Battery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: To accurately estimate the State of Charge (SOC) of a Li-ion battery, it is essential to develop a model that captures the dynamics of the battery efficiently. This paper presents the implementation of a second-order Thevenin (2RC) battery model based on state-space equations, incorporating temperature (T) effects. The primary goal is to create an embedded platform for real hardware implementation. Simulink-MATLAB was used for developing and validating the state-space (SS) based 2RC model. The model showed high suitability for code generation, and Arduino Due was selected as the embedded hardware for deploying the generated code. The performance of the generated code was evaluated using four key metrics: Execution Time, Build Time, Lines of Code (LOC), and Max Cyclomatic Complexity. These metrics provide insights into the code efficiency and complexity, ensuring its real-time application viability for SOC estimation algorithms. The model was tested under Worldwide Harmonized Light Vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and Constant Current Constant Voltage (CC-CV) profiles at various temperatures. The results were compared with data collected from the cycler for SONY VTC6 Li-ion cell, demonstrating high accuracy and robustness, highlighting the practical utility of the model for real-world applications.

Author Keywords: Worldwide Harmonized Light Vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP)

articleTitle: Accurate Modeling Approach of Litz-Wire Based Planar DD Spiral Coils for WPT Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The litz wires are used in wireless power transfer (WPT)to address the skin effect and eddy losses. The WPT coils are designed with the help of finite element analysis (FEA) software like ANSYS Maxwell 3D. Due to the twisting and stranding effect, the litz wire structure becomes complex and requires an efficient and massive computation effort to design a WPT coil. Several traditional analytical models treat Litz wire as equivalent solid conductors with uniform current distribution models, leading to unacceptable low accuracy in the self-inductance calculation. At the early stage of coil design, an analytical method including geometrical features of the litz wire will accelerate the design process. Also, for mutual inductance calculation, over-simplifications in coil layout are made to reduce the complexity of the analytical model, which in turn gives erroneous results. This paper proposes improved analytical modeling for the Litz wire-based DD-type planar spiral coils to calculate self and mutual inductance precisely. The accuracy of the proposed modeling is compared with existing modeling methods and the simulation results obtained from the ANSYS Maxwell 3D. The experimental results obtained from the 380mm * 240mm spiral coil hardware prototypes are reported to validate the proposed model.

articleTitle: A New Control Scheme for V2G Power Transfer in Modified Series-Parallel Resonant Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The dual active bridge (DAB) modified series-parallel resonant converter (MSPRC) is best suited for grid-to-vehicle (G2V) power transfer due to the narrow frequency range of operation, good short-circuit protection performance, and minimized circulating losses. For vehicle-to-grid (V2G) power transfer of MSPRC, efficiency is poor when the battery discharges to its lowest voltage. This paper proposes a new control scheme for V2G power transfer in MSPRC. The proposed constant power discharge frequency modulation scheme gives high conversion efficiency for V2G operation. The input voltage is maintained constant during the discharging operation for the wide variations in battery voltage. All the switches in the primary and secondary bridge of the proposed converter achieve soft switching. A three-level structure on the primary bridge allows the usage of low on-state resistance switches, thereby minimizing the switch conduction losses. The converter and its proposed control scheme are applicable for three-phase on-board battery chargers where the DC link voltage is very high. The experimental results from a 3.3-kW prototype validate the performance of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Control of Flexible Bevel-Tip Needles in Minimally Invasive Surgery Utilizing Adaptive Multi-Layer Perceptron Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In Minimally Invasive Surgical (MIS) procedures, needles are extensively employed for percutaneous interventions, significantly enhancing the accuracy of target-reaching. The primary goal of percutaneous interventional method is to prioritize the patient safety while achieving precise targeting of the intended position. Therefore, the objective of this research work is to devise and deploy a needle steering controller within the tissue environment, utilizing adaptive Multi-layer Perceptron (MLP) architecture. Initially, the kinematic model is formulated to describe the motion characteristics of the steerable needles within tissue, adhering to a unicycle model while incorporating non-holonomic constraints. Subsequently, an AI-driven closed loop needle steering strategy is devised to achieve a precise needle-placement on a desired plane. The efficacy of the proposed controller is validated through the simulation studies along with comparative analysis involving existing controllers.

articleTitle: Compensation Tuning for Efficiency Maximization in LCC/LCC Compensated Inductive Power Transfer Based Charging Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Compensation is pivotal in boosting power transfer and efficiency in an inductive power charging (IPC) system. The LCC/LCC configuration is widely utilized in the literature due to its resilience to loads and alignment variations. Under resonant conditions, the system performance hinges on the selection of compensation parameters. In this connection, this work presents a methodology to choose the optimal compensation elements to enhance the efficiency of the LCC/LCC compensated IPC system for different types of loads. The compensation factors are defined and varied at different loading conditions to validate the behaviour of the system with the proposed design, hence the efficiency and power transfer. The work also derives the conditions for optimal compensation factors for maximizing efficiency. The variation in the efficiency while fixing the optimal compensation elements for the load changes is analyzed to determine the best fit for a considered application. These optimal values are then analyzed for different load conditions, demonstrating that the efficiency is maximized and aligns with desired and analytically derived values.

articleTitle: Influence of Insulation Requirement on PMSM Design and Performance Driven by a Multi-Level Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs) offer high efficiency, power density, and controllability, making them attractive for electric vehicle (EV) propulsion application. However, insulation paper thickness and copper winding insulation thickness occupy valuable real estate within the slots of the stator and limit the slot fill factor. This limitation negatively impacts the machine's performance and cost enhancement. Insulation thickness requirement is significantly influenced by the type of excitation, temperature rating and DC bus voltage. Keeping the DC bus voltage and temperature rating constant, this paper discusses findings that provide machine designers and researchers with valuable insights to optimize PMSM designs with lower insulation thickness requirements driven by multilevel inverter excitation. High speed traction motor designed for EV propulsion is used as a baseline motor. Finite element simulations are carried out to optimize the baseline motor design with reduced insulation thickness in the stator. It was found that reduced insulation thickness can be used to obtain benefits such as improved heat transfer, reduced use of rare-earth permanent magnets, reduced cost, high specific torque and power density.

articleTitle: Parameter Estimation and Optimal Charging Discharging Pattern for Supercapacitor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Charging and discharging patterns of supercapacitors play a crucial role in estimating the parameters that decide the overall performance, efficiency, and suitability for many applications. Engineers and researchers focus on optimizing these parameters to enhance the capabilities and reliability of supercapacitor-based systems. This paper focuses on identifying the optimal charging and discharging pattern for a supercapacitor to estimate the optimum values of the parameters to realize an accurate model. The experimental results are validated by simulating a three-branch model named Zubieta model. Later, the errors between the actual voltage and the estimated voltage are compared. It is found that most of the errors are minimum with a pattern with a long rest period and the multiple cycle pattern with a short rest period is the second best minimum pattern in the charging and discharging patterns. It comes to know that rest time and cyclic process play an important role in deciding the optimal pattern for different applications like high-power electrical and low-power electronics applications.

articleTitle: Multi-Area Load Frequency Control Using an Adaptive Reaching Law-Based Integral Terminal Sliding Mode Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In a multi-area load frequency control (LFC) system, the dynamic frequency response of each indicates its ability to balance local loads and exchange power with neighboring regions. To enhance the multi-area LFC performance, an adaptive nonlinear reaching law-based integral terminal sliding mode controller (ANRL-ITSMC) is proposed this paper for the secondary frequency regulation in renewable energy-based multi-area power systems. The Lyapunov direct method is employed for the stability analysis and the performance of the proposed controller is evaluated under various uncertain conditions, including external load fluctuations, system loading changes, variations in inertia constant parameters, and significant integration of renewable energy sources. Comparative analysis with an existing SMC shows that the designed ANRL-ITSMC outperforms in stabilizing dynamic responses, improving settling time, and reducing peak overshoots and undershoots.

articleTitle: Modeling & Control of SPV Integration with HESS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A recent increase in electrical energy generation from renewable sources poses significant challenges in continuously providing and maintaining efficient, reliable, high-quality power. Integrating energy storage systems (ESS) with renewable sources is a promising option. Integrating different ESSs, commonly known as hybrid energy storage systems (HESS), is an ongoing research that seeks to utilize their advantages. This paper discusses the collaboration of SPV array with HESS consisting of a battery energy storage system(BESS) and Solid Oxide Fuel Cell(SOFC) with their power electronic interfacing(PEI) and a DC bus as a test system. Additionally, it also presents an averaged linear small-signal model of a test system. The authors implemented two control algorithms in this paper using MATLAB/Simulink software.: 1) A fuzzy-based algorithm to track the SPV array maximum power point(MPP). 2) An outer voltage control loop to maintain DC bus voltage and an inner current control loop algorithm to regulate the HESS to meet the load requirement.

articleTitle: Frequency Control of Two Area Thermal-Hydro System Using HSSDEA Based PIDF Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Frequency in power systems experiences continual variations, making the load frequency control problem challenging to address. This paper presents a solution to this problem, considering a two-area system, featuring thermal and hydropower plants in the respective areas. The study encompasses comprehensive modeling of both hydro and thermal generators. For frequency regulation, a proportional integral derivative with a filter (PIDF) controller is applied. Controller gains are optimized using a hybrid salp swarm differential evolution algorithm (HSSDEA). The efficacy of the proposed HSSDEA-based PIDF controller for enhancing frequency regulation is compared to conventional I and PI controllers. Sensitivity analysis has also been carried out by varying certain parameters to assess controller robustness.

articleTitle: Development of Non-Isolated Bidirectional Quadratic DC-DC Converter with Reduced Switch Current Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper introduces a bidirectional quadratic DC-DC converter designed to reduce voltage stress on capacitors and current stress on switches. The proposed converter achieves these reductions by incorporating an additional MOSFET and inductor on the Low Voltage (LV) side and by utilizing series capacitors to supply the High Voltage (HV) side. These modifications result in lower ratings for the LV side MOSFET and HV side capacitor, while also enhancing efficiency by reducing conduction loss in the LV side switches. The paper includes a steady-state analysis of the converter, along with equivalent circuits and analytical waveforms. The components are designed for a power rating of 200 W, a high voltage side of 400 V, a low voltage side of 48 V, and a switching frequency of 50 kHz. Experimental results obtained from a laboratory prototype are presented, and the performance is compared with several recently reported converters. Additionally, the proposed converter features a common ground between the input and output ports, contributing to reduced stress and improved efficiency.

articleTitle: A Simplified Multi-Objective Technique for Placement of RESs and Capacitor Banks in Unbalanced Radial Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Recent advancements in renewable energy generation technologies, changes in utility infrastructure, and government policies have increased the interest in integrating renewable-based distributed generation units (DGs) into distribution networks. To achieve reduced power losses, voltage unbalance among phases, renewable energy systems (RESs) installation costs, and improved bus voltage stability in distribution networks, it is essential to control the optimal flow of both active and reactive power. Therefore, the optimal allocation of RESs and capacitor banks (CBs) plays a crucial role in enhancing the performance of distribution systems. The optimal allocation of RESs reduces active power losses, while the optimal allocation of CBs improves bus voltages. This paper proposes a weight-aggregated particle swarm optimization (WA-PSO) approach for the optimal allocation of RESs and CBs. The primary objective of the proposed algorithm is to achieve technical, economic, and environmental benefits. To assess the performance of the proposed WA-PSO approach, five different cases were considered. The proposed algorithm was tested on an Indian 19-bus unbalanced radial distribution network. The proposed approach has achieved the technical benefits of reduced power losses, improved voltage stability, reduced voltage unbalance index, and reduced RESs installation costs.

articleTitle: Demand Response Based on Anomaly Detection and Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) can give a breakdown of energy consumption per appliance downstream of the energy meter. It is planned in India that the Time of Use tariff be implemented in the residential sector with tariff during solar hours being less by 10-20% and increased by 10-20% during peak periods. To help the user make informed decisions about his energy usage, appropriate alerts and recommendations should be provided especially in case of peak load conditions in the grid and the ability to control or schedule loads. NILM can be used to disaggregate loads which can then be used to check anomalous behaviour of loads. An experimental setup was developed to enable NILM and scheduling of appliances and anomaly detection. The challenge in detecting anomalous energy consumption is choosing the right feature for detection and the pass/fail criteria. Anomaly detection using cumulative sum (CUSUM) of energy consumption and a model of average consumption is used to detect unusually high energy consumption with z score as the margin criteria.

articleTitle: State Feedback Speed Control of PMSM using Multithreaded Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper explores the use of the Multithreaded State Controller (MTSC) method for speed control in permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drives. The unpopularity of state feedback control (SFC) structures among practitioners is mainly due to the inherent challenge of imposing constraints on internal state variables, as there are no set points for them. The MTSC-based method has facilitated the usage of state feedback control structure for a nonlinear plant model like PMSM by making the imposition of limits on the inner controlled variable ( current) as simple as introduction of a saturation block in cascaded control systems. Using a state-feedback linearization approach, a linear model of the PMSM is derived in the rotating reference frame. Through appropriate selection of states and the linear quadratic (LQR) design method, individual state feedback controllers for controlling d-axis current, q-axis current, and speed are designed. A zero d-axis current control strategy is adopted and all these controllers are executed simultaneously, and an appropriate control signal amongst them is selected in real-time and fed into the plant to achieve the goal of speed control while keeping the current within safe bounds and mitigating the problem of slower dynamics encountered with non-constrained SFC.The simulation study conducted in MAT LAB confirmed the effectiveness of this control approach.

articleTitle: Single Source Floating Capacitor Fed Multi-Level Open-End Winding Induction Motor Drive with Extended Linear Modulation Range and Minimum Number of Switches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a strategy to increase the linear modulation range (LMR) of a cascade 2-level inverter in the maximal distention mode (MDM). A conventional 2-level inverter with a DC source is connected to one end of the open-end winding induction machine (OEWIM). The other end of the machine is connected to another 2-level inverter with a floating capacitor, whose voltage is controlled at 0.5 V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dc</inf> in order to attain maximal distention. Maximal distention mode accounts for low voltage stress and improves power quality as it has largest number of effective pole voltages in this mode. In maximal distention mode the DC link voltage could not be used appropriately due to charge balance issue of the floating capacitor. The proposed modulation strategy achieves almost 39 % increase in the DC link utilisation compared to existing techniques with the lowest number of switches and single DC source, while maintaining the floating capacitor voltage at the desired level which is a significant achievement. The proposed scheme is simulated on a 4 kW, 415 V, 50 Hz Induction Motor, using MATLAB Simulink with PLECS (Piecewise Linear Electrical Circuit Simulation) and found to be satisfactory.

articleTitle: Loop Shaping Based Robust Controller Design for Boost Converter in DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Maintaining constant power at the load end leads to an increase in output voltage and a proportional decrease in output current and vice versa. Constant power loads (CPLs) introduce hunting instability. Negative impedance characteristics of CPLs can disrupt the balance between generation and load, potentially leading to voltage collapses. Control scheme of the boost converter needs to be designed to accommodate the unstable load characteristic as discussed above. Proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller has been considered in the present work, because of its popularity in industrial applications. Furthermore, it needs tuning of only three parameters and gives satisfactory closed-loop performance. This paper proposes a novel quantitative feedback theory (QFT) based PID controller for boost converter in DC microgrid. QFT is a powerful design approach in the frequency domain that allows the user to design a controller to achieve the desired performance for any given uncertainty in plant parameters. Experimental results demonstrate that the closed-loop system achieves a significant enhancement compared to the most recently reported control strategies.

articleTitle: Master-Slave Control Design on High Powered Interleaved Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In High power applications, where the input voltage is limited which results in high input current, paralleling the boost converters is advisable and can be operated by interleaving. For an Interleaved Boost Converter (IBC) two control aspects are required voltage regulation and equal current sharing among its phases. This paper uses a Master-Slave Control (MSC) algorithm that takes care of both the aspects. This dual loop MSC is evaluated through experiment and simulation. MSC algorithm is implemented experimentally on a 10kW two-phase interleaved boost converter (TP-IBC) prototype and also simulation results are obtained for the same using MATLAB Simulink. The MSC algorithm is implemented digitally using DSP (TMS320F28379D).

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Cost-Effective AC/DC Current Probe for Academia
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of a high-current AC/DC current probe circuit capable of providing reliable current measurements while being affordable for students and academic researchers. The proposed current probe circuit is based on a hall-effect current transducer. The current probe circuit has two outputs-one with the range -10V to +10V for interfacing with oscilloscopes and the other being an isolated output with 0 to +3.3 V range compatible with processors for data acquisition. The design of the transducer-based circuit and associated signal conditioning network are presented and the circuit simulation is carried out. A hardware prototype of the proposed current probe circuit is developed and its performance is validated experimentally.

articleTitle: Speed Sensor-less Power Hardware In the Loop Emulation of PMDC Machine with Fuzzy Based Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This research work examines the implementation of a power hardware in the loop (PHIL) emulation for a permanent magnet DC (PMDC) motor with speed sensor-less operation. The PMDC motor is modelled in software and its behaviour is synthesized with the help of a two level power converter. The emulator power converter is operated in current control mode to synthesize the dynamic back emf and will closely mimic the behaviour of a DC machine. The PMDC drive is operated with speed sensor-less mode and a fuzzy-based speed observer is developed in the drive control system to showcase the operation of speed sensor-less functionality. This observer can be used to smoothly transit from sensor-based control to sensor-less control during the sensor failure scenarios. The PMDC drive and emulator converter operate using a bipolar modulation method, resulting in a single DC link operation. The digital control system and the fuzzy inference system is designed using MATLAB. The speed sensor-less PHIL system is tested with PLECS TMS320F28379D behavioural simulation environment under several dynamic testing conditions and the results are provided.

articleTitle: Renewable Energy-Based Hybrid Power Conversion System for Induction Motor Driven Light Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper validates a solar photovoltaic (SPV) based induction motor (IM) system using a modified quasi-impedance source inverter (qZSI) for electric vehicles. The system employs a Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm to control the Solar Photovoltaic (SPV) output, connected to a modified qZSI. This study covers the design, control, and performance analysis of a powertrain for electric vehicles driven by a battery and solar-fed induction motor. The DC-link modified qZSI converter offers high gain voltage conversion in both charging and discharging modes, interfacing with the low voltage battery. Solar energy is integrated through the modified qZSI, which manages MPPT, maximizes efficiency, and reduces current ripple at the SPV end. The Perturb and Observe (P&O) technique is used to maximise the PV panel's power output. The induction motor operates in open-loop mode, and active power flow is controlled via DC-link voltage regulation. This setup generates an AC voltage higher than the DC input based on the instantaneous duty cycle, unlike traditional VSI systems. The proposed system uses a three-phase hybrid qZSI converter to power an induction motor drive, which is isolated with an isolation transformer for safety. The qZSI boosts the DC voltage of the solar array, with switches controlled by Pulse Width Modulation and shoot-through signals from the MPPT connected to the SPV. Benefits include fewer required switches and improved output voltage quality, and efficiency, enabling a variable frequency induction motor drive and extending the driving range. Detailed analysis, including mathematical expressions and real-time simulations, has been conducted using the Typhoon HIL 402 real-time emulator.

articleTitle: An Analytical Approach of Higher Order Electric Vehicle System Reduction Using Truncation Based Approximation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this research, reduction of fifth-order electric vehicle (EV) transfer function (TF) is accomplished by exploiting direct truncation method. The higher order TF (HOTF) of order five is approximated to obtain the reduced order transfer function (ROTF) of comparatively lower order. The truncation of numerator and denominator coefficients is done to determine the desired EV ROTF. The graphical representation of step, error, Nichols and Bode responses are presented in the support of EV ROTFs obtained for EV HOTF. The error indices data and time domain specifications data are also provided in tabulated form to prove the efficacy of proposed ROTFs.

articleTitle: A Modified HVAC Wind Energy Collection System Without Offshore Substation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A modified structure of the high voltage (HV) AC energy collection system for offshore wind farms (OWF) is proposed in this paper which can help to reduce the installation cost significantly. For this, a three winding transformer is considered on all wind turbine (WT) nacelles instead of the two-winding first level step-up transformer. A parallel-series connection of the windings of this transformer is introduced, which helps to obviate the second level bulky step-up transformer and the costly offshore sub-station (OSS). The suitability of the proposed structure is verified through simulation in PSCAD platform under normal operating condition and various probable contingencies,

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Deep Learning-based Prognostication for Power Grid Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The rapid increase in renewable energy sources, known for their unpredictability, is challenging the stability of the electricity grid. In response, this study introduces a deeplearning-based forecasting method to maintain a sustainable grid operation, focusing on the New England IEEE 39-Bus Power System (NEPS). The proposed approach is meticulously compared with current methods, emphasizing system dynamics to ascertain its effectiveness. Further validation is provided through a model-in-the-loop analysis, ensuring the functionality of the forecasting strategy. Overall, this research highlights the potential of advanced data-driven techniques in enhancing grid reliability amidst the surge of renewable energy sources.

articleTitle: Power Transfer from 400V Charging Piles to 800V Electric Vehicles Using Motor Winding and Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Range anxiety is one of the main problems for electric vehicles (EVs) due to low battery power density and low charging speeds. The charging speed can be improved by increasing the charging power. The maximum charging power can be increased by raising the battery voltage level from 400V to 800V. However, if the number of new 800V DC fast charging piles cannot increase quickly, charging will become a new problem for 800V EVs. To solve this problem, a method is proposed to allow the 400V charging station to charge the 800V EV. The motor winding and inverter are used to form a boost converter that connects to the 400V charging station through the DC charging port of EVs. With one additional switch, the proposed method can be compatible with 400V and 800V charging piles. The proposed method is verified by simulation and a 500W laboratory prototype.

articleTitle: Improved ANPC Three-Level Inverter with Voltage Boosting Ability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: To address the high DC-link voltage requirements of conventional neutral point clamped topologies, this article introduces a novel single-stage ANPC-type dynamic boost 3L inverter topology. In addition, the proposed topology has low voltage stress on the components and features simple regulation of output voltage without compromising the benefits of neutral-point-clamped topologies. A comparative study demonstrates the proposed topology's superiority over conventional three-level inverters with integrated DC-DC converters. Furthermore, a 650 W prototype hardware setup is used to verify the proposed topology, and the results are discussed. During the experimental test, the maximum efficiency of ≈97% is recorded.

articleTitle: Design of ACE-Based Neighborhood Microgrid Controller Towards Self-Resilient Net Zero Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The sources of greenhouse gas emissions need to be replaced by renewable energy sources (RES) to reduce carbon emissions by 45% by 2030 and accomplish net zero by 2050, as proposed in the Paris Agreement. Microgrids have received wide attention in this regard. However, with the increase of RES-based microgrids, it has been noticed that when there is an excess generation or any power transaction between neighboring houses, the grid experiences instability due to unplanned and redundant power. To address this problem, in this paper, a fast power flow solution using the Newton-Raphson method is demonstrated, and a multi-variable controller is proposed. The controller is designed based on area control error where, with the help of the primary controller, the secondary control biases are found. The results validate that the controller is capable of maintaining generation with respect to load demand as well as smooth power transactions between neighborhood microgrids without affecting the grid. It is also observed that the controller takes minimum time to control the system. The power flow solution is executed in C++, and the controller design is carried out in Python. This paper is expected to contribute to establishing the concept of prosumer (producer-consumer) while keeping the grid stable and achieving the mission towards net zero carbon emission.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Soft Switched Current-Fed Full Bridge DC-DC Converter for Renewable Energy Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A full bridge current fed modified series parallel quasi resonant DC to DC converter for DC micro-grid applications is presented in this paper. Zero current switching is achieved during the overlap switching states of device by generating a resonant pulse within the modified series parallel quasi resonant tank, reducing the current to zero in the exiting switches. The proposed converter facilitates steady output voltage across a broad range of variations in both output load and input source by using variable frequency modulation technique. Furthermore, voltage stress experienced by each semiconductor switches on the primary side of the transformer is less than the output voltage. A 400V/500W converter prototype is implemented and tested in the laboratory in order to verify the zero current switching performance.

articleTitle: Optimized IGWO Based MPPT for High-Gain 13-Level Switched Capacitor Multilevel Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents an improved grey wolf optimization (IGWO)-based maximum power point tracking (MPPT) technique for a high-gain 13-level switched capacitor multilevel inverter (13-L HGSC-MLI). The proposed 13-L HGSC-MLI has two main parts: a front-end DC/DC converter that keeps the input current continuous, and a switched capacitor (SC) unit with 11 switches, 2 diodes, and 3 capacitors that boost the voltage. The continuous input current of the boost converter effectively reduces the large charging currents of capacitors, hence improving the problem of inrush current. Switching ensures capacitors are self-balanced. Additionally, the proposed 13-L HGSC-MLI reduces dominant lower-order harmonics by using selective harmonic elimination pulse-width modulation (SHE-PWM), which is also based on IGWO. The IGWO-based MPPT algorithm adjusts dynamically to temperature and sun irradiance to maximize solar power extraction. The integration of the IGWO algorithm with the boost converter and HGSC-MLI results in a highly efficient, reliable, and cost-effective solution for renewable energy systems. The experimental results validate the superior performance of the proposed system, demonstrating significant improvements in power output and efficiency.

Author Keywords: selective harmonic elimination pulse width modulation (SHE PWM)
high gain switched capacitor multilevel inverter (HGSC-MLI)

articleTitle: Enhancing Load Frequency Control with Non-Linear ADRC for Cyber-Attacks Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In modern power systems, integrating smart devices and computer-based control has increased the reliance on data for measuring and controlling grid operations. While this rises in data-dependent approaches, grid control capabilities for quick decisions also introduce vulnerabilities. Disruptions or alterations in the data flow may result in erroneous commands at the control centre, potentially destabilising the entire grid. This paper discussed applying a non-linear active disturbance rejection control strategy to mitigate cyber-attacks targeting load frequency control (LFC). This study analyses and presents a non-linear active disturbance rejection controller (NLADRC) within a power system. Then, various cyber-attacks are examined, including their impact on LFC stability and performance degradation. These attacks include exponential load attacks, random load attacks, and Denial of service attacks. Finally, the effectiveness of the NLADRC approach is demonstrated through simulations in MATLAB/SIMULINK involving load frequency control in the power system.

articleTitle: Synchronised IPMSM Drive Operation for EVs Over Complete Speed Range
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of the Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (IPMSM) drive in the complete speed range operation for Electrical Vehicle (EV) applications. Complete speed range operation of an IPMSM drive under the best efficiency would be based on Maximum Torque per Ampere (MTPA), Maximum Torque per Volt (MTPV) and flux weakening operation. Based on the operating constraints for these modes, a new method has been proposed for adapting the suitable operation based on EV and motor requirements. Unlike the conventional approaches, a state transition method for complete speed range operation of the IPMSM drive for EV application has been proposed. Transitions between various states of IPMSM operation and iterative methods for respective state operations have been discussed. IPMSM drive control with the proposed method has been simulated and verified through hardware implementation.

Author Keywords: IPMSM - Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor

articleTitle: Intelligent Inductor Characterization for Power Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Designing a power converter requires careful consideration to ensure high operational efficiency. Additionally, component selection, based on thorough analysis, significantly influences the thermal modeling of converters, which is crucial for volumetric optimization. To enhance converter design, this paper emphasizes the implementation of an analytical component selection framework alongside intelligent inductor loss assessment using multiple core materials to ensure optimal inductor selection. A 1kW boost converter design was used for the assessment. The evaluation was conducted across various switching frequencies and inductor ripple currents while considering different inductor cores. This approach provided a comprehensive range of estimated core and copper losses for the inductor design, thereby facilitating the pursuit of optimal performance.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a Ferrite-Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Motor for Mid-Mounted Electric Two-Wheeler
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Ferrite Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Motor (FeASynRM) is a sustainable, efficient and economical solution for variable speed drive applications such as electric transportation and various industrial and agricultural applications. An optimized motor design and efficient control are necessary for optimum performance in a complete drive range. The paper presents a comprehensive performance analysis of an optimized FeASynRM to validate its feasibility as a viable alternative for mid-mount electric two-wheeler. The FeASynRM rotor design has been optimized and analyzed using the finite element (FE) platform (ANSYS Maxwell and Simplorer). Once the simulation results are optimum, the machine is manufactured, and experimentation has been performed for a broad torque speed range to validate the design and control. The paper elaborates on the machine performance obtained through an FE-based platform and experiments performed for different operating regions, validating motor for mid-mount electric two-wheeler application.

articleTitle: Amplitude Error Based Frequency Deviation Detection for Grid Voltage Parameters Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this work, for the estimation of three-phase utility voltage parameters, a pseudo open-loop synchronization technique (OLST) with nominal-frequency tuned guaranteed stable sliding discrete Fourier transform (GSDFT) as pre-filter is presented. When the utility frequency is off-nominal, due to asynchronous sampling, amplitude and phase errors are introduced in the in-phase and quadrature components of GSDFT output. Mathematically it is shown that there exists a relationship between the ratio of peak value of Sine and Cosine components of GSDFT output and frequency deviation. Based on this finding, an algorithm is developed to detect the input signal frequency deviation from the nominal frequency. Subsequently, with curve fit technique, amplitude and phase errors are compensated. With a test case comprising of simultaneous change in amplitude, phase and frequency, harmonic and dc offset distortion, the real-time performance of the proposed OLST is proven.

articleTitle: Effect of Parasitic Inductance on Switching Transition for Four-Quadrant SiC-Based Current Source Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The four quadrant (FQ) switch is used in current source inverter (CSI) as it possesses reverse voltage blocking (RVB) characteristics which is a basic requirement for CSI. The FQ switch can be realized using two SiC-MOSFETs in anti-series configuration. Due to additional switches used, the designing of FQ switch in printed circuit board (PCB) is a challenge as it increases the power loop inductance. So, to get an optimal power loop, several calculated loop inductances are considered for observation and simulated using LT spice application. This paper shows the effect in switching transition behavior of FQ switch due to various loop inductance. It also compares the behavior of gate to source voltage by varying the gate loop inductance.

articleTitle: Adaptive Reconfigurable Battery Pack Employing Switching Matrix Circuit to Maximize the Capacity of the Battery Bank
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this article, a reconfigurable battery pack is proposed to enhance the performance of the battery pack for electric vehicle (EV) applications. The SoC mismatches between the battery cells in the battery pack will limit the capacity utilization. This proposed system employs a MOSFET based switching matrix circuit (SMC) to reconfigure the battery pack based on its present state of charge (SoC) to mitigate the SoC mismatches between the battery cells in the battery pack. The adaptive part of the battery cells will balance the fixed part of the pack with the proposed SMC system. This technique will maximize the capacity utilization of the battery pack under the mismatching SoC level while charging. The proposed system is validated in the MATLAB / SIMULINK platform for the battery pack size of 4 × 4 which consists of 16 battery cells with a total capacity of 176 Wh. The proposed achieves the maximum capacity of 97.7%.

articleTitle: Securing BESS Modules: Anomaly Detection in Cell Voltages Through Statistical Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Ensuring safety in Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) is paramount to prevent failures and enhance reliability. This paper introduces a novel algorithm for detecting abnormal behaviour by analyzing the voltage distribution of cells within a module. The method uses z-scores to calculate the relative percentage of anomalies in each cell and standardized moments to capture voltage deviations across the entire module. From these metrics, an anomaly score is derived for each cell. The algorithm is validated using data from a 4-cell in-series (4S) module model, demonstrating its effectiveness. Additionally, a sensitivity analysis of the configurable parameters highlights their impact on the anomaly score. This innovative algorithm is crucial for BESS safety, as it ensures early detection of potential issues, thereby preventing failures and enhancing the reliability and longevity of the system.

articleTitle: High Gain DC-DC Converter Fed PMSM Drive With Field-Oriented Control Techniques for Fuel Cell-Based Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) traction drives are more competitive due to advancements such as permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs), which enhance efficiency and power density. The PMSM for the EV control system is impacted by changes in the motor's properties and outside interference, which stops the motor system from providing prompt, high-caliber dynamic performance. Since the torque and speed of an electric vehicle always vary, operating an efficient vehicle requires varying voltage levels. This research thoroughly investigates a PMSM drive powered by a high-gain DC-DC converter, especially for fuel-cell electric vehicles (FC-EVs). The addition of high-gain DC-DC converters improves the efficiency and performance of the drive system. Additionally, it used fuzzy logic and FOC methods to enable PMSM for EV applications to operate efficiently. Fuzzy logic is employed to determine <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_{p}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_{i}$</tex> values under various PMSM driving circumstances. The effectiveness of fuzzy-PI-based FOC approaches is confirmed by comparing them to traditional FOC techniques. The experiment findings ultimately validate the efficacy of the hybrid control systems and recommended converter design for PMSM drive in 3-wheeler EV applications. The suggested architecture tested under various dynamic condition to confirm the system's effectiveness.

articleTitle: A Novel Three-Output Port Isolated DC-DC Converter with Four Switches Providing High Gain Quadratic Non-Inverting Buck-Boost or Derived Boost Characteristics Along with Continuous Input Battery Current Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A novel four-switch three-port isolated Direct Current (DC)-Direct Current (DC) high gain converter derived from the modified Input Parallel Output Series (IPOS) cascaded connection of input boost and buck-boost converters and output flyback converter is portrayed in this paper. In the continuous Conduction Mode (CCM), this converter can provide a quadratic non-inverting buck-boost characteristic or a derived boost characteristic at the isolated output port using two distinct switching combinations and utilizing the turns ratio N offered by the High-Frequency Transformer (HFT). Two non-isolated output ports characterize a boost and a non-inverting buck-boost output respectively. The boost inductor at the battery-interfacing input side renders a continuous current operation from the battery, allowing increased battery life and integration possibility to Distributed Energy Resources (DER) like a Photovoltaic (PV) array. CCM analysis of the ideal converter in the steady-state is documented in detail and the voltage gains are penned down. MATLAB® SIMULINK platform is used to simulate the converter and its results validate the proposed operation. Closed-loop current controller is designed and its efficacy is validated using step changes in load.

articleTitle: A Quadruple Boost Nine Level Inverter Performance in Power Conversion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This article present a single DC source-based nine-level inverter having a common ground (CG) configuration with quadruple boosting capability. Self-balancing Switched Capacitors (SC) are used to produce the desired output. It uses 10 switches and three SCs to achieve output voltage. Inverter control is achieved by the pulse width modulation (PWM) techniques. It also controls the charging and discharging of the SCs at fundamental frequency. The switching pulse of each power switch is analysed. A brief discussion on capacitor selection and detailed comparative analysis is performed with the existing state to illustrate the advantage of the inverter configuration. Voltage and current stress across each power component is carried out. The inverter performance is validated for both resistive, inductive and dynamic load conditions in the Matlab/Simulink and PLECS. Voltage and current THD are analysed for both output voltage and current. The inverter achieved an efficiency of 97.62 % at a 1 kW load.

articleTitle: Analysis of IGBT and GaN Based Hybrid Switch Under Diverse Switching Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In half-bridge circuits, paralleling devices is a common strategy to boost current handling capacity and cost-effectiveness, addressing the limitations of individual components. A significant advancement in power electronics is the parallel operation of Si/SiC MOSFETs and Si IGBTs. However, GaN devices offer even greater efficiency and higher frequency operation than SiC. This study investigates the use of a hybrid switch combining IGBTs and GaN MOSFETs and further, analyzes switching losses under various operating scenarios, considering different turn-on and turn-off delays. The results reveal that introducing a controlled delay between the turn-off of the IGBT and the GaN device minimizes switching losses. This approach achieves a remarkable 50% reduction in losses compared to simultaneous switching. These findings provide valuable insights for optimizing the performance and reliability of hybrid power switches in high-power applications.

articleTitle: Modelling and Analysis of a Dual-Loop Current Control Strategy for Grid-Tied Inverters with LCL Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In the recent development of microgrids, grid-tied inverters and their control techniques have played a vital role in the power injections from the renewables into the grid. Different control techniques exist in the literature on the ability to suppress the resonance peak of an LCL filter using active and passive damping techniques for grid-tied inverter applications. However, the most crucial challenging factor for the various control techniques is the presence of computational delays and dead time involved in real-world systems, which can potentially impact the stability and performance of controllers. This paper presents the formulation of a dual-loop current control strategy in a synchronous reference frame for grid-tied inverters equipped with an LCL filter. It brings out the significance of feedforward and decoupling terms in obtaining proper plant models and the capacitor voltage buildup for smooth synchronization. Finally, the impact of inverter delay and dead time on controller design is validated through MATLAB/Simulink and HIL results.

articleTitle: Multi-Stage CC-CV Charging of an Off-Board Charger Using Modulated Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The most popular configuration for the off-board charging is a two-stage power conversion system, which consists of a three-phase, two-level voltage source rectifier (2L-VSR) followed by a non-isolated DC-DC buck converter. This paper presents a new duty-cycle controlled model predictive control (MPC) of 2L-VSR and buck converter to obtain a fixed switching frequency operation. This method optimizes the grid and battery currents based on duty cycles and cost functions. It combines the classical MPC's fast dynamic response with the traditional linear control's fixed switching frequency operation. To verify the feasibility of the developed MPC method, simulation studies are conducted on a 50 kW off-board charging system under constant current (CC) - constant voltage (CV) and multi-stage constant current (MSCC) charging profiles. Finally, the charger's performance using the proposed MPC method is compared with classical linear and MPC methods under the MSCC and CC-CV charging profiles.

articleTitle: A Data Driven Energy Efficient Control of Induction Motor Drive with Vector Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel online energy optimization algorithm for field-oriented control of induction motor (IM) drives. The control strategy incorporates an artificial neural network in the outer loop of the control technique to determine the optimized flux component that meets load demands while maintaining the motor's desired speed. Under light-load conditions, this approach significantly reduces the drive losses, thereby decreasing the motor's input power consumption making it ideal for energy-efficient systems. The proposed scheme ensures maximum efficiency with high accuracy, low computational burden, and fast dynamic response. Moreover, the scheme incurs no additional costs, enhancing its practicality and performance in manufacturing, transportation, and energy management sectors. The proposed controller is rigorously tested in MATLAB/Simulink to validate its high dynamic response and optimal efficiency with a 2.2 kW IM drive.

articleTitle: A Sine-Cosine Algorithm Optimized PI-PD Cascade Controller for Load Frequency Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Frequency in power systems experiences continual variations, making the load frequency problem extremely challenging to address. This paper presents a thorough exploration of this problem in a two-area networked power system configu-ration, featuring thermal and geothermal power plants (GTPP) in the respective areas. The study presents detailed modeling of the entire system, including generators, loads, tie lines, and small-signal models for both thermal and geothermal turbines. A cascade control structure employing proportional-integral (PI) and proportional-derivative (PD) controllers (PI-PD controller) is implemented for frequency regulation. Moreover, a population-based sine-cosine algorithm (SCA) effectively optimizes the value of controller gains. The performance of the proposed SCA-based PI - PD controller is compared with conventional control strategies like I, PI, and PID controllers. This analysis demonstrates that the recommended coordinated technique is superior at maintaining system stability and frequency regulation. Further-more, sensitivity analyses are carried out to evaluate the PI - PD controller's robustness under varying operating conditions. These analyses involve modifying system parameters such as small load perturbation (SLP) and area capacity.

articleTitle: Truncation Based Reduction of Interconnected Hybrid Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The objective of this paper is implementation of model reduction technique (MRT) to simplify hybrid power system. In this technique, both denominator and numerator polynomials of lower order system are determined by direct truncation technique. By applying direct truncation technique for MRT on hybrid power system, thirteen order transfer function is decreased to sixth, fifth, fourth, third, and second orders. These simplified models are very useful and preserve property of parameters with accuracy. The results of simplified models indicate the effectiveness of the method. The demonstrated diagrams like step, impulse, Bode, and Nyquist plots for higher-order model and its lower order reduced models are shown. The stability, steady state value and other features are similar to original higher-order system.

articleTitle: Switched Capacitor-Based Buck/Boost DC-DC Converter for Low Power Application with Less Number of Switch Count
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper discusses the switched capacitor converters (SCC) leveraging the mathematical series to opti-mize voltage conversion efficiency and reduce the component count to generate buck/boost voltage ratios. The series offers a unique way to achieve nonstandard voltage ratios (VR). In this work, buck/boost conversion is possible using fewer semiconductor devices for various chip parts to act as power sources. This topology is analyzed theoretically, simulated and validated using an experiment prototype of its performance under various operating conditions using PSIM. Different fractions like 1/2, 1/3, 2/5, 3/5, 2, 3, etc.,(Total 12 VR) are generated using mathematical sequences.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of a Non-Isolated Bidirectional DC-DC Converter with High Voltage Ratio for Battery Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The energy storage system strengthens the grid resiliency and reliability and also has the ability to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. But the most energy storage sources such as batteries and ultra-capacitors, have low terminal voltage. To integrate these energy sources into hybrid system necessitate high voltage conversion ratio power electronic topologies to meet the load requirement of the system. Practically, the traditional step-up or step-down DC-DC converters are not feasible to meet a wide range of conversions. A hybrid structure of a bi-directional high-gain DC-DC converter (HGBDC) has been developed by integrating capacitors and inductors. This converter offers enhanced conversion ratio at lower duty ratios and enables bi-directional energy transfer with a simplified component layout while utilizing fewer semiconductors and passive components. The operational principles, steady-state analysis, and performance of this topology have been thoroughly explained. Additionally, a comprehensive comparative study has been conducted with the recent literature to show superiority of proposed converter. To validate the performance and feasibility of the proposed bidirectional converter MATLAB/Simulink simulation results for output power of 500 W are presented.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Multiport Boost Converter and Z-Source Multiport Converter for EV Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper explores recent advancements in multiport DC-DC converters, with a focus on their development and application. A multiport boost converter is evaluated for use in hybrid electric vehicles, showing superior output performance over traditional designs. It combines various input sources, including FC, PV panel, and energy storage. Notably, the converter maintains load power supply even when one or two input sources are absent. Additionally, a Z-source-based multiport converter is evaluated for efficient power transfer between input sources, load, and battery. Single-stage power transfer includes a bidirectional interface that allows for battery discharge and recharge, making it incredibly efficient. Both converters are compared and evaluated based on different aspects along with their simulation results and performance.

articleTitle: Reduced Power Processing High Efficient LED Driver
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a circuit for a single-stage active LED driver with continuous current output, minimal power processing, and power factor adjustment is presented. The main goal is to incorporate power factor correction and consistent current output–two features usually found in two–stage driver solutions-into a single-stage design. Crucially, the circuit distributes input power efficiently without the need for extra switches. It makes use of a straightforward ripple cancellation control mechanism to properly align DC power and AC ripple power. This enables the use of longer-lasting film capacitors instead of typical electrolytic capacitors, extending the LED driver's operational life. In addition, the design reduces power processing by processing a small portion of the input power twice instead of the full input power as is the case with traditional twostage driver circuits. This article examines the configuration of a single input, dual-output power factor correction converter. A 30W simulation model has been carefully developed using PSIM, and the findings have been carefully confirmed.

articleTitle: A Design Procedure for Double Stator Axial Flux Switched Reluctance Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Conventional design methods of a double stator axial flux switched reluctance motor (DS-AFSRM) decides the number of turns in stator winding based on the specific electric loading which is an arbitrary choice of the designer. This affects the stator phase inductance values and the slope of inductance profile with respect to rotor position. This paper proposes a design method for DS-AFSRM in which, slope of inductance profile with respect to rotor position is used as a critical design parameter and it is calculated from target specifications of motor. The number of turns of stator winding are designed based on this critical parameter. An analytical model to evaluate stator phase inductance is developed for DS-AFSRM. Based on the proposed design method and the developed analytical model of stator phase inductance, a 5 HP, 120 Volts, 6/4 DS-AFSRM is designed and it is validated using Finite Element Analysis (FEA) platform and MATLAB software.

Author Keywords: double stator axial flux switched reluctance motor

articleTitle: Real Coefficient Assessment with Improved Adaptive Control for Grid-Tied DSTATCOM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper introduces a unique controller design to integrate battery energy storage systems (BESS) into DSTATCOM. The core innovation lies in a weight-based control strategy that improves performance while streamlining computational processes. We propose a combined step size (CSS) approach within a RIP-ASPA. This facilitates rapid convergence and minimizes steady-state errors, leading to superior power quality. The CSS-RIP-APSA's central function is to accurately select the fundamental weight component associated with distorted load currents. This component is crucial for reactive power compensation and ensuring a stable power factor. The BESSDSTATCOM controller intelligently utilizes two step sizes to balance convergence speed and steady-state precision. Additionally, a modified sigmoid function allows the inverter to function seamlessly as a shunt compensator. Experimental validation on a grid-tied DSTATCOM system demonstrates the efficacy of the proposed algorithm. This work paves the way for refined weightbased control strategies in the BESS-DSTATCOM integration, offering a new controller that increases system performance and efficiency.

Author Keywords: real-coefficient improved proportionate affine projection sign algorithm (RIP-ASPA)

articleTitle: Maximum Power Estimation of a Partially Shaded PV String Using a Novel Elliptical Foci Based Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this article, a novel elliptical foci based MPP estimation method is proposed for photovoltaic (PV) string under partial shading conditions (PSCs). In this method, an implicit I-V characteristic equation of single diode model (SDM) PV module is used. In partially shaded string, the proposed method first identifies the voltage range in which the global maximum power point (GMPP) exists. Afterwards, the maximum power is estimated using elliptical foci technique. The major advantage of the proposed method is that the MPP can be estimated without the need of approximation in current-voltage (I-V) expression or plotting of the whole I-V curve. The proposed method is developed and tested under different environmental conditions (DECs) using MATLAB platform. Further, to validate the accuracy of the proposed method, 3 uniform and 3 nonuniform shading conditions are considered. A comparison of proposed method with different existing MPP methods is carried out. The results show the proposed method is more accurate and efficient.

articleTitle: Hybrid Converter with Simultaneous DC and AC Outputs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel hybrid converter topology capable of delivering both DC and AC outputs concurrently. The core component of this hybrid converter is the Conventional Positive Output Elementary Superlift Luo (POESL) converter. Unlike traditional converters, which typically handle either DC or AC loads separately, this hybrid topology combines both functionalities. By utilizing small DC inputs, the hybrid converter achieves a significantly larger DC output―up to three times the input voltage. This feature is particularly advantageous for applications requiring high DC voltage levels. The innovation lies in introducing an AC output alongside the DC output. To achieve this, an inverter with four switches is inserted into the single switch of the POESL converter. These switches are controlled using unipolar sine pulse-width modulation (PWM). The entire hybrid converter topology is meticulously modelled and simulated in the MATLAB/Simulink environment. The simulation results validate the feasibility of achieving both DC and sinusoidal AC outputs simultaneously.

articleTitle: Generating High Switching Frequency by Integration of FPGA with DSP Using SPI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Power electronic converters are essential for energy conversion, and advancements in wide bandgap devices like SiC MOSFETs and GaN HEMTs have enabled use of higher switching frequencies. Sophisticated control method of power electronic converters increasingly require digital platforms like DSPs and FPGAs for implementation. However, when only DSPs are used, they are limited to switching frequencies of around 50 kHz. In contrast, FPGAs support higher switching frequencies but are costly due to the need for large number of logic gates for complex algorithms. This paper proposes a hybrid approach in which control methods are implemented on DSP, and high-frequency PWM generation is implemented on inexpensive FPGA. Serial peripheral interface (SPI) protocol for communication between DSP and FPGA is used. Existing literature does not provide clear methods for such hybrid implementation. Proposed approach reduces the need for expensive FPGAs and utilizes the computational power of DSP to maximum. The proposed method is experimentally verified by controlling a DC-DC converter at a high switching frequency.

articleTitle: Enhancing Performance of Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines Through Rotor Surfacing and Flux Guide Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The performance of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines (PMSM) machine depends on flux density produced by magnets in rotor. The path taken by the flux lines depends on the reluctance offered by the rotor and stator making rotor surfacing and the flux guides a crucial part of machine design. This paper explores the impact of rotor surfacing and flux guides on reducing torque ripple, improving saliency ratio thereby enhancing power density of PMSM machine. This work covers the design process of flux guides, rotor surfacing. It also provides valuable insights into their effects on electromagnetic parameters such as torque, air gap flux density, flux linkage, back EMF (B_EMF), direct axis inductance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(L_{d})$</tex> and quadrature axis inductances <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(L_{q})$</tex>, as well as core and copper losses of the machine. The findings contribute to developing efficient and compact electric machine, which are crucial for various electrical applications.

articleTitle: A PV Grid Tied Modified Z-Source Inverter for an Inductive Wireless EV Charging System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Solar energy is widely used in residential and commercial applications, and energy storage systems play an important role in managing fluctuations in energy supply. Z-source inverter technology emerged as a simple solution for power conversion, enabling efficient charging of electric vehicle batteries and integration of wireless coil systems. This innovative technology eliminates the need for multiple switching stages by combining voltage amplification and DC-to-AC power conversion into one efficient system. Passive components such as capacitors and inductors are essential to integrate energy storage systems into Z-source converters to improve their overall efficiency and versatility. The research presented in the article focuses on the research, development, and operation of a state-of-the-art Z-source inverter (ZSI). The improved ZSI is designed with a split primary coil and an insulated secondary coil connected to a battery charger designed for charging DC electric vehicle batteries.
