Both simulation and experimental results are presented to verify the performance of the proposed inverter, which demonstrates its potential in real-world applications and shows its ability to efficiently charge electric vehicle batteries using wireless charging technology.

articleTitle: Solar Microinverter with ESS for Rural Households
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a solar microinverter integrated with an Energy Storage System (ESS) for rural households. The primary objective is to enhance energy accessibility and reliability in off-grid and semi-grid rural areas, addressing issues of power intermittency and accessibility. The proposed solution employs a 350W solar panel, with a solar charge controller to store DC power in a battery and microinverter. The work focuses on achieving cost-effectiveness, ease of installation, and minimal maintenance. The system's key contribution is its ability to maintain a continuous power supply during periods of low solar irradiance. The implementation methodology includes detailed simulation to validate performance and efficiency. The findings demonstrate that the system offers a sustainable and reliable energy solution for rural development, promoting energy equity and sustainable development.

articleTitle: Comparative Studies of Wire-Wound and Planar Transformers in a PSFB Converter for Welding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents comparative studies between conventional wire-wound and planar magnetics, typically used in the isolation transformer of a phase-shifted full-bridge (PSFB) converter for low voltage (LV), high current (HC) applications such as welding. The design considerations of planar magnetics for a desired application are provided at first. The detailed design of both the transformers and the winding configurations are also presented. Standard commercially available finite element software packages have been used to simulate the transformers and validate them against analytical calculations. To compare the performance of the transformers, experiments have been performed on a laboratory-fabricated SiC-based phase-shifted inverter (PSI) with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$380\ V$</tex> DC Bus and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$500\ kHz$</tex> switching frequency, feeding a current doubler synchronous rectifier (CDSR) circuit with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$24\ V,60\ A$</tex> DC output. The equivalent circuit of the transformer comprising the winding AC resistance, leakage inductance and the inter-turn, inter-winding parasitic capacitance is presented here. The values of parasitic capacitances are evaluated analytically from the experimental data. Different aspects of comparison between both the transformers are carried out and presented to comment on their advantages and disadvantages for the proposed application.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Battery with Multiple Input Bidirectional DC-DC Converter for Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Electric vehicle technology is rapidly advancing worldwide, transforming the mobility sector into e-mobility through innovations in battery technology, electrical drives, and various motor types. This research focuses on integrating a reconfigurable battery pack with a bidirectional multiple input DC-DC converter. The reconfiguration of the battery pack is achieved by equalizing the input voltage level within the reconfigurable circuit, facilitated by the boost converter circuit. The boost converter maintains the output voltage level of each battery module, ensuring reconfiguration without violating current laws. The integration of the battery module with multiple input converter illustrates multiple satisfactory results pertaining to reconfiguration of battery which enhance overall performance and range of the battery in electric vehicles. The proposed work has been simulated and analyzed in MATLB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Design of a Robust $H_{\infty}$ Plasma Position Controller for Aditya-U Tokamak
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In the Aditya-U Tokamak, the position and shape of the plasma are controlled based on measurements of the toroidal and poloidal magnetic fields. The objective is to maintain the plasma at the equilibrium position, or the center of magnetic confinement, to prevent contact with the surrounding vacuum vessel of the Tokamak. The traditional Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller may not be a suitable choice for handling uncertainties and disturbances in the system. Therefore, a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> controller is proposed in this paper for controlling the plasma position in the Aditya-U Tokamak. The aim is to regulate the plasma position by managing the Fast Feedback Power Supply (FFPS) input to the system. The controller generates the control signal for the Fast Feedback Power Supply (FFPS) to produce an appropriate magnetic field that stabilizes the plasma position. The simulation results obtained with the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> controller are compared with the responses of the traditional Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller. The robustness of the proposed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> controller is verified through simulation after introducing an external sinusoidal disturbance into the system. The response exhibits superior performance compared to the traditional Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller.

articleTitle: Resilient PMSM Motor Control: Advanced Fault-Tolerant Strategies for Open-Phase Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: To ensure continuous and reliable motor operation, fault detection and localization are crucial to preventing system failure. This paper examines the optimised MPCC approach based fault tolerant control of PMSM-based drives. Furthermore, comprehensive modeling, analyses, and performance assessments for validation are provided under both healthy and open-phase fault conditions. The proposed dual-framework MPCC model extends the control horizons, improving control accuracy and system performance. The OCF diagnosis is achieved by monitoring the average current and analyzing variations in the cost function while fault localization is carried out by using the polarity of normalized <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha\beta$</tex> - average current under diverse OCF conditions. The results indicate that the system response is found satisfactory under both healthy and faulty test conditions.

articleTitle: Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) Technology: Global Scenario, Future Scope, Challenges, and Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Transportation electrification is seen as a major subject of R&D as well as investment owing to climate change. Land transportation electrification is the first before the air and sea transport electrification and is seeing many major changes on engine, infrastructure, connectivity, policy, promotions, and challenges. This paper articulates the ongoing implementation and vision for V2G across the globe. Geographical influences on the implementation of V2G technology have been reported. Grid side challenges and the key components for V2G infrastructure development have been discussed. Finally, the critical aspects of power electronics for the design of efficient and reliable V2G chargers have been presented.

articleTitle: Taxonomy of Fault Analysis Methods for Protection of Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Transmission lines are bridging elements between the generation and load centre. Thus, any disturbance to it results in an unreliable electric supply to the consumers and also degrades equipment's life. It will be more severe if this prevails in complex power grids. Therefore, this inevitable condition should be sensed early to take necessary protection and control actions. This paper presents a taxonomy of fault analysis methodologies of transmission lines. This paper will be a good reference on the state of art fault analysis methods for the researchers, the academicians, and the power system engineers.

articleTitle: Integrating Data Intrusion Defense Strategy in PV Power Forecasting Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Smart grid networks are gradually participating in highly efficient and advanced intelligent cyber-physical systems with high renewable energy penetration and information technologies. The reliable operation of the grid depends on forecasting methods widely used in the industrial, commercial, and residential sectors. The forecast's accuracy depends upon the data's quality, which is vulnerable to cyberattacks. False data attacks in training data pose a significant threat to forecasting accuracy. This study introduces a data-driven, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) data poisoning technique that effectively compromises the forecasting model, even in the presence of outlier identification. This work investigated the impact of poisoning attacks on short-term solar forecasting with outlier identification. The XAI and t-SNE models are used for feature extraction and reduction, respectively. The various forecasting models are utilised, and performance results show that CNN-LSTM-Attentation is the most effective for forecasting compared to others. The obtained performance matrices MAE, MSE, RMSE, R2 score with the proposed model are 0.089, 0.026, 0.161, and 99.69%, respectively.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis of Thermal Effects on PMSM Drive Control in Small Commercial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a detailed study on the thermal effects impacting the control performance of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSM) in light commercial vehicles (LCVs). It examines thermal behaviors under various operational conditions to identify and mitigate heat generation and dissipation challenges, which affect efficiency and reliability. The analysis incorporates both mathematical analysis and considering real-time drive scenarios, to validate proposed thermal management strategies, ensuring optimal performance and longevity of PMSM drives. A neural network (NN) approach is employed to predict the derating factor (DF) based on sensor data for torque, speed, voltage, and current, significantly enhancing motor performance and ensuring smoother operation. Validations confirm substantial improvements in speed stability, enhancing user experience, longevity, and reliability of EV drives. Future work will refine these strategies and explore their applications across various EV models and driving conditions using different drive cycles.

articleTitle: An Improved Soft Switched SEPIC Topology for High Gain Static Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, the single ended primary inductor converter (SEPIC) topology is configured in such a way to achieve both zero voltage switching (ZVS) and zero current switching (ZCS) for high DC gain and reduction of major switching power losses. Novel modeling and performance evaluations are carried out by simple PWM control strategy of the (SEPIC) in addition with an auxiliary circuit to reduce the voltage and current stress across the main and auxiliary power switches as merits of the proposed topology for the versatile applications of the static converters

articleTitle: Sustainable Microgrids: TLBO Driven Multi Objective Optimization Modeling for Cost Effective Emission-Embedded Solution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This research integrates renewable energy resources into microgrid systems to address cost, emissions, and reliability concerns. Employing multi-objective optimization, the Teaching-Learning-Based Optimization (TLBO) algorithm emerges as highly effective, achieving substantial cost and greenhouse gas reductions. TLBO showcases rapid convergence and superior performance for the proposed microgrid architecture, offering valuable insights for sustainable energy planning. The proposed microgrid architecture includes micro-turbine (MT), a solar photovoltaic (PV) system, a wind turbine (WT), and a battery energy storage system (BESS). The numerical results of the proposed system compared with load supplied by main grid. The achieved cost savings of the proposed system is 66.85 % and GHG cost savings is 67.77% compared to load supplied by grid.

articleTitle: Integration of Fuel Cell System with Doubly Fed Induction Generator for Distributed Power Generation with Improved Power Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper investigates the integration of Fuel Cell System (FCS) with Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) to enhance distributed power generation. The paper begins by providing a comprehensive overview of fuel cell technology, emphasizing its advantages, limitations, and operational characteristics. The DC-DC converter steps up the voltage from the FCS to match the DC link voltage of the DFIG, enabling seamless interconnection. MPPT controller algorithm ensure that both the FCS and DFIG operate at their maximum power points, extracting optimal power from their respective fuel sources (hydrogen for FCS and wind for DFIG). Subsequently, modelling of FCS with DFIG and connection of grid, along with a non-linear load, through VSC using Kernel Control is presented in MATLAB-Simulink and verified in Real Time using OPAL-RT. Finally, the study shows optimized design and operation of integrating FCS and DFIG to improve the power quality, for a more flexible and sustainable energy infrastructure.

articleTitle: A Generalized Multilevel Converter System and its State Observation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Multilevel converters (MCs) are an integral part of many medium/high voltage and power applications. Most of the existing multilevel converter topologies share similar mathematical structures. Encapsulating numerous converter topologies, a generalized multilevel converter system (GMCS) model is proposed considering the behaviour and operating principle of MCs. For the operation of MCs, voltage sensors across the capacitors are required, which increases the complexity, and degree of maintenance. An observer design for the GMCS helps in reducing the number of sensors and provides a framework for voltage estimation for numerous MCs. It is worth mentioning that a classical Luenberger observer cannot be designed for the GMCS model due to its structural properties. Therefore, a sliding mode observer (SMO) is designed for the proposed GMCS for state observation. A modular multilevel converter (MMC) is taken as a test case of the proposed GMCS and its state observation problem is solved using the proposed SMO.

articleTitle: High-Power Three-Port Converter for Efficient EV Fast Charging Using Partial Power Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The market for battery-powered electric vehicles (EVs) has experienced significant growth, driving the demand for efficient fast-charging infrastructure. This paper presents a high-power, three-port converter designed for EV fast charging, utilizing Partial Power Processing (PPP) to enhance overall efficiency. The proposed converter features two input ports connected to the grid and a battery system, and one output port dedicated to fast charging. A key feature of this converter is the direct connection between the battery and the charging port, allowing for improved power transfer capabilities. Additionally, a series resonant converter (SRC) is employed to enable unidirectional fast charging, optimizing the converter's performance for high-power applications. Through a series of simulations, the converter's efficiency and power-handling capabilities were analyzed, confirming its ability to significantly reduce power losses while ensuring reliable and efficient fast charging. The results demonstrate the converter's potential to meet the growing demands of EV infrastructure by improving power density, lowering system costs, and maintaining essential isolation between the grid and the vehicle.

articleTitle: Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading Among Electricity-Hydrogen DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This article presents the optimal operation of a community of “non-positive aggregate energy importing” DC microgrids in a local energy-sharing environment. DC microgrid community aims to minimize its social cost by participating in a day-ahead and peer-to-peer energy market, and local hydrogen market. Based on the price signals from the grid, the DC microgrids determine their power exchange with the grid and schedule its dispatchable sources (fuel cell and microturbine), renewable power generation (solar and wind), energy storage (battery energy storage system and hydrogen storage system), and flexible loads (electrolyzer, thermostatically-controlled load, and plug-in electric vehicle) in a privacy-preserving decentralized manner. Further, each DC microgrid has bidding price flexibility when participating in peer-to-peer transactions. Simulation studies are carried out on a community of three six-bus DC microgrid systems. Fixed-price peer-to-peer trading increases social welfare by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 74.23\%$</tex> compared to no peer-to-peer trading. Bidding price flexibility adds <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 1.83\%$</tex> to social welfare, reduces renewable curtailment by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 2.58\%$</tex>, raises cumulative peer-to-peer transactions by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 13.42\%$</tex>, and lowers the average peer-to-peer price by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 30.47\%$</tex>. Increasing the DC microgrid's hydrogen storage system size further improves social welfare. Transitioning from no peer-to-peer trading to fixed and then flexible bidding price peer-to-peer trading increases DC microgrid energy diversion from the grid towards the DC microgrid cluster's self-sufficiency.

articleTitle: Hybrid Deep LSTM-XGBoost Based Fault Line Identification and Distance Estimation in Grids with Distributed Generators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Worldwide, electricity use is growing in popularity to promote sustainable human living and economic prosperity. Human existence is extremely impossible without power, and the nation's ability to function normally will collapse. In order to meet the world's power demand, distributed renewable energy generator integration is growing rapidly these days. Power systems frequently experience faults, which are not totally prevented. However, sophisticated techniques mitigate the fault quickly, allowing the power system to recover. Two difficult yet essential tasks for the power system to function continuously are fault distance estimation and fault line identification. Because distributed energy sources integrate dynamically and have bidirectional current flow with a low magnitude of fault current, fault diagnosis becomes more difficult. Although machine learning models have gained popularity recently, feature engineering on them requires manual preprocessing. This study proposes a hybrid of deep learning and ensemble learning models, i.e., Deep Long-sort term memory and Extreme Gradient Boosting (LSTM-XGBoost), for fault line identification and fault distance estimation tasks. Two different distributed generators have been used to perform this task: a Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) wind turbine and a diesel generator. Different fault configurations have been created, including resistances, initiation angles, and locations. A hybrid of the Deep LSTM-XGBoost model gives better 99.58 % accuracy and 0.0045 MAE for the intended tasks. Various comparisons with existing deep learning models from literature surveys have been discussed. Hardware in Loop (HIL) simulation has been performed to validate the robustness and flexibility of the proposed model using the OPAL-RT 4510 real-time simulator.

articleTitle: Flexibility Trading from P2P Networks to Improve the Grid Frequency Response in the Presence of RTEM and MARL-Based AGC Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: With the gradual shift from conventional units to renewable energy sources (RES), the modern grid is facing diminished frequency regulation (FR) capabilities, making traditional control methods less effective. In response, this paper proposes an advanced multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) control strategy for FR in a RES-dominated power system. The system includes a residential microgrid with diverse distributed energy resources engaged in peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading at the distribution level, while automatic generation control (AGC) and a dynamic real-time energy market (RTEM) coordinate at the transmission level to balance load and generation. The RTEM dispatches energy every five minutes to support the FR process, complementing AGC operations. Following disturbances, the microgrid utilizes demand-side flexibility alongside AGC and RTEM operations to quickly restore system frequency to its steady state. MARL, implemented using the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient algorithm, is applied to both AGC and microgrid systems. Here, P2P trading is facilitated through a consumer-prosumer contract participation matrix. The results show that flexibility from P2P networks, in conjunction with AGC and RTEM systems, significantly improves grid frequency response.

articleTitle: A Transistorized DC Commutatorless Series Motor Drive with Reduced Torque Ripple for Electrified Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a Transistorized DC Commutatorless Series Motor Drive (CLSM) which will find applications for electrified vehicles (EV) for its natural inverse torque-speed characteristics with low torque ripples. The basic configuration of the solid-state power electronic converter and the machine is presented first with its operation explained. Mathematical model of the drive is presented next, followed by the developed phasor diagram. The results of the numerical simulation are presented later. The conclusions are presented at the end. The simulation results prove that the proposed drive will be a strong contender for traction applications because of its natural ‘series’ type of torque-speed, current-speed and torque-current characteristics, lower low-frequency component of torque ripples, lower ‘dv/dt’ stress to machine armature windings, simplicity of drive control and operability from a low-voltage DC battery pack.

articleTitle: Soft Switching Region Expansion for Three-Phase Dual Active Bridge based on Phase Shift Design of Wye-Asymmetric Extended Delta Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The three-phase dual active bridge (3p-DAB) converter plays a crucial role in high-power applications due to its superior power density compared to single-phase variants. However, during light load operation, the 3p-DAB can suffer from reduced efficiency due to the loss of soft-switching capability. This paper presents a generalized mathematical model for the three-limb transformer, highlighting the effect of partitioning the secondary phase windings on the transformer's phase shift angle. By dividing the secondary winding into two unevenly distributed sets of windings, the soft-switching region of the 3p-DAB can be improved. The analysis in this paper also utilizes a complex variable stationary reference frame to capture the exact solution of the winding currents, providing a comprehensive understanding of the system behaviour. Furthermore, the paper examines the impact of secondary winding partitioning on the soft-switching region of the 3p-DAB, particularly for the extended delta transformer connection. The insights and analytical techniques presented in this digest can be valuable for engineers and researchers working on the design and optimization of3p-DAB converters, enabling them to enhance the efficiency and performance of these high-power density systems.

articleTitle: Circulating Current Mitigation Among Sources in DC Microgrid Using Distributed Secondary Controllers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In general droop controllers are utilized in microgrids to ensure fair power sharing between similar sources when feeding different loads. Nevertheless, due to the difference in feeding line impedances, the supplied power from different sources varies from its expected values. To mitigate this problem a modified method of droop controller that utilizes the shift and/or adjustment in the droop gain is proposed in this literature. The current used techniques give an improved performance as it allows a higher degree of freedom to the controller. Nevertheless, these techniques use distributed proportional-integral control, that can cause a winding-up phenomenon. Further, the dynamic response of the secondary controller is poor while taking the action to improve the current sharing accuracy among the source current converters. To alleviate the issue, a modified secondary controller with the employment of full communication system has been proposed in the paper. The information of each source current is shared among the sources by low bandwidth communication. The suggested secondary controller ensures proportional sharing of current among the sources and improves the dynamic response of dc microgrid. To improve the dynamic response of the microgrid, the step size by which the secondary controller modifies the droop gain of the sources is adaptively changed so as to damp out the oscillations occurring in the microgrid during step variation in load demand. The proposed controller enhances the effective damping of dc source converter and suppressing unwanted oscillations occurring in dc microgrid. The performance of the suggested modified secondary controller is validated from the simulation studies taken place under MATLAB/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: A Novel Trapezoidal EMF Flux Switching Brushless DC Motor for a Pedal-Assist E-Bicycle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Recent pollution levels worldwide have led the world to search for a clean and efficient way of transportation as an alternative to internal combustion (IC) engine vehicles. In this paper, the design of a novel trapezoidal electromagnetic force (EMF) flux-switching brushless dc (FS BLDC) hub motor for a pedal-assist E-bicycle is proposed. The proposed motor is similar to a flux-switching permanent magnet (FSPM) motor. However, the EMF of FSPM motor is sinusoidal making it necessary to use encoders for position sensing. The proposed FS BLDC motor has a trapezoidal back-EMF and it is operated like a brushless dc (BLDC) motor. Further, ferrite permanent magnets (PMs) are used in the motor to make it economical. The hub-drive based E-bicycles usually employ conventional BLDC motors which have less rotor outer diameter for placing the PMs. Hence, a conventional FSPM motor is redesigned with a trapezoidal EMF, which has more magnetic loading due to the placement of magnets in the stator. Further, a 2-D finite element (FE) analysis of the proposed 24-slot, 20-pole trapezoidal EMF outer rotor FS BLDC motor is carried-out and the results are presented. In addition, a prototype is fabricated, experimental validation is carried-out and the results are presented.

articleTitle: Investigations on Rotary Transformer Configurations for Brushless Operation of Electrically-Excited Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Permanent magnet AC (PMAC) machines are popular in high-end applications due to their high power density and efficiency but rely on rare-earth materials, require complex and limited field weakening operations, and are prone to the risk of demagnetization of permanent magnets. On the other hand, the electrically/hybrid-excited synchronous machines (EESMs/HESMs) are immune to these problems but employ brush and slip ring-based field excitation mechanism, which poses a challenge for high-performance applications. In this regard, rotary transformer-based technology offers a promising brushless field excitation mechanism. Therefore, in this paper, several configurations of rotary transformer reported in literature are studied and the five most promising ones are selected for further investigations. These five configurations are analytically modeled and simulated using finite element analysis (FEA), maintaining consistent nominal ratings. The results of analytical models and 3D FEA simulations show good agreement. Finally, the parameters and performance indices of the five configurations are compared, and based on the relative merits, the most suitable configuration is recommended for EESMs/HESMs.

articleTitle: Decentralized Frequency and DC-Voltage Deviation Control in Multi-Terminal HVDC (MTDC) Grids with High Penetration of Renewable Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In the AC surrounded MTDC (AC-MTDC) grids, Frequency and DC-Voltage Deviation (FDVD) control are decisive for the system stability, and reliability. Accomplishing it through the decentralized manner while reducing interaction between droop controls is more exigent. To address this problem, FDVD based Adaptive Droop Control (FDVD-ADC) has been proposed in this paper. It adaptively changes Grid Side Voltage Source Converters (GS-VSC's), and Renewable Source side Voltage Source Converters (RS-VSCs) say Wind Farm VSC (WF-VSC) or Solar Farms VSC (SF-VSC) droop values based upon the deviation in frequency, and DC-voltage in the AC-MTDC grid. With the proposed method, renewable sources (like solar and wind farms) are also utilized to reduce FDVD in the AC-MTDC grid. To extract this support, these bulk solar and wind farms are operated in the Derated Mode of Operation (DMO). The simulation of the proposed method has been implemented on the CIGRE B4 DC benchmark model integrated into the two-area power system in PSCAD/EMTDC software. The efficacy of the proposed methodology is validated by comparing the traditional double droop control <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(PV^{2}F)$</tex> with the proposed method.

articleTitle: Modular Hybrid Series-Parallel DC-DC Converter for HVDC to MVDC Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The benefits of high voltage direct Current (HVDC) technology have made it indispensable for power systems. They consist of lower losses, simpler asynchronous grid connections, better controllability, increased system availability, and a decrease in short-circuit currents. This article introduces a new modular hybrid series-parallel DC-DC Converter (MHSPDC) topology designed for efficient power transfer in HVDC- medium voltage direct current (MVDC) applications. Each phase of a series DC-AC structure and a parallel AC-DC structure, interconnected by a single-phase isolated transformer. This new topology offers significant reductions in footprint and initial investment costs while enhancing converter efficiency. The article provides a brief description of the circuit configuration, operational principles of the converter and mathematical analysis of capacitor sizing used in the converter topology. The MATLAB/PSCAD simulation software is utilized to validate the novel configuration. During the simulation, a phase disposition technique is employed as PWM for converter switching.

articleTitle: Closed Loop Control of Induction Motor Operated with Hybrid PWM(SVM+SOPWM) at Low Switching Frequency for Traction Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper addresses challenges related to harmonic distortion in closed-loop control systems for high-power traction motors operating at low switching frequencies (<400 Hz) using a 2-level inverter. While low switching frequencies aim to minimize semiconductor switching losses, they often lead to increased harmonic distortion, motor losses, and torque ripple. To tackle these issues, the paper proposes a novel pulse width modulation (PWM) technique that integrates asynchronous and synchronous space vector modulation (SVM) with synchronized optimal modulation for a 2-level inverter. The PWM method incorporates various pulse numbers, including SVM-based asynchronous pulse numbers, SVM-based synchronous pulse numbers (21, 15), and synchronous optimal (SOPWM) pulse numbers (11, 9, 7, 5, 3). The SOPWM technique exclusively employs continuous optimal switching angles for true optimality through nonlinear constrained optimization, without considering post-optimization techniques. Furthermore, the proposed PWM technique enhances the fundamental voltage without the need for pre-modulation. Experimental results, demonstrating the efficacy of the PWM technique in reducing harmonic distortion and improving motor performance, are presented for a two-level inverter feeding an induction machine in a closed-loop control manner across the entire speed range.

articleTitle: Seamless Operation and Improved Control of a Standalone Solar-Wind-BES Driven 3P4W System Designed for Remote Onshore Island Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Remote onshore island-based power systems require necessity of neutral point due to presence of single-phase loads. Moreover, existence of nonlinear loads overloads neutral wire of wind system transformer, especially in remote systems driven by wind generators, making them more prone to heating and failure. This work presents a novel configuration of a three phase four-wire islanded doubly fed induction generator (DFIG)-based wind energy conversion system (WECS) tied to a local grid formed by a local grid-forming converter (LGFC), supported at DC link by a battery energy storage (BES) and a solar photovoltaic (SPV) array. System utilizes fourth leg of LGFC to compensate for load neutral current demand, ensuring reactive power and harmonic current compensation for unity power factor (UP F) operation of WECS. Rotor end converter (REC) ensures maximum power point tracking (MPPT) of wind turbine and supplements machine reactive power requirement. Suboptimal wind speeds and maintenance require disconnection of DFIG stator without interrupting power flow to loads. Reactive, negative sequence, and harmonic current requirements of connected loads is compensated by LGFC. This enables smooth power exchange among sources and ensures continuous power flow to loads, regardless of DFIG power generation. A seamless adaptation strategy is presented for smooth disconnection/ reconnection of DFIG stator. This seamless control strategy enables uninterrupted transitions. To mitigate power quality issues arising from loads, an improved generalized robust logarithmic family least absolute difference (IGRLF-LAD) control is implemented to enhance PCC voltage and stator current quality. Simulation results demonstrate alignment of system operation with IEEE std. 1547.

articleTitle: Evaluation of an Intelligent Controller for Electric Vehicle Charging with Vienna Rectifier Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The Vienna rectifier is a widely used topology in a variety of industrial applications, including electric vehicle (EV) charging. Although conventional control approaches exist, the nonlinear and highly dynamic nature of the Vienna rectifier as well as many existing uncertainties within the system hinder the development of a performant controller based on classic control theory. This paper proposes a model-free controller based on reinforcement learning (RL) to optimize the performance of the DC-link voltage control loop with concurrent regulation of the power factor. We developed a state-space model of the Vienna rectifier in MATLAB/Simulink and a classical proportional-integral (PI) controller for quantitative comparison. The RL controller's ability to handle system nonlinearities and component uncertainties, such as inductor and capacitor tolerances, enables it to outperform classical control strategies. Furthermore, this paper benchmarks multiple RL-based algorithms including deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) as well as twin delayed DDPG (TD3) in the voltage control loop. The results demonstrate that TD3 can reduce 2.5 percent voltage ripple and has a shorter settling time of 0.75 s at the cost of higher computational requirements.

articleTitle: A Variable Switching Frequency PWM Technique to Reduce Conducted Emissions of SiC MOSFET Based Active Front End Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Wide band gap (WBG) device based power electronic converters are evolving nowadays due to their high switching frequency and high power density. The conducted emission noise due to the switching frequency of the converter violates electromagnetic interference (EMI) standards. Large passive EMI filters are typically used to comply with the standards. The present work proposes a variable switching frequency based modulation technique to attenuate the low-frequency conducted emission of an active front end (AFE) converter. The majority of frequency dithering methods ignore the issues related to the resolution band width (RBW) of the spectrum analyzer. RBW refers to the bandwidth of the band-pass filter of the spectrum analyzer, which accumulates the energies of all frequency components falling within this band and displays a single frequency spectrum. While measuring the noise, it must be fixed at 9kHz as specified by international regulations. This article addresses the impact of RBW on noise measurement, and a modification in the existing technique is also presented such that the noise spectrum of different frequencies does not overlap within a 9kHz bandwidth to obtain maximum noise reduction. The proposed method has been implemented on a 22kW, 800V, three-phase AFE converter through MATLAB Simulink. A reduction of 16dBμV and 5.5dBμV on conducted emission noises have been observed for 500Hz and 9kHz RBW, respectively, and the results are compared with those of constant switching frequency operation.

articleTitle: Realization of Machine Learning Algorithms for Diagnosing Winding Faults in Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The reliability and efficiency of squirrel cage induction motors (SCIMs) are most important in industrial applications, where failures can lead to significant downtime and economic losses. Among the common faults, stator winding faults are particularly detrimental, leading to degraded motor performance and potentially catastrophic failures if undetected at the incipient stage. Various approaches aiding machine learning algorithms are adapted for diagnosing machine faults. This paper realizes different machine learning algorithms to diagnose the winding faults of SCIM. A comprehensive dataset of motor current signatures is trained and validated with several machine-learning models using Python in the Anaconda platform. A detailed comparative analysis of the model's performance is conducted based on metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and computational efficiency. This research highlights the potential of integrating machine learning techniques into SCIM monitoring systems, offering a proactive approach to maintenance and reducing unscheduled downtimes. Future work will explore the deployment of these models in real-time monitoring systems and the expansion of the dataset to include various motor types and fault conditions.

articleTitle: Ageing Estimation of Transformer Oil by Ladder Phenomena
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this work, condition of acid aged transformer oil based insulation is assessed. For this purpose, three types of oil insulation (Mineral oil, Natural Ester and Synthetic Ester) are selected as base oil. In addition, formic, acetic and levulinic acids are chosen to prepare different aged insulation. Therefore, the prepared samples are subjected to a non-invasive FDS test to obtain important dielectric parameters such as AC conductivity and dielectric loss. It is observed from the AC conductivity profiles that it exhibits an imperative property i.e. “Ladder phenomena”. Considering this phenomenon, different threshold frequencies are calculated and found to be aging sensitive. Therefore, the impact of acid ageing corresponding to different polarization and relaxation mechanisms are discussed using those novel aging sensitive parameters.

articleTitle: SOGI-FLL Based Advanced Adaptive Control of a PV-BES System for Weak Grid Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a weak grid operation of a utility-integrated Photovoltaic (PV) - battery energy storage (BES) system delivering a non-linear load at the distribution end. The weak grid operational capabilities of the PV-BES system are ensured by second-order generalized integrated (SOGI) - fixed frequency loop (FLL) assisted constrained generalized maximum correntropy criteria (CGMCC) based adaptive control. The SOGI algorithm filters the grid voltage harmonics, subdues the effect of grid voltage sag/swell and unbalancing, and produces distortion-free and sinusoidal unit templates during weak grid conditions (WGC). FLL delivers the desired reference frequency to the voltage source converter (VSC) control algorithm. Likewise, CGMCC overcomes the current-related power quality issues arising from the non-linear load, i.e., current harmonics suppression, load balancing, active power control, and reactive power compensation at the point of common coupling (PCC). The FLL-SOGI complements the CGMCC algorithm in controlling VSC, keeping the PV-BES system stable, delivering PV power to the grid, and performing ancillary services. The BES system further enhances the DC bus stability by minimizing the effect of irregular PV power generation and reducing the DC bus voltage variations during diverse, dynamic conditions. The presented system's performance under numerous dynamic conditions and WGC is satisfactory per IEEE 1547–2019 standard.

articleTitle: Open Circuit Fault-Tolerant Two-Level STATCOM with Balanced Line Currents
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Three phase Static Compensators (STATCOM) using Pulse Width Modulated (PWM) converters are widely used for shunt compensation in transmission lines. In case only two of the STATCOM legs remain connected to the grid due to an open circuit fault in one of its legs or line reactors, existing fault-tolerant schemes cannot continue operation with balanced grid side line currents. A new scheme is presented in this paper in which the STATCOM can continue operation during single line open circuit fault and inject balanced line currents, without additional redundant leg or switches. The proposed fault-tolerant technique adjusts the phase shift between the current in the two operative leg of the STATCOM and uses a full VA rated delta-star coupling/isolation transformer to inject balanced VAr into the grid. This arrangement provides a simple solution for incorporating fault-tolerant capability during design of 3-leg STATCOM. Simulation and experimental results are presented to validate the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Comparison of Sub-Modules for Cascaded Multi-Level MVAC to DC Solid State Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: High-power DC applications require medium voltage grid integration to reduce transmission losses as it requires lower current for the same power. Conventionally the DC port is interfaced to the medium voltage grid using low voltage power electronic converter and line frequency transformers (LFT) to step up low voltage AC (LVAC) to medium voltage AC (MVAC). Line frequency transformer-less MV grid integration is an attractive solution as it gets rid of heavy LFT, improving the power density, configurability, and efficiency of the overall system. Cascaded modular multi-level converters have become one of the most preferred choices with input series output parallel (ISOP) structure per phase using low voltage devices and modules. There are different kinds of sub-modules used for the input series output parallel architecture. Though two-stage and single-stage sub-modules are used in this ISOP structure, a detailed comparison between them in terms of size and efficiency is missing in the literature. A comprehensive comparison is made between the two-stage and single-stage sub-modules within ISOP solutions, and it is presented in this paper. Three central matrices, semiconductor VA rating, efficiency and power density/volume, are the basis for the comparison. The results are presented for a theoretical design of 400 kW, 11 kV/50 Hz MVAC to 800V LVDC system using SiC devices, and the conclusions are drawn.

articleTitle: Hybrid Renewable Energy Sources for Grid Connected System with Model Predictive Control for Maximum Power Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a finite-set model predictive torque control (FS-MPTC) for a wind energy conversion system (WECS) to maximize power extraction. The method focuses on optimizing the wind generator system (WGS) control to efficiently convert wind energy into electrical power. In parallel, the paper also explores the application of model predictive control (MPC) for photovoltaic systems (PVS). With this method, the photovoltaic system is guaranteed to continually extract the maximum power, maximizing energy acquisition in the face of fluctuating solar irradiation conditions. Additionally, MPC is utilized on the grid side to manage and regulate both active and reactive power, ensuring stable and efficient operation of the entire energy system. The hybrid system includes both WGS and the PVS which are connected to the same DC link via controlled rectifier and DC-DC converter, respectively. Then, a three-phase inverter is used to feed the power into the grid. The MPC is adopted in this work to eliminate the proportional-integral (PI) controllers and the associated tuning complexities. Moreover, the MPC offers a more responsive control strategy, which is necessary for managing the dynamic response of renewable energy sources. The system performances are validated through simulations and testing under fixed wind speed and varying solar irradiation. This testing condition highlights the potential of MPC in improving the efficiency of hybrid renewable energy systems by demonstrating the capacity to maintain maximum output power and reliable grid integration.

articleTitle: Design of an Active PFC Flyback Converter for Auxiliary Power Supply in Power Converter Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Power electronic converter requires a low-power auxiliary supply to operate its control circuits. This paper presents the design and implementation of an auxiliary power supply for a three-phase inverter utilizing an active power factor correction(PFC)-based flyback converter. The auxiliary power supply provides an isolated and stable DC voltage to IGBT gate drivers, DSP controller, sensing circuit, power relay circuits and heat sink fans in three-phase inverters. The active PFC flyback converter rated for 48 W, converts universal input of 90–265 V, 50 Hz AC to 24 V, 2 A DC output. The LT3798 controller IC provides a powerful and efficient solution for designing a flyback converter with active PFC. It ensures that the input current closely follows the input voltage, achieving a power factor equal to unity. This improves power quality, minimizes harmonic distortion and ensures EMI compliance with international standards such as CISPR 32. This IC regulates the output voltage and current at varying load conditions for a wide range of input voltage. The design method involves selecting the appropriate transformer, output capacitor, snubber circuit for the MOSFET and diode, an EMI filter, and protection circuits for the controller. In addition, the paper discusses practical hardware aspects related to thermal management using PCB layout. The experimental results validate the performance of the proposed design, affirming its suitability and effectiveness for the required application.

articleTitle: Speed Control of PV-Fed BLDC Motor with Energy Storage Integration Using Modified Adaptable Step-Size P&O MPPT Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a proportional-integral (PI) controller-based speed control mechanism for a PV array-fed electronically commutated brushless direct current (BLDC) drive system integrated with a Li-ion battery as an energy storage solution. The proposed system employs a 2-channel direct coupled interleaved boost (2C-DCIB) converter to improve ripple content and perform forward stage voltage boosting operation. To optimize the power extraction from the PV array, a modified adaptable step-size P&O (MASP) MPPT technique is utilized. This technique dynamically adjusts the step size in response to the rate of change in power, voltage and current ensuring faster to reach the true maximum power point (MPP) of the array under varying weather conditions with reduced steady-state oscillation and less power loss. The integration of the Li-ion battery through bidirectional DC-DC converter (BDDC) provides additional energy buffering during fluctuating solar irradiance. Simulation results validate the efficacy of the proposed control strategy, showing that the motor speed closely follows the reference speed command even under dynamic irradiation profiles. The DC-bus voltage exhibits minimal fluctuations despite variations in solar power input, demonstrating the controller's ability to regulate voltage consistently and ensure stable power delivery to the motor, making it suitable for various solar-powered applications, including aqua pumping with varying flow rates.

articleTitle: Interleaved Sigma-Delta Current Sense for Improved Direct Torque Control of PMSM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Motor control is a prominent aspect of many industry applications. Although field-oriented control (FOC) is an established concept in industrial drives, direct torque control (DTC) can offer simpler implementation and faster dynamics. Existing literature focuses on evaluating hybrid DTC techniques on FPGA-DSP sets to achieve the desired speed and precision through the FPGA, while the DSP allows more complex control routines for the motor control. Controllers with ARM architecture on the other hand lack the necessary speed on the sensing chain for precise and fast-responding DTC controls. This paper evaluates DTC on an ARM microcontroller and uses external interleaved delta-sigma analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) for fast high-precision current sensing, which is crucial for an effective DTC. We present an interleaved current sensing approach with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$<\mathbf{4}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{s}$</tex> update rate, which the state of the art could at best achieve through an expensive FPGA. Additionally, the ARM architecture offers a low-cost alternative to existing FPGA systems. The solution scales well and can be extrapolated to achieve even higher update rates. The simulation in MATLAB/Simulink and measurements on the real motor and electronics hardware demonstrate the performance of the solution.

articleTitle: Congestion Management in Distribution System through Distribution Congestion Prices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: With the advancement of technology and the development of smart grid systems, there has been significant increase in electricity demand, which is traditionally addressed through fixed methods. In this paper, Optimal Power Flow (OPF) is considered and executed for cases involving limits, referred to as congestion, as well as for cases without limits, referred to as non-congestion. In a deregulated power system, it is understood that without regulation and congestion limits, inefficiencies in generation can be avoided. This paper introduces an innovative approach for estimating Distribution Congestion Prices (DCPs) based on nodal market mechanism. In recent years, congestion management was formulated traditionally in the transmission system level however due to the growing use of Distributed Generator (DG) and anticipated loading demand, congestion management procedure must also be implemented in the distribution system. The analysis utilizes Nodal Congestion Pricing (NCP) method, which influences the interaction between distribution system operators (DSOs) and the overall Distribution Congestion Prices are calculated. Finally, a practical 6-bus distribution system network is used as a test case to demonstrate the present of congestion in the distributed network.

articleTitle: Validation of a Novel Hybrid on-Board Charging System for Light Electric Vehicles in Hilly Terrain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The growing interest of automakers, governments, and consumers in electric vehicles (EVs) and hybrid EVs (HEVs) is driven by increasing environmental concerns. Among these alternatives, plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs) are gaining popularity. These vehicles require their batteries to be charged either at home using regular outlets or at business parking lots, impacting the distribution grid with additional electrical loads. This can lead to power losses and voltage fluctuations, especially when charging is uncoordinated, causing disorganized electricity usage and local grid issues. Smart grids face significant challenges due to unpredictable load demands and the intermittent nature of renewable energy sources (RESs). One effective solution is using storage devices to store excess energy from RESs and release it back into the grid as needed. To improve power management and resource utilization, a novel hybrid on-board charging system for hilly terrain is proposed. This system integrates a solar photovoltaic system with converters, batteries, supercapacitors, and drive systems to ensure efficient energy use and charging, even when external power sources are unavailable. The key objectives are to optimize charging operations, drive operations, and energy management. The inclusion of regenerative braking further extends the driving range of EVs and enhances energy efficiency. Compared to other methods, the proposed system shows superior realization, robustness, and efficiency. The simulation findings are presented in open-loop control, demonstrating the feasibility and benefits of the proposed method. Finally, the system's effectiveness is validated using Typhoon HIL 402, which analyzes the state of charge of Li-ion batteries in different modes during standstill conditions.

articleTitle: Three-Phase Interleaved Bidirectional Resonant Converter for Charging / Discharging Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The introduction of electric vehicles (EVs) has caused the transportation sector to shift from conventional gasoline-based energy to an electricity-based energy solution. However, in order to optimize the charging cost, localization of electricity generation using renewable sources such as solar and wind energy and microgrid-based charging stations is essential. In order to charge different segments of EVs, different voltage and current ratings are required. This article presents a three-phase interleaved bidirectional resonant converter (TPIBRC) with the capability of power flow in both the directions. The interleaving of the resonant converter reduces ripple current, and splitting into multiphase reduces the peak current of the converter. The converter is designed for charging / discharging a three-wheeler 72V battery pack using a 360V dc bus. A control methodology is developed for implementing pulse width modulation and frequency modulation to regulate the output power and voltage for TPIBRC. The simulation results have been presented with ZVS soft switching for a variation of input voltage from 350V to 370V.

articleTitle: Saliency Enhancement Design of PMaSynRM through Kriging Surrogate Modeling Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: PMaSynRM is emerging as a promising alternative to PMSMs used in electric vehicle propulsion systems. PMaSynRM inherits high reluctance torque with minimal magnet contribution. The traditional method of optimizing the performance of electric motors is complex, as it involves many parameters and is also time-consuming. In the context of improving the performance of PMaSynRM with minimal computational cost, this paper proposes a Kriging surrogate modeling approach integrated with the Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm-II. In this approach, initially, the rotor parameters that influence the performance characteristics of PMaSynRM, such as torque, torque ripple and saliency, are identified. These significant rotor parameters are sampled within their bounds using the Halton sequence method, and with these samples the Design of Experiments (DOE) is conducted using the full factorial method. The responses obtained from DOE through FEA simulations are considered as true responses. A surrogate model is also created using these samples to predict the response and its accuracy is assessed by comparing it with the true response. To showcase the effectiveness of the optimization approach, this paper considers a 1.5 kW 36-slot 6-pole PMaSynRM with a fluid flux barrier rotor. The proposed approach results in a saliency of 6.64 and torque ripple of about 7.03 % respectively. Saliency is improved nearly by 2.5 times compared to a recent work having the same torque ripple.

articleTitle: Intelligent Algorithms for Fault Localization in Unbalanced Active Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The accuracy of conventional fault location schemes relies on extracted fundamental phasor during fault and linearity of the system. However, the addition of renewable-based sources adds nonlinearity and increases the power quality issues; this results in erroneous fault distance computation leading to an increase in restoration time, which is not desirable. Further, with increased nonlinear controllers and loads, it is difficult to establish a relation between the system and its measurements in an unbalanced active distribution system (UADS). However, smart intelligent meters and advanced grid communication gather huge data sets which are utilized for monitoring, and control purposes and can also be applicable for identifying faulty sections and fault locations. Nevertheless, handling features extracted from huge data sets requires a machine learning (ML) approach. In this paper, the change in phase and sequence currents is utilized as input to ML algorithms to classify different types of faults and locate accurate fault locations in UADS. A comparative analysis of various supervised ML algorithms is presented, including Support Vector Machine (SVM), k-nearest Neighbours (KNN), Random Forest Algorithm (RFA), Logistic Regression (LR), and Naive Bayes (NB). The performance of these algorithms is analysed via simulations of IEEE 33-bus system with photovoltaic integration, in MATLAB/SIMULINK 2023 and Jupyter Notebook for various loading conditions and different types of faults with variations in resistances and found satisfactory.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Charging Techniques for Lithium-Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: As electric vehicles (EVs) continue to gain widespread use, enhancing battery charging efficiency and minimizing deterioration have become key priorities. The charging patterns of the EV battery substantially impact charging time and battery deterioration. This paper assesses various charging techniques for Lithium-ion (Li-ion) cells, focusing on key parameters such as current, terminal voltage, state of charge (SoC), and temperature variation over time. The charging techniques analyzed include constant current-constant voltage (CC-CV), boost charging, constant power-constant voltage (CP-CV), constant temperature-constant voltage (CT-CV), pulse charging, and sinusoidal ripple charging (SRC). These methods were simulated under identical conditions to evaluate their impact on charging time and temperature rise. This paper offers critical insights into optimizing battery charging, enhancing performance, and extending battery longevity by evaluating the efficacy of various strategies.

articleTitle: Tilt Integral Derivative Frequency Controller for Isolated Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The complex nature of microgrid systems involving components such as solar, wind-turbine, fuel cell, and energy storage systems, has posed a significant problem for load-frequency control (LFC). This digest article proposes a tilt integral derivative (TID<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">μ</sup>) controller with a single tuneable parameter for enhanced resiliency of an isolated microgrid. The sole tuning parameter of TID<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">μ</sup> controller is intended to accomplish a good trade-off between performance and resilience. The effectiveness of the proposed controller is assessed in the occurrence of parametric uncertainties and random load disturbance. Based on these simulation results, it is clear that the proposed controller has better resilience compared to the state of the art.

articleTitle: A Sensing Coil in Inductive EV Charging Systems for Estimating the Coupling Coefficient and Receiver Resonant Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for the construction and implementation of a sensing coil in wireless Inductive Power Transfer (IPT) systems, specifically aimed at observing and predicting the coupling coefficient as well as the receiver-side resonant frequency in LCC-S compensated systems of the receiving coil. remains an enigma. The method revealed here has universal applicability for wireless charging solutions, targeting Two, Three, and Four-wheeled vehicles, all without requiring prior knowledge of the specific parameters of the receiving coil. The sensing coil is disconnected from the transmitting coil, instead forming a link with the receiving coil to assimilate the phase data of the current flowing at the receiver end. A solitary zero-crossing voltage sensor is used to record the voltage across the sensing coil. The approach relies on two deliberate frequency sweeps designed to locate the point at which the AC output voltage aligns in phase or deviates in phase with respect to the AC input. This innovation enables meticulous approximation of vital parameters, thereby improving the accuracy and reliability of wireless inductive power transmission systems.

articleTitle: A Rule-Based Energy Management System for Remote Area Hybrid Standalone Energy Systems with Hydrogen Energy Storage Systems to Improve the Reliability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The variability of RESs and their intermittent output power against the stochastic energy consumption, especially for standalone hybrid power systems, have spurred the development of new long-term energy storage solutions for improving the reliability in remote areas. Currently, the reliability of remote area hybrid standalone energy systems is affected due to the absence of long-term energy storage systems, as existing systems include batteries that are not capable of ensuring short-term reliability. Hence, there is an ongoing discussion on solar-powered water electrolysis systems to produce and store hydrogen utilizing excess generation, which can later be to generate electricity through fuel cells for providing long-term storage solutions. Though new long-term hydrogen storage solutions can improve the reliability, the optimal utilization of different components of remote area hybrid energy systems having solar photovoltaic systems, batteries, electrolyzers, hydrogen tanks, fuel cells; is a complex issue and the overall techno-economic benefits will be significantly affected if the energy coordination among different components is not properly carried out. This paper proposes a rule-based energy management system (RL-EMS) for appropriately coordinating energy in remote area hybrid energy systems and determining optimal sizes of different components so that the overall system cost is reduced while meeting the supply-demand balance. Simulations are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed RL-EMS under changing power supply and load demand conditions. The simulation results confirm that the RL-EMS assist in meeting continuously changing load demands (with a maximum load of 20 kW) through a 20 kW solar PV, 5 kW battery, 10 kW fuel cell, 12 kW electrolyzer, and a 10 kg hydrogen tank, while achieving a minimum levelized cost of electricity of $0.2743 per kWh and improving the reliability.

articleTitle: Design, Analysis and Comparison of 5kW Synchronous Reluctance Motor and Interior PM Synchronous Motor for EV Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents the design and comparative analysis of a Synchronous Reluctance Motor (SynRM) and an Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (IPMSM) for electric vehicle applications. The primary objective is to evaluate the feasibility of SynRM, a rare-earth-magnet-free motor, as a viable alternative to PM-based motors. A 5 kW, 3000 RPM IPMSM is used as a reference design, providing the benchmark for developing two SynRM variants for equivalent power and torque ratings. A comprehensive analysis is conducted at both rated and peak operating points, comparing flux densities and electromagnetic performance of the motor. The study reveals that due to the lack of rotor excitation in SynRM, achieving comparable performance requires trade-offs in current density or motor size. To match the peak torque of the IPMSM within the same frame size, significantly higher current densities are necessary for the SynRM, primarily due to core saturation effects. Further, the influence of current magnitude and current angle on the saliency ratio and inductances of the SynRM is also examined. Finally, the Finite Element Analysis (FEA) and Maximum Torque per Ampere (MTPA) characteristic of the SynRM variant with 30% higher motor volume is presented compared to the IPMSM. The results show that SynRM achieves the desired rated performance, i.e., rated torque of 16.8 Nm with a torque ripple of 8% at 2982 RPM and efficiency of 91.7%.

articleTitle: A Smart Control for Multi-Functional 3P4W Grid Interfaced PV-BES System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, control algorithm for robust variable step size-least mean square (RVSS-LMS) adaptive filter is designed and put to use for solar photo voltaic (PV)-three-phase, four-wire, grid-interfaced system. Such a system is powered by a hybrid combination of PV and an optimum sized battery. The controller aims to operate the system so as to inject the surplus power obtained (after catering to loads) as an active power to the utility mains. Therefore, the voltage source converter (VSC) in the grid interfaced solar energy conversion system also operates as a distribution static compensator. As a result, harmonic currents appearing in the utility neutral line gets eliminated and power quality indices on the AC mains side are improved. RVSS-LMS algorithm extracts the active weight component of load currents from non-linear loads connected at the point of common coupling. System performance using proposed RVSS-LMS algorithm, is also compared with conventional state-of-art adaptive filter algorithms. The system is realised in MATLAB environment in discrete time frame using simulink and sim power system toolboxes. Observed results demonstrate superiority in system performance using RVSS-LMS filter. The total harmonic distortion of grid current is observed within 5% which is in coherence with IEEE-519.

articleTitle: Design of a Low Leakage Pulse Transformer for Gate Driving of Multiple SiC MOSFETs for Induction Heating Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Parallel connected SiC MOSFETs are preferred as a single switch for near continuous-duty converter operation. The gate voltage is highly asymmetrical for these devices, and due to the small gate threshold voltage, they are sensitive to ringing in gate signals. This work proposes a novel low-leakage pulse transformer for a magnetically coupled Gate Drive Circuit (GDC) to feed the gate voltage to multiple isolated devices. The proposed pulse transformer can avoid spurious turn-on. The leakage- and self-inductances of the proposed transformer are computed using Finite Element Method (FEM) simulations. The calculated inductances are in agreement with the measured values. The performance of the magnetically coupled GDC with the proposed pulse transformer is experimentally verified by driving two parallel connected SiC MOSFETs for a high-speed offline induction cap sealing controller.
